• Congenital cataract, congenital deafness, congenital heart disease
• Retinopathy of prematurity

Deficiencies:

• Anemia especially severe anemia
• Vitamin A deficiency
• Vitamin D deficiency
• Severe acute malnutrition
• Goitre

Diseases:

• Scabies, fungal infections, and eczema
• Otitis media
• Rheumatic heart disease
• Reactive airway disease
• Dental caries
• Convulsive disorders

Developmental delays and disabilities:

• Vision, hearing, and neuro-motor impairment
• Motor, cognitive and language delay
• Autism
• Learning disorder
• Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the dosage of iron and folic acid for adult women under the Anemia Mukth Bharath initiative?
options: 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid daily
60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid weekly
100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid weekly
100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid daily
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid weekly

According to the Anemia Mukt Bharat initiative, adult women need to take 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid tablets once a week. These tablets are sugar-coated, and red in color.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is a marker of the heat stability of vaccines?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. VVM

Vaccine Vial Monitors (VVM) are heat-sensitive indicators that are routinely used to monitor vaccine viability as the vaccine vial moves across the supply chain.

VVM records cumulative heat exposure through a gradual change in color. If the color of the inner square is the same or is darker than the outer circle, the vaccine has been exposed to too much temperature and should be discarded.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is a non-parametric test?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Friedman test

Friedman test is a non-parametric test. It is used to test for differences between groups when the dependent variable being measured is ordinal.

Other options:

Student t-test, analysis of variation (ANOVA) test, and pearson correlation are all based on quantitative data and hence grouped under parametric tests.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is true about the reference woman used in the calculation of the recommended daily allowance (RDA)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Weight 55 kgs

The reference woman used in the calculation of recommended daily allowance (RDA) weighs about 55 Kgs and is aged between 19-39 years, nonpregnant, non-lactating with a height of 1.61 meters, and a BMI of 21.2, is free from disease and physically fit for active work.

On each working day, she must be engaged in 8 hours of occupation/work, which usually involves moderate activity. When not at work she spends 8 hours in bed, 4-6 hours in sitting and moving about, 2 hours in walking, and in active recreation or household duties.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is true regarding nikshay poshan yojana?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Rs 500 is given per month

Under nikshay poshan yojana, a financial incentive of Rs.500 per month is provided for nutritional support to each notified TB patient for the duration of anti-TB treatment.

For pediatric TB patients who do not have bank accounts, the money shall be deposited in parent's/guardian's accounts whose details are to be sought and entered in nikshay against the patient’s records.

The processing of payment is on the 7th of every month.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following methods is not effective against preventing the spread of COVID 19?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1% glutaraldehyde

1% glutaraldehyde is not effective against preventing the spread of COVID 19.

Effective everyday practices that prevent the spread include actions like keeping a social distance (at least 6 feet) from others, washing your hands with soap and water for 20 seconds or using a hand sanitizer with at least 70% alcohol, and wearing a face mask when you have to go out in public.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following quantitative methods is the best to study previous research studies?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Meta-analysis

The quantitative method which is the best to study previous research studies of a selected topic/research question is meta-analysis.

A systematic review is a process of collecting, reviewing, and presenting information from earlier research to answer a question. It is a qualitative technique. It may or may not involve a meta-analysis.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: You are a medical officer at a PHC. Which of the following would you advise for mass prophylaxis/ treatment for anemia?
options: FeSO4 + Vit C + Folate + Vit B12
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. FeSO4 + Vit C + Folate + Vit B12

Among the given options, FeSO4 + vitamin C + Folate + vitamin B12 may be considered for mass prophylaxis against anemia.

Vit C enhances the absorption of iron from the stomach by acting as a reducing substance.

Subclinical folate deficiency is seen in up to 30% of North Indian pregnant women. Moreover, it may be masked by widespread iron deficiency. It is, for this reason, iron and folate supplementation is carried out in national programmes.

Clinical vitamin B12 deficiency is not commonly encountered, but subclinical cases might be seen in up to 30% of adults and children due to widespread restriction to consumption of vegetarian products only. Hence supplementing vitamin B12 is a good idea provided the cost factor is not an issue.

Option B: Iron (III) hydroxide polymaltose was marketed as being superior to iron sulfate in terms of efficacy, but it lacked any data to back up the evidence.

Option C: Ferrous fumarate may be considered for the treatment of iron deficiency anemia with similar efficacy as that of ferrous sulfate.

Option D: Injection iron sucrose or any parenteral form is not used as a first-line option. It is only indicated if the oral form is not tolerated.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: 6 interventions in Anemia Mukt Bharat includes all except:
options: Testing for anemia using a digital hemoglobinometer
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Biennial deworming

Anemia Mukt Bharat includes 1) iron-folic acid supplementation, 2) behavior change communication, 3) digital hemoglobin testing, and 4) bi- annual deworming (done on 10 Feb and 10 Aug), not biennial deworming.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A “Fully immunized child” refers to one who has received:
options: BCG, 3 doses OPV, 3 doses Pentavalent, 3 doses RVV, 2 doses fIPV, 1 dose PCV (primary), Measles/MR-1
BCG, 2 doses OPV, 1 dose Pentavalent, 2 doses RVV, 1 dose fIPV, 1 dose PCV (primary), Measles/MR-1
BCG, 3 doses OPV, 3 doses Pentavalent, 3 doses RVV, 2 doses fIPV, 1 dose PCV (primary), Measles/MR-1, MR-2, DPT booster-1, OPV booster
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. BCG, 3 doses OPV, 3 doses Pentavalent, 3 doses RVV, 2 doses fIPV, 1 dose PCV (primary), Measles/MR-1

• Fully immunized child = received BCG, 3 doses OPV, 3 doses Pentavalent, 3 doses RVV, 2 doses fIPV, 1 dose PCV (primary), Measles/MR-1 — all before completing 1 year.
• "Completely immunized" = includes 2nd year doses too (MR-2, DPT booster-1, OPV booster).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 1-gram quantity of double fortified salt (DFS) typically contains approximately:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 30 μg iodine and 1 mg iron

Double Fortified Salt (DFS) is iodized salt additionally fortified with iron (usually encapsulated ferrous fumarate) to address iodine deficiency disorders (IDD) and iron deficiency anemia (IDA) simultaneously.

Standard composition (per 1 g of DFS):

• Iodine: ≈ 30 μg
• Iron: ≈ 1 mg

This formulation ensures:

• Adequate iodine intake with usual salt consumption
• Meaningful iron supplementation without altering taste or color

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 10-year-old child from a hilly region has neck swelling and poor school performance. The PHC is discussing iodine deficiency disorder indicators. Which is considered the principal impact indicator for iodine deficiency in population monitoring?
options: Median urinary iodine excretion in the population
Iodine content in household salt only
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Median urinary iodine excretion in the population

For population monitoring of iodine deficiency disorders, the principal impact indicator is the median urinary iodine concentration or excretion in a representative sample, typically school-age children or pregnant women depending on the program question. Urinary iodine reflects recent iodine intake, because most absorbed iodine is excreted in urine. This makes it the most sensitive and program-responsive indicator for judging whether the population is currently iodine sufficient after interventions like universal salt iodization.

Goitre rate is an impact indicator too, but it is a lag indicator. Thyroid enlargement reflects longer-term iodine status and can persist even after iodine repletion, so it is less useful as the principal indicator once iodization programs are underway.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 2 month old child comes to the OPD with complaints of fever, pain and fluctuant swelling at the Left upper limb where he recently received a vaccine. Which of the following steps should be done in the treatment of this child?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Incision and drainage

A fluctuant swelling at the vaccination site indicates a cold abscess, most commonly due to improper technique or contamination. The correct management is incision and drainage. Conservative management is inadequate once fluctuation appears, and antitubercular therapy is not indicated unless there is evidence of disseminated disease.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 2-year-old child from a country without a routine BCG program is brought to India for long-term stay. The child has never received BCG vaccination. According to the Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) immunization schedule, what is the most appropriate recommendation regarding BCG administration?
options: BCG cannot be given after 1 year of age
BCG can only be given in newborn period
Administer BCG now, as it can be given up to 5 years of age
BCG should be deferred until school entry
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Administer BCG now, as it can be given up to 5 years of age

IAP catch-up policy:

• BCG can be given up to 5 years of age in unvaccinated children.
• After 5 years → not routinely recommended (tuberculous sensitization already high in population)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 2-year-old undergoing chemotherapy for leukemia presents for vaccination counselling. Which of the following statements regarding live vaccines is accurate for this patient?
options: Live vaccines are contraindicated even after chemotherapy is completed.
Live vaccines can be safely administered during chemotherapy as long as the patient is afebrile.
Live vaccines are contraindicated in immunocompromised states, but household contacts can safely receive them.
Live vaccines are contraindicated in leukemia patients only if they are in remission.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Live vaccines are contraindicated in immunocompromised states, but household contacts can safely receive them.

• A child undergoing chemotherapy for leukemia is severely immunocompromised.
•

Live attenuated vaccines (e.g., BCG, OPV, MMR, varicella) are contraindicated in such patients due to risk of vaccine-derived infection.

•

Household contacts of immunocompromised patients can and should receive live vaccines (e.g., OPV replaced by IPV in India; MMR, varicella are safe).

• This indirectly protects the immunocompromised child by reducing exposure risk.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 24-year-old man is diagnosed with Syphilis. During counseling, he is asked to identify individuals in the same socio-sexual network who may also be infected, even if they are not direct sexual contacts. Which method of case detection is being used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Cluster testing

• Cluster testing involves identifying and testing people belonging to the same socio-sexual network or environment, not just direct contacts.
• Contact tracing: Direct sexual contacts only.
• Cluster testing: Entire socio-sexual group/network.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 28-year-old pregnant woman employed in a garment factory is entitled to specific benefits under the ESI scheme. Which of the following correctly describes the maternity benefit provision?
options: Full wages for 91 days after delivery
Full wages for 26 weeks for pregnancy and childbirth, including a premature delivery
80% of daily wages for 14 days post-tubectomy
90% of wages as a pension for the dependents of the insured person
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Full wages for 26 weeks for pregnancy and childbirth, including a premature delivery

The ESI Act provides social security benefits to insured workers, including maternity benefits. Under current provisions, insured women are entitled to full wages for 26 weeks for pregnancy and childbirth, including premature delivery. This reflects a rights-based approach to maternal health and worker welfare. Understanding such entitlements is important for public health physicians working in occupational and community health settings.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 28-year-old woman comes to the OPD to establish care. She usually eats fast food for lunch, and cooks in the evenings. She goes to the gym about once every 2 weeks. The patient's temperature is 36.7 C (98F), blood pressure is 118/64 mm Hg, pulse is 60/min, and respirations are 14/min. Her BMI is 24.6 kg/m2. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory results are within the normal range. Counselling this patient regarding diet and exercise habits would be an example of which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Primary prevention

Counseling a person with normal labs and no disease to improve diet and exercise aims to prevent the initial occurrence of disease. This is primary prevention, not primordial (policy-level), secondary (screening), or tertiary (rehabilitation).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 3-month-old infant develops a fluctuant abscess at the BCG injection site without systemic symptoms. What is the least appropriate management?
options: Incision followed by topical INH/PAS powder if persistent
Observation if the abscess is small
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Oral isoniazid therapy for 6 months

Localized BCG abscess does not require systemic antitubercular therapy. Management:

• Aspiration if fluctuant.
• Persistent lesion → incision and topical INH/PAS powder.
• Avoid routine systemic INH.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 3-year-old girl presented to the PHC with difficulty in walking and bowing of legs. She was undernourished and had minimal exposure to the sun. Which programme deals with nutritional deficiency in children below 6 years of age?
options: National Nutritional Deficiency and Control Programme
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Integrated Child Development Services

ICDS covers children 0–6 years — supplementary nutrition, immunization, health check-ups, referral, pre-school education, nutrition/health education for mothers. This case (rickets — bowing of legs, poor sun exposure, malnutrition) falls under ICDS's nutrition/health monitoring for under-6 children.

Why not others:

• A. Anaemia Mukt Bharat: Targets anemia specifically, across life stages, not general nutrition for <6 yrs
• C. National Nutritional Deficiency and Control Programme: No such programme by this name
• D. Mid-Day Meal: School-going children (6–14 yrs), not <6 yrs

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 30-year-old man attends a routine health check-up. He has no medical illnesses, but he has a sedentary lifestyle and frequently consumes processed food. His physician advises regular exercise and a balanced diet despite normal examination findings. This intervention is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Health promotion

Health promotion encourages healthy lifestyle behaviors before disease develops (primary prevention).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 32-year-old community health officer in Jaipur, Dr. Priya Malhotra, is reviewing the healthcare statistics of her jurisdiction. She's observed an upward trend in vaccine-preventable diseases over the past few months. Concerned about this, she's keen on revisiting the immunization strategies to enhance vaccine coverage. She believes that understanding the most recent immunization patterns is pivotal. Which of the following data sources would best provide her with the latest trends of immunization in the community?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. District-level household survey

The District Level Household Survey (DLHS) is an important source of community-level data on maternal and child health indicators, including immunization coverage, making it useful for assessing recent vaccination trends and program performance.

Key features of DLHS:

• Provides district-level health indicators
• Evaluates reproductive and child health services
• Assesses immunization status, institutional deliveries, family planning, and healthcare utilization
• Helps in planning and monitoring public health programs

Why other options are incorrect:

• Census data → Conducted every 10 years; demographic rather than immunization-focused
• Rural survey → Not a standardized national source for immunization trends
• Sample Registration System (SRS) → Primarily provides birth rate, death rate, and infant mortality statistics

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 32-year-old man is diagnosed with sputum-positive pulmonary tuberculosis at a district hospital. As part of the public health response, his household members and close workplace contacts are identified and screened for tuberculosis. Asymptomatic contacts are followed up and offered appropriate preventive therapy. This activity is best described as:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Secondary prevention

The described activity includes:

• Identification and screening of contacts of a sputum-positive TB case
• Early detection of disease among contacts
• Follow-up of asymptomatic contacts with preventive therapy (e.g., TPT)

These actions are aimed at early diagnosis and prompt intervention, which defines secondary prevention.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 32-year-old woman dies on Day 45 post-delivery due to puerperal sepsis. All of the following are true except:
options: This death is not counted as maternal death
PPH is the most common cause of maternal mortality
Accidents during pregnancy are excluded from maternal death
Electrocution during pregnancy is counted as maternal death
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Electrocution during pregnancy is counted as maternal death

• Why: Maternal death = female death <42 days of delivery due to pregnancy/related causes — explicitly EXCLUDING accidents and electrocution. Day 45 is beyond 42 days → not maternal death.
• This Q tests 3 facts simultaneously: time cutoff, exclusions, and the clinical scenario trap.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 35-year-old farmer from Bihar presents with progressive lower limb weakness over 3 months. He walks with difficulty using one stick. Dietary history reveals exclusive khesri dal consumption during drought. Which stage, toxin, and preventive method are correctly matched?
options: Stage 3; BOAA Vitamin C + steeping + parboiling
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Stage 3; BOAA Vitamin C + steeping + parboiling

• One stick = Stage 3 of neurolathyrism. Khesri dal = Lathyrus sativus.
• Toxin = BOAA (Beta-Oxalyl Amino Alanine).
• Prevention = Vitamin C, steeping, parboiling.
• All correctly matched in option A.
• Options C and D mix toxins from different diseases (sanguinarine = epidemic dropsy; pyrrolizidine = endemic ascites).

| Disease | Toxin | Food | Prevention | Stages (neurolathyrism)

| ------- | ----- | ---- | ---------- | -----------------------

| Neurolathyrism | BOAA | Khesri dal | Vit C, steeping, parboiling | 1=silent, 2=no stick, 3=one stick, 4=two sticks, 5=crawler

| Endemic ascites | Pyrrolizidine | Adulterated millets | Sieving | —

| Epidemic dropsy | Sanguinarine | Adulterated mustard oil | Nitric acid chromatography, de-weeding | —

| Aflatoxicosis | Aflatoxin (A. flavus) | Stored groundnuts | Low humidity + ventilation | —

| Ergotism | Ergot alkaloid (Claviceps) | Rye, sorghum, bhajra | Float in 20% salt solution | —

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 35-year-old woman visits a Health and Wellness Centre for population-based screening under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD). Which of the following cancers is not included in routine screening?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Colon cancer

Under NP-NCD, population-based screening includes:

• Hypertension
• Diabetes mellitus
• Oral cancer
• Breast cancer
• Cervical cancer

Colon cancer is not included in routine NP-NCD screening.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 39-year-old male develops progressive weakness starting in the feet and ascending to involve both legs and arms over the course of several days. He reports tingling sensations, and examination reveals areflexia in the lower limbs. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows elevated protein with normal cell counts. Which of the following vaccines has historically been associated with this rare adverse neurological event?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Influenza vaccine

The clinical picture describes Guillain–Barré Syndrome (GBS):

• Ascending symmetric weakness
• Areflexia
• Paresthesias
•

CSF: albuminocytologic dissociation (↑ protein, normal cell count)

•

Influenza vaccine

• Historically associated with a very small increased risk of GBS, most notably after the 1976 swine flu vaccination campaign.
• Current influenza vaccines carry an extremely low risk (≈1–2 excess cases per million), and benefits far outweigh risks.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 4-month-old infant from a rural village presents with cyanosis, irritability, and feeding difficulty. The family reports using shallow well water for preparing formula milk. Water testing from the area shows excessive contamination. Which contaminant in drinking water is most likely responsible for this presentation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Nitrates

A 4-month-old infant with cyanosis, irritability, and feeding difficulty after consuming formula prepared with shallow well water is a classic presentation of methemoglobinemia (Blue Baby Syndrome).

• Nitrates in well water (from agricultural runoff, sewage contamination) are converted to nitrites in the infant gut.
• Nitrites oxidize hemoglobin (Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺) → methemoglobin, which cannot carry oxygen → cyanosis.
• Infants <6 months are especially vulnerable due to:

o    Low gastric acidity

o    Immature methemoglobin reductase enzyme system

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 4-year-old with nephrotic syndrome achieves complete remission on prednisolone (2 mg/kg/day x 6 weeks). He is about to receive MMR vaccine. Regarding live vaccine administration, which statement is correct?
options: MMR can be given during low-dose alternate-day prednisolone
MMR must be avoided for 4 weeks after stopping steroids only if on high-dose (≥2 mg/kg/day x ≥2 weeks)
MMR is completely contraindicated in all nephrotic patients on steroids
MMR can be given any time as nephrotic syndrome is not immunosuppressive
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. MMR must be avoided for 4 weeks after stopping steroids only if on high-dose (≥2 mg/kg/day x ≥2 weeks)

MMR must be avoided for 4 weeks after stopping steroids only if on high-dose (≥2 mg/kg/day or ≥20 mg/day for ≥2 weeks).

Live attenuated vaccines such as MMR and varicella should not be administered during high-dose systemic corticosteroid therapy because of the risk of uncontrolled replication of the vaccine strain in an immunosuppressed host. High-dose steroid therapy is defined as prednisolone ≥2 mg/kg/day (or ≥20 mg/day) for ≥2 weeks. In such children, live vaccines should be deferred until at least 4 weeks after discontinuation of steroids. However, low-dose, alternate-day, short-course (<14 days), topical, inhaled, or physiological replacement doses are not contraindications to live vaccination.

High-Yield

• High-dose steroids (≥2 mg/kg/day or ≥20 mg/day for ≥2 weeks) → Avoid live vaccines; wait 4 weeks after stopping.
• Low-dose/alternate-day or short-course steroids (<14 days) → Live vaccines can be administered.
• Inactivated vaccines can be given during steroid therapy, although the immune response may be reduced.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 46-year-old man with diabetes is studied for association between smoking and CAD. Age is suspected to distort the association. Which is the best method to control a known confounder at the analysis stage?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Stratification

A confounder is controlled at different stages of a study.

At the analysis stage, a known confounder such as age is best controlled by methods that adjust the association after data collection. The classic and most directly tested method is stratification, where the smoking–CAD association is examined within strata of age. If the stratum-specific estimates are similar, they can be combined using a weighted method such as

Mantel–Haenszel adjustment. This removes distortion due to age.

Randomization and restriction are design-stage methods. Blinding prevents information bias, not confounding. Increasing response rate addresses non-response bias, not confounding.

• Confounding control at the analysis stage includes stratification and multivariable regression.
• Confounding control at the design stage includes randomization, restriction, and matching.
• Blinding is for minimizing information bias, not confounding.
• If stratification shows heterogeneous stratum-specific effects, that suggests effect modification rather than confounding.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 5-month-old infant is brought to the immunization clinic for administration of OPV. The child currently has acute watery diarrhea, but is otherwise active, hydrated, and afebrile. What is the most appropriate course of action?
options: Postpone OPV until diarrhea completely resolves
Withhold OPV and give IPV instead
Administer OPV now, but do not count the dose; repeat the dose later
Do not give OPV during episodes of diarrhea due to vaccine failure risk
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Administer OPV now, but do not count the dose; repeat the dose later

Mild diarrhea → OPV can be given

• BUT intestinal infection may interfere with OPV uptake

Therefore:

• Dose is administered but not “counted” → repeat OPV later

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 5-year-old child develops acute flaccid paralysis. AFP surveillance is initiated. Stool samples are collected 36 hours after reporting. Two samples are taken with a 20-hour gap. Samples weigh 6g and reach the lab in 80 hours stored at 4°C. Which surveillance parameter is correctly met and which is violated?
options: Sensitivity met; completeness of case investigation violated
Operation efficacy met; completeness of case investigation violated
Completeness of case investigation violated; operation efficacy violated
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Completeness of case investigation violated; operation efficacy violated

AFP surveillance indicators:

| Indicator | Target | Case details | Assessment

| --------- | ------ | ------------ | ----------

| Sensitivity of surveillance | >1 AFP/lac/year in <15 yrs | — | Not assessable here

| Completeness of case investigation | >80% adequate stool collection: 2 samples\, min 24hr gap\, collected <14 days\, weight >8g each | 20hr gap + weight 6g | VIOLATED

| Completeness of follow up | >80% AFP cases with residual paralysis check at 60 days | Not yet | Pending

| Operation efficacy | Stool must reach lab <72 hours of collection | 80 hours | VIOLATED

Sample collection within 48 hours of reporting but gap between samples should be >24 hrs. Weight >8g needed. Lab receipt should be <72 hrs

Two parameters violated: Completeness of case investigation + Operation efficacy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 50-year-old historian is researching the impact of medical advancements on society. He notes a significant shift in the leading causes of mortality from infectious to chronic diseases over the past century. This observation is crucial for understanding how public health strategies have evolved. What term best describes this shift in disease prevalence?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Epidemiological transition

The observed change in leading causes of death from infectious diseases to chronic, non-communicable diseases is termed the epidemiological transition. It reflects improvements in sanitation, nutrition, and healthcare alongside lifestyle changes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 52-year-old pesticide factory worker develops unexplained restrictive lung disease. The occupational medicine unit suspects that asbestos exposure is a necessary component cause for this disease in this cluster, but not sufficient by itself. Which causal model best explains that multiple “component causes” together form a “sufficient cause,” and removing 1 component can prevent disease in some individuals?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Rothman causal pie model

The stem explicitly describes the idea of a necessary component cause that is not sufficient alone, and it asks for the model in which multiple component causes together form a sufficient cause. This is the core idea of the Rothman causal pie model.

In Rothman’s model:

• A “sufficient cause” is represented by a whole pie, meaning a complete set of causal components that, together, inevitably produce the disease.
• Each slice is a “component cause.”
• A component can be necessary in a particular causal pathway if it appears in every sufficient cause for that disease in that population, but it is still not sufficient by itself.
• Removing 1 component cause can prevent disease in those individuals whose sufficient cause required that component. It will not prevent all disease if there are alternative pies that do not include that component.

This fits the occupational cluster description where asbestos might be one crucial piece among several, such as co-exposures, smoking, genetic susceptibility, intensity-duration, and other workplace factors.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 55-year-old man undergoes screening for colorectal cancer with a new stool DNA test. The test was performed in a group of 1000 patients, of whom 200 were confirmed to have colorectal cancer on colonoscopy. Of these 200 patients, 180 tested positive with the new DNA test, while 20 tested negative. Which of the following best represents the property of the test demonstrated by the proportion of patients with colorectal cancer who had a positive DNA test?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Sensitivity

Sensitivity = True Positives / (True Positives + False Negatives)

In this question:

• True positives = 180
• False negatives = 20

Sensitivity = 180 / (180 + 20) = 180 / 200 = 90%

Sensitivity means the ability of a test to correctly identify people who actually have the disease.

• High sensitivity → few false negatives
• Good screening tests are usually highly sensitive

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 58-year-old male with a history of hypercholesterolemia is enrolled in a clinical study to evaluate the efficacy of a new statin medication. The research team records his fasting cholesterol levels, which are notably elevated. He is then started on the statin therapy, and his cholesterol levels are re-measured after 6 weeks of consistent medication use. The primary aim of the study is to determine the statistical significance of the change in his cholesterol levels before and after the intervention. Given this scenario, which statistical test is most appropriate for analyzing the data?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Paired t-test

A paired t-test is used to compare the means of a continuous variable measured twice in the same individuals (eg, before-and-after measurements).

In this study:

• Cholesterol level is a continuous variable
• Measurements are taken in the same patient before and after statin therapy
• Therefore, the observations are paired/dependent

Hence, the correct test is the paired t-test.

Key distinctions:

• Unpaired (independent) t-test → compares means between 2 different independent groups
• ANOVA → compares means among ≥3 groups
• Chi-square test → analyzes associations between categorical variables

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 58-year-old male with T2DM presents with high grade fever and cough. He is diagnosed with COVID-19 and is admitted. He dies on the 7th day of illness. As part of surveillance, his death is recorded. What type of surveillance is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Passive

Death recorded as part of routine reporting (hospital records death, reports through standard case-reporting channels) — no active case-finding effort by health authority. Passive surveillance relies on routine, ongoing reporting by healthcare facilities/providers.

| Type | Definition

| ---- | ----------

| Active | Health worker actively visits/collects data (e.g., house-to-house case search)

| Passive | Routine reporting by facilities without active seeking (this case)

| Sentinel | Selected reporting sites represent larger population trend

| Syndromic | Based on symptom clusters/patterns, before confirmed diagnosis

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 6-week-old infant is brought to the immunization clinic for the first time. The child was delivered at home and has not received any vaccines. On examination, the infant is healthy, weighs 4.5 kg, and has no contraindications to vaccination. Which of the following is the most appropriate immunization strategy at this visit?
options: Give BCG, OPV-1, Pentavalent-1, fIPV-1, Rotavirus-1, PCV-1 and Hepatitis B-1
Defer BCG because the child is older than 4 weeks and administer the remaining vaccines
Administer live vaccines, including BCG followed by killed vaccine one week later
Administer only Pentavalent-1 and advise return after 4 weeks for the remaining vaccines
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Give BCG, OPV-1, Pentavalent-1, fIPV-1, Rotavirus-1, PCV-1 and Hepatitis B-1

• Catch-up immunization; BCG can be administered up to 1 year of age in an unvaccinated infant.
• This child has missed the birth vaccines, but vaccination should never be restarted. Instead, follow the catch-up immunization schedule.
•

At 6 weeks, the child is eligible for:

• BCG (can be given up to 1 year if unvaccinated)
• OPV
• Pentavalent
• Hepatitis B
• Rotavirus
• fIPV
• PCV

•

Multiple vaccines can safely be given during the same visit at different anatomical sites.

• Delaying vaccines unnecessarily increases susceptibility to preventable diseases.

Why are others wrong?

B. Defer BCG because the child is older than 4 weeks and administer the remaining vaccines: Incorrect. BCG is not contraindicated after 4 weeks; it can be given up to 1 year.

D. Administer only Pentavalent-1 and advise return after 4 weeks for the remaining vaccines: There is no reason to delay the remaining vaccines.

NEET PG Pearl: "Missed opportunity for vaccination should be avoided.”

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 6-year-old child from a Below Poverty Line (BPL) family is diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. The child requires high-cost treatment at a tertiary government hospital, which the family cannot afford. The treating physician advises applying for a government scheme that provides one-time financial assistance for patients with major life-threatening illnesses. Which of the following schemes is most appropriate in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN)

Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) provides one-time financial assistance to BPL patients suffering from major life-threatening illnesses treated at government hospitals. It directly addresses high-cost treatments like leukemia. Other schemes focus on preventive care, infrastructure, or general insurance, making RAN the most appropriate option.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 62-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia comes to the emergency department of an academic medical center with chest pain, nausea, vomiting, and diaphoresis. Investigators are designing a randomized control trial to test the hypothesis that drug B will decrease the mortality associated with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction compared to standard of care. To ensure that investigators will not miss a difference between drug B and standard of care (if a difference truly exists), which of the following would they want to maximize?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1- beta

To avoid missing a real difference between treatments (i.e., reducing Type II error), investigators aim to maximize statistical power, which equals 1 − β. Higher power increases the likelihood of detecting a true effect if it exists. Alpha (α) relates to Type I error, not this concern.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 62-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes visits his physician for a routine checkup. His physician discusses recent research on a new antihypertensive drug that may reduce the risk of stroke. The physician explains that although one trial compared the new drug with placebo, the results were inconclusive. In that trial, only 50 patients with hypertension were randomized to either the new drug or placebo and followed for 2 years. At the end of the study, 2 patients in the treatment group and 3 patients in the placebo group experienced a stroke. Statistical analysis showed no significant difference between groups (p = 0.65). Which of the following best explains why this study was unable to demonstrate a difference despite the likelihood that the new drug is effective?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Insufficient statistical power

Statistical power is the probability that a study will detect a true difference when one actually exists. Studies with small sample sizes or very few outcome events are prone to insufficient statistical power, increasing the risk of a Type II error (false-negative result).

Key points:

• Increasing sample size increases statistical power
• Power is also improved by larger effect size and higher event rates
• A nonsignificant p-value does not always mean the treatment is ineffective; the study may simply be underpowered

Other options:

• Confounding by indication → treatment selection influenced by disease severity
• Effect modification → effect differs across subgroups
• Recall bias → inaccurate recollection of past exposures, common in case-control studies.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 7-month-old child from UP receives JE vaccine. The ANM notes the VVM is on the body of the vial. She reconstitutes it with phosphate saline and administers it subcutaneously in the left upper arm. Identify all errors in this scenario:
options: Wrong vaccine type being used + wrong route + wrong site
Wrong VVM location interpretation + wrong route + wrong site
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Wrong VVM location interpretation + wrong route + wrong site

JE vaccine comparison:

| Feature | JE Live vaccine | JE Killed vaccine

| ------- | --------------- | -----------------

| VVM location | Cap of vial | Body of vial

| Open vial policy | Does NOT follow | Follows (28 days)

| Heat sensitivity | Heat sensitive | Freeze sensitive

| Reconstitution | Phosphate saline | No reconstitution

| Route | Subcutaneous | Intramuscular

| Site | Left upper arm | Left anterolateral thigh

| Currently used | No (discontinued) | Yes (under NVBDCP)

VVM on BODY = killed vaccine. Killed vaccine = NO reconstitution, IM route, left anterolateral thigh.

Errors:

• Reconstituted with phosphate saline (killed vaccine needs no reconstitution — that's live vaccine)
• Given SC (should be IM)
• Given in left upper arm (should be left anterolateral thigh)

JE killed vaccine schedule: 9 months → repeat at 16–24 months. Can give till 15 years if unimmunized.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 9-month-old child attends immunization clinic. All vaccines given at this age are correct except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. fIPV - 2nd dose

Why:

| Age | Vaccines

| --- | --------

| Birth | BCG, OPV-0, Hep B birth dose

| 6 weeks | OPV-1, Rota-1, Pentavalent-1, fIPV-1, PCV-1

| 10 weeks | OPV-2, Rota-2, Pentavalent-2

| 14 weeks | OPV-3, Rota-3, Pentavalent-3, fIPV-2, PCV-2

| 9 months | Measles/MR-1, Vit A, PCV booster, fIPV-3, JE-1

| 16–24 months | Measles/MR-2, DPT booster, OPV booster, JE-2

| 5–6 years | DPT booster

| 10 & 16 years | Td

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 9-month-old infant from an urban slum has repeated exposure to unsafe water. The mother asks for the most appropriate typhoid vaccine option that is licensed for this age and provides programmatic feasibility with a single dose. Which vaccine best fits?
options: No typhoid vaccine is indicated before 2 years
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Typhoid conjugate vaccine

The Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV) is licensed for use from 6 months of age, provides long-lasting immunity, and is given as a single dose, making it programmatically feasible. Live oral Ty21a and Vi polysaccharide vaccines are not suitable at this age. Hence, TCV is the most appropriate option for infants in high-risk settings.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A biostatistician is analyzing a small dataset of serum potassium values collected from 10 patients. One value appears suspiciously high compared to the rest. To determine whether this extreme value should be statistically rejected as an outlier, the most appropriate test to apply is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Dixon’s Q-test

When dealing with a small sample size (typically n ≤ 30, especially n < 10–12) and one suspected extreme value, the most appropriate statistical test to assess whether it is an outlier is Dixon’s Q-test.

• Designed specifically for small datasets
• Used when there is only one suspected outlier
• Commonly applied in laboratory and clinical measurements
• Compares the gap between the suspicious value and its nearest neighbor relative to the range of the dataset

A. Grubbs’ test ❌

→ Also for outliers, but more appropriate for larger samples (n ≥ 20–30).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A biostatistician wants to measure the linear relationship between systolic blood pressure and serum cholesterol levels in a group of adults. Both variables are continuous and approximately normally distributed. Which statistical measure is most appropriate to quantify the strength and direction of this linear association?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Pearson correlation coefficient (r)

Pearson r measures:

✔ strength

✔ direction

✔ linear association

between two continuous variables

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A biostatistics faculty member is teaching postgraduate residents about internationally accepted reporting guidelines used for different types of biomedical research studies. During viva voce, students are asked to correctly match the study design with its appropriate reporting guideline. List I (Study Type) A. Randomized controlled trial B. Observational study C. Diagnostic accuracy study D. Case report/case series E. Systematic review and meta-analysis List II (Reporting Guideline) 1. STARD 2. CARE 3. CONSORT 4. PRISMA 5. STROBE
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. A-3, B-5, C-1, D-2, E-4

| Guideline | Used For

| --------- | --------

| CONSORT | Randomized Controlled Trials

| STROBE | Observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional)

| STARD | Diagnostic accuracy studies

| CARE | Case reports/case series

| PRISMA | Systematic reviews and meta-analyses

| MOOSE | Meta-analysis of observational studies

| SRQR | Qualitative research

| SQUIRE | Quality improvement studies

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A cardiology research team is investigating factors that contribute to the development of left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in patients with long-standing hypertension. They enroll 1,200 hypertensive patients and collect data on age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, and daily sodium intake. Echocardiography is used to measure left ventricular mass index (a continuous variable). The investigators want to determine the independent association between sodium intake and left ventricular mass index while controlling for age, sex, BMI, and smoking. Which of the following is the most appropriate statistical method for this analysis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Regression analysis

Regression analysis is used to evaluate the relationship between a dependent outcome variable and one or more independent predictor variables, while adjusting for potential confounders. In this study:

• Dependent variable: Left ventricular mass index (continuous variable)
• Independent variables: Sodium intake, age, sex, BMI, smoking status

Because the outcome is continuous, the appropriate method is multiple linear regression, which estimates the independent effect of sodium intake on LV mass after controlling for other variables. Key distinctions:

• Chi-square test → association between categorical variables
• Independent t-test → compares means between 2 groups
• Correlation coefficient → measures strength/direction of association between 2 continuous variables but does not adjust for confounders
• Regression analysis → assesses independent associations and controls for multiple variables simultaneously.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A child came for DPT vaccination at 10 weeks with a past history of fever more than 40°C and inconsolable cry at 6 weeks following vaccination. What should be done next?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Give DTaP vaccine

A history of high fever (>40°C) and inconsolable crying after DPT is a precaution, not a contraindication. In such cases, DTaP (acellular pertussis vaccine) is preferred as it causes fewer adverse reactions. Avoiding all vaccination is incorrect, and DT alone would omit pertussis protection unnecessarily. See the detailed video explanation for guidelines and Park reference.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A city has 70,00,000 urban population, 30% of which live in slums. How many UPHCs are required for the slum population according to NUHM norms?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 42

• Slum population = 30% × 70,00,000 = 21,00,000
• NUHM norm: 1 UPHC per 50,000 population → 21,00,000 / 50,000 = 42

| Facility | Population Norm

| -------- | ---------------

| UPHC (Urban PHC) | 1 per 50,000 population

| UCHC (Urban CHC) | 1 per 5,00,000 population

| ANM (sub-centre level, urban) | 1 per 10,000–12,000

| ASHA (urban) | 1 per 1,000–2,500 (slum/vulnerable areas)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A clinical laboratory reports serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels from a sample of 100 ambulatory adult patients undergoing routine thyroid function testing. The following summary statistics are observed: • Mean = 3.1 mIU/L, • Median = 2.5 mIU/L, • Mode = 1.8 mIU/L. Based on this data, which of the following best describes the shape of the distribution of serum TSH levels in this sample?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Right-skewed

The relationship between mean, median, and mode helps identify the shape of a distribution. For a right-skewed (positively skewed) distribution: Mean > Median > Mode

In this question:

• Mean = 3.1
• Median = 2.5
• Mode = 1.8

Therefore: Mean > Median > Mode → Right-skewed distribution

• In right skewness, a few very high values pull the mean toward the right tail.
• Common right-skewed biological variables include:

• TSH levels
• Income
• Hospital stay duration

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A clinical trial compares a new drug with placebo in patients with chronic heart failure. Neither the participants nor the treating physicians know which treatment has been assigned until the study is completed. This study design primarily helps prevent:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Observer bias

Double blinding prevents investigators' expectations from influencing assessment of outcomes, thereby reducing observer (ascertainment) bias.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A clinical trial evaluates the safety profile of a new medication compared to a placebo in preventing adverse events. The study enrolled 20,000 participants, evenly randomized into two groups (new drug vs. placebo). After one year of follow-up, 2000 participants in the new drug group and 1500 participants in the placebo group experienced adverse events. Based on these findings, which of the following is the number needed to harm (NNH)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 20

Adverse event rate

• New drug group = 2000 / 10,000 = 0.20 (20%)
• Placebo group = 1500 / 10,000 = 0.15 (15%)

Absolute Risk Increase (ARI)

= 0.20 − 0.15 = 0.05

Number Needed to Harm (NNH)

= 1 / ARI

= 1 / 0.05

= 20

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A clinical trial of a new topical retinoid for acne finds p = 0.03. The null hypothesis states "no difference between retinoid and placebo." The investigator concludes the drug works and publishes. If the drug actually has no benefit, the error committed is:
options: Type II error — null hypothesis accepted when false
Type I error — null hypothesis rejected when true
No error — p<0.05 confirms drug works definitively
Ecological fallacy — population-level data applied incorrectly
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Type I error — null hypothesis rejected when true

• p<0.05 = reject null hypothesis.
• If null hypothesis is actually true (drug has no effect) but is rejected = Type I error (false positive result).
• Type I = "alpha error" = more serious error.
• Type II = null hypothesis false but accepted (false negative = missed real effect).
• p<0.05 = significant but doesn't guarantee truth — chance of Type I error = 5% at this threshold.

| Error | Null hypothesis status | Decision | Consequence

| ----- | ---------------------- | -------- | -----------

| Type I (α) | True (no real effect) | Rejected (conclude effect) | False positive — more serious

| Type II (β) | False (real effect exists) | Accepted (miss effect) | False negative

| No error | True | Accepted | Correct

| No error | False | Rejected | Correct

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A cohort study reports that smokers have a relative risk of 1.5 for developing chronic kidney disease compared with nonsmokers. The 95% confidence interval is 1.10–2.05. Which p-value is most consistent with these findings?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 0.03

Because the 95% CI does not include 1, the result is statistically significant (p < 0.05). Among the options, 0.03 is the best match.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A community-based pediatric screening program is conducted to estimate the burden of developmental disabilities in children aged 3–10 years across a district. Which of the following is the most appropriate epidemiological tool for this purpose?
options: Wing’s Comprehensive Handicaps, Behaviour and Skills Schedule
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Wing’s Comprehensive Handicaps, Behaviour and Skills Schedule

• Wing’s Comprehensive Handicaps, Behaviour and Skills Schedule (CHBSS) is an epidemiological screening tool specifically designed to assess the prevalence and pattern of developmental disabilities in children at the community level.
• It evaluates multiple domains:

• Motor skills
• Communication
• Social interaction
• Behavioral patterns
• Adaptive functioning

• It is particularly useful in large-scale surveys and public health programs, where a standardized, multidimensional assessment is required rather than detailed individual diagnosis.

Why not other options:

A. Activities of Daily Living (ADL) scale:

• Assesses functional independence, mainly in elderly or disabled adults
• Not specific for pediatric developmental screening

C. Stanford-Binet Intelligence Test:

• Measures IQ
• Used for individual diagnostic assessment, not community surveys

D. Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI):

• Measures population-level well-being (infant mortality, life expectancy, literacy)
• Not a tool for developmental disability screening

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A country’s population in 2022 was estimated at 5,000,000. At the beginning of the year, 50,000 individuals were already living with chronic hepatitis B. By the end of the same year, the Ministry of Health reported 12,000 new cases of hepatitis B and 1,500 deaths directly attributable to hepatitis B. An additional 40,000 deaths from other causes also occurred during 2022. What was the cumulative incidence of hepatitis B in this population during 2022?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 12,000 / 4,950,000

Cumulative incidence (incidence proportion) measures the risk of developing a disease over a specified period.

Formula:

Cumulative Incidence = New cases during time period / Population at risk at beginning of period

Individuals who already have the disease at the start are not at risk of developing a new case and must be excluded from the denominator.

In this question:

• Total population = 5,000,000
• Existing hepatitis B cases = 50,000
• Population at risk: 5,000,000 - 50,000 = 4,950,000
• New cases during 2022 = 12,000

Thus:

• Cumulative incidence = 12,000 / 4,950,000
• Deaths occurring during the year do not affect the denominator in cumulative incidence calculations unless person-time incidence is being calculated.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A demographer explains that Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is the average number of children a woman would have if she experienced the current age-specific fertility rates throughout her reproductive span. Which is the key advantage of TFR over CBR?
options: TFR is independent of the age-sex structure of the population
TFR uses total population in denominator, so it is simpler
TFR measures only married women, so it avoids bias
TFR is affected strongly by migration patterns only
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. TFR is independent of the age-sex structure of the population

Total Fertility Rate (TFR) represents the average number of children a woman would bear if she were to experience the current age-specific fertility rates (ASFRs) throughout her reproductive life (15–49 years).

• TFR is independent of the age–sex composition of the population ✔️

→ It considers only women in reproductive age and adjusts for fertility at each age group.

→ Allows valid comparison between populations and across time.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A devastating cyclone strikes the eastern coast of India, leading to mass casualties, infrastructure collapse, and flooding across multiple districts. A specialized multidisciplinary force trained in collapsed-structure search and rescue, deep-water rescue, and management of chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) emergencies is deployed immediately. The personnel at the disaster site are seen carrying the emblem shown above. Which of the following statements regarding the organization represented by this logo are correct? A. It was established under the Disaster Management Act, 2005 B. It functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Defence C. Its battalions are primarily constituted from Central Armed Police Forces D. It serves as the apex national authority responsible for framing disaster management policies E. It is trained to respond to both natural disasters and CBRN emergencies F. The Prime Minister of India serves as its ex-officio chairperson
options: A, B, D, and F only
B, C, E, and F only
A, C, D, E, and F only
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. A, C, and E only

The logo represents the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF).

• Established under the Disaster Management Act, 2005
• Functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs
• Battalions are drawn from CAPFs such as CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP, etc.
• Specialized in:

• Earthquake and flood rescue
• Cyclone response
• Collapsed-structure rescue
• CBRN emergencies

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A diabetic patient is diagnosed with proliferative diabetic retinopathy during routine screening. Laser photocoagulation is performed immediately to preserve vision and prevent blindness. This intervention is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Secondary prevention

Prompt treatment of an early diagnosed disease to prevent disability is secondary prevention.

Exam pearl:

• Treatment before disability → Secondary prevention.
• Rehabilitation after disability → Tertiary prevention.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A diagnostic test for dementia has sensitivity 80% and specificity 90%. It is used in two elderly female populations: • Population 1: dementia prevalence 15% • Population 2: dementia prevalence 30% Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. NPV₁ > NPV₂; PPV₁ < PPV₂

As disease prevalence increases:

• PPV increases
• NPV decreases

So, lower prevalence population has higher NPV, and higher prevalence population has higher PPV.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A disease has low prevalence and high individual risk if missed. A clinician uses parallel testing to screen. Compared to series testing, all of the following are true except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Parallel testing increases PPV

• Parallel = positive if ANY test positive → casts wider net → catches more true positives AND more false positives.
• More FP → PPV decreases (PPV = TP/TP+FP). Series = both tests positive → fewer FP → higher PPV.
• Parallel = high Sn, high NPV, low Sp, low PPV.

| Test combination | Sensitivity | Specificity | NPV | PPV

| ---------------- | ----------- | ----------- | --- | ---

| Series (both positive) | Low | High | Low | High

| Parallel (either positive) | High | Low | High | Low

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A disease outbreak investigator uses four time variables. A cholera patient develops symptoms 18 hours after ingesting contaminated water, and transmits the organism maximally at 36 hours after ingestion. His neighbor develops symptoms 3 days later. Which correctly identifies the generation time in this scenario?
options: Time between risk factor onset and symptom development
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 36 hours

| Time variable | Definition | This scenario

| ------------- | ---------- | -------------

| Incubation period | Entry → 1st symptom | 18 hours

| Generation time | Entry → maximum communicability | 36 hours

| Serial interval | Primary case → secondary case | 3 days

| Latent time | Risk factor onset → symptoms of NCD | Not applicable here

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district hospital compares mean hemoglobin levels between 2 independent groups of pregnant women, those receiving standard IFA and those receiving an enhanced counseling intervention. Hemoglobin is approximately normally distributed in both groups. Which test best compares the means?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Unpaired t test

When comparing means of a continuous, normally distributed variable between two independent groups, the appropriate test is the unpaired (independent) t-test. A paired t-test is used only when the same individuals are measured twice. McNemar and Fisher’s exact tests are used for categorical data, not continuous variables like hemoglobin.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district hospital undergoes external evaluation under a Ministry of Health and Family Welfare program that assesses patient rights, infection control practices, support services, clinical standards, and quality management systems before granting certification status. During inspection, the assessors identify the logo shown above, depicting a stylized “Q” surrounded by symbols of healthcare delivery services. The logo most appropriately represents which of the following?
options: National Quality Accreditation Scheme for Health Services
National Quality Assurance Standards for Public Health Facilities
National Qualitative Assessment System for Healthcare Institutions
National Quality Audit Strategy for Secondary Healthcare
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. National Quality Assurance Standards for Public Health Facilities

• NQAS (National Quality Assurance Standards) is the official quality certification framework developed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for public healthcare facilities in India.
• It evaluates healthcare institutions across multiple domains including:

• Patient rights
• Clinical care
• Infection control
• Support services
• Quality management

• Frequently confused in examinations with similarly expanded abbreviations involving:

• Accreditation
• Audit
• Assessment
• Assurance
• Standards/System/Strategy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district implements an intensive malaria control program with widespread vector control and early diagnosis. After one year, the public health officer wants to assess the efficacy of the program. Which epidemiological measure would be the best indicator?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Incidence

Incidence measures new cases occurring over a period of time. A reduction in incidence indicates that the health program is effectively preventing new cases.

Exam Pearl: Incidence = Best indicator of efficacy of preventive health programs.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district in Madhya Pradesh has CBR 19/1000 LB and CDR is 6/1000 LB. Find the annual growth rate of the district.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1.3%

Annual growth rate (natural increase) is calculated as:

Growth rate = CBR − CDR

Given:

• CBR = 19 per 1000
• CDR = 6 per 1000

Natural increase = 19 − 6 = 13 per 1000 population

So,

Annual growth rate = 13 / 1000 = 1.3% per year

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district is considering mass antibiotics to all contacts in a cholera outbreak. According to standard public health practice, the correct statement is:
options: Mass chemoprophylaxis is recommended for all contacts
Mass chemoprophylaxis is recommended only for children
Mass chemoprophylaxis is generally not recommended
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Mass chemoprophylaxis is generally not recommended

In cholera outbreaks, routine public health practice prioritizes rapid case management and WASH measures rather than giving antibiotics to all contacts. Mass chemoprophylaxis is generally discouraged because it has limited impact on outbreak control, promotes antimicrobial resistance, can cause adverse drug effects, and diverts resources from interventions that actually reduce transmission.

Core outbreak control pillars are:

• Early detection and prompt rehydration (ORS for most, IV Ringer lactate for severe dehydration).
• Antibiotics for moderate to severe cholera to shorten duration and reduce stool volume, used for cases rather than mass contacts.
• Safe water, sanitation, and hygiene including chlorination, safe storage, hand hygiene, and safe food practices.
• Risk communication, surveillance, and in some settings, oral cholera vaccine as an adjunct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district medical officer wants to evaluate how a staff nurse in a primary health center distributes her time during duty hours. Instead of continuously observing her throughout the day, the officer makes random, intermittent observations at different times over several days to record whether she is involved in direct patient care, documentation work, cleaning work, or waiting for patients. The objective is to estimate the percentage of time spent on productive vs. non productive activities. This method of time analysis is known as: This method of time analysis is known as:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Work sampling technique

Work Sampling =

👉 Intermittent, random observations

👉 Classifies activities (productive vs non-productive)

👉 Estimates proportion of time spent on different tasks

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district needs annual estimates of birth rate and death rate with better accuracy than routine CRS in many areas. Which Indian system is specifically designed to provide reliable annual birth and death rates?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. SRS

When routine Civil Registration System data are incomplete or variable across areas, India uses a dedicated system to generate reliable annual estimates of birth rate and death rate. The Sample Registration System (SRS) is specifically designed for this purpose. It provides continuous, sample-based, dual-record registration of births and deaths with periodic independent surveys to measure and correct under-reporting, allowing robust annual estimates at national and state levels and for many indicators over time.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district plans to conduct a survey on hypertension prevalence. The investigator wants a sampling approach that first selects villages and then selects households within selected villages. This is best described as:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Multistage sampling

The described approach selects sampling units in stages. First, villages are selected as primary sampling units. Next, households are selected within the chosen villages as secondary sampling units. This is the classic definition of multistage sampling, commonly used in community prevalence surveys because it is logistically feasible when a complete list of all households in the district is not easily available.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district reports 7,500 deaths in 2025 and mid-year population 1,500,000. What is the crude death rate per 1,000 population?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 5

Crude Death Rate (CDR)

= (Number of deaths / Mid-year population) × 1,000

= (7,500 / 1,500,000) × 1,000

= 5 deaths per 1,000 population

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district reports that after introducing a screening program for cervical cancer, the 5-year survival among detected cases improved, but district-level mortality due to cervical cancer did not change over several years. Which bias most plausibly explains this pattern?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Lead-time bias

An apparent improvement in survival after introducing a screening program, without any change in mortality, is explained by lead-time bias. Screening detects disease earlier, increasing the time from diagnosis to death without actually prolonging life. This falsely inflates survival statistics while true disease outcomes (mortality) remain unchanged.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district uses weekly reporting from selected health facilities that represent larger areas to track trends in influenza-like illness, rather than collecting from every facility. This is best described as:
options: Active case search for every household
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Sentinel surveillance

The scenario describes a district that deliberately selects a limited number of health facilities that are meant to represent larger geographic areas and uses their regular reports to monitor time trends in influenza-like illness. This is the defining feature of sentinel surveillance. Sentinel sites are chosen for feasibility, quality, and representativeness, and the goal is to detect trends, seasonality, and early signals of increase without the cost of universal reporting from every facility.

Passive surveillance refers to routine reporting from all reporting units without special selection and without special active effort to search for cases. Active case search involves proactive field work, often house-to-house or targeted outreach to identify cases, which is much more resource intensive. Syndromic surveillance refers to surveillance based on a clinical syndrome such as influenza-like illness, but the key distinguishing feature in this stem is the use of selected representative sites, which makes it sentinel surveillance rather than “syndromic only.”

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A district wants to align local NCD targets with WHO Global Action Plan 2013–2020 targets. Which target is correctly paired?
options: 30% reduction in raised blood pressure and 25% reduction in tobacco use
25% reduction in premature mortality from major NCDs and 30% reduction in tobacco use
Halt rise in diabetes and 50% reduction in salt intake
10% reduction in obesity and 30% reduction in physical inactivity
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 25% reduction in premature mortality from major NCDs and 30% reduction in tobacco use

The WHO Global Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of NCDs 2013–2020 framed the “9 voluntary global targets” for achievement by 2025.

•

Premature NCD mortality target is 25% relative reduction.

•

Tobacco target is 30% relative reduction in current tobacco use.

• Raised blood pressure target is 25% relative reduction.
• Salt intake target is 30% relative reduction.
• Harmful alcohol use target is 10% relative reduction, and physical inactivity target is 10% relative reduction.
• Diabetes and obesity's target is to halt the rise.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A few hours after vaccination, the parents noticed that the child had become unusually quiet, had markedly reduced spontaneous movements, appeared pale, and did not respond appropriately to handling. There was no fever or convulsion. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is true?
options: It is a contraindication to further vaccination by the same vaccine
It is a coincidental event unrelated to immunization
The episode typically occurs within 0–48 hours following vaccination
It is caused by improper vaccine storage and cold chain failure
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. The episode typically occurs within 0–48 hours following vaccination

The described episode is Hypotonic–Hyporesponsive Episode (HHE).

• Most commonly reported after DTwP/DTP-containing vaccines
• Timing: Within 0–48 hours after vaccination ✔

A) Contraindication to further vaccination ❌

→ Not a contraindication; future doses can be given with observation

B) Coincidental event unrelated to immunization ❌

→ Recognized AEFI temporally associated with vaccination

D) Caused by cold chain failure ❌

→ Cold chain failure causes ineffective vaccine or local reactions, not HHE

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A group of investigators is planning a phase III clinical trial to assess whether the histone deacetylase 3 inhibitor BG45 should be used in the treatment of multiple myeloma (MM). Which of the following sets of characteristics best describes this clinical trial Phase?
options: Evaluate safety of BG45 - Small healthy volunteer group
Evaluate safety and efficacy of BG45 against standard of care - Large group of patients
Evaluate safety of BG45 - Large group of patients
Evaluate safety and efficacy of BG45 against standard of care - Small group of patients
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Evaluate safety and efficacy of BG45 against standard of care - Large group of patients

Phase III trials are conducted on a large group of patients, comparing the new drug with standard therapy or placebo, focusing on efficacy and safety. They confirm therapeutic benefit before approval. Hence, evaluating safety and efficacy against standard of care in a large patient group is correct.

| Trial Phase | Typical Participants | Approximate Sample Size | Main Objective | Key Assessments | Major Outcome

| ----------- | -------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------- | --------------- | -------------

| Preclinical | Animals, cell cultures | Variable | Evaluate basic safety before human exposure | Toxicity, pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), teratogenicity, carcinogenicity | Determines whether drug can enter human testing

| Phase 0 | Healthy volunteers | 10–15 | Exploratory microdosing study | Preliminary PK/PD | Early human biologic behavior

| Phase I | Usually healthy volunteers (patients in cancer/HIV drugs) | 20–100 | Safety and dose finding | Maximum tolerated dose (MTD), adverse effects, PK/PD | Establishes safe dose range

| Phase II | Patients with target disease | 100–300 | Efficacy assessment | Therapeutic response, dose optimization, continued safety monitoring | Determines whether drug works

| Phase III | Large patient population | Hundreds to thousands | Compare with standard therapy or placebo | Efficacy, safety, risk-benefit ratio, adverse events | Basis for regulatory approval

| Phase IV | General population after approval | Very large/ongoing | Post-marketing surveillance | Rare adverse drug reactions, long-term safety, real-world effectiveness | Detects uncommon or delayed complications

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A group of investigators who are studying individuals infected with Trypanosoma cruzi is evaluating the ELISA absorbance cutoff value of serum samples for diagnosis of infection. The previous cutoff point is found to be too high, and the researchers decide to lower the threshold by 15%. Which of the following outcomes is most likely to result from this decision?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Increased negative predictive value

Why lowering the cutoff changes test performance

When the ELISA cutoff is lowered (threshold reduced by 15%):

• More samples will be labeled positive
• False negatives decrease
• Sensitivity/NPV increases
• Specificity/PPV decreases

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A group of researchers want to identify factors related to hospital-acquired bacteremia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). A total of 45 patients were enrolled in the study after MRSA was isolated from a blood sample taken from them on the third or subsequent day after admission. In addition, 90 patients admitted to the hospital over the same period with a length of stay >2 days who did not have bacteremia were randomly selected. The frequency of factors such as insertion of a central line or urinary catheter and surgical site infection were then compared between the 2 groups. Which of the following is the most appropriate null hypothesis for this study?
options: Hazard ratio is not equal to 1
Odds ratio is not equal to 1
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Odds ratio is equal to 1

This is a case–control study of MRSA bacteremia. The null hypothesis states that there is no association between exposure and outcome, which translates to an odds ratio of 1. Hence, option C is correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A healthcare provider is evaluating the effectiveness of a new diagnostic test for early-stage pancreatic cancer. The test has been reported to have a sensitivity of 85% and a specificity of 95%. In a population where the prevalence of early-stage pancreatic cancer is 5%, what is the probability that a person who tests positive actually has the disease?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 47%

The probability that a person with a positive test actually has the disease is called the Positive Predictive Value (PPV). PPV depends on:

• Sensitivity
• Specificity
• Disease prevalence (very important)

Formula: PPV = True Positives / {True Positives + False Positives}

Using a hypothetical population of 1000:

• Prevalence = 5% → Diseased = 50, Non-diseased = 950
• Sensitivity = 85%

• True positives = 85% of 50 = 42.5
• False negatives = 7.5

• Specificity = 95%

• True negatives = 95% of 950 = 902.5
• False positives = 47.5

Now:

• PPV =  42.5 / ( 42.5 + 47.5) =  42.5 / 90 = approx 47%
• In low-prevalence diseases, even highly specific tests can have a relatively low PPV due to increased false positives. Increasing prevalence increases PPV and decreases NPV.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A hospital biostatistician analyzes patient wait times over several months to find patterns and outliers for optimizing patient flow. After analyzing four different months, the following box plots are created to illustrate the findings. Based on the given plots, match the correct description.
options: Normal distribution, evident outliers, negative skewness, positive skewness
Evident positive skewness, normal distribution, negative skewness, outliers present
Typical distribution, positive skewed, skewed negatively, outliers
Standard distribution, outliers present, evident positive skewness, negative skewness
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Normal distribution, evident outliers, negative skewness, positive skewness

• Longer tail = direction of skewness
• Tail to left → negative skew
• Tail to right → positive skew
• Dots outside whiskers = outliers

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A hospital wants to estimate the prevalence of diabetic nephropathy. Kidney biopsy samples are obtained from 500 adult patients with diabetes who receive care at the hospital. The samples are then interpreted by 10 different pathologists, 5 of whom work at the hospital and 5 of whom work at nearby institutions. A preliminary analysis shows that the pathologists who work for the hospital are 3 times more likely to interpret the biopsy samples as diabetic nephropathy compared to those who do not work for the hospital. Which of the following most likely explains this difference in interpretation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Observer bias
