Hospital-employed pathologists are more likely to diagnose diabetic nephropathy, indicating observer bias. Observer bias occurs when the investigator’s expectations or affiliations influence interpretation of results. This is not confounding or selection bias, as the samples are the same; only interpretation differs.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A laboratory is comparing two tests for measuring hemoglobin levels. Test A produces results as 10.5, 10.7, 10.9 ,11.1g/dL, while Test B produces results as 9, 11, 13, 15 g/dL. The true hemoglobin value is 13 g/dL. Which of the following is true regarding these tests?
options: Test A has higher validity but lower reliability compared to Test B.
Test A has higher reliability but lower validity compared to Test B.
Test A has both higher reliability and validity compared to Test B.
Test A has lower reliability and lower validity compared to Test B.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Test A has higher reliability but lower validity compared to Test B.

• Test A values: 10.5, 10.7, 10.9, 11.1

• Closely clustered → high reliability

• Test B values: 9, 11, 13, 15

• Widely spread → low reliability

Validity (Accuracy)

• True Hb value = 13 g/dL
• Test A results are consistently around \~11 g/dL → far from true value
• Test B includes 13 g/dL (exact true value) and averages closer to truth

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A large textile factory conducts an occupational health audit to comply with statutory reporting requirements under national labor and health regulations. As part of the audit, the factory physician compiles a list of diseases that must be formally notified to the authorities. Which of the following occupational diseases is not required to be notified?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Bagassosis

Bagassosis is an occupational hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by inhalation of dust from mouldy sugarcane residue (bagasse). It commonly affects workers in sugar mills and paper industries, leading to fever, cough, dyspnea, and diffuse lung infiltrates on exposure. It is not a reportable occupational disease under Factory Act.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A medical officer is preparing an immunization session. During vaccine transportation, the holes provided on the surface of conditioned ice packs are used to keep certain reconstituted vaccines upright. Which of the following vaccines should not be placed in these holes?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Killed Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine

The holes on conditioned ice packs are used to keep reconstituted BCG, Measles, and MR vaccines in an upright position during immunization sessions. JE vaccine is not kept in these holes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A medical researcher is analyzing a large data set to understand the distribution of systolic blood pressure readings among a group of patients with hypertension. The researcher aims to apply the appropriate statistical tests to determine if the data follow a normal distribution, which is a crucial assumption for many parametric statistical tests. Given the importance of selecting the right method to assess normality, which combination of graphical and statistical tools should the researcher employ to comprehensively evaluate the normality of the blood pressure readings? 1. Histogram 2. Box and whisker plot 3. Shapiro wilk test 4. Q-Q plot
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2, 3, 4

Assessment of normal distribution is important before applying parametric statistical tests (eg, t-test, ANOVA, Pearson correlation). A comprehensive evaluation of normality includes both graphical methods and statistical tests.

Graphical methods:

• Histogram → assesses overall distribution shape and symmetry
• Box-and-whisker plot → identifies skewness and outliers
• Q-Q (quantile–quantile) plot → compares observed data distribution with an expected normal distribution; points lying near the straight line suggest normality

Statistical test:

• Shapiro-Wilk test → commonly used formal test for normality, especially in small-to-moderate sample sizes

Therefore, using all four tools together provides the most complete assessment of normality.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A meta-analysis is performed to evaluate the effect of daily fish oil supplementation on systolic blood pressure (SBP). The pooled results from multiple randomized controlled trials are shown below. All trials measured the change in SBP after 8 weeks of intervention. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
options: Fish oil supplementation was associated with a statistically significant reduction in SBP overall
Fish oil supplementation should be recommended as first-line therapy for hypertension
Studies 2 and 5 demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in SBP
Fish oil supplementation had no statistically significant effect on SBP overall
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Fish oil supplementation was associated with a statistically significant reduction in SBP overall

| Study | Mean difference in SBP (fish oil – control, mm Hg) | 95% CI

| ----- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------

| 1 | –6.0 | –9.0 to –3.0

| 2 | –2.1 | –5.0 to 1.0

| 3 | –4.5 | –7.0 to –2.0

| 4 | –3.2 | –5.0 to –1.5

| 5 | –0.8 | –3.0 to 1.5

| Total | –2.7 | –3.5 to –1.4

A. Fish oil supplementation was associated with a statistically significant reduction in SBP overall

B. Fish oil supplementation should be recommended as first-line therapy for hypertension

C. Studies 2 and 5 demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in SBP

D. Fish oil supplementation had no statistically significant effect on SBP overall

Correct Answer: A. Fish oil supplementation was associated with a statistically significant reduction in SBP overall

In a meta-analysis, the overall (pooled) effect is interpreted from the Total row:

• Total mean difference = –2.7 mm Hg
• 95% CI = –3.5 to –1.4

Since the 95% CI does not cross 0, the pooled reduction is statistically significant → fish oil is associated with lower SBP overall.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A multicentric trial compares mean systolic blood pressure among five treatment groups. Data are normally distributed with equal variances. Which test is appropriate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. One-way ANOVA

Use One-way ANOVA when:

• Comparing means.
• More than two independent groups.
• Data are normally distributed.
• Variances are approximately equal.

Other options:

• A. Paired t-test: Two related samples (before vs after).
• C. Chi-square: Categorical variables.
• D. Kruskal-Wallis: Non-parametric alternative to ANOVA when data are not normally distributed.

NEET PG Pearl:

• 2 groups → Student's t-test
• 2 groups → ANOVA
• Non-normal >2 groups → Kruskal-Wallis

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new automated blood pressure device is being evaluated against a standard mercury sphygmomanometer. Researchers record paired measurements from multiple patients and plot the difference between the two readings against their mean to analyze how closely the two devices agree with each other. Which statistical method is being used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Bland–Altman analysis

Bland–Altman analysis:

• Uses paired measurements
• Plots difference between the two methods (Y-axis) against their mean (X-axis)
• Assesses:

o    Bias (mean difference)

o    Limits of agreement (mean ± 1.96 SD)
• Gold standard for evaluating interchangeability of devices

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new diagnostic test for pulmonary tuberculosis has a sensitivity of 98% but a specificity of only 60%. The test is introduced in a community where the prevalence of tuberculosis is very low. Which of the following is the most likely consequence?
options: Positive predictive value will increase significantly
Negative predictive value will remain high, while many positive results will be false positives
Both positive and negative predictive values will increase
False-negative results will outnumber false-positive results
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Negative predictive value will remain high, while many positive results will be false positives

Concept: In low-prevalence settings, even highly sensitive tests have a low PPV, whereas NPV remains high.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new estrogen receptor agonist is being evaluated for the treatment of postmenopausal symptoms. A prospective study shows that the drug increases the risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in treated women who smoke compared to untreated women who smoke, with a relative risk (RR) of 1.70 and p-value of 0.01. In nonsmokers, no increased risk of DVT is evident with use of the drug (RR = 0.96; p-value = 0.68). Which of the following describes this phenomenon?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Effect modification

The estrogen agonist increases DVT risk in smokers but not in non-smokers. This indicates that smoking modifies the effect of the drug on DVT risk. This phenomenon is called effect modification (interaction) and should be reported, not adjusted away like confounding.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new glucometer gives readings of 95, 96, and 95 mg/dL when testing the same blood sample. The laboratory reference value for that sample is 130 mg/dL. Which best describes the device?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Low accuracy; high precision

The readings are very consistent (high precision) but far from the true value (low accuracy).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new monoclonal antibody targeting tumor necrosis factor–alpha (TNF-α) has completed phase 1 safety testing. Researchers now want to determine whether the drug is effective in reducing disease activity in patients with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. They enroll 200 patients with rheumatoid arthritis and randomize them to receive either the new antibody or placebo for 6 months. The study evaluates clinical improvement using a standardized joint inflammation score. Adverse effects are also monitored. Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of this study?
options: To assess drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers
To determine the efficacy of the drug in patients with the disease of interest
To compare the new drug to existing standard therapy in a large patient population
To detect rare adverse effects after FDA approval
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. To determine the efficacy of the drug in patients with the disease of interest

This study describes a Phase II clinical trial, whose primary purpose is to evaluate the efficacy of a drug in patients with the target disease while continuing to assess short-term safety.

Characteristics of clinical trial phases:

• Phase I:

• Small number of healthy volunteers (or patients in toxic drugs)
• Assesses safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and maximum tolerated dose

• Phase II:

• Patients with the disease of interest
• Evaluates efficacy and side effects

• Phase III:

• Large patient populations
• Compares new treatment with standard therapy/placebo
• Basis for FDA approval

• Phase IV:

• Post-marketing surveillance
• Detects rare or long-term adverse effects

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new portable cholesterol-measuring device is being developed for use in medically underserved communities. During clinical trials of an early prototype, a patient's cholesterol level is found to be 200 mg/dl, 201 mg/dl, and 200 mg/dL on 3 separate measurements of the same blood sample. Using the gold standard measurement method, the same sample is found to have a cholesterol level of 260 mg/dl. Which of the following descriptions best characterizes the new cholesterol-measuring device?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Low accuracy; high precision

The device shows very similar repeated measurements (200, 201, 200 mg/dL), indicating high precision. However, the true cholesterol value is 260 mg/dL, meaning the readings are far from the true value, indicating low accuracy. Precision reflects reproducibility, while accuracy reflects closeness to the true value. Hence, the device has low accuracy but high precision.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new rapid bedside test is developed to detect gestational diabetes. To evaluate how accurate this new test is, researchers compare its results directly with the gold standard OGTT (Oral Glucose Tolerance Test). The extent to which the new test’s results agree with the gold standard is a measure of:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Criterion validity

Criterion validity measures how well a new test correlates with an established gold standard.

Two types:

• Concurrent validity → measured at the same time
• Predictive validity → predicts a future outcome

In this question, the new test is being compared directly with the gold standard → criterion validity.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new rapid test for dengue is being validated. The test has a sensitivity of 90% and a specificity of 85%. Investigators want to assess the overall discriminative ability of the test by using the Youden Index. Which of the following represents the correct calculation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. (0.90 + 0.85) − 1

Youden Index = Sensitivity + Specificity − 1

Here: 0.90 + 0.85 − 1 = 0.75

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new rapid test for the diagnosis of a viral respiratory infection is evaluated in 200 study participants. At a given cutoff, the test shows a true-negative rate of approximately 70% and a true-positive rate of approximately 65%. Which of the following labeled graphs is most likely to represent this diagnostic test?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. B

Diagnostic test performance is often represented using ROC curves. Sensitivity (true-positive rate) and specificity (true-negative rate) together determine how useful a test is. A test with moderate sensitivity and specificity will plot near the diagonal but above it. Identifying the correct ROC curve helps interpret diagnostic accuracy and cutoff selection. This concept is crucial in screening programs and evaluation of new diagnostic tools.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new screening test detects colorectal cancer approximately 8 months earlier than conventional methods. Patients diagnosed by the new test appear to survive longer after diagnosis, but overall mortality remains unchanged. The apparent survival benefit is best explained by:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Lead-time bias

Earlier diagnosis increases the measured survival time without actually delaying death.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A newborn screening committee is considering introducing a universal screening program for carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS I) deficiency, a rare urea cycle disorder. Untreated affected infants can develop severe hyperammonemia within the first few days of life, leading to irreversible neurological damage or death. Since early diagnosis can be lifesaving, the initial screening test should be designed to minimize missed cases. Which of the following characteristics is most important for this screening test?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. High sensitivity

For an initial screening test, especially for a serious but treatable disease, the priority is to identify as many affected individuals as possible. Therefore, the test should have high sensitivity, which minimizes false-negative results.

• High sensitivity → Very few affected newborns are missed.
• Infants who test positive can then undergo a more specific confirmatory test.

Why the other options are incorrect

• A. High cutoff value: Increasing the cutoff generally decreases sensitivity and increases false negatives.
• B. High number of true negatives: This reflects specificity and disease prevalence, not the primary goal of screening.
• C. High positive predictive value: PPV depends heavily on disease prevalence. Since CPS I deficiency is extremely rare, PPV is not the primary design goal for the initial screening test.
• E. High specificity: Specificity is desirable for confirmatory tests to reduce false positives, but in screening, missing affected infants is a greater concern than falsely identifying healthy ones.

Exam Pearl:

• Screening test → High Sensitivity ("SnNout": a highly Sensitive test, when Negative, rules OUT disease).
• Confirmatory test → High Specificity ("SpPin": a highly Specific test, when Positive, rules IN disease).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A newly established hospital aims to maintain the highest standards of care and ensure patient safety by standardizing injection practices among health workers. They seek a reliable method for real-time assessment of these practices. Which of the following would be the most appropriate method to monitor the injection practices of health workers?
options: Direct observation with a structured checklist
In-depth interview with the healthcare provider
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Direct observation with a structured checklist

The most reliable method for real-time assessment of injection practices is direct observation using a structured checklist. This method objectively captures adherence to safety protocols. CCTV surveillance raises ethical issues, while interviews rely on recall and may introduce bias. Direct observation is the gold standard in quality audits.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A nurse is disposing of used hypodermic needles after giving injections in a vaccination clinic. Which of the following is the correct method of disposal?
options: Autoclaving followed by mutilation/shredding and disposal in a sanitary landfill
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Autoclaving followed by mutilation/shredding and disposal in a sanitary landfill

Sharps should never be incinerated. Correct sequence:

• Autoclaving
• Mutilation/Shredding
• Final disposal in a sanitary landfill

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A nurse removes a blood-soaked dressing from a patient known to be HIV-positive in a surgical ward. Which of the following is the most appropriate and recommended method for disposal of this dressing material as per biomedical waste management protocols?
options: Soak the dressing in 1% sodium hypochlorite solution and then send it for incineration
Soak the dressing in 5% sodium hypochlorite solution before discarding it in a yellow bag
Treat the dressing with 10% non-chlorinated disinfectant and dispose of it as general waste
Dispose of the dressing directly into the appropriate biomedical waste bag and send for incineration
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Dispose of the dressing directly into the appropriate biomedical waste bag and send for incineration

• Dispose of the dressing directly into the appropriate biomedical waste bag and send for incineration
• No pre-soaking or chemical disinfection is required before placing it in the yellow bag.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A patient with leprosy comes to the primary health centre with multiple cuts and abrasions on his feet. He reports having reduced sensation in his feet. Which of the following is incorrect regarding govt. incentives for him?
options: The ministry of health and family welfare has sponsored this program
Dressing materials and ulcer kits are provided
Amount of 8000 monthly is provided to all leprosy patients from BPL families
The district unit will supply the microcellular footwear
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Amount of 8000 monthly is provided to all leprosy patients from BPL families

The leprosy welfare program is sponsored by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides dressing materials and ulcer care kits, and microcellular footwear. Welfare allowance (now 12000) is only for those needing reconstructive Surgery.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A patient's systolic blood pressure is recorded 20 times over 2 hours and ranges between 118–122 mmHg. The next reading is 190 mmHg due to an acute event. Which statistical measure is most likely to remain unchanged?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Mode

A single extreme value changes the mean, range, variance, and SD but usually does not change the most frequently occurring value (mode).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A pediatrician counsels parents regarding the inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) administered under the Universal Immunization Programme. How many poliovirus strains are included in the conventional IPV?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Three

Conventional IPV is trivalent, containing inactivated poliovirus types 1, 2, and 3 (Mahoney, MEF-1, and Saukett strains).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A person with a documented anaphylactic allergy to neomycin should not receive which vaccine?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Varicella

• Varicella - Contains neomycin

Contraindicated
• MMR/IPV - Trace neomycin

Observe / precaution

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A pharmaceutical company conducts a cross-over study to compare the efficacy of two antihypertensive medications, Drug X and Drug Y. Participants receive Drug X for 4 weeks, undergo a 2-week washout period, and then receive Drug Y for 4 weeks. Upon analyzing the data, researchers observe that blood pressure measurements during the Drug Y phase are significantly lower than during the Drug X phase. However, they also note a progressive decrease in blood pressure readings over the entire study duration, irrespective of the treatment administered. Which of the following phenomena is most likely responsible for this observation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Period effect

• A period effect refers to changes in the outcome variable that occur due to the passage of time rather than the specific treatments administered.
• In this scenario, the progressive decrease in blood pressure over time, regardless of whether the participant is receiving Drug X or Drug Y, suggests a period effect.
• This could be due to factors such as lifestyle modifications, increased adherence to study protocols, or other time-related influences that affect blood pressure.

Other Options:

Option A. Carryover effect: This occurs when the effects of the first treatment persist into the period when the second treatment is administered. The presence of a washout period is intended to minimize this effect. In this case, the consistent decline over time does not align with a carryover effect.

Option C. Regression to the mean: This statistical phenomenon occurs when extreme measurements tend to move closer to the average upon subsequent testing. It does not adequately explain a continuous downward trend over the study period.

Option D. Sequence effect: This refers to differences in outcomes depending on the order in which treatments are administered. The observed trend is independent of treatment sequence, making this explanation less likely.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A pharmaceutical company is evaluating the effect of a new migraine medication compared with placebo. Forty patients with chronic migraines are enrolled. Each patient is randomly assigned to one of two groups: • Group A: New drug for 6 weeks → 2-week washout → placebo for 6 weeks • Group B: Placebo for 6 weeks → 2-week washout → new drug for 6 weeks At the end of each treatment period, patients report the number of migraine episodes per week. The researchers then compare outcomes between the new drug and placebo within the same patients. Which of the following best describes the main advantage of this study design?
options: Avoids recall bias by blinding participants
Increases external validity by using multiple centers
Minimizes confounding by using each subject as their own control
Prevents selection bias through random sampling of the population
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Minimizes confounding by using each subject as their own control

This study uses a crossover design, in which participants receive both the intervention and placebo sequentially, separated by a washout period. The major advantage of this design is that each participant serves as their own control, which:

• Minimizes interindividual variability
• Reduces confounding from fixed patient characteristics (eg, genetics, pain threshold, lifestyle)
• Increases statistical power with smaller sample sizes

A washout period is important to prevent carryover effects from the first treatment phase.

Key limitations:

• Not suitable for diseases that permanently change over time
• Carryover effects may still occur if washout is inadequate
• Participant dropout can affect validity.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A physician is assessing the body composition of patients using various anthropometric indices. Which of the following indices can he measure without height?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Corpulence index

• The Corpulence index does not require height for its calculation.
• Other indices like Quetelet (BMI), Broca, and Ponderal index all depend on height measurements.
• Therefore, corpulence index is useful when height measurement is difficult or unreliable.

1. Body Mass Index (BMI)= Quetelet index

• BMI = Weight (kg) / [Height (m)]²

2. Ponderal Index

• PI = Height (cm) / (Cube root of Body Weight (kg)

3. Brocca Index

• Ideal Weight = Height (cm) - 100

4. Lorentz’s Formula

5. Corpulence Index

• CI = Actual Weight / Desirable Weight
•

Should not exceed 1.2

•

Skin fold thickness: Mid triceps/ Biceps/ subscapular/ suprailiac

•

Sum <40mm males/50mm females

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A postgraduate student preparing for Community Medicine viva is asked to identify various national health initiatives, portals, campaigns, and WHO projects frequently tested in recent AIIMS examinations. Match the entities in List I with their most appropriate descriptions in List II. List I A. MONICA B. Nikshay C. LaQshya D. EVIN E. Tele-MANAS F. SUMAN List II 1. Electronic cold-chain and vaccine logistics platform 2. WHO project for monitoring cardiovascular disease trends 3. Mental health helpline initiative 4. Labour room quality improvement initiative 5. TB notification and patient tracking portal 6. Assured dignified maternal and newborn care
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. A-2, B-5, C-4, D-1, E-3, F-6

Educational Objective

• MONICA = Monitoring of Trends and Determinants in Cardiovascular Disease (WHO project).
• Nikshay = National TB notification and patient management portal under NTEP.
• LaQshya = Labour room quality improvement initiative aimed at reducing maternal and neonatal morbidity/mortality.
• EVIN = Electronic Vaccine Intelligence Network for vaccine stock and cold-chain monitoring.
• Tele-MANAS = National tele-mental health assistance and networking service.
• SUMAN = Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan initiative ensuring respectful and free maternal-newborn healthcare services.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A pregnant woman has completed her first ANC and just had an institutional delivery. How much has she received under PMMVY so far?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Rs. 3000

Under PMMVY 2.0, the 1st installment of ₹3000 is released on pregnancy registration + 1st ANC. Institutional delivery does not itself trigger a payment; the 2nd installment (₹2000) requires birth registration + completion of the first immunization cycle (14 weeks). So after ANC + delivery (pre-immunization), she has received ₹3000.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A prospective cohort study evaluates the association between high dietary salt intake and hypertension. During follow-up, 25% of participants are lost, and most of those lost belong to the high-salt intake group. Which bias is most likely?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Selection bias

Differential loss to follow-up causes attrition (selection) bias, making the remaining sample unrepresentative.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A prospective study evaluates antioxidant supplement use and stroke risk. Compared with nonusers: • Use for <5 years: RR = 0.95, p = 0.45 • Use for ≥5 years: RR = 0.75, p < 0.01 After adjustment for baseline health differences, longer supplement use is associated with lower stroke risk. Which factor best explains this finding?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Accumulation effect

A stronger association with longer exposure suggests a dose-duration/accumulation effect, where benefit appears after prolonged use.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health campaign increases vaccination rates against HPV 16 and 18. Increased vaccination rates would have which of the following effects on the Papanicolaou test?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Decreased positive predictive value

Why?

HPV vaccination against types 16 and 18 reduces the prevalence of cervical precancer and cancer in the population. When disease prevalence decreases:

• Sensitivity & specificity of the Pap test remain unchanged
• Positive predictive value (PPV) ↓ (fewer true cases among positives)
• Negative predictive value (NPV) ↑
• True negative rate (specificity) unchanged
• Negative likelihood ratio unchanged

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health manager is planning a district immunization campaign. To monitor the progress of multiple activities such as staff training, vaccine logistics, cold chain preparation, and outreach sessions, she uses a chart that displays activities against a time scale, showing planned vs actual progress. This type of project management tool is known as:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Gantt chart

A Gantt chart:

• Plots tasks/activities on Y-axis
• Plots time on X-axis
• Shows planned vs actual progress
• Used for project scheduling & control
• Helps identify delays & bottlenecks

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health officer is outlining the responsibilities of a male health worker in a community health center. Which of the following are included in the job duties of a male health worker? 1. Sputum collection 2. ORS distribution 3. DOTS supervision 4. Growth monitoring 5. Environmental sanitation Use the following key to mark the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2, 3, 5

Duties of a Male Health Worker (MPW-Male)

Included responsibilities:

1. Sputum collection

– Under NTEP (TB control)
2. ORS distribution

– Diarrheal disease control, outreach activities
3. DOTS supervision

– Treatment supervision for TB patients
4.

Environmental sanitation

– Water safety, waste disposal, vector control activities

5.

Male Health Worker → TB, sanitation, chlorination, surveillance, ORS

6. Female Health Worker → MCH, growth monitoring, immunization

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health officer is teaching medical students about the composition of municipal solid waste. Which of the following should not be considered a component of solid waste?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Night soil

Night soil refers to untreated human excreta (feces) and is not a component of municipal solid waste.

• Solid waste includes:

• Garbage
• Rubbish
• Demolition waste
• Sewage treatment residue
• Dead animals

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health researcher is conducting a street-based survey to assess awareness regarding hypertension. To ensure representation, the researcher plans to include a fixed number of participants from each age group and socioeconomic category, based on the known distribution in the city. Interviewers then approach passers-by and recruit participants until the required numbers in each subgroup are reached. No random selection is performed. Which sampling method is being used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Quota sampling

The key features described are:

• Fixed numbers from predefined subgroups (age, socioeconomic status)
• Based on known population distribution
• No random selection within subgroups
• Participants recruited conveniently (street-based) until quotas are filled

This is characteristic of Quota sampling.

Why Quota sampling fits:

• Non-probability sampling method
• Population is divided into subgroups (quotas)
• Interviewers select subjects non-randomly until each quota is met

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health researcher uses hospital records to estimate the prevalence of diabetes in a district. However, many patient files have incorrect diagnoses, incomplete entries, and inconsistent coding. Despite applying advanced statistical software, the final results are inaccurate and misleading. This error is best explained by which of the following concepts?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Garbage in, garbage out effect

Garbage in, garbage out (GIGO) effect means that the quality of output depends on the quality of input. In epidemiology and biostatistics, incorrect, biased, or incomplete data lead to misleading results and conclusions, regardless of how sophisticated the analysis or statistical methods used.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health team evaluates the impact of a school-based nutritional program on BMI reduction. The intervention was non-randomized and implemented at the community level. While preparing the manuscript, the investigators want to use an established guideline for transparent reporting of such studies. Which reporting guideline is most appropriate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. TREND

• CONSORT: Randomized controlled trials
• TREND: Non-randomized public health / behavioral interventions
• STROBE: Observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional)
• PRISMA: Systematic reviews & meta-analyses

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health team is evaluating the effectiveness of the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (NIDDCP) in a mountainous district with historically high endemic goitre prevalence. During assessment, investigators collect household salt samples, neonatal screening data, and urinary iodine measurements from school-going children. The team wishes to identify: 1. The best epidemiological indicator of recent iodine intake in the community 2. The most appropriate indicator for assessing population-level iodine sufficiency in neonates 3. The minimum recommended iodine concentration in household salt at the point of consumption Which of the following combinations is correct?
options: Serum T4 | Urinary iodine excretion | 30 ppm
Urinary iodine excretion | Neonatal TSH | 15 ppm
Serum TSH | Cord blood T4 | 5 ppm
Thyroid size by ultrasound | Neonatal TSH | 30 ppm
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Urinary iodine excretion | Neonatal TSH | 15 ppm

• Urinary iodine excretion (UIE) is the best epidemiological indicator and the best marker of recent iodine intake, as >90% of ingested iodine is excreted in urine.
• Neonatal TSH is considered the best indicator for assessing population iodine sufficiency, especially in neonatal screening programs.
• Under public health recommendations, iodine content of household salt should be at least 15 ppm at the consumer level.
• Daily iodine requirement:

• Adults: 150 µg/day
• Pregnancy/lactation: 250 µg/day.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A randomized controlled trial is conducted to compare a new oral anticoagulant with warfarin for the prevention of stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation. Patients are randomized into two groups: new anticoagulant (n = 1000) or warfarin (n = 1000). During the study, 150 patients in the new anticoagulant group discontinue therapy due to side effects and switch to warfarin. Additionally, 100 patients in the warfarin group discontinue therapy and switch to the new anticoagulant. The investigators choose to analyze outcomes according to the initial randomization group assignment, regardless of whether patients actually adhered to the assigned treatment. Which of the following best describes this approach?
options: Maintains randomization by including all participants in their original groups
Includes only participants who strictly followed the study protocol
Reassigns participants to groups based on the treatment actually received
Excludes participants who withdrew or crossed over
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Maintains randomization by including all participants in their original groups

• Intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis is the preferred method of analyzing randomized controlled trials because it preserves the benefits of randomization and minimizes bias.
• In ITT, patients are analyzed in the groups to which they were originally randomized, regardless of treatment adherence, withdrawal, or crossover.
• ITT provides a real-world estimate of treatment effectiveness, reflecting clinical practice where noncompliance is common.
• In contrast:

o    Per-protocol analysis includes only those who fully adhered to the study → may overestimate efficacy.

As-treated analysis reclassifies participants based on actual treatment received → breaks randomization, increases bias.

o    As-treated analysis reclassifies participants based on actual treatment received → breaks randomization, increases bias.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A rapid test for hepatitis has sensitivity 90% and specificity 95%. In a screening camp where true prevalence is 1%, the most accurate statement is:
options: Negative predictive value will be high
Positive predictive value will be high
False negatives will exceed false positives
Likelihood ratio positive will be less than 1
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Negative predictive value will be high

In a population with low disease prevalence (1%), even tests with good sensitivity and specificity produce a high negative predictive value (NPV) and a low positive predictive value (PPV). This occurs because most individuals tested are disease-free, so negative results are usually true negatives. Therefore, NPV will be high, making the test useful for ruling out disease in screening settings.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A rapidly expanding urban municipality generates a large amount of solid waste daily. The area has adequate land availability, suitable soil conditions, and proper infrastructure for waste disposal. The local health authority wants to adopt the most appropriate and sanitary method of solid waste disposal under these conditions. Which of the following methods should be preferred?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Controlled tipping

Controlled tipping / sanitary landfill is the method of choice when:

• Adequate land is available
• Proper covering and compaction can be ensured

Why other options are incorrect?

• A. Dumping ❌: Open, unscientific, causes environmental pollution
• C. Incineration ❌: Costly; preferred where land is scarce and waste is combustible
• D. Manure-over-pit method ❌: Used for small rural communities, not large municipalities

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A research group conducted a placebo-controlled clinical trial to assess whether a new drug to treat acute migraine with or without aura in adults is more effective than standard therapy. During the data analysis phase, the researchers decide to set alpha at 0.01 rather than 0.05. Which of the following is the most likely result of this change?
options: Any significant findings will be reported with greater confidence
There will be a higher probability of a type I error
There will be a higher probability of finding statistically significant results
The study will have more statistical power
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Any significant findings will be reported with greater confidence

Reducing alpha makes the test more stringent, lowering Type I error. As a result, any statistically significant findings are reported with greater confidence, but power may decrease. Hence, option A is correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A research laboratory develops a new serologic test for detecting prostate cancer. The new assay is compared to biopsy. It is found that the test result is negative in 95% of patients who do not have the disease. If the new assay is used on 8 blood samples taken from patients without prostate cancer, what is the probability of all 8 test results coming back negative?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 0.95 (raised to power 8)

The test correctly identifies negatives 95% of the time (specificity = 0.95). The probability that all 8 independent samples return negative is calculated as 0.95⁸. This follows basic probability rules where repeated independent events are multiplied. Hence, option D is correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher conducts a study to determine the value of measuring kidney volume with computed tomography (CT) to help diagnose chronic kidney disease and quantify kidney damage. In total, 251 patients are enrolled in the study. Correlation analyses are then conducted to evaluate the relationships between kidney volume as measured on CT scans and both glomerular filtration rate and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c). Initial study results show that lower values of HbA1c tended to relate to higher values of kidney volume, and that the relationship was strong and statistically significant. Based on this information, which of the following statements would best describe the associated correlation coefficient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. -0.8

The study shows a strong inverse relationship: lower HbA1c values are associated with higher kidney volume. A strong negative correlation is best represented by a value close to −1, hence −0.8 is the most appropriate correlation coefficient. Positive values or weaker negatives do not fit the description.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher evaluates the effect of a new iron supplementation program on hemoglobin levels in 12 anemic women. Hemoglobin levels are measured before and after 8 weeks of therapy. The data are not normally distributed. Which of the following statistical tests is most appropriate to analyze the change in hemoglobin levels?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Wilcoxon signed-rank test

• Same subjects measured twice → paired data (before vs after)
• Small sample size (n = 12)
• Data not normally distributed

👉 The appropriate non-parametric test for paired samples is the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher is analysing the results of a study comparing two antihypertensive drugs in an Indian population. She comes across the term "p-value" in her statistical analyses. Which of the following best describes the interpretation of a p-value with regard to the probability related to the null hypothesis?
options: Not rejecting a null hypothesis when it is true
Rejecting a null hypothesis when it is true
Not rejecting a null hypothesis when it is false
Rejecting a null hypothesis when it is false
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Rejecting a null hypothesis when it is true

p-value relates to the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis, which corresponds to a Type I error (α error). Thus, the correct interpretation is “rejecting a null hypothesis when it is true.” Other options describe β error or incorrect interpretations of statistical testing.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher is comparing three different groups with non-normally distributed data and small sample sizes. Which of the following tests is best suited for analyzing this non-parametric data?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Friedman test

When comparing three or more groups with non-normally distributed data and small sample sizes, the appropriate non-parametric test is the Friedman test. It is the non-parametric equivalent of repeated-measures ANOVA.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher is interested in studying whether there is an association between neural tube defects and use of acetaminophen during the first 3 months of pregnancy. He randomly chooses a group of women who have just delivered babies with neural tube defects, and a second group of women who delivered apparently healthy babies. These 2 groups were then asked about their use of acetaminophen during the first 3 months of pregnancy. Which of the following measures of association are the investigators most likely to report?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Odds ratio

In a case–control design, participants are selected based on disease status, and past exposure is assessed. Because incidence cannot be directly calculated, the appropriate measure of association is the odds ratio, which approximates relative risk when the disease is rare.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher measures serum calcium levels in 8 patients. One value appears to be an extreme outlier. Which statistical test is most appropriate to determine whether this value should be excluded?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Dixon's Q test

• Dixon's Q test is specifically designed for very small sample sizes.
• Best for n < 10 (classically 3–10; some references extend it to 25–30).
• Used to detect one suspected outlier.

Exam Pearl: If the sample size is 8, Dixon's Q test is preferred.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher studies the incidence of measles in a population of 100 children, where 10 children have a previous history of measles, and 20 have been affected by the disease for the first time. What is the incidence?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 22.22%

• Population at risk excludes those already immune (10 prior cases).
• At-risk population = 100 − 10 = 90.
• New cases = 20.
• Incidence = 20/90 × 100 = 22.22%

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher studying prevalence of psoriasis (estimated 2%) wants absolute allowable error of 1%. Sample size required is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 784

2-step reasoning:

•

Formula: n = 4pq/l². p = 2 = 2%, q = 100−2 = 98, l = 1 (absolute error %).

• n = 4 × 2 × 98/1² = 4 × 196/1 = 784.

•

Trap:

• Using p = 0.02 and l = 0.01 (decimals) gives same answer: 4×0.02×0.98/0.01² = 0.0784/0.0001 = 784.
• Using l = 2 (doubled error) gives 196 — wrong.
• Using p + q = 100 confirms: 4 × 2 × 98 = 784.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher wants to predict systolic blood pressure from body mass index (BMI) using statistical analysis. Which statistical measure is most appropriate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Coefficient of regression

Regression is used when:

• One variable is used to predict another variable.

Example:

• BMI → Predict BP
• Age → Predict lung function

Regression equation:

Y = a + bX

where, b is the regression coefficient.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A school study measured and compared the heights of students from grade 5 to 10. Which statistical test is most appropriate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. ANOVA

ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) is used to compare the means of a continuous variable among three or more independent groups.

In this study:

• Variable measured = height (continuous variable)
• Groups compared = students from grades 5 to 10 (more than 2 groups)

Therefore, the appropriate test is ANOVA

Key distinctions:

• Unpaired t-test → compares means between 2 independent groups
• Paired t-test → compares means before and after in the same group
• Chi-square test → compares categorical variables/proportions

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A staff nurse is disposing of used IV tubing, urinary catheter, gloves, and syringe after treating a patient with hepatitis B. All items are visibly contaminated with blood. These items should be discarded in which color-coded bag?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Red bag

The Red bag is used for contaminated recyclable plastic waste.

Examples include:

• IV tubing and infusion sets
• Urinary catheters
• Ryle's tubes
• Oxygen masks
• Gloves
• Suction tubing
• Syringes without needles

These items are disinfected (e.g., autoclaving/microwaving/hydroclaving) and then sent for recycling.

Why other options are incorrect

• A. Yellow bag: Human anatomical waste, soiled waste, microbiology waste, expired medicines, and other waste destined for incineration.
• C. White (translucent) puncture-proof container: Sharps such as needles, scalpels, and blades.
• D. Blue container: Glass waste such as broken vials, ampoules, and metallic implants.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A standard test based on a serum marker is used to diagnose disease X. The distribution of the marker for this standard test in healthy and diseased patients is shown by the red curves in the graph below. A competitive company developed a new test based on the same marker. The distribution of the marker for the new test in healthy and diseased patients is shown by the black curves in the graph below. Compared to the old test, the new test has:
options: Higher sensitivity and the same specificity
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Higher sensitivity and higher specificity

Black curves (new test) show narrower distributions with less overlap between healthy and diseased populations compared to red curves (old test). Reduced overlap at the same cutoff = fewer false positives (↑specificity) and fewer false negatives (↑sensitivity) simultaneously, better discriminatory test.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a new ECG algorithm in diagnosing myocardial infarction (MI). The table below summarizes the results. Based on the data, which of the following statements is true regarding the diagnostic performance of the ECG algorithm?
options: Sensitivity is the same as specificity
Positive Predictive Value (PPV) is more than Negative Predictive Value (NPV)
PPV is the same as NPV
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. PPV is the same as NPV

From the table:

• TP = 300
• FP = 100
• FN = 25
• TN = 75

Calculations:

• Sensitivity = TP / (TP + FN) = 300 / 325 ≈ 92%
• Specificity = TN / (TN + FP) = 75 / 175 ≈ 43%
• PPV = TP / (TP + FP) = 300 / 400 = 75%
• NPV = TN / (TN + FN) = 75 / 100 = 75%

Thus, PPV equals NPV.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study assessed the association between a new vaccine and traveler's diarrhea (TD). Researchers selected a random sample of people who intended to travel to regions where they were at increased risk for TD and who had received the new vaccine and another independent random sample of people who intended to travel to the same regions and who had not received the new vaccine. These 2 samples of travelers were assessed for the occurrence of TD during the trip and for 7 days after returning home. What is the study design?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Prospective cohort

Participants were selected based on exposure status (vaccinated vs non-vaccinated) and then followed forward in time to assess development of traveler’s diarrhea. This design is a prospective cohort study, as outcomes are assessed after exposure without randomization.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study assessing the efficacy of spironolactone in patients with heart failure is performed. Five hundred patients are randomized to receive either spironolactone or placebo for 2 years. Neither the patient nor the physician knows who receives the drug or placebo. The study setup described above is most effective in preventing:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Observer bias

The study described is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial:

• Randomization → balances known and unknown confounders
• Blinding of patient and physician (double blind) → prevents differential assessment of outcomes

Primary bias prevented by blinding:

• Observer bias ✔️

o    Occurs when investigators’ expectations influence outcome assessment.

o    Double blinding ensures outcomes are assessed objectively, independent of treatment knowledge.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study calculated the correlation coefficient between smoking and lung cancer incidence as 1.4. What does this result indicate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Mistake in calculation

A correlation coefficient must lie between –1 and +1. A reported value of 1.4 is mathematically impossible and indicates a calculation or reporting error. Therefore, the correct interpretation is that there is a mistake in the calculation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study finds that a poor diet is associated with hypertension. After stratifying by socioeconomic status, the association disappears in every stratum. Which best explains this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Confounding by socioeconomic status

The key clue is that the crude association between poor diet and hypertension disappears after stratification by socioeconomic status (SES), and it disappears in every stratum. This pattern is classic for confounding.

Confounding occurs when a third variable is:

• Associated with the exposure (poor diet is more common in certain SES groups).
• Independently associated with the outcome (hypertension risk differs by SES through access to healthcare, stress, obesity patterns, salt intake, physical activity, etc).
• Not on the causal pathway between exposure and outcome.

When SES is a confounder, the crude estimate is distorted. After stratification, if the exposure–outcome association becomes null in all strata, it implies that the original association was largely due to differences in SES distribution between exposed and unexposed groups rather than a true causal effect of diet.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study is conducted to describe the age-sex distribution of a certain country. According to national data, the population pyramid of the country has the shape shown below. Which of the following is true?
options: The country seems to have high birth rates; therefore, the population must be growing
The country seems to have a high death rate; therefore, the population must be shrinking
The country seems to have a low birth rate; therefore, the population must be old
The country seems to have a short life expectancy; therefore, the population must be young
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. The country seems to have a low birth rate; therefore, the population must be old

Population pyramids reflect age-sex distribution and provide insights into fertility, mortality, and population growth trends. A broad base indicates high birth rates, while a narrow base suggests declining fertility. Such demographic analysis helps policymakers plan health, education, and social services according to population needs.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study is conducted to estimate the prevalence of hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) in a surgical intensive care unit (ICU). The figure below shows the onset and recovery of HAP cases among ICU patients during the month of May. Each horizontal bar represents the time course of HAP in an individual patient. Which of the following is the number of prevalent cases on May 31?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 4

Point prevalence refers to the total number of existing cases of a disease present in a population at a specific point in time.

In timeline/bar diagrams:

• Each horizontal bar represents the duration of disease in one patient.
• To calculate prevalence on a given date, count all bars that intersect that date.

For May 31, The number of bars crossing the May 31 line = 4 prevalent cases

Key concepts:

• Prevalence = Existing cases
• Incidence = New cases
• Prevalence depends on both:

• incidence of disease
• duration of illness

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study is conducted to estimate the prevalence of hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) in a surgical intensive care unit (ICU). The figure below shows the onset and recovery of HAP cases among ICU patients during the month of May. Each horizontal bar represents the time course of HAP in an individual patient. Which of the following is the number of prevalent cases on May 31?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 4

• Prevalence = number of people with a disease at a specific point in time
• Different from incidence, which counts new cases within a time frame.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study is conducted to investigate the relationship between smoking and lung cancer. The findings suggest that the association between smoking and lung cancer is stronger in individuals who exercise less and weaker in individuals who exercise more. In this case, exercise is considered:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Effect modifier

• The strength of association between smoking (exposure) and lung cancer (outcome) changes across levels of exercise.
• This indicates interaction, not distortion.

Therefore, exercise modifies the effect of smoking on lung cancer risk.

• Association is stronger in low-exercise individuals
• Association is weaker in high-exercise individuals
• The effect is real and biologically meaningful, not an error

A) Bias ❌

→ Systematic error in study design or conduct

C) Confounding factor ❌

→ Distorts the true association; removed by stratification/adjustment

D) Collinear factor ❌

→ Statistical issue in regression (highly correlated predictors)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study on 2000 children assessed the link between screen time and Autism spectrum. 1600 had >2hours/day exposure. The correlation coefficient was r = 0.9 (p = 0.03). What does this imply?
options: Study is invalid due to low p-value
No correlation between screen time and ADHD
Data is insufficient to conclude correlation
Valid study with strong positive correlation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Valid study with strong positive correlation

The correlation coefficient (r) measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables.

Interpretation in this study:

• r = +0.9 → very strong positive correlation

• As screen time increases, autism spectrum–related findings also increase

• p = 0.03 → statistically significant association

• Since p < 0.05, the observed correlation is unlikely due to chance

Therefore, The study demonstrates a strong, statistically significant positive correlation.

• r ranges from −1 to +1

• +1 → perfect positive correlation
• 0 → no correlation
• −1 → perfect negative correlation

Strength of correlation:

• 0–0.3 → weak
• 0.3–0.7 → moderate
• 0.7 → strong

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was conducted to assess the association between air pollution and asthma. The p-value obtained was 0.03. Which of the following is the most appropriate inference?
options: There is a 3% probability that the observed association is due to random chance, assuming the null hypothesis is true
There is a 97% probability that pollution causes asthma
The null hypothesis is accepted because p-value is greater than 0.01
There is a 95% probability that the alternative hypothesis is false
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. There is a 3% probability that the observed association is due to random chance, assuming the null hypothesis is true

p-value of 0.03 means that if the null hypothesis were true, there is a 3% probability of observing the given association (or a more extreme one) purely due to chance. It does not mean that there is a 97% chance the exposure causes the disease, nor does it give the probability that the alternative hypothesis is true or false. Since p < 0.05, the association is statistically significant at the 5% level.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was done to investigate whether three new antibiotics used for urinary tract infections cured the disease or not. Which of the following statistical tests can be used to test the significance of this study?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Chi-square test

The outcome in this study is whether urinary tract infection was “cured” or “not cured,” which is a categorical variable.

Since the study compares categorical outcomes among multiple antibiotic groups, the appropriate statistical test is Chi-square test. Chi-square test evaluates association/difference between categorical variables.

Why other options are incorrect:

• Student’s t-test → compares means between 2 groups for continuous data

• Paired t-test → compares paired continuous observations

• ANOVA → compares means among ≥3 groups for continuous variables

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A team of epidemiologists is planning to conduct a survey on the prevalence of malnutrition in a village. What is the correct sequence of steps involved in the planning of this activity? 1. Establishment of objectives and goals 2. Fixing priorities 3. Analysis of the health situation 4. Assessment of resources
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 3, 1, 4, 2

The correct sequence in health planning starts with analysis of the health situation, followed by establishing objectives, then assessment of available resources, and finally fixing priorities. This logical order ensures that goals are evidence-based, feasible, and aligned with available manpower and finances. Hence, the correct order is 3 → 1 → 4 → 2.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A team of researchers is conducting investigations to evaluate the impact of interventions targeting a specific disease. Study A utilized an intervention denoted as "X", and Study B utilized an intervention denoted as "Y". Both studies incorporate control groups. The calculated p-values for studies A and B, with 95% confidence intervals, were found to be 0.02 and 0.001, respectively. Based on this information, which of the following conclusions is most appropriate? 1. Study B is more precise than study A and intervention Y is more significant compared to Intervention X. 2. Study A is more precise than study B and intervention X is more significant compared to Intervention Y. 3. Both X and Y show a significant variation, but Study B is more significant than Study A. 4. Both study A and B show a significant variation and both interventions have similar statistical significance.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. If 1 and 3 are correct

Both studies have statistically significant p-values (<0.05). Study B (p = 0.001) is more statistically significant than Study A (p = 0.02). However, p-value alone does not determine precision without confidence interval width. Thus, conclusions 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A tertiary care hospital is commissioning a biomedical waste incinerator. Before starting operations, the infection control committee reviews the list of wastes that should not be disposed of by incineration. Which of the following wastes is most appropriate to exclude from incineration?
options: Human anatomical waste from amputated limbs
Blood-soaked gauze and dressings contaminated with body fluids
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Mercury-containing broken thermometer

Mercury is a heavy metal that vaporizes on incineration, releasing highly toxic fumes into the environment. Therefore, mercury-containing waste must never be incinerated.

Items suitable for incineration:

• Human anatomical waste
• Soiled waste
• Microbiology/biotechnology waste (after appropriate pre-treatment, as applicable)

Items not suitable for incineration:

• Sharps
• Mercury- and cadmium-containing waste
• PVC plastics
• Pressurized gas containers
• Reactive chemical waste
• Photographic/radiographic waste

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A tertiary care hospital plans a prospective cohort study to evaluate the association between long-term exposure to biomass fuel smoke and the development of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) among adult women. Before enrolling participants and starting follow-up, which of the following is the most essential methodological step to ensure the validity of the study?
options: Include all patients irrespective of the treatment they are currently receiving
Include all patients on whom pulmonary function tests will be performed
Exclude all patients already diagnosed with COPD at the time of enrolment
Exclude all patients who have a positive spirometry test during follow-up
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Exclude all patients already diagnosed with COPD at the time of enrolment

In a prospective cohort study, participants must be free of the outcome at baseline. Since the objective is to study the incidence of COPD following exposure to biomass fuel smoke, including women who already have COPD would distort the temporal relationship and invalidate risk estimation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A town recently experienced an outbreak of typhoid fever. The incubation period for typhoid is approximately 14 days. After control measures are implemented, no new cases are reported. According to standard epidemiological principles, after what minimum period without new cases can the area be declared free from the epidemic?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 28 days

An epidemic is considered over when no new cases appear for at least twice the incubation period of the disease.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A tribal population gradually adopts the language, clothing, dietary habits, and customs of a neighboring urban community through increasing interaction over several decades. This process is best described as:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Acculturation

Acculturation is the diffusion or exchange of culture between two culturally different groups following prolonged contact. It is also known as culture contact.

Option-by-option analysis

| Option | Definition | Why here

| ------ | ---------- | --------

| A. Enculturation | Learning one's own native culture (from childhood, within one's own group) | No new/foreign culture involved — opposite of the stem

| B. Acculturation | Cultural change from continuous contact between two cultures; traits adopted while distinct identity is retained | Exactly the scenario — gradual trait adoption through interaction

| C. Assimilation | Complete absorption — the group loses its own identity and merges, becoming indistinguishable from the dominant group | Stem never says the tribe lost its identity or fully merged

| D. Socialization | Lifelong learning of the norms/values/roles needed to function in society (any society) | Too general; not about inter-cultural contact

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A typhoid patient recovers clinically but continues to excrete Salmonella typhi in stool for 4 months without symptoms. He is simultaneously classified under multiple carrier types. Which combination is correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Chronic carrier + Convalescent carrier

• 4 months = ≥3 months → chronic carrier. Post-illness excretion = convalescent carrier (recovery phase, still shedding). Both apply simultaneously.
• Healthy carrier = arises from subclinical case or non-virulent strain — this patient had clinical disease, so not healthy carrier.
• Incubatory = during incubation, pre-symptom — not applicable post-recovery.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A village in West Bengal reports an outbreak of bilateral pitting leg edema, ascites, and glaucoma following consumption of mustard oil purchased from a local vendor. The toxin responsible acts by:
options: Inhibiting alkaline phosphatase → oxidative damage to RBCs
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Inhibiting alkaline phosphatase → oxidative damage to RBCs

• This is Epidemic Dropsy — caused by mustard oil contaminated with Argemone mexicana oil.
• Active toxin: Sanguinarine.
• Mechanism: Inhibits oxidative enzymes → capillary damage → non-inflammatory edema.
• Also causes glaucoma, high-output cardiac failure, and skin erythema.
• Distinguish from aflatoxicosis (groundnut storage workers, Aspergillus flavus, hepatocellular carcinoma risk).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A village with 50 households lacks an underground sewerage system. The medical officer recommends a septic tank for sewage disposal. However, another nearby town with a population of 1 lakh is advised against using septic tanks. What is the most appropriate reason?
options: Septic tanks require electricity to function
Septic tanks are suitable only for industrial waste
Septic tanks are designed for household sewage and are not recommended for large communities
Septic tanks cannot digest organic matter
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Septic tanks are designed for household sewage and are not recommended for large communities

• A septic tank is a water-tight underground tank used for household sewage treatment where there is no underground sewerage system.
• It is not suitable for large communities because of the large volume of sewage generated.

NEET PG Pearl: Septic tank = Individual house/small community, not cities.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A woman with severe vaginal bleeding after 36 weeks of pregnancy remains at home for 5 hours while the family debates whether to take her to a health facility. Which “D” contributes to maternal risk here?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. First D

“3-D model” for maternal mortality

• Delay in Decision → Delay in Reaching → Delay in Receiving

The Three Delays Model explains preventable causes of maternal deaths:

1. First D – Delay in decision to seek care

Due to lack of awareness, cultural beliefs, family indecision, or underestimating severity.

In this case: The woman stayed at home for 5 hours while the family debated → classic First Delay ✅
2. Second D – Delay in reaching a health facility

Transport problems, distance, cost, poor roads.
3. Third D – Delay in receiving adequate care at facility

Shortage of staff, blood, drugs, equipment, or poor quality care.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to a study, pure vegetarians had a lower incidence of colon cancer than non-vegetarians, and this led researchers to the conclusion that beta-carotene is protective against cancer. This may not be the case since vegetarian subjects may be eating a high-fiber diet that lowers their risk of developing cancer. This is an illustration of:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Confounding factor

Fiber intake is a confounder — associated with both exposure (vegetarian diet) and outcome (colon cancer risk), distorting the apparent causal link between beta-carotene and cancer protection. True effect may be due to fiber, not beta-carotene.

Confounding criteria: Confounder must be

1. Associated with exposure
2. Independent risk factor for outcome
3. Hot an intermediate step in the causal pathway.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to McKeown’s theory, the major reason for the decline in tuberculosis prevalence is due to:
options: Improvement in social and environmental factors
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Improvement in social and environmental factors

McKeown’s theory states that the major decline in mortality from infectious diseases (including tuberculosis) occurred before the advent of effective medical therapy. The primary driver was improvement in social and environmental conditions, such as:

• Better nutrition
• Improved housing
• Reduced overcrowding
• Improved sanitation and living standards

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to NUHM, arrange the following in the correct order as per population covered from highest level to lowest. 1. Urban Primary Health Centre 2. Urban Community Health Centre 3. Auxiliary Nurse Midwife 4. Urban Social Health Activist 5. Mahila Arogya Samiti
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2, 1, 3, 4, 5

Under the National Urban Health Mission (NUHM), service coverage decreases from higher-level facilities to community-level workers. Urban Community Health Centres (UCHCs) serve the largest population, followed by Urban Primary Health Centres (UPHCs). Below them are ANMs, then ASHAs, and finally Mahila Arogya Samitis (MAS) at the community group level. Hence, the correct descending order is 2 → 1 → 3 → 4 → 5.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: After a major cyclone strikes a coastal district, the administration undertakes the following interventions: 1. Enforcement of cyclone-resistant building codes and coastal hazard zoning 2. Conducting mock drills, evacuation planning, and stockpiling emergency medicines 3. Search-and-rescue operations, emergency triage, and temporary shelter establishment during the disaster 4. Reconstruction of damaged infrastructure and rehabilitation of displaced populations Which of the following correctly matches interventions 1–4 with the phases of the disaster management cycle?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1-Mitigation, 2-Preparedness, 3-Response, 4-Recovery

The disaster management cycle consists of four major phases:

1. Mitigation – Measures taken to reduce disaster risk and impact before a disaster occurs

• Examples: hazard zoning, cyclone-resistant buildings, flood barriers

2. Preparedness – Planning and training to improve readiness for disasters

• Examples: mock drills, evacuation plans, stockpiling medicines and supplies

3. Response – Immediate actions taken during and immediately after the disaster to save lives

• Examples: search-and-rescue, emergency medical care, temporary shelters

4. Recovery – Long-term restoration and rehabilitation after the disaster

• Examples: rebuilding infrastructure, rehabilitation of displaced populations, livelihood restoration

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: After learning in a lecture that caesarean section rates vary from < 0.5% to over 30% across countries, a student wants to investigate if national caesarean section rates correlate with national maternal mortality rates worldwide. For his investigation, the student obtains population data from an international registry that contains tabulated caesarean section rates and maternal mortality rates from the last 10 years for a total of 119 countries. Which of the following best describes this study design?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Ecological study

• Unit of analysis = groups/populations, not individuals

→ Here: 119 countries
• Uses aggregate (national-level) data

→ Caesarean section rates & maternal mortality rates per country
• Examines correlation between exposure and outcome at population level
• This exactly defines an ecological study.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All are true about JANANI except:
options: JANANI (Journey of Antenatal, Natal and Neonatal Integrated Care) replaces the RCH portal
It enables registration via ABHA, Aadhaar and mobile number, with QR-enabled digital MCH cards
It syncs nationally with U-WIN and POSHAN and allows pan-India beneficiary search
It is a cash-benefit transfer scheme that replaces Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) for institutional deliveries
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. It is a cash-benefit transfer scheme that replaces Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) for institutional deliveries

JANANI is a digital tracking platform, not a cash scheme; JSY/JSSK remain the cash/entitlement schemes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All are true about Samagra Shishu Bal Swasthya Karyakram (SSBSK) except:
options: It integrates HBNC and HBYC into a single continuum from birth to 36 months
'At-risk' newborns receive up to 9 home visits in the first 42 days, and 'at-risk' young children up to 8 visits till 36 months
It introduces Well-Baby Sessions at VHSND, monthly Shishu Shivir, and post-partum maternal mental-health screening
A healthy newborn receives 6 home visits — on days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. A healthy newborn receives 6 home visits — on days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42

None

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All are true regarding this except:
options: ASHA receives same rural incentive regardless of state performance
Urban mother in high performing state gets Rs. 700
Urban ASHA gets Rs. 400 in both low and high performing states
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Urban mother in high performing state gets Rs. 700

JSY Why: Urban mother in high performing state = Rs. 600, not 700. Rs. 700 = rural mother in high performing state.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following are health care delivery indicators, except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Bed turnover ratio

Bed turnover ratio is a hospital utilization/efficiency indicator, not a health care delivery indicator. Population–bed ratio, doctor–nurse ratio, and population per trained birth attendant reflect service availability and delivery. Hence, bed turnover ratio is the correct exception.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following are true about the Anaemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (2026) except:
options: Low-birth-weight babies (0–6 months) are the newly added 7th beneficiary group, and "Eating Right" is the 7th intervention
It marks a shift from prophylactic to therapeutic care, with T3 (Test, Treat, Talk) expanded to T4 by adding "Track"
Haemoglobin data converge into a unified AMB Abhiyaan portal from the JANANI, RBSK and U-WIN portals
Intravenous ferric carboxymaltose and iron sucrose have replaced oral IFA as first-line supplementation for all pregnant women
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Intravenous ferric carboxymaltose and iron sucrose have replaced oral IFA as first-line supplementation for all pregnant women

None

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following statements are true for confounding factor except:
options: It can be reduced by matching
It is associated individually with both cause and effect
It is distributed equally in both study and control groups
It is associated with the exposure of the study
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. It is distributed equally in both study and control groups

A confounding factor is an extraneous variable that distorts the true association between an exposure and an outcome. A variable is considered a confounder if it:

• Is associated with the exposure
• Is independently associated with the outcome
