• Is not an intermediate step in the causal pathway

Confounding can falsely increase, decrease, or reverse an observed association. Methods to control confounding:

• Randomization
• Matching
• Restriction
• Stratification
• Multivariable regression analysis

The incorrect statement is: “It is distributed equally in both study and control groups”

A confounder causes bias precisely because it is unequally distributed between comparison groups.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An impounding reservoir receives water from the surrounding land where rainwater drains into the reservoir. This surrounding land is known as the:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Catchment area

The catchment area is the land from which rainwater drains into a reservoir. It is the main source of impurities entering the reservoir through runoff.

Option-by-option analysis

| Option | Reasoning

| ------ | ---------

| B. Catchment area | The land area draining rainwater/runoff into the reservoir — exact PSM term for this.

| A. Watershed area | In everyday usage "watershed" is often used interchangeably with catchment (drainage basin). But strictly/technically a watershed is the boundary line (the ridge/divide) separating two adjacent catchments — it demarcates, it isn't the collecting land itself. In the PSM/Park's framework, the collecting land of an impounding reservoir is specifically termed the catchment area → B is the intended answer.

| C. Recharge zone | A groundwater concept — the surface area where water percolates down to replenish an aquifer, not surface drainage into a reservoir.

| D. Percolation basin | An engineered structure/basin used to hold water so it percolates into the ground (artificial groundwater recharge) — again groundwater, not reservoir runoff.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An intern in the endocrinology department is asked to complete a chart review of cholesterol levels of all patients hospitalized with diabetes mellitus-related cardiovascular complications in the past 6 months. The intern's preliminary data analysis reveals that there were 400 such patients, and that serum cholesterol levels were normally distributed among the patients with a mean of 220 mg/dL and a standard deviation of 10 mg/dL. Based on these results, how many patients in this study would be expected to have serum cholesterol ≥240 mg/dL?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 10

• Mean cholesterol = 220 mg/dL, SD = 10 mg/dL.
• A value of 240 mg/dL is +2 SD above the mean. In a normal distribution, about 2.5% lie above +2 SD.
• 2.5% of 400 ≈ 10 patients, making option B correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An internist in India is seeing a patient from a minority cultural and linguistic group. To foster therapeutic alliance and provide the best care possible, which of the following approaches should the physician prioritize? 1. Insist on good communication. 2. Insist on communication only via an interpreter. 3. Treat them regardless of their cultural perceptions. 4. Consider the patient's religion and cultural perception.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 4

Good medical care requires effective communication and consideration of the patient’s cultural and religious beliefs. Insisting only on interpreters or ignoring cultural context harms the therapeutic alliance. Therefore, prioritizing communication and cultural sensitivity (statements 1 and 4) is the correct approach.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An investigator is conducting a study to identify potential risk factors for post-transplant hypertension. The investigator selects post-transplant patients with hypertension and gathers detailed information regarding their age, gender, preoperative blood pressure readings, and current medications. The results of the study reveal that some of the patients had been treated with cyclosporine. This study is best described as which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Case series

• The investigator selects only patients with the outcome → Post-transplant hypertension
• There is no comparison group (no non-hypertensive transplant patients).
• The study simply describes characteristics and exposures (e.g., cyclosporine use) among these patients.
• This fits the definition of a case series.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An investigator is studying the frequency of polycythemia in a population of a remote, mountainous region. A representative sample of 100 men shows a normal distribution of hemoglobin concentration with a mean concentration of 17g/dl and a standard error of 0.1 g/dl. Which of the following best represents the probability that a subject will have a hemoglobin concentration greater than 18 g/dL?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 16%

• Mean hemoglobin = 17 g/dL, SD = 1 g/dL.
• Hb of 18 g/dL is +1 SD above mean.
• In a normal distribution, the proportion beyond +1 SD is approximately 16%.
• Hence, the probability that a subject has Hb >18 g/dL is 16%.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Any of the following should be considered as evidence of an outbreak of polio except:
options: Detection of VDPV in a case of Acute Flaccid Paralysis
Detection of a single case of wild polio in a person with Acute Flaccid Paralysis
Detection of any cVDPV infected individuals
Detection of wild PV infection in a healthy asymptomatic individual
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Detection of VDPV in a case of Acute Flaccid Paralysis

Single case of wild poliovirus or detection of circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus (cVDPV) constitutes evidence of an outbreak. However, detection of VDPV in a single AFP case alone does not automatically indicate an outbreak unless circulation is demonstrated. Therefore, detection of VDPV in an AFP case is not sufficient evidence of an outbreak.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Arrange the following steps of an interview in the correct order in a sequence. 1. Starting an interview 2. Encouragement 3. Establishing contact 4. Securing rapport
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 3-1-4-2

Technique of Interview

1. Establishing Contact
2. Starting an Interview
3. Securing Rapport
4. Recall
5. Probe Questions
6. Encouragement
7. Guiding the Interview
8. Recording
9. Closing the Interview
10. Report

Establishing contact initiates interaction, starting the interview sets the purpose, rapport builds trust, and encouragement sustains communication. Proper sequencing improves data quality and participant cooperation, which is essential in public health interviews and surveys.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As a Medical Officer at a Community Health Center (CHC), you're consulted by a mother about starting immunizations for her 13-month-old son who hasn't received any vaccines since birth. Based on the national immunization schedule, which combination of vaccines would you recommend for this child's initial immunization?
options: BCG, OPV 1st dose, Pentavalent 1st dose, Rota virus 1st dose
OPV 1st dose, Pentavalent 1st dose, Measles 1st dose
OPV 1st dose, DPT 1st dose, Measles 1st dose
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. OPV 1st dose, DPT 1st dose, Measles 1st dose

At 13 months, rotavirus and pentavalent vaccines are not initiated. The correct catch-up schedule includes OPV 1st dose, DPT 1st dose, and Measles 1st dose. BCG is not routinely given after infancy in national schedules. Hence, option D is correct.

Upper limit of vaccines:

• BCG/ HEP B/ IPV/ ROTA/ PENTA/ PCV – 1 year
• MR/ VIT A/ OPV - 5 years
• Hib - 6 years
• DTP - 7 years
• JE - 15 years

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As a part of a public health project, you are analyzing maternal mortality in a town over a six-month period. In this time, there were 2,500 live births. The recorded maternal deaths include 5 due to peripartum infection, 2 due to obstructed labor, and 3 due to postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), 10 from electrocution. Based on this data, calculate the Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) for this period.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 4 per 1,000 live births

Maternal deaths (eligible for MMR):

Include only deaths related to pregnancy, childbirth, or within 42 days of termination.

• Peripartum infection = 5
• Obstructed labor = 2
• Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) = 3

Total maternal deaths = 10

Exclude deaths due to unrelated causes (e.g., electrocution = 10)

Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: At a local laboratory, the normal reference range for serum free T4 levels is 5-12 μg/dL. Free T4 levels are measured in 2 patient samples, one from a population of healthy patients without thyroid disease and one from a population of patients with hyperthyroidism. If the laboratory increases the upper limit of normal serum free T4 levels to 13 μg/dL, how would the sensitivity and specificity of free T4 level measurements for detecting hyperthyroidism in the samples change?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Specificity increase, Sensitivity decrease

• Normal range increased from 5–12 → 5–13 μg/dL
• This effectively raises the cutoff for calling a test positive for hyperthyroidism.

Effect of raising the cutoff

•

Fewer people labeled positive

• ↓ False positives
• ↑ True negatives

•

Specificity/PPV increases

• Sensitivity/NPV decreases

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: At an epidemiology conference in Toronto, Dr. Arjun Singh, an esteemed epidemiologist, showcased a compelling longitudinal study. In his study, 45,000 men were diligently monitored over 25 years, of which 2,500 developed prostate cancer. In an attempt to enhance the depth of the study, an additional 3,500 men confirmed to be healthy were included as controls. Dr. Singh highlighted that at the start of the study, potential risk factors were deduced from baseline data gathered through questionnaires disseminated to both sets of participants along with their blood samples which were stored after proper labelling. This strategic approach was designed to trace the onset of disease over an extended period, subsequently analysing it with the baseline data. Which terminology best describes this study design?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Nested case-control study

A nested case-control study is a type of case-control study conducted within a previously established cohort.

• A large cohort is followed over time
• Participants who develop the disease become “cases”
• Controls are selected from disease-free members of the same cohort
• Exposure data and biologic samples are often collected at baseline before disease develops

Advantages:

• Less expensive and time-consuming than analyzing the entire cohort
• Reduces recall bias because exposure data were collected before disease onset
• Useful for biomarker and genetic studies using stored samples

High-yield comparison:

• Cohort study → starts with exposure, follows for disease
• Case-control study → starts with disease, looks backward for exposure
• Nested case-control → case-control study “nested” inside a cohort

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Banana is a good source of all of the following nutrients except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Iron

Banana is a good source of:

• Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine)
• Vitamin C
• Phosphorus (in modest amounts)

However,

• Iron ❌ → Banana contains very small, nutritionally insignificant amounts of iron and is not considered a good source.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Based on the depiction in the accompanying image, which model is being illustrated?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. PERT model

The image depicts multiple interconnected causes influencing disease, without a single linear pathway. This represents the web of causation model, which explains multifactorial disease causation, especially in non-communicable diseases.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Based on the graphical representation provided, which of the following equations corresponds to the regression model of the plotted graph?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. y=11+2x

The graph shows a straight-line relationship with a positive slope of 2 and a Y-intercept of 11. Therefore, the Linear regression equation is y = 11 + 2x, which correctly represents the plotted data.

REGRESSION formulae:

• y=a+bx – Simple linear regression
• y=a+b_1 x_1+b_2 x_2+⋯+b_n x_n – Multiple linear regression
• y=a+bx+cx2 – Curvilinear regression

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Components evaluated in Sample Registration System (SRS): 1. Crude Birth Rate 2. Crude Death Rate 3. Infant Mortality Rate 4. Maternal Mortality Ratio
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2, 3, 4

• SRS (Registrar General of India) provides reliable annual estimates of vital events at national/state level.
• Provides annual estimates of: CBR, CDR, IMR, MMR, TFR, GFR, cause of death (via verbal autopsy).
• Based on dual record system: continuous enumeration by resident part-time enumerator + independent 6-monthly retrospective survey by supervisor.
• Discrepancies reconciled by field verification (matching).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During a rubella outbreak, priority of vaccination from high to low is:
options: Infants → Adolescent females → Reproductive age women
Reproductive age women (20–25 yr, non-pregnant) → Adolescent females → Infants
Pregnant women → Reproductive age women → Infants
Adolescent females → Infants → Reproductive age women
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Reproductive age women (20–25 yr, non-pregnant) → Adolescent females → Infants

Why:

• Priority 1 = 20–25 year non-pregnant reproductive age females (to prevent CRS).
• Priority 2 = Adolescent females.
• Priority 3 = Infants and children.

Rubella vaccine = contraindicated in pregnancy → hence non-pregnant women get priority.

Rubella Ig = only for pregnant females with known exposure.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During a summer wedding reception, 150 guests were served a buffet meal that included chicken salad, seafood pasta, and fruit desserts. Within 8–12 hours, dozens of guests begin experiencing sudden-onset abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. By the next morning, nearly all affected guests had symptoms, but no new cases occurred after 24–36 hours. An epidemiologic investigation reveals that illness was strongly associated with eating the chicken salad, which was later found to have been contaminated with Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxin. Which of the following best describes the epidemic pattern of this outbreak?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Point source single exposure epidemic

Key features of the outbreak:

• Single event (wedding reception)
• Common exposure (chicken salad contaminated with Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxin)
• Short incubation period (8–12 hours → preformed toxin)
• Sudden surge of cases, followed by rapid decline
• No secondary cases after 24–36 hours

These are classic characteristics of a point source (single exposure) epidemic.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During a wedding dinner, 140 of 200 attendees develop sudden vomiting within 3 hours. The outbreak investigation team interviews attendees about foods consumed and calculates attack rates for each item. Which study approach is most appropriate in this setting?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Retrospective cohort study

This is a classic point-source foodborne outbreak in a well-defined, closed group with a known denominator. There are 200 attendees, and investigators can ascertain exposure history to specific food items for both those who became ill and those who did not. In such settings, the most appropriate analytic approach is a retrospective cohort study.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During polio eradication efforts, a child develops paralytic polio after receiving OPV. Investigation reveals the causative strain is OPV P2. It has mutated and is transmissible in the community. What is this condition called and what was the rationale behind the National Switch Day on 25th April 2016?
options: VAPP associated with OPV P3; switch to remove P2 strain from trivalent OPV
VDPV caused by mutation of OPV P2; switch from trivalent to bivalent OPV removing P2 strain
VAPP caused by OPV P2; switch from bivalent to trivalent OPV
VDPV; switch from OPV to IPV entirely across India
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. VDPV caused by mutation of OPV P2; switch from trivalent to bivalent OPV removing P2 strain

VDPV vs VAPP:

| Feature | VDPV | VAPP

| ------- | ---- | ----

| Full form | Vaccine Derived Polio Virus | Vaccine Associated Paralytic Polio

| Mechanism | Mutation of OPV | Immune reaction

| Associated strain | OPV P2 | OPV P3

| Transmission | + (transmissible, more dangerous) | — (not transmitted)

| Key concern | Community spread | Individual risk

Mutated + transmissible = VDPV (not VAPP). VAPP = immune-mediated, individual, not transmitted.

National Switch Day: 25th April 2016 → Trivalent OPV (P1+P2+P3) → Bivalent OPV (P1+P3 only).

• P2 strain removed because: P2 was already eradicated globally AND P2 was the strain most associated with VDPV mutations → removing P2 from OPV eliminates VDPV risk from P2.
• End game strategy: fIPV at 6 and 14 weeks (right upper arm, ID) + 9 months (left upper arm, as MR given at 9 months in right upper arm).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During the assessment of an immunization program in a rural district, it was observed that vaccine potency loss was more common at the peripheral point of vaccine storage and use. At which level of the health system is the highest likelihood of cold chain failure expected?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. At the village level

Cold chain failure is most likely to occur at the peripheral end of the immunization system.

Why the village level is highest risk:

• Vaccines are handled at subcentres / outreach sessions
• Longer exposure time outside cold chain during transport and sessions
• Intermittent electricity or no power supply
• Limited supervision and monitoring
• Greater dependence on ice packs and vaccine carriers

Hence, vaccine potency loss is most common at the village level.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: For calculating the life expectancy index in Human Development Index (HDI), what are the minimum and maximum values used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 20 years and 85 years

Life Expectancy Index = (Actual value − 20) / (85 − 20)

HDI - Three Dimensions:

| Dimension | Indicator | Min | Max

| --------- | --------- | --- | ---

| Health | Life expectancy at birth | 20 yrs | 85 yrs

| Education | Mean years of schooling + Expected years of schooling | 0 / 0 | 15 / 18

| Standard of living | GNI per capita | 100 | 75,000

Formula (each dimension index):

Dimension Index = (Actual − Min) / (Max − Min)

HDI = Geometric mean of the three dimension indices = (Health Index × Education Index × Income Index)^(1/3)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Given the constraints and the need to ensure minimal nutritional adequacy, what should the minimum supplementation be in the Mid-Day Meal to support the children's needs?
options: 1/3 of the total protein requirement + ½ of total energy requirement for minimum 250 days in a year
2/3 of the total protein requirement + ½ of total energy requirement for minimum 200 days in a year
½ of the total protein requirement + 1/3 of total energy requirement for minimum 200 days in a year
½ of the total protein requirement + 2/3 of total energy requirement for minimum 250 days in a year
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. ½ of the total protein requirement + 1/3 of total energy requirement for minimum 200 days in a year

The Mid-Day Meal Scheme aims to provide nutritional support, not full dietary replacement. The minimum requirement is ½ of total protein requirement and ⅓ of total energy requirement for at least 200 days in a year. This ensures dietary adequacy while remaining programmatically feasible at the population level.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: How can lead time in disease screening programs be minimized?
options: By implementing periodic screening of the target population
By delaying diagnostic confirmation until symptoms appear
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. By implementing periodic screening of the target population

Lead time is the interval between detection of disease by screening and usual clinical diagnosis. Excessive lead time can distort survival statistics (lead time bias).

How to minimize lead time in screening programs:

• Periodic (regular) screening ensures cases are detected closer to the time they would become clinically apparent, rather than too early.
• This reduces artificial inflation of survival time without truly improving prognosis.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: How many total doses of DPT will a child receive by 2 years of age according to NIS?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 4

Under the National Immunization Schedule, a child receives 3 primary doses of DPT at 6, 10, and 14 weeks, plus 1 booster at 16–24 months, totalling 4 doses by 2 years of age.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the correct pair of BMW management: 1. Human waste - Incineration 2. Urobag - Microwave 3. Vacutainer - Recycling 4. Chemicals - Collect in chlorinated containers and send for disposal
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2, 3

Human anatomical waste is disposed by incineration. Urobags can be treated by microwave, and vacutainers (after disinfection) can be recycled. Chemicals are not handled as stated in option 4. Therefore, the correct set is 1, 2, and 3, making option C correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the correct statements about vaccines: 1. Influenza and yellow fever vaccines are CI in egg allergy 2. Abscess formation post-BCG is treated conservatively 3. Live vaccines should not be given with Human immunoglobulin except measles 4. All of the following are killed vaccines: Pertussis, Salk, SA14-14-2, 17D 5. NS is used as diluent for Danish 1331
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 5

Influenza and yellow fever vaccines are contraindicated in severe egg allergy, and normal saline is used as diluent for Danish 1331 BCG strain.

Other statements are incorrect:

• BCG abscess is managed by Incision and drainage
• Live vaccines should not be given with Human immunoglobulin without exception.
• Killed vaccines: Pertussis, Salk (SA14-14-2-JE, 17D-yellow fever are live vaccines)

Hence, statements 1 and 5 are correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the correct statements: 1. Role of Social factors in Disease causation is studied under Social Pathology 2. Birth of a baby should be registered within 21days 3. Birth dose of BCG is 0.05ml intra-dermal 4. Base of a population pyramid denotes fertility
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2, 3, 4

All statements are correct:

• Social factors in disease causation are studied under social pathology
• Births (and deaths as well) should be registered within 21 days
• BCG birth dose is 0.05 ml intradermal (if given in one month after birth; after that: 0.1ml)
• Base of population pyramid reflects fertility and births.

Hence, all options are correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the correctly matched pair of health-related observance and date:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. World Health Day — 7 April

World Health Day is observed on 7 April, marking the founding of WHO in 1948.

Other options are incorrect:

• World TB Day is on 24 March,
• World Population Day is on 11 July,
• World AIDS Day is on 1 December.

Hence, option B is the only correctly matched pair.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the image:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Pareto plot

A Pareto chart displays bars in descending order of frequency along with a cumulative percentage curve. It is based on the 80–20 rule, highlighting the most important contributors to a problem. It is commonly used in quality control and public health management to prioritize interventions.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement:
options: Rideal-Walker Coefficient (RWC) is used to represent the germicidal power of a disinfectant.
For workrooms with exposure to contaminants, the minimum recommended number of air changes per hour is 4-6 to maintain air quality and protect worker health.
Demographic trap is seen in Stage 2 of demographic cycle.
Nodal Ministry for Disaster Management is ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Nodal Ministry for Disaster Management is ministry of Health and Family Welfare

The nodal ministry for disaster management in India is the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), not the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

Other statements are correct:

A. Rideal–Walker coefficient measures disinfectant efficacy

B. recommended air changes in workrooms are 4–6 per hour

C. Demographic trap occurs in Stage 2

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a cohort study investigating the link between heavy smoking and bronchogenic carcinoma, the incidence among smokers was found to be 10 per 1,000 person-years, while the incidence among non-smokers was 1 per 1,000 person-years. Which of the following cannot be concluded based on the information provided above?
options: If smoking were eliminated from the entire population, the incidence of bronchogenic carcinoma would fall by 90%.
For every 10 cases of carcinoma among smokers, 9 are due to their habit of smoking.
Smokers are 10 times as likely to get cancer as non-smokers.
10% of the cases among smokers can be attributed to baseline risk factors that also affect non-smokers.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. If smoking were eliminated from the entire population, the incidence of bronchogenic carcinoma would fall by 90%.

From the given incidences (10/1000 in smokers vs 1/1000 in non-smokers), the relative risk is 10, and attributable fraction among exposed is 90%, meaning most cases among smokers are due to smoking. However, the statement that eliminating smoking would reduce population incidence by 90% cannot be concluded without knowing the prevalence of smoking in the population, which is required to calculate population attributable risk.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a cohort study on alcohol and cirrhosis, calculate Attributable Risk and interpret what it means for a policy decision:
options: AR = 20%; eliminating alcohol would prevent 20% of cirrhosis in exposed drinkers
AR = 30%; eliminating alcohol would prevent 30% of cases in the total population
AR = 30%; eliminating alcohol would prevent 30% of cirrhosis in exposed drinkers
AR = 10%; eliminating alcohol prevents 10% of total population cirrhosis
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. AR = 30%; eliminating alcohol would prevent 30% of cirrhosis in exposed drinkers

| Measure | Formula | Denominator | Policy use

| ------- | ------- | ----------- | ----------

| AR | (Ie−Ine)/Ie | Incidence in exposed | How much risk eliminated in exposed group

| PAR | (Itotal−Ine)/Itotal | Incidence in total population | How much disease reduced in whole population

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a drug trial for MI prevention: CER, EER, ARR, NNT, and RRR — which statement is incorrect?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. NNT = 100

| Measure | Formula | Value

| ------- | ------- | -----

| CER | c/(c+d) | 40/200 = 20%

| EER | a/(a+b) | 20/200 = 10%

| ARR | CER – EER | 20−10 = 10% = 0.10

| NNT | 1/ARR (decimal) | 1/0.10 = 10

| RRR | (CER−EER)/CER | 10/20 = 50%

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a population of 500,000, 3,000 people die in a year. 600 of these die from tuberculosis. The proportional mortality rate for TB is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 20%

• PMR = (Deaths from specific disease / Total deaths) × 100.
• Not total population in denominator. PMR = (600/3000) × 100 = 20%.

| Formula | Denominator | Result | Measure

| ------- | ----------- | ------ | -------

| TB deaths/Total deaths × 100 | 3,000 | 20% | PMR

| TB deaths/Mid-year population × 1000 | 500,000 | 1.2/1000 | Cause-specific death rate

| Total deaths/Mid-year population × 1000 | 500,000 | 6/1000 | CDR

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a reference sample of hundreds of healthy subjects, the laboratory reference range for a novel marker of cardiac injury is 0.04-0.08 U/m l at the standard 95% level of probability. The marker has very high sensitivity and specificity for myocardial tissue. The clinical cardiology team would like to use a 99.7% reference range to assess patients who come to the emergency department with chest pain and have a high pretest probability of cardiac ischemia. An elevated value of the marker is defined as exceeding the 99.7th percentile of the reference sample. Assuming a normal (Gaussian) distribution with a mean of 0.06 U/ml, which of the following most closely approximates the corresponding reference range?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 0.03 to 0.09

99.7% reference range corresponds to ±3 standard deviations from the mean in a normal distribution. The given 95% range (0.04–0.08) represents ±2 SD around a mean of 0.06. Extending this to ±3 SD gives an approximate range of 0.03 to 0.09 U/ml, making option A the correct answer.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a study on smoking and life expectancy, a linear regression model shows that 36% of the variability in life expectancy is explained by smoking, while the remaining variability is attributed to other factors. What is the correlation coefficient (r) between smoking and life expectancy in this study?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 0.60

The phrase "36% of the variability in life expectancy is explained by smoking" is the definition of the coefficient of determination (r²). So: To get the correlation coefficient, take the square root

Option-by-option (distractor logic)

| Option | Value | Trap it catches

| ------ | ----- | ---------------

| A) 0.36 | Reports r² itself | Student confuses r with r² — doesn't take the square root

| B) 0.60 | √0.36 | Correct — recognizes 36% = r², so r = √0.36

| C) 0.64 | The unexplained variance (1 − 0.36) | Student grabs the "remaining 64%" figure

| D) 0.18 | 0.36 ÷ 2 | Student wrongly "halves" instead of taking √

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In determining nutrient requirements for a population, which of the following nutrients is not included in the calculation for Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) for 97.5% of the population?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Energy

Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) is the daily nutrient intake level sufficient to meet the requirements of 97.5% of healthy individuals in a particular age and sex group.

However, energy requirements are not expressed as RDA because:

• Excess intake of energy can lead to obesity
• Energy needs vary widely depending on physical activity and metabolism
• Therefore, energy is estimated as the Average Requirement rather than an intake covering 97.5% of the population

Nutrients commonly expressed as RDA:

• Protein
• Vitamins (eg, Vitamin A)
• Minerals (eg, Iron)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC), number of postnatal visits by ASHA after LSCS is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 5

For LSCS deliveries, HBNC visits are on Day 7, 14, 21, 28, 42 (5 visits) — the Day-3 visit is omitted since the mother/baby are still under institutional post-op care at that point.

HBNC Postnatal Visit Schedule (ASHA)

| Delivery type | Number of visits | Days

| ------------- | ---------------- | ----

| Institutional delivery | 6 | 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42

| Home delivery | 7 | 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42

| LSCS delivery | 5 | 7, 14, 21, 28, 42

| SNCU-discharged/LBW/preterm | 6 (from day of discharge) + quarterly follow-up till 1 year | Discharge day = Day 1, then 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42; then 3, 6, 9, 12 months

Activities during each visit:

• Check danger signs (poor feeding, lethargy, hypothermia, convulsions, fast/difficult breathing)
• Weight monitoring, exclusive breastfeeding counseling
• Cord care, temperature maintenance (KMC counseling for LBW)
• Postpartum maternal care — bleeding, infection signs, family planning counseling
• BCG/OPV-0/Hep B-0 verification

Incentive: ₹250 per newborn on completion of full visit schedule.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In immunization cold chain management, a dial thermometer is often used to monitor the temperature of an ILR. This instrument works on which underlying physical principle?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Thermocouple

A thermocouple is a temperature-measuring device that works on the Seebeck effect. It consists of two dissimilar metal wires joined at one end. When the junction experiences a temperature change, a small voltage is generated proportional to that temperature difference.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the campaign shown in the image, what does the acronym stand for?
options: Social Awareness and Action plan to Neutralise Pneumonia Successfully
Society Act and Awareness plan to Neutralise Pneumonia Successfully
Social Act and Action plan to Neutralise Pneumonia Successfully
Society Achievement and Activity to Neutralise Pneumonia Successfully
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Social Awareness and Action plan to Neutralise Pneumonia Successfully

SAANS is a Government of India initiative under the National Health Mission aimed at reducing childhood deaths due to pneumonia.

SAANS stands for Social Awareness and Action to Neutralise Pneumonia Successfully

• Early identification of childhood pneumonia
• Timely treatment and referral
• Community awareness regarding danger signs

Major components:

• Promotion of exclusive breastfeeding
• Adequate nutrition
• Immunization
• Hand hygiene
• Reduction of indoor air pollution
• Early care-seeking for fast breathing and chest indrawing

Population size is at its maximum and stable

• Population reaches maximum and stabilizes only in Stage 4.
• Stage 5 = BR < DR = declining population (Japan, Greece, Norway).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Kappa statistic is used to assess inter-observer agreement beyond chance. A Kappa value is considered “good agreement” when it lies within:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 0.61 – 0.80

Kappa value (κ) measures inter-observer agreement for qualitative (categorical) data beyond chance.

Formula:

κ = (Observed agreement − Expected agreement) / (1 − Expected agreement)

Interpretation:

| Cohen’s Kappa | Interpretation

| ------------- | --------------

| 0.10 – 0.20 | Slight/ poor agreement

| 0.21 – 0.40 | Fair agreement

| 0.41 – 0.60 | Moderate agreement

| 0.61 – 0.80 | Substantial/good agreement

| 0.81 – 0.99 | Near-perfect/very good agreement

| 1 | Perfect agreement

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Officials of a public health department report a higher than normal prevalence of AML among children age 5-12 in their community. They observe that some households in the community are exposed to chemical waste from a nearby factory and worry that exposure to this waste is responsible for the increased prevalence of AML. A case-control study is designed to evaluate the health department officials' claim that exposure to chemical waste is associated with AML in childhood. Which of the following populations should be selected as the control group?
options: Children who do not have AML and are exposed to chemical waste
Children who do not have AML and are not exposed to chemical waste
Children who do not have AML, regardless of exposure status to chemical waste
Children who have AML, regardless of exposure status to chemical waste
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Children who do not have AML, regardless of exposure status to chemical waste

Controls should represent the population from which cases arose, regardless of exposure status. Therefore, children without AML, irrespective of chemical exposure, form the correct control group. This avoids selection bias and allows valid estimation of odds ratio.

questions.text: Primary level of prevention includes: 1. Screening of disease 2. Quarantine 3. Isolation 4. Diagnosis 5. Vaccination
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 2, 3, 5

Primary prevention aims to prevent the occurrence of disease by reducing exposure or increasing resistance.

Included in Primary Prevention:

• 2. Quarantine

NOT included:

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Public health officials involved in developing nutritional guidelines commission a study to determine how dietary eating patterns influence total body iron stores in children age 5-17. As part of the study, researchers want to assess how 2 independent variables, red meat consumption and egg consumption (both reported in units of ounces/week), affect serum ferritin concentrations while adjusting for age and gender. Which of the following statistical techniques is most helpful for determining the association between the study variables?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Regression analysis

When assessing how multiple independent variables (red meat intake, egg intake) affect a continuous dependent variable (serum ferritin), while adjusting for confounders like age and gender, regression analysis is the most appropriate method. It allows simultaneous adjustment and estimation of independent effects, unlike ANOVA or odds ratios.

questions.explanation:

A Total cholesterol/HDL ratio <3.5 is considered an optimal target for reducing CHD risk. Lower values indicate lower cardiovascular risk.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Regarding sputum smear microscopy (Ziehl–Neelsen staining) for diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis, which of the following is most correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Low sensitivity and high specificity

Sputum smear microscopy (Ziehl–Neelsen staining) detects acid-fast bacilli (AFB).

Test characteristics

• Sensitivity – LOW
• Requires \~10⁴–10⁵ bacilli/mL of sputum
• Misses paucibacillary disease, early TB, HIV-associated TB
• Specificity – HIGH
• Presence of AFB in sputum is highly suggestive of TB in endemic areas
• False positives are uncommon

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Regarding the Eijkman test, which of the following statements are correct? 1. It involves incubation at 44°C 2. It detects fecal contamination of water 3. It is specific for E. coli 4. It demonstrates acid and gas formation from glucose
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. All are correct

Eijkman test is a bacteriological test used to detect fecal contamination of water. It is based on the ability of Escherichia coli to ferment lactose with acid and gas production at 44–45°C, helping distinguish fecal coliforms from non-fecal coliforms.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Regarding the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11), which of the following statements are correct? 1. ICD-11 includes a supplementary chapter on traditional medicine conditions. 2. Gender incongruence has been reclassified outside the mental disorders chapter. 3. ICD-11 became effective for use from 1 January 2022. 4. Chapter 6 in ICD-11 deals with mental, behavioural, and neurodevelopmental disorders. 5. ICD-11 is available exclusively in printed format and not digitally adaptable.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2, 3, 4

ICD-11 includes a traditional medicine chapter, reclassifies gender incongruence outside mental disorders, became effective from 1 Jan 2022, and Chapter 6 covers mental, behavioral, and neurodevelopmental disorders. It is also digitally adaptable, making option A (1–4) correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Researchers are interested in the association between colorectal carcinoma and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug use. They first interview a group of patients with biopsy-proven colorectal carcinoma and then interview a group consisting of the patients' neighbors who are of similar age and race. The analysis is based on comparing the results of pairs of individuals who have similar characteristics. This design technique best helps address which of the following potential problems with this study?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Confounding

Matching cases with neighbors of similar age and race is done to control confounding. By ensuring that cases and controls are comparable on known confounders, the association between NSAID use and colorectal cancer is less distorted. Matching does not prevent recall or observer bias but specifically addresses confounding at the design stage.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Researchers are studying the prevalence of intravenous drug use in a large metropolitan area. Because this is a stigmatized and hard-to-reach population, investigators initially identify a small group of participants through community outreach programs. Each participant is then asked to refer friends or acquaintances who also use intravenous drugs, and those referrals are further asked to recruit others. The sample gradually expands until the desired sample size is reached. Which of the following best describes the sampling strategy used in this study?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Snowball sampling

Snowball sampling is a non-probability sampling method used to recruit participants from hidden, stigmatized, or hard-to-reach populations such as intravenous drug users, sex workers, or undocumented immigrants. Initial participants recruit additional subjects from their personal networks, causing the sample to expand progressively.

Key features:

• Useful when a formal sampling frame is unavailable
• Cost-effective for rare populations
• Recruitment depends on participant referrals

Major limitation: High risk of selection bias and limited generalizability because participants are not selected randomly.

Comparison with other methods:

• Simple random sampling → every individual has equal chance of selection
• Stratified sampling → population divided into subgroups before random sampling
• Cluster sampling → random selection of naturally occurring groups/clusters.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Researchers are studying the relationship between essential hypertension and a common mutation in the structure of a sodium channel protein. A study population is randomly selected and blood samples are obtained for leukocyte genotyping. The prevalence of hypertension is determined based on mean blood pressure measurements obtained using standardized ambulatory blood pressure monitoring conducted over 1 week. Based on the analysis results, the researchers conclude that the sodium channel structure mutation is associated with hypertension. Which of the following best describes the study design used by the investigators?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cross-sectional study

Exposure (sodium channel mutation) and outcome (hypertension prevalence) are assessed at the same time in a randomly selected population. There is no follow-up. This design measures prevalence and associations simultaneously, fitting a cross-sectional study.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Researchers at an academic trauma center conducted a randomized clinical trial comparing 2 surgical techniques (Technique A and Technique B) for repairing a mandible fracture. They examined rates of infectious complications and rates of malocclusion. A total of 100 patients were enrolled in the study. Results showed that the relative rate of infection with Technique A compared with Technique B was 0.86 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.57-1.28. What is a correct statement?
options: Technique A is superior to Technique B
Technique B is superior to Technique A
The techniques should not be used in a clinical care setting
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Neither surgery technique is superior

The relative risk of 0.86 has a 95% confidence interval of 0.57–1.28, which crosses 1. This indicates no statistically significant difference between the two surgical techniques. Therefore, neither technique can be considered superior based on the available data.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Researchers conduct a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effect of a new exercise program versus standard lifestyle advice on lowering systolic blood pressure (SBP) in adults with prehypertension. A total of 200 participants are randomized equally between the two groups. After 6 months, the mean decrease in SBP is –6 mm Hg greater in the exercise group compared to the control group. The analysis yields a p-value of 0.02 (predetermined significance level = 0.05). Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of this result?
options: The probability that the null hypothesis (no difference in SBP) is true is 2%
The probability of obtaining these results by chance if the null hypothesis is true is 2%
There is a 2% chance that any individual in the exercise group will experience at least a 6 mm Hg decrease in SBP
There is a 2% chance that the mean SBP reduction is biased in favor of the exercise group
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. The probability of obtaining these results by chance if the null hypothesis is true is 2%

A p-value of 0.02 means:

• Assuming the null hypothesis is true (no real difference in SBP), there is a 2% probability of observing a result as extreme as—or more extreme than—the one obtained purely due to random chance.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Researchers conduct a randomized controlled trial to evaluate whether adding tranexamic acid (TXA) to routine oxytocin prophylaxis reduces the risk of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) after vaginal delivery. The study reports a relative risk (RR) of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.66–0.96) for PPH in the TXA group compared with the control group. Which of the following best interprets these findings?
options: TXA increases the risk of PPH by 20%.
TXA reduces the risk of PPH by 80%.
TXA reduces the risk of PPH by 20%.
The absolute risk of PPH with TXA is 0.8%.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. TXA reduces the risk of PPH by 20%.

Relative Risk Reduction = 1 − RR = 1 − 0.80 = 0.20 (20%). Since the confidence interval does not cross 1, the reduction is statistically significant.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Researchers develop a new test to detect the presence of a recently identified biomarker NMP22 for ca UB. The initial evaluation of the test shows the following. Which of the following is the likelihood that a patient with a negative test does not have ca UB?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 0.96

This question asks for the Negative Predictive Value (NPV), which is the probability that a person truly does not have disease given a negative test result. Based on the data provided, the NPV is 0.96, meaning there is a 96% chance that a patient with a negative test truly does not have carcinoma of the urinary bladder. NPV depends strongly on disease prevalence.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Researchers studying the effects of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) on the risk of myocardial infarction (Ml) among postmenopausal women calculate the relative risk (RR) of Ml to be 1.30 (p = 0.07) among women who are taking HRT compared to those who are not. The researchers conclude that there is no statistically significant increased risk of Ml with HRT. Subsequently, the results of a meta-analysis determine that there actually is an increased risk of Ml, with an overall RR= 1.32 (p = 0.03) among postmenopausal women who are taking HRT compared to those who are not. Which of the following was the most likely problem in the first study?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Sample size

• The first study reported:

• RR = 1.30
• p = 0.07 → not statistically significant

• The meta-analysis later showed:

• RR = 1.32
• p = 0.03 → statistically significant

Key observation:

The effect size is almost identical in both analyses (≈1.3), but statistical significance differs.

Why this happens

• A small sample size → low statistical power
• Low power increases the chance of a Type II error (false negative)
• Meta-analysis increases effective sample size, reducing random error and making the association statistically significant

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Secondary attack rate among household contacts of the 60 ill patients is being calculated. 60 ill patients have a total of 180 household contacts. Of these, 20 were already immune. 40 developed illness within the next incubation period. SAR is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 25%

• SAR formula = Secondary cases / (Total susceptible contacts − primary cases) × 100.
• Susceptible contacts = 180 − 20 (immune) = 160. Primary cases not in this household pool (they are the source).
• SAR = 40/160 × 100 = 25%.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) was launched as part of the National Mental Health Programme to improve access to basic mental health care at the district level. Which of the following is NOT a component of the District Mental Health Programme?
options: Early detection and treatment of mental illnesses
Providing data for future mental health planning
Screening of the general population for mental disorders
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Screening of the general population for mental disorders

The District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) focuses on service delivery, capacity building, and integration of mental health into general health care, not mass population screening.

Core components of DMHP include:

• Training of health-care personnel (medical officers, nurses, ASHAs) ✔️
• Early detection and treatment through OPDs at district/CHC/PHC levels ✔️
• Data collection and reporting to support monitoring and future mental health planning ✔️
• Screening of the general population for mental disorders ❌

o DMHP follows an opportunistic and referral-based approach, not universal screening.

The District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) is a key component of India’s National Mental Health Programme. It aims to decentralize mental health services by integrating them into district-level healthcare, ensuring early detection, treatment, rehabilitation, and community awareness for common mental disorders through trained primary care staff.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The image shows two data distribution curves from separate studies within the same population: one depicted with a red line and the other with a blue line. Given the graphical representation, which of the following correctly represents the relationship among the mean, median, and mode for the data presented?
options: Mean = median, not equal to mode
Mode = median, not equal to mean
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Mean = median, not equal to mode

The curve shown represents a symmetrical distribution with an abnormal peak, where mean equals median, but mode differs. This pattern commonly occurs in bimodal or irregular symmetric distributions. Therefore, the correct relationship is mean = median ≠ mode.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The Kyoto Protocol is primarily concerned with:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The mean systolic blood pressure was measured in a sample population of elderly females as 125 mm Hg with a standard deviation of 10. 95% of people would have blood pressure above:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 110 mm Hg

• For a normally distributed variable, the value above which 95% of observations lie corresponds to the 5th percentile.
• Using the normal distribution: Z = -1.645

Given:

• Mean = 125 mm Hg
• SD = 10 mm Hg

Calculation: 125 - (1.645 * 10) =  125 - 16.45 = approx 108.5 mm Hg

Closest option: 110 mm Hg

Therefore, approximately 95% of people would have systolic blood pressure above 110 mm Hg.

Key concepts:

• 95% within ±2 SD applies to the central distribution
• One-sided 95% cutoff uses 1.645 SD, not 2 SD.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The most common operation performed by an ophthalmologist at a district hospital / CHC level is:

questions.subject: Community Medicine

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The Stanford Three-Community Study, the North Karelia Project, and the Lipid Research Clinics Study are well-known research efforts. What type of study design best describes these efforts?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Risk factor intervention trials

• These studies are examples of risk factor intervention trials, which involve actively modifying specific risk factors, such as smoking, dietary habits, or cholesterol levels, to observe their effects on health outcomes.
• The goal of these trials is to implement and measure the impact of behavioral or clinical interventions in a population, tracking changes in disease incidence based on the modified risk factors.
• The Stanford Three-Community Study, North Karelia Project, and Lipid Research Clinics Study are risk factor intervention trials focused on reducing health risks through targeted interventions, rather than merely observing outcomes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The table provided illustrates a multivariate analysis assessing the relationship between the risk of blindness and various factors including age, literacy rate, place of residence, and gender. Which of the subsequent statements accurately interprets this data? 1. Female population is at greater risk of developing blindness. 2. People dwelling in rural areas are at increased risk of developing blindness. 3. Risk of developing blindness increases with age. 4. Illiteracy leads to increased risk of developing blindness.

The table shows a progressive increase in odds of blindness with age, and illiteracy is associated with higher risk. Gender and rural residence are not consistently significant. questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The target demographic for latest RMNCAH+N includes which of the following? a. Maternal and child health b. Family planning services c. Geriatric health d. Adolescent health

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under NTEP, a private practitioner notifies a new TB case through NIKSHAY and also reports the treatment outcome after completion. What is the total incentive amount the private provider receives, and what is the Nikshay Poshan Yojana amount the patient receives monthly?
options: Private provider: INR 500 total; Patient: INR 1000/month
Private provider: INR 1000 total; Patient: INR 1000/month
Private provider: INR 500 total; Patient: INR 500/month
Private provider: INR 1500 total; Patient: INR 500/month
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Private provider: INR 1000 total; Patient: INR 1000/month

Private practitioners (including private clinics and hospitals) receive a total incentive of ₹1,000 per notified case. This amount is disbursed in two stages through the ₹500 for the initial case notification and ₹500 for successful treatment outcome declaration upon completion.

Nikshay Poshan Yojana: ₹1,000 per month for the patient, for the entire duration of treatment. Nutrition support under NPY was increased from ₹500/month to ₹1,000/month per patient for the entire treatment duration — this revision took effect from 1 November 2024, so ₹1,000 is the current correct answer.

Energy Dense Nutritional Supplementation (EDNS) was introduced for all TB patients with BMI <18.5 at diagnosis, and Ni-kshay Mitra support under PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was extended to household contacts of TB patients

questions.subject: Community Medicine

Correct answer: C. ₹1 per pad

Scheme: Jan Aushadhi Suvidha sanitary napkins

Cost: ₹1 per pad

Objective: affordable menstrual hygiene

Implemented through: Jan Aushadhi Kendras

Focus: adolescent & reproductive-age women

Part of broader initiative: PMBJP (Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Vaccination against which of the following is recommended in the elderly? 1. Varicella zoster virus 2. COVID-19 3. Measles 4. Pneumococcal meningitis 5. HPV 6. Td
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2, 4, 6

Vaccines recommended in the elderly include:

• Varicella zoster vaccine – prevents herpes zoster (shingles) and post-herpetic neuralgia.
• COVID-19 vaccine – reduces risk of severe disease, hospitalization, and mortality.
• Pneumococcal vaccine – protects against pneumococcal pneumonia, bacteremia, and meningitis.
• Td / Tdap booster – protects against tetanus and diphtheria, given every 10 years.

Vaccines generally not routinely recommended in the elderly:

• Measles vaccine – usually unnecessary because most elderly individuals have natural immunity from prior infection.
• HPV vaccine – recommended mainly for adolescents and young adults, not older adults.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the aim of the following program?
options: To improve the cleanliness, hygiene of public health facilities
Provides health care to senior citizens
Plant more trees in government institutes

questions.text: What is the schedule for oral typhoid vaccine?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Day 1, 3, 5, 7

Oral live attenuated Ty21a vaccine — 4 capsules on alternate days (Day 1, 3, 5, 7), on empty stomach. Booster every 3 years if continued exposure.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What will be the 95% confidence interval (CI) for an estimated prevalence of 10% and a sample size of 100?
options: Given data inadequate for calculation of class intervals
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 4–16

For prevalence, CI ≈ p ± 2√(pq/n).

Here p = 10%, q = 90%, n = 100.

SE ≈ √(9/100) = 3%.

95% CI ≈ 10 ± 6 → 4% to 16%.

Hence, option B is correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which international initiative focuses on providing vaccines to children in developing countries to prevent diseases such as measles, polio, and tetanus?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. GAVI

• Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance is a global public–private partnership dedicated to improving access to immunization in low- and middle-income countries, targeting diseases like measles, polio, tetanus, hepatitis B, and others.
• World Bank Group focuses on development financing and policy support.
• Doctors Without Borders (MSF) provides emergency medical aid, not a global vaccine-financing initiative.
• Global Fund primarily addresses HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria, not routine childhood immunization.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following conditions would not be managed through mass drug administration?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Vitamin A deficiency

Mass drug administration (MDA) is used for worm infestation, scabies, and filariasis, where community-wide treatment interrupts transmission. Vitamin A deficiency is addressed through targeted supplementation, not MDA. Hence, vitamin A deficiency is not managed via MDA.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following conference-city pairs is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Geneva – Abortion ethics

Geneva is famous in this context for the Declaration of Geneva (adopted by the World Medical Association, 1948) — the physician's oath / modern reformulation of the Hippocratic Oath — and as the headquarters of the WHO. "Abortion ethics" is a fabricated pairing, so D is the odd one out → the correct answer.

| Pair | Match

| ---- | -----

| A. Alma-Ata – Primary Health Care | Alma-Ata Declaration, 1978 (WHO-UNICEF) → "Health for All by 2000," birth of the PHC concept

| B. Montreal – Ozone-depleting substances | Montreal Protocol, 1987 → phase-out of CFCs/ODS (ozone layer protection)

| C. Kyoto – Greenhouse gas emission reduction | Kyoto Protocol, 1997 → binding GHG emission cuts (under UNFCCC)

| D. Geneva – Abortion ethics | No such conference; Geneva = Declaration of Geneva (physician's oath) / WHO HQ

High-yield conference/declaration–place pairings (frequently tested as a set):

| Place | Landmark event | Year | Theme

| ----- | -------------- | ---- | -----

| Alma-Ata | Declaration of Alma-Ata | 1978 | Primary Health Care, "Health for All by 2000"

| Ottawa | Ottawa Charter | 1986 | Health Promotion (1st International Conference on Health Promotion)

| Montreal | Montreal Protocol | 1987 | Ozone-depleting substances (CFCs)

| Rio de Janeiro | Earth Summit (UNCED) | 1992 | Sustainable development, Agenda 21, CBD, UNFCCC

| Kyoto | Kyoto Protocol | 1997 | Greenhouse gas reduction (binding targets)

| Paris | Paris Agreement | 2015 | Climate — limit warming <2°C (ideally 1.5°C)

| Cairo | ICPD | 1994 | Reproductive health & rights, population

| Beijing | 4th World Conf. on Women | 1995 | Gender equality, women's rights

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the chlorine demand of water?
options: Chlorine which appears after the break point has been reached
Chlorine required to oxidize all organic matter and destroy the bacteria
Chlorine which prevents subsequent microbial contamination during storage
Chlorine amount that allows sustainable residual chlorine for 6 months
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Chlorine required to oxidize all organic matter and destroy the bacteria

Chlorine demand refers to the amount of chlorine required to oxidize all organic matter and destroy bacteria present in water before free residual chlorine appears. It does not refer to residual chlorine after breakpoint or taste/odor prevention. Understanding chlorine demand is essential for effective water disinfection.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following health interventions is included in SABLA?
options: Antenatal care and skilled birth attendance
Iron–folic acid (IFA) supplementation and health check-ups
Tuberculosis screening for all family members
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Iron–folic acid (IFA) supplementation and health check-ups

SABLA (Rajiv Gandhi Scheme for Empowerment of Adolescent Girls) is a Government of India program targeting girls aged 11–18 years. It aims to improve nutrition, health, education, life skills, and vocational training, and to reduce anemia and school dropouts.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following infections does maternal antibody transfer not provide effective immunity to the neonate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Polio

Maternal IgG antibodies are actively transferred across the placenta during the third trimester and provide passive protection against several toxin-mediated and viral infections, including tetanus, diphtheria, and measles during the first few months of life. However, maternal antibodies do not provide reliable protection against poliovirus infection, particularly at the intestinal mucosal level where poliovirus initially replicates. Consequently, newborns remain susceptible to poliovirus despite transplacental antibody transfer, which is why polio vaccination is started early in infancy according to the national immunization schedule.

• Passive maternal IgG protects: Tetanus, Diphtheria, Measles, Rubella
• Does not provide reliable protection: Polio (especially mucosal infection).
• IgG crosses the placenta; IgM does not.
• Maximum transplacental antibody transfer occurs during the third trimester, making preterm infants more susceptible to infections.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following interventions would be most effective in helping a country escape a demographic trap?
options: Increasing the availability of advanced medical care
Promoting the use of contraception and family planning
Improving economic opportunities in rural areas
Expanding immunization coverage for childhood diseases
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Promoting the use of contraception and family planning

• Demographic trap: Applies to a country whose population is growing rapidly due to a high birth rate and low death rate.
• To escape the demographic trap, countries need to lower fertility rates.
• Promoting family planning and contraception reduces birth rates, helping to stabilize population growth and reduce pressure on resources.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is a social institution?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Marriage

A social institution is an established, abstract pattern of norms and roles organized around a basic societal need — distinct from an association, which is a concrete organized group of people formed to pursue it.

| Option | What it actually is | Why it's a strong distractor

| ------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------

| A. A tertiary-care hospital | Association (a concrete organization) | Students are loosely taught "hospital = institution" → tempting

| B. A medical college | Association | Same trap as "school = institution"

| C. Marriage | Social institution (abstract normative pattern) | The correct answer — an established pattern of norms around a societal need

| D. The Indian Medical Association | Association (literally named one!) | Named "Association" — catches students who don't know the technical distinction

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of cyclopropagative biological transmission in vectors?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Plasmodia in Anopheles

Cyclopropagative transmission = organism undergoes both multiplication and morphological change in vector.

| Type | Example | Change in vector

| ---- | ------- | ----------------

| Propagative | Plague in rat flea, YF in Aedes | Multiplication only, no change in form

| Cyclodevelopmental | Microfilaria in Culex | Change in form only, no multiplication

| Cyclopropagative | Plasmodium in Anopheles | Both multiplication AND change in form

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is an inactivated vaccine?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Salk polio vaccine

• Salk polio vaccine (IPV) is a killed (inactivated) vaccine
• Contains inactivated poliovirus (types 1, 2, 3)
• Administered parenterally (IM/SC)
• Induces strong humoral immunity (IgG) → prevents paralytic disease

Why the others are incorrect

B. Ty21a typhoral vaccine

• Live attenuated oral vaccine (Salmonella typhi Ty21a strain)

C. HDC-Edmonston-Zagreb measles strain

• Live attenuated measles vaccine strain

D. BCG

Distributing sterile needles and syringes to IDUs
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Mandatory HIV testing

Targeted interventions include free condoms, STI screening and treatment, and harm-reduction strategies. Mandatory HIV testing is not part of NACO’s approach, as testing must be voluntary and consent-based. Hence, mandatory HIV testing is the incorrect statement.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is most accurately matched regarding a biomedical waste (BMW) treatment method and the mechanism involved?
options: Plasma pyrolysis — Molecular dissociation via ionized gas
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Plasma pyrolysis — Molecular dissociation via ionized gas

• Gamma irradiation: Uses ionizing radiation, not moist heat.
• Hydroclave: Works on moist heat (steam) under pressure with agitation, not dry heat.
• Incineration: Used for combustion and volume reduction of waste, not for sterilizing glassware.
• Plasma pyrolysis: Uses high-energy ionized gas (plasma) causing molecular dissociation of waste into simpler, non-toxic components

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a measure of validity?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Positive predictive value

Validity refers to how well a test identifies the true disease status.

Measures of validity:

• Sensitivity ✅ → Ability to correctly identify diseased individuals
• Specificity ✅ → Ability to correctly identify non-diseased individuals
• Accuracy ✅ → Overall correctness of the test

Why PPV is NOT a measure of validity:

• Positive Predictive Value (PPV) depends on disease prevalence
• It reflects test performance in a population, not intrinsic test validity

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a recognized approach to health education?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Socio-environmental approach

The four recognized approaches to health education are:

• Regulatory approach
• Service approach
• Health education (educational) approach
• Primary health care approach

Socio-environmental approach is not one of the standard approaches described in Park's PSM.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not used to express the strength of sewage?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. E. Coli Count

Strength of sewage refers to the concentration of organic and inorganic matter present in sewage—i.e., its pollution load.

Parameters used to express sewage strength:

• Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD)

→ Measures biodegradable organic matter
• Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD)

→ Measures total oxidizable matter (biodegradable + non-biodegradable)
• Suspended solids / suspended particles

→ Indicates physical pollution load

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is true about the steps of acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) surveillance?
options: Fecal samples should arrive at the lab within 48 hours of collection
All children with AFP should be tested within 72 hours of onset
Detect atleast 1 case of AFP/100000 children under 15 years
Fecal specimens should be transported at -2°C
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Detect atleast 1 case of AFP/100000 children under 15 years

Why C is correct

• AFP surveillance (part of polio eradication programs) uses sensitivity indicators.
• The key benchmark is ≥1 non-polio AFP case per 100,000 children <15 years.
• This ensures the system is sensitive enough to detect potential poliovirus circulation.

Why the other options are incorrect

A. Fecal samples should arrive at the lab within 48 hours of collection

• Correct standard: within 72 hours of collection (maintaining reverse cold chain).

B. All children with AFP should be tested within 72 hours of onset

• Incorrect framing.
• What is required: two stool samples collected within 14 days of onset, 24 hours apart—not “testing within 72 hours.”

D. Fecal specimens should be transported at -2°C

• Incorrect temperature.
• Correct: 2–8°C (reverse cold chain)
• Freezing (-20°C) may be used later in labs, but not during routine transport.

High-yield AFP surveillance checklist (exam-ready)

• Case definition: Any child <15 years with acute flaccid paralysis
• Stool samples: 2 samples, 24 hrs apart, within 14 days of onset
• Transport: Reverse cold chain (2–8°C), reach lab within 72 hrs
• Indicator: ≥1 non-polio AFP / 100,000 (<15 yrs)
• Follow-up: 60-day residual paralysis assessment

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describe the operation and management of Mobile Medical Units (MMUs)? 1. MMUs are run by the government 2. MMUs are run by external agencies with medical supplies given by the government. 3. MMUs are run by the government and medical supplies are also given by the government. 4. MMUs are run by external agencies and medical supplies are also given by the external agency.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2 and 3

MMUs under NHM may function through:

• Government model
• Outsourcing/PPP model
• Hybrid operational systems

But:

• Drug logistics and essential supplies are generally under government oversight.

Hence, statement 4 is typically excluded.

| Statement | Correct? | Explanation

| --------- | -------- | -----------

| 1. MMUs are run by the government | ✅ | In some states/districts, MMUs are directly operated by the government health department.

| 2. MMUs are run by external agencies with medical supplies given by the government | ✅ | This is the most common Public–Private Partnership (PPP) model under NHM.

| 4. MMUs are run by external agencies and medical supplies are also given by the external agency | ❌ | Usually incorrect in NHM framework, because essential drugs and supplies are generally provided through government procurement systems even if operations are outsourced.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding evaluation?
options: It focuses on how well it happened
All of the above are correct
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. It focuses on how well it happened

Evaluation is a systematic, periodic assessment of a program to determine how well it worked and whether objectives were achieved.

• Evaluation examines:

• Effectiveness
• Efficiency
• Outcomes and impact

• In short: “How well did it happen?”

Monitoring = continuous, process-oriented

Evaluation = periodic, outcome-oriented

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding random errors in epidemiological studies?
options: Sampling errors are examples of random errors
Random errors can cause bias in a study
Random errors cannot be completely eliminated
Systematic errors are different from random errors
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Random errors can cause bias in a study

Random error refers to chance variation in measurements or sampling. It affects precision, not validity.

• Bias = systematic error, not random error
• Random error causes imprecision (results fluctuate around the true value)
• It does not consistently push results in one direction, so it does not cause bias

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB)?
options: It is a priority-based budgeting system
It proceeds from resources to targets
It does not depend on data from the previous budget
Every line item of the budget must be justified and approved
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. It proceeds from resources to targets

Distractor-by-distractor analysis:

• A. It is a priority-based budgeting system: True. ZBB is inherently a priority-based system. Managers prepare "decision packages" for every activity, which are then ranked in order of priority, and resources are allocated down that ranking until funds are exhausted.
• B. It proceeds from resources to targets: False. ZBB proceeds from targets to resources, not the other way around. You first define objectives/activities, justify them from a zero base, and then work out what resources they require. Proceeding from resources to targets — letting the existing resource envelope dictate what gets done — is the hallmark of conventional/incremental budgeting.
• C. It does not depend on data from the previous budget: True. The defining feature of ZBB: each budgeting cycle starts from a "zero base" with no reference to the previous year's allocations. Last year's budget carries no automatic legitimacy.
• D. Every line item of the budget must be justified and approved: True. Every line item and every activity must be justified afresh and approved on its own merits — nothing is carried forward by default.

High-yield contrast table:

| Feature | Incremental (traditional) budgeting | Zero-Based Budgeting

| ------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------------

| Starting point | Previous year's budget ± increment | Zero base every cycle

| Direction | Resources → targets | Targets → resources

| Justification | Only the increment is justified | Every item justified

| Basis of allocation | Historical precedent | Priority-ranked decision packages

| Effort/cost | Low | High (time- and paper-intensive)

Exam pearl: ZBB was popularized by Peter Pyhrr (Texas Instruments, 1970s) and is asked in PSM under health planning and management. The "targets → resources" direction is the classic trap — it mirrors the planning cycle itself, where objectives are set first and resources mobilized to meet them.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements is true about hospice care? A. Disease is the centre of concern B. The patient is sovereign C. Death should neither be prolonged nor hastened D. The aim is to improve the quality of life E. The intention is to cure F. Done when expected survival is <6months
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. B, C, D, F

Hospice care emphasizes patient autonomy, aims to neither hasten nor prolong death, focuses on quality of life, and is usually provided when life expectancy is <6 months. It is not disease-centered and does not aim to cure. Hence, statements B, C, D, and F are correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding a systematic review is most appropriate?
options: It includes only randomized controlled trials
Literature search is selective and narrative
It follows a predefined protocol with explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria
Statistical pooling of results is mandatory
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. It follows a predefined protocol with explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria

A systematic review is a structured, scientific approach to summarizing evidence.

• Predefined protocol (decided before starting the review)
• Explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria
• Comprehensive, reproducible literature search
• Critical appraisal of included studies

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding BCG vaccination is true?
options: Distilled water is used as a diluent
Injection site should be cleaned with spirit before administration
Mantoux test becomes positive within 1 week of vaccination
BCG is derived from an attenuated strain of Mycobacterium bovis
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. BCG is derived from an attenuated strain of Mycobacterium bovis

• BCG is a live attenuated vaccine derived from M. bovis; saline is used as diluent, spirit is avoided, and Mantoux becomes positive after \~6–8 weeks.
• BCG (Bacillus Calmette–Guérin) vaccine is prepared from a live attenuated strain of Mycobacterium bovis, developed by Calmette and Guérin.

A. Distilled water is used as a diluent
