→ BCG is reconstituted with normal saline supplied by the manufacturer, not distilled water

B. Injection site should be cleaned with spirit before administration

→ Spirit/alcohol should NOT be used, as it can inactivate the live vaccine.

C. Mantoux test becomes positive within 1 week

→ Mantoux usually becomes positive after 4–6 weeks post-BCG vaccination.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding district and sub-district hospitals in India is correct?
options: Sub-district hospitals are mandatory administrative units in every district
The recommended bed strength of a sub-district hospital is at least 100 beds
District hospitals function only as referral centers and do not provide secondary care
Postgraduate training such as DNB is not permitted in district hospitals
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. The recommended bed strength of a sub-district hospital is at least 100 beds

Sub-district hospitals (SDHs) are secondary-level facilities under the public health system. They are not mandatory administrative units but are recommended to have a minimum bed strength of 100 beds. District hospitals provide both secondary and referral care and can conduct postgraduate training such as DNB. Hence, option B is correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding NITI Aayog is correct?
options: It is a constitutional body created by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment
It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015 to serve as the Government of India’s policy think tank
It has statutory authority to allocate funds to States
It directly implements centrally sponsored health programmes
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015 to serve as the Government of India’s policy think tank

NITI Aayog was established in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission, and functions as the policy think tank of the Government of India. It is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body and does not allocate funds or directly implement health programs. Its role is advisory, focusing on cooperative federalism, policy formulation, and long-term strategic planning rather than execution.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the Employees’ State Insurance Act are correct? A. The ESI Act was enacted in 1948 as a social security legislation for workers B. Medical benefit under ESI is available only after completion of a minimum contribution period C. Employment injury benefit can be provided from the very first day of entering insurable employment D. The wage ceiling for ESI eligibility is revised periodically by the government E. ESI is administered by Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) F. Dependents’ benefit may be provided in case of death due to employment injury
options: A, C, D, and F only
A, B, C, and E only
B, D, E, and F only
A, C, E, and F only
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. A, C, D, and F only

Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Act — High-Yield Facts

• Enacted: 1948
• Nature: Social security and health insurance legislation for workers
• Administered by: Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), under Ministry of Labour & Employment

Benefits under ESIC

• Sickness benefit
• Maternity benefit
• Temporary/permanent disablement benefit
• Dependents’ benefit
• Medical benefit
• Funeral expenses

Important Concepts

• Employment injury benefits are available from day 1 of insurable employment.
• Wage ceiling for eligibility is revised periodically by the government.
• ESIC ≠ EPFO:

• ESIC → health insurance/social security
• EPFO → provident fund and pension-related schemes

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding VED analysis is correct?
options: Drugs are classified according to annual expenditure.
Drugs are classified according to clinical importance.
Drugs are classified according to frequency of use.
Drugs are classified according to expiry date.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Drugs are classified according to clinical importance.

VED classification:

• V – Vital: Stock-out cannot be tolerated.
• E – Essential: Temporary shortage can be managed.
• D – Desirable: Shortage causes minimal impact.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following vaccines is administered intradermally in the right upper arm during infancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. fIPV 1

| Vaccine | Route | Site

| ------- | ----- | ----

| BCG | Intradermal | Left upper arm

| fIPV-1 | Intradermal | Right upper arm

| fIPV-3 | Intradermal | Left upper arm

| JE (live) | Subcutaneous | Left upper arm

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following water-associated diseases is wrongly matched?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Water-washed disease - Dracunculiasis

Dracunculiasis is a water-based disease, transmitted by ingestion of Cyclops, not a water-washed disease. Water-washed diseases result from poor hygiene and lack of water (e.g., scabies, trachoma). Therefore, the pairing of water-washed disease – Dracunculiasis is incorrect.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the provided options align with the depicted equivalence margin graph? 1. ‘A’ represents superiority of new treatment 2. ‘I’ represents Inferiority of new treatment 3. ‘E’ represents Non-inferior treatment 4. ‘C’ is inconclusive
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2 and 3

In equivalence and non-inferiority trials, zones represent superiority, inferiority, non-inferiority, and inconclusive results. In the depicted graph, A = superiority, I = inferiority, and E = non-inferiority are correctly labeled. Thus, statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct.

| Conclusion | Image interpretation (95% CI position)

| ---------- | --------------------------------------

| Superior | Does not touch either null value (0) or delta margin (Δ)

| Non-inferior | Touch null value (0), not delta

1. 95% CI lies between null value and delta margin

| Inconclusive | Touches delta margin (Δ)

| Inferior | Lies beyond the delta margin (Δ)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Who is credited with coining the term "Social Medicine"?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Jules Guérin

Jules Guérin, a French orthopaedist, coined the term "Social Medicine" in the mid-19th century while serving as editor of the Gazette Médicale de Paris.

| Options | | Description

| ------- | --- | -----------

| A. John Ryle | British physician | Left clinical medicine to become the first Professor of Social Medicine (Oxford, 1943); championed social medicine in Britain — but a 20th-century populariser/institution-builder, not the coiner of the term

| B. Jules Guérin | French physician | Coined "social medicine" (1848) in the Gazette Médicale de Paris → correct

| C. Alfred Grotjahn | German physician | Developed "social pathology" (Soziale Pathologie, 1912) — systematized the study of social factors in disease, but that's a later, distinct contribution, not the origin of the term

| D. Francis A. E. Crew | British (Edinburgh) | Associated with academic social medicine in Britain (Edinburgh, mid-20th C.) — again a later institutional figure, not the coiner

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Who performs syndromic surveillance in IDSP?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Health Workers

IDSP has 3-tier surveillance:

• S (Syndromic) by health workers at peripheral level using symptom clusters
• P (Probable) by medical officers using history + clinical exam
• L (Laboratory) confirmed by labs.

Health workers have no diagnostic authority, hence only syndrome-based reporting.

| Type | Done by | Basis

| ---- | ------- | -----

| Syndromic (S) | Health workers | Syndromes & field surveys

| Probable (P) | Medical officers | History + clinical exam

| Laboratory (L) | Laboratories | Lab results

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Within 24 hours of a college annual function, more than 120 students develop vomiting, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea. The health team interviews all attendees regarding the foods they consumed during the event and compares the attack rates among those who ate each food item with those who did not. Which epidemiological study design is being used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Retrospective cohort study

Concept: In a point-source outbreak where the exposed population is known, a retrospective cohort study is preferred.

A retrospective cohort study is ideal because:

• The exposed population (all attendees) is known.
• Exposure occurred in the past.
• Investigators compare disease occurrence between exposed and unexposed groups.

The attack rate is calculated for each food item, and the food with the highest attack rate ratio is likely responsible.

Other options:

• A. Case-control: Used when the exposed population is not well defined or the disease is rare.
• B. Cross-sectional: Measures prevalence at a single point in time.
• D. Ecological: Compares populations, not individuals.

NEET PG Pearl: Point-source outbreak + defined exposed population = Retrospective cohort study.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The table below shows the results of ELISA test for HIV infection. Consider the following statements: 1. The sensitivity is 98%. 2. The specificity is 99%. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Both 1 and 2

Sensitivity and specificity are measures of the validity of a diagnostic test.

• Sensitivity = Ability of a test to correctly identify diseased individuals (true positives).
• Specificity = Ability of a test to correctly identify non-diseased individuals (true negatives).

From the table:

• True Positive (TP) = 4900
• False Negative (FN) = 100
• True Negative (TN) = 94,050
• False Positive (FP) = 950

Sensitivity = TP / (TP + FN) × 100

= 4900 / (4900 + 100) × 100

= 4900 / 5000 × 100 = 98% ✓

Specificity = TN / (TN + FP) × 100

= 94,050 / (94,050 + 950) × 100

= 94,050 / 95,000 × 100 = 99% ✓

Hence, both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 28-year-old woman presented to your hospital emergency with pregnancy 22 weeks, which was a result of rape. Correct statement regarding Medical Termination of Pregnancy is?
options: MTP can be done routinely after 24 weeks POG
MTP is permissible for 20-24 weeks POG in this case
MTP is permissible for 20-24 weeks POG in this case only if it threatens the life of the mother
MTP is permissible for 20-24 weeks POG in this case with 1 Doctor’s opinion only
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. MTP is permissible for 20-24 weeks POG in this case

As per the amended MTP Act (2021), termination of pregnancy is permissible between 20–24 weeks for specified categories of women, which explicitly includes survivors of rape.

In this gestational age group, opinion of two registered medical practitioners is required, and threat to the mother’s life is not mandatory for eligibility.

Termination beyond 24 weeks requires Medical Board approval and is restricted to cases of substantial fetal abnormalities.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 29-year-old woman had an IUD inserted at a PHC. After a few months, she conceives. On examination, the IUD is still in place with threads visualised. She wants to continue with her pregnancy. Next best step of management is?
options: Remove IUD gently, then do MTP
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Remove IUD gently

If pregnancy occurs with an IUD in situ and the woman wishes to continue the pregnancy, the IUD should be gently removed, provided the strings are visible.

Early removal reduces the risk of spontaneous abortion, septic abortion, preterm labor, and chorioamnionitis.

Leaving the IUD in situ significantly increases obstetric complications, while MTP is not indicated since the patient desires continuation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 32-year-old woman with no significant medical history, who has been using depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) for contraception, presents to the clinic after missing her scheduled injection by 14 days. She denies any sexual activity since her last injection. Her last menstrual period was 10 weeks ago, and she has no signs of pregnancy. What is the most appropriate recommendation for this patient regarding contraception?
options: Give DMPA with 7 days of barrier
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Give DMPA

Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (DMPA) is a progestin-only injectable contraceptive that provides long-acting reversible contraception.

The drug is Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate. It works mainly by:

• Suppressing ovulation
• Thickening cervical mucus
• Thinning the endometrium

Protection lasts for approximately 3 months (12–13 weeks).

DMPA Schedule

However, there is an acceptable grace period.

For DMPA (3-monthly injectable), a grace period of up to 4 weeks late beyond the scheduled date and 2 weeks early is allowed, hence it can be injected immediately. But if it is beyond the date, UPT can be done.

In this question:

• Patient is 14 days late
• This falls within the 2-week grace period

Thus, contraceptive protection is still adequate.

A. Urine pregnancy test before DMPA- Pregnancy testing is needed only when:

• Injection is >2 weeks late, or
• There is possibility of pregnancy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 4-year-old girl is rescued from a building collapse after an earthquake. She presents with severe swelling of the foot and a painful laceration. According to disaster triage protocol, which color category should be assigned to her?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Yellow

In mass-casualty disaster triage, patients are categorized by urgency using a color-coded system:

| Color | Category | Meaning | Examples

| ----- | -------- | ------- | --------

| Red | Immediate | Life-threatening injuries requiring urgent intervention | Airway obstruction, severe hemorrhage, shock

| Yellow | Delayed | Serious injuries but not immediately life-threatening | Fractures, large wounds, significant soft-tissue injury

| Green | Minor | Walking wounded, minor injuries | Small cuts, abrasions

| Black | Expectant/Dead | Dead or injuries incompatible with survival | No breathing after airway repositioning

Application to the Case

• 4-year-old child rescued after building collapse
• Severe swelling of the foot + painful laceration
• No information suggesting:

o    airway compromise

o    severe bleeding

o    shock

o    altered consciousness

These injuries are significant but not immediately life-threatening, meaning treatment can be safely delayed while higher-priority victims are managed first.

Therefore → Yellow category (Delayed).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A town has 100 live births, 200 deaths, and a mid-year population of 20,000. What is the crude birth rate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 5

Crude Birth Rate (CBR) = (Number of live births / Mid-year population) × 1000

= (100 / 20,000) × 1000

= 5 per 1,000 population

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A woman has been using combined oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for contraception. The use of combined OCPs is associated with a reduced risk of several cancers. Which of the following cancers does not have a reduced risk with OCP use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cervical cancer

Use of combined oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) is associated with a reduced risk of ovarian, endometrial, and colorectal cancers due to suppression of ovulation and endometrial proliferation.

In contrast, long-term OCP use is associated with an increased risk of cervical cancer, not a protective effect.

Hence, cervical cancer does not show reduced risk with OCP use.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, the opinion of two registered medical practitioners is required for termination of pregnancy at how many weeks of gestation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 20-24

As per the amended MTP Act (2021), termination up to 20 weeks requires the opinion of one registered medical practitioner.

For pregnancies between 20–24 weeks, the opinion of two registered medical practitioners is mandatory for specified categories of women.

| Gestational age | Whose opinion is needed | Conditions

| --------------- | ----------------------- | ----------

| Up to 20 weeks | ONE RMP | Any of the standard MTP indications

| 20–24 weeks | TWO RMPs ✅ | Only for 7 prescribed categories of women (Rule 3B, MTP Rules 2021)

1. Survivors of sexual assault, rape, or incest
2. Minors
3. Change of marital status during ongoing pregnancy (widowhood or divorce)
4. Women with physical disabilities (major disability as per RPwD Act, 2016)
5. Mentally ill women, including intellectual disability
6. Foetal malformation with substantial risk of being incompatible with life, or serious handicap if born/ SIgnificant threat to maternal health
7. Pregnancy in humanitarian settings / disaster / emergency, as declared by Government

| Beyond 24 weeks | State-level Medical Board

• Gynaecologist
• Paediatrician
• Radiologist or Sonologist

| Only for substantial foetal abnormalities/Maternal threat

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to the RCH (Reproductive and Child Health) program guidelines, when should CuT 380A ideally be inserted to ensure maximum compliance? 1. Within 48 hours of delivery 2. Immediate post-partum 3. Within first 5-7 days of menstrual cycle 4. Within 7 days of next menstrual cycle
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2, 3

CuT-380A is a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) widely promoted under India’s Reproductive and Child Health Programme and National Health Mission. It is a copper intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) effective for up to 10 years. IUCD is part of spacing methods in family planning.

As per RCH guidelines, CuT 380A insertion is ideal immediate post-partum, within 48 hours of delivery (PPIUCD), and within 5–7 days of the menstrual cycle, as these timings ensure high acceptance, convenience, and compliance.

Insertion within 7 days of the next menstrual cycle is not an ideal recommended window.

Advantages of CuT-380A are that it is long lasting, reversible, hormone free and cost effective.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following correctly represent the basic criteria for identifying “at risk” infants, except:
options: Failure to gain weight during three successive months
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Birth order 3 and above

The basic criteria used to identify “at-risk” infants include:

• Twins or multiple births → At risk because of increased risk of prematurity and low birth weight.
• Failure to gain weight for three successive months → Indicates possible nutritional or underlying health problems.
• Artificial feeding → Increases the risk of infections and nutritional problems compared with appropriate breastfeeding.
• Birth order ≥3 is not a standard criterion for identifying an individual infant as “at risk.”

Therefore, the exception is A. Birth order 3 and above.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Arrange the steps of the Demographic cycle in the correct chronological sequence: 1. Low stationary 2. High stationary 3. Declining 4. Early expanding 5. Late expanding
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 2, 4, 5, 1, 3

The demographic cycle describes population change over time as a country develops.

It begins with the high stationary stage (high birth and death rates), followed by early expanding (death rate falls), then late expanding (birth rate begins to fall).

This is followed by the low stationary stage (both rates low), and finally the declining stage (birth rate falls below death rate).

Thus, the correct chronological sequence is 2 → 4 → 5 → 1 → 3.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As per the United Nations definition of a vital events registration system, vital events include which of the following? 1. Foetal deaths 2. School admissions 3. Legal separations 4. College graduations Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1 and 3

A Vital Registration System (Civil Registration System) is defined by the United Nations as the continuous, permanent, compulsory, and universal recording of vital events occurring in a population. It provides the legal basis for vital statistics and demographic planning.

• 1. Foetal deaths ✓

• Fetal deaths (stillbirths) are recognized vital events and are included in the civil registration system.

• 2. School admissions ✗

• School admissions are administrative events, not vital events.

• 3. Legal separations ✓

• Legal separation is a vital event recognized by the UN because it affects civil status.

• 4. College graduations ✗

• Educational achievements are not vital events.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Frontline health workers are employed to record the births and deaths in countries which have made slow progress in the development of a comprehensive vital registration system. This approach is known as:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Lay reporting

Lay reporting is a method of collecting birth and death data in areas where a complete Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) system is not yet fully developed. In this approach, frontline health workers, teachers, village volunteers, or other community-based workers record vital events and report them to the health system.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Registration of vital events: Refers to the official, continuous, compulsory, and permanent registration of births, deaths, marriages, etc., under the Civil Registration System (CRS).
• C. Sample Registration System (SRS) ✗

• India’s Sample Registration System is a dual-record system involving:

• Continuous enumeration by a resident part-time enumerator.
• Independent six-monthly survey by a supervisor.

• It is not based solely on frontline health workers.

• D. Census: Census is conducted once every 10 years and provides demographic information but does not continuously record births and deaths.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: HDI is calculated by using: 1. Life expectancy at birth 2. Mean years of schooling 3. GNI (Gross National Income) per capita
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. All three

The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite measure based on three dimensions: health, education, and standard of living.

| Dimension | Indicator(s) | Index

| --------- | ------------ | -----

| Health / Long & healthy life | Life expectancy at birth | Life Expectancy Index

| Knowledge / Education | Mean years of schooling (adults ≥25 y) + Expected years of schooling (children of school-entering age) | Education Index (arithmetic mean of the two sub-indices)

| Standard of living | GNI per capita (PPP $, log-transformed) | Income Index

HDI = geometric mean of the three dimension indices — ∛(Health × Education × Income).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a community, there were 550 births in a year out of which 50 were stillbirths. There were 09 deaths among newborns during 0-7 days of life. An additional 41 deaths occurred during 8-28 days of life. Calculate the Early Neonatal Mortality rate for the given community.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 18

Early Neonatal Mortality Rate (ENMR) is defined as the number of deaths during 0–7 days of life per 1,000 live births.

In this question:

• Early neonatal deaths = 9
• Late neonatal deaths = 41

Live births = Total births − Stillbirths = 550 − 50 = 500.

Early neonatal deaths = 9.

ENMR = (9 ÷ 500) × 1,000 = 18 per 1,000 live births.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a contraceptive efficacy study, 500 women used a particular contraceptive method continuously for 6 months each, during which 4 unintended pregnancies were reported. Calculate the Pearl Index for this contraceptive method.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1.6

Pearl Index measures contraceptive failure rate and is expressed per 100 woman-years.

Calculation:

• Accidental pregnancies = 4
• Total months of exposure = 500 women × 6 months = 3000 months
• Multiplier = 1200 (constant; converts to per 100 woman-years)

Pearl Index = 1.6 pregnancies per 100 woman-years.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a given population of a town, 6000 were below the age of 15 years. At the same time, there were 2000 above the age of 65 years. A total of 20000 members were there in the town. Calculate the dependency ratio?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 0.66

Dependency ratio = (Population below 15 years + Population above 65 years) ÷ Working (earning) population.

Dependent population = 6000 + 2000 = 8000.

Working population = 12000.

Dependency ratio = 8000 ÷ 12000 = 0.66

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a town with one lakh population (1,00,000) there are a total of 2500 live births in a year. There were 75 total deaths of children before the age of one month, total 200 deaths before the age of one year, and a total 300 deaths before the age of three years. Which of the following statements regarding Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) of the town for the given year are correct? 1. The denominator is 1,00,000. 2. The IMR of the town is higher than the current national average of IMR for India. 3. The numerator is the number of children dying before the age of one month. 4. The IMR of the town is 80 per 1000 live births. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2 and 4 only

Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is defined as: Number of deaths of infants (<1 year of age) during a year ÷ Number of live births during the same year × 1000

Calculation:

• Infant deaths (<1 year) = 200
• Live births = 2500

IMR = (200 ÷ 2500) × 1000 = 80 per 1000 live births

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. The denominator is 1\,00\,000❌: Incorrect. The denominator is 2500 live births, not the total population.
• 2. The IMR of the town is higher than the current national average of IMR for India✔️: Correct. 80/1000 is much higher than the current national average.
• 3. The numerator is the number of children dying before the age of one month❌: Incorrect. The numerator is deaths before 1 year of age (200).
• 4. The IMR of the town is 80 per 1000 live births:✔️: Correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In Demographic cycle, B curve represents:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Death rate

In the Demographic Cycle, the B-curve represents the death rate, while the A-curve represents the birth rate.

The fall in the death rate occurs earlier due to improvements in sanitation, nutrition, and medical care, preceding changes in birth rate.

The gap between the birth and death rate curves determines the population growth rate at different stages of the cycle.

India's Demographic Stage

India is currently in the late expanding stage of the demographic cycle.

Characteristics include:

• Declining birth rate
• Low death rate
• Continued population growth

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In family life cycle terminology, the phase that lasts from the birth of the last child until the first child leaves home is referred to as which stage?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Complete extension

Phases of Family Life Cycle

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the Census of India, the ‘de facto’ system is used for data collection. This implies that the data are collected for which of the following groups?
options: Individual's location during the enumeration period
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Individual's location during the enumeration period

Census enumeration can be conducted using two major systems:

1️⃣ De facto method

2️⃣ De jure method

In the de facto census system, individuals are counted where they are physically present at the time of enumeration, regardless of their usual place of residence.

India follows the de facto method to capture the actual population distribution on the census date. Census System in India

Historically, India primarily used the de facto approach, though modern census operations incorporate elements of de jure enumeration through household schedules.

The census in India is conducted every 10 years under the Census Act 1948.

In contrast, the de jure system counts individuals at their usual place of residence, highlighting the conceptual difference between the two approaches.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the Maha Kumbh mela, what was the primary purpose of Mobile medical vans having multiple surveillance units for fever, diarrhoea and respiratory illnesses?
options: To reduce number of health workers and professionals
For immediate quarantine measures of symptomatic individuals
To diagnose with lab tests and give potential warning for early outbreaks of fever, diarrhoea, respiratory infections
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. To diagnose with lab tests and give potential warning for early outbreaks of fever, diarrhoea, respiratory infections

During mass gatherings like the Maha Kumbh Mela, mobile medical vans with surveillance units function as early warning systems. Such mass gatherings create a high risk for communicable disease outbreaks due to overcrowding, poor sanitation, shared water sources, high person-to-person contact & rapid movement of people.

They enable rapid diagnosis, syndromic surveillance, and real-time data collection for fever, diarrhoeal, and respiratory illnesses, allowing early detection of outbreaks and timely public health response. In India, surveillance is mainly conducted under the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the most widespread calculation of Stillbirth Rate, the numerator is defined as foetal deaths weighing over ‘X’ gram at birth, during the year. Which one of the following is the correct value for ‘X’?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1000

The Stillbirth Rate (SBR) is an important indicator of maternal and perinatal health. In the traditional and most widely used definition (Park’s PSM), a stillbirth is defined as the birth of a dead fetus weighing 1000 g or more (or after 28 weeks of gestation) during a given year.

Stillbirth Rate = (Number of stillbirths ≥1000 g ÷ Total births [Live births + Stillbirths]) × 1000

Hence, the correct value of ‘X’ is 1000 g.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Maternal deaths per 1,00,000 women in the reproductive age group is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Maternal mortality rate

Maternal Mortality Rate (MMRate) is defined as the number of maternal deaths per 1,00,000 women of reproductive age (15–49 years) in a given time period.

It reflects the risk of maternal death among women in the reproductive age group, irrespective of pregnancy frequency.

In contrast, Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) uses live births as the denominator, not women of reproductive age.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Maternal infection that may lead to teratogenic effect is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. All of the above

Several maternal viral infections can cross the placenta and cause teratogenic effects in the fetus. These infections are often grouped under the TORCH complex.

Rubella leads to congenital rubella syndrome, CMV causes microcephaly and sensorineural hearing loss, and varicella (chicken pox) can result in congenital varicella syndrome.

Hence, all listed infections are associated with fetal malformations, especially when infection occurs in early pregnancy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: PQLI indicators include: 1. Literacy rate 2. Infant mortality rate 3. Life expectancy at birth 4. Income per capita
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Only two of these

The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is a composite index that assesses social and health outcomes, independent of economic indicators.

It includes infant mortality rate, life expectancy at one year, and basic literacy, each scaled from 0 to 100, which is why only two of the listed indicators (infant mortality rate and literacy are counted here.

| Human Development Index (HDI)-UNDP
India: 0.68 (Rank-130) | Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI)-WHO | The Global Hunger Index
(GHI)
India: 25.8 (Serious hunger)

| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------

| Knowledge: (Mean & expected years of schooling) | Literacy rate | Proportion of the population that is undernourished

| Income: real GNI per capita | Infant Mortality Rate | Prevalence of underweight in children under five (in %)

| Life expectancy at birth (20-85) | Life expectancy at one year | Proportion of children dying before the age of five (in %)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Preferable time for IUCD insertion in a 28-year-old woman who has just delivered a healthy newborn is?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Up to 48 hours

After a normal vaginal delivery, an IUCD can be ideally inserted in the postpartum period within 48 hours, known as postpartum IUCD insertion.

During this time, the cervix remains dilated, facilitating insertion and improving acceptability.

Insertion after 48 hours but before 6 weeks is generally avoided due to a higher risk of infection and expulsion.

If IUCD is not inserted within 48 hours, it should be delayed until after 6 weeks due to increased infection risk.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The life expectancy at birth for a country A is 64 years. The minimum and maximum values of life expectancy are 20 years and 86 years respectively. As part of Human Development Index (HDI), what is the Life Expectancy Index for the country A?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 0.667

The Human Development Index (HDI) is published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and measures a country’s development based on health, education, and standard of living.

The Life Expectancy Index (LEI) is calculated using the formula:

Life Expectancy Index = (Actual life expectancy − Minimum value) / (Maximum value − Minimum value)

• Life expectancy at birth = 64 years
• Minimum value = 20 years
• Maximum value = 86 years

LEI = (64 − 20) / (86 − 20) = 44 / 66 = 0.667

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: There were 4000 live births in a community in a year. Do MMR Calculation if you come to know that 6 women died during pregnancy, labor/delivery, or within 42 days of delivery - 2 due to Obstructed labor, 1 due to Sepsis, 1 due to PPH, 1 due to Snake bite and 1 due to electrocution.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 100

Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) includes only maternal deaths due to obstetric causes occurring during pregnancy, delivery, or within 42 days of termination.

Maternal deaths here are due to obstructed labor (2), sepsis (1), and PPH (1) = 4 maternal deaths; deaths due to snake bite and electrocution are accidental and excluded.

MMR = (4 ÷ 4000) × 1,00,000 = 100 per 1,00,000 live births.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under MTP Act of India, for cases of MTP after 24 weeks POG, there has to be a Medical board to advise. It comprises of all except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Legal advisor

Under the amended MTP Act (2021), termination beyond 24 weeks is permitted only after approval by a Medical Board.

The Board includes a gynecologist, pediatrician, radiologist/sonologist, and other specialists as required to assess fetal abnormalities.

A legal advisor is not a mandated member of the Medical Board, as the decision is based on medical and fetal criteria, not legal adjudication.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act in India, what is the minimum age at which a woman can undergo MTP?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 16 years

Under the MTP Act, India, a woman aged 18 years or above can give valid consent for medical termination of pregnancy on her own.

For women below 18 years, guardian consent is mandatory.

Min age for MTP: There is no min age of MTP as long as consent is obtained from legal guardian in females below 18 years.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under which of the following data sets can information be found on monitoring fertility, family planning, maternal and child health, nutrition, and infectious diseases?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. National family health survey

The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) provides comprehensive data on fertility, family planning, maternal and child health, nutrition, and infectious diseases in India.

It is a large-scale, periodic household survey that supports policy formulation, program monitoring, and evaluation.

In contrast, the Census focuses on population counts, SRS on fertility and mortality rates, and CRS on registration of births and deaths, not detailed health indicators.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is Demographic gap?
options: Crude birth rate – Crude death rate
Crude birth rate + Crude death rate
Crude birth rate / Crude death rate
Crude birth rate × Crude death rate
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Crude birth rate – Crude death rate

The demographic gap is defined as the difference between the crude birth rate (CBR) and crude death rate (CDR).

It represents the rate of natural population increase in a community.

A wider gap indicates rapid population growth, commonly seen in the early and middle stages of the demographic transition.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is demographic transition as a country passes through the demographic cycle?
options: Transition from infectious pandemic diseases to man-made diseases
Transition from low literacy levels to high literacy levels
Transition from high birth rate & death rate to low birth rate & death rate
Transition from unfavorable sex ratio to favorable sex ratio
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Transition from high birth rate & death rate to low birth rate & death rate

Demographic transition refers to the long-term shift in population patterns as a country develops.

It is characterized by a transition from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates, driven by improvements in healthcare, sanitation, nutrition, and socioeconomic conditions.

This transition explains changes in population growth trends observed across the stages of the demographic cycle.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is Net Reproduction Rate?
options: The average number of children who are going to be born to a newborn girl in her reproductive lifespan
The average number of surviving children who are going to be born to a newborn girl in her reproductive lifespan
The average number of daughters who are going to be born to a newborn girl in her reproductive lifespan
The average number of surviving daughters who are going to be born to a newborn girl in her reproductive lifespan
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. The average number of surviving daughters who are going to be born to a newborn girl in her reproductive lifespan

The Net Reproduction Rate (NRR) is the average number of surviving daughters that a newborn girl is expected to bear during her reproductive years, taking into account both fertility and female mortality. An NRR of 1 indicates replacement-level fertility, where one generation of women exactly replaces itself.

Why not the other options?

• A. Average number of children: Describes Total Fertility Rate (TFR), not NRR.
• B. Average number of surviving children: Includes both sexes; NRR considers only surviving daughters.
• C. Average number of daughters: Equivalent to the Gross Reproduction Rate (GRR), which does not account for female mortality.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the ideal time for insertion of post-placental IUD in contraception?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Within 10 minutes

The ideal time for insertion of a post-placental intrauterine device (PPIUD) is within 10 minutes of placental delivery. This timing ensures high fundal placement, minimal discomfort, and lower expulsion rates compared with later insertions.

Key points to remember:

• Post-placental PPIUD: Within 10 minutes of placental delivery → ideal
• Immediate postpartum: Up to 48 hours (acceptable but higher expulsion than post-placental)
• >48 hours to <4 weeks: Not recommended (higher infection/expulsion risk)
• Interval insertion: ≥6 weeks postpartum

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the purpose of conducting a HEADSS evaluation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Adolescents

The HEADSS assessment is a structured psychosocial evaluation tool designed specifically for adolescents.

It covers Home, Education/Employment, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide/Depression, helping clinicians identify risk behaviours and psychosocial issues.

It is routinely used in adolescent health clinics and school health programs to guide counselling and early intervention.

Application in Public Health- Adolescent health services in India, such as Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram, emphasize psychosocial evaluation and counseling.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which HPV strains are the most common cause of cervical cancer in India?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. HPV 16, 18

HPV types 16 and 18 are high-risk oncogenic strains responsible for the majority of cervical cancer cases in India, accounting for nearly 70% of cases. HPV 6 and 11 cause genital warts, while 31, 33, 52, and 58 are fewer common contributors.

Pathogenesis of HPV in Cervical Cancer- The virus infects squamous epithelial cells of the cervix, especially the transformation zone.

Oncogenic HPV strains produce viral proteins -E6 protein → inhibits p53 tumor suppressor & E7 protein → inhibits Rb protein. This leads to uncontrolled cell proliferation, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) & eventually invasive cervical cancer.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following conditions allows the safe use of combined oral contraceptive pills (OCPs)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. HIV

Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills (COCs) contain:

• Estrogen
• Progestin

These pills prevent pregnancy by:

• Suppressing ovulation
• Thickening cervical mucus
• Altering endometrial lining

The World Health Organization classifies contraceptive safety using MEC categories (1–4).

| Category | Meaning

| -------- | -------

| 1 | No restriction

| 2 | Advantages outweigh risks

| 3 | Risks usually outweigh benefits

| 4 | Absolute contraindication

According to WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria, HIV infection (without AIDS-related complications) is not a contraindication to the use of combined oral contraceptive pills (OCPs).

In contrast, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes (especially with vascular involvement or long duration) increase the risk of thromboembolic and cardiovascular events, making OCP use unsafe or restricted.

Therefore, HIV-positive women can safely use combined OCPs when appropriately evaluated.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following correctly represents “late expanding”, i.e. the third stage in the demographic cycle?
options: High birthrates and high death rates
Decline in death rates and decline in birthrates
Decline in death rates and rising birthrates
Low death rates and low birthrates
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Decline in death rates and decline in birthrates

The demographic cycle (demographic transition) is classically divided into four stages:

1. High stationary: High birth rate + high death rate
2. Early expanding: High birth rate + declining death rate
3. Late expanding: Declining birth rate + low/declining death rate
4. Low stationary: Low birth rate + low death rate

Therefore, the third stage (late expanding) is characterized by declining death rates and declining birth rates.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication of Implanon - a Long-term reversible contraceptive (LARC)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Unexplained bleeding

Implanon (etonogestrel implant) is a long-acting reversible contraceptive that is safe in most medical conditions, including diabetes, hypertension, and tuberculosis.

Key Features-

| Feature | Detail

| ------- | ------

| Type | Subdermal hormonal implant

| Duration | 3 years

| Hormone | Etonogestrel

| Mechanism | Suppresses ovulation, thickens cervical mucus

However, unexplained vaginal bleeding is an absolute contraindication, as underlying pathology such as malignancy must be excluded before insertion.

Implanon should not be used in women with:

| Condition | Reason

| --------- | ------

| Unexplained vaginal bleeding | Underlying pathology must be ruled out

| Active breast cancer | Hormone-sensitive tumor

| Severe liver disease | Hormone metabolism affected

Once the cause of bleeding is evaluated and treated, the implant can be considered if appropriate.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the sensitive indicator to assess the availability, utilization, and effectiveness of healthcare in a community?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Infant mortality rate

The Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is considered the most sensitive indicator of a community’s health status and health-care delivery system.

It reflects:

• Availability of healthcare
• Utilization of maternal and child health services
• Effectiveness of healthcare systems

It reflects the combined effects of maternal health, nutrition, socioeconomic conditions, environmental sanitation, and access to quality health services.

Because infants are highly vulnerable, changes in IMR quickly signal improvements or deficiencies in availability, utilization, and effectiveness of health care.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following publications is/are brought out by the World Health Organization? 1. CD Alert 2. Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report 3. Weekly Epidemiological Record Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 3 only

The World Health Organization (WHO) publishes several global health reports and surveillance bulletins. Among them, the Weekly Epidemiological Record (WER) is the official WHO publication that provides updates on outbreaks, vaccine-preventable diseases, and international public health events.

• 1. CD Alert ✗

• Published by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), India, not WHO.

• 2. Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) ✗

• Published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), USA.

• 3. Weekly Epidemiological Record (WER) ✓

• Official WHO weekly publication providing global surveillance data, disease outbreaks, immunization updates, and public health recommendations.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one among the following was used for measuring economic status of households, in the National Family Health Survey-III (NFHS-III)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Wealth index

In NFHS-III (2005–06), the economic status of households was assessed using the Wealth Index, which is based on household assets, housing characteristics, and access to amenities, rather than income. It is constructed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA).

Why not the other options?

• A. Kuppuswamy’s scale❌: Used for urban socioeconomic status based on education, occupation, and family income.
• B. Pareek scale❌: Used for rural socioeconomic status.
• C. Lifestyle index❌: Not used in NFHS.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following fertility-related statistics most appropriately gives the approximate magnitude of “completed family size”?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Total Fertility Rate (TFR)

• Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is the average number of children a woman would bear during her reproductive lifetime if she experienced the current age-specific fertility rates throughout her reproductive years.
• Therefore, TFR provides the best approximate measure of a population’s completed family size.

Why not the others?

• (a) Total Fertility Rate TFR — Correct: Approximates the average completed family size under prevailing fertility rates.
• (b) Total Marital Fertility Rate TMFR: Measures fertility among married women only; it is not the standard overall measure of completed family size.
• (c) Net Reproduction Rate NRR: Measures the average number of daughters a newborn girl will bear during her lifetime; it reflects replacement rather than family size.
• (d) Age-Specific Fertility Rate ASFR: Gives the fertility rate for a specific age group, not the total reproductive performance.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following statements regarding Sample Registration System is not correct?
options: It is a dual record system.
It is a continuous enumeration by local enumerators and an independent survey every year by an investigator-supervisor.
It has facilitated more reliable estimates of births and deaths even at State level.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. It is a continuous enumeration by local enumerators and an independent survey every year by an investigator-supervisor.

The Sample Registration System (SRS) is a dual-record system used in India to provide reliable estimates of birth and death rates.

Its two components are:

1. Continuous enumeration → carried out by a resident/local enumerator.
2. Independent retrospective survey → carried out every 6 months by an investigator/supervisor, not annually.

Therefore, statement B. is incorrect because it says the independent survey is conducted every year.

• A. It is a dual record system: Correct. SRS is a dual-record system.
• B. It is a continuous enumeration by local enumerators and an independent survey every year by an investigator-supervisor: Incorrect. Independent survey is conducted every 6 months.
• C. It covers the entire country: Correct. SRS covers the country through its sample areas.
• D. It has facilitated more reliable estimates of births and deaths even at State level: Correct. It provides reliable estimates of vital rates, including at the State level.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: While calculating the ‘total dependency ratio’, which one of the following is used in the denominator?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Population 15 to 64 years

The Total Dependency Ratio (TDR) measures the burden of the dependent population on the working-age population.

Formula:

• Total Dependency Ratio = [(Population 0–14 years + Population ≥65 years) ÷ Population 15–64 years] × 100

Why is C. correct?

• Population 15–64 years forms the denominator because it represents the economically productive (working-age) population.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A child presents with developmental delays, learning disabilities, and signs of organ damage. His mother reports a habit of eating wall paint. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Lead poisoning

Children sometimes develop pica, a condition where they eat non-food substances such as:

• Soil
• Chalk
• Paint chips

Old wall paints often contain lead, leading to Lead poisoning, also called plumbism.

The history of eating wall paint (pica) strongly suggests lead exposure, especially from lead-based paints.

| System | Manifestations

| ------ | --------------

| Neurological | Developmental delay, learning disabilities

| Gastrointestinal | Abdominal pain, vomiting

| Hematological | Anemia

| Renal | Kidney damage

Chronic lead poisoning in children leads to developmental delay, learning disabilities, and multi-organ involvement, particularly affecting the nervous system.

Iron deficiency may cause pica but does not explain organ damage, while sideroblastic anemia and lithium toxicity have different clinical contexts.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A cotton swab, pus stained, is disposed in which color of BMW management category?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Yellow category

Under Biomedical Waste Management Rules, items soiled with blood or body fluids such as cotton swabs, gauze, and dressings are classified as soiled waste.

Soiled waste is disposed of in the yellow category, which is meant for incineration or deep burial.

The red category is reserved for contaminated but recyclable plastics, while white and blue categories are used for sharps and glassware respectively.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A man working as a mason in a sand mine for a Kota stone factory in Rajasthan presents with the chest X-ray, as shown below. Which of the following occupational exposures is the most likely contributing factor to his condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Silicosis

Working as a mason in a sand mine and Kota stone factory involves chronic exposure to free crystalline silica dust.

Silica dust is commonly generated during:

• Mining
• Stone cutting
• Sand blasting
• Quarry work
• Masonry work

Workers in stone mines and sandstone industries (like Kota stone) are at very high risk.

Inhalation of silica leads to silicosis, characterized by nodular opacities and upper-lobe involvement on chest X-ray.

| Finding | Description

| ------- | -----------

| Small rounded nodules | Upper lung zones

| Progressive massive fibrosis | Advanced disease

| Egg-shell calcification | Hilar lymph nodes

Asbestosis is linked to asbestos exposure, bagassosis to sugarcane bagasse dust, and anthracosis to coal dust, making silicosis the most likely diagnosis here.

| Disease | Exposure

| ------- | --------

| Silicosis | Silica dust (mines, stone cutting)

| Asbestosis | Asbestos fibers

| Bagassosis | Sugarcane bagasse dust

| Anthracosis | Coal dust

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A patient presents to PHC OPD in Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh with bowing of legs. He also complained about bone pain, stiffness, and restricted movement in joints. Which of the following would be useful in the management of the patient?
options: Checking the protein intake of the population
Addition of Lime and Alum to water
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Addition of Lime and Alum to water

The clinical features described are suggestive of skeletal fluorosis, caused by chronic excess fluoride intake from drinking water, which is endemic in parts of Andhra Pradesh.

Management focuses on reducing fluoride exposure by providing safe drinking water, using surface water sources, or applying defluoridation methods sucSh as lime and alum.

Fluoridation of water would worsen fluoride toxicity and therefore has no role in management.

Do not confuse it with Lathyrism!!

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A person reported to OPD alongside his 32-year-old brother working in a factory. The brother was recently subjected to a test – Coproporphyrin in urine. The physician should suspect:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Lead poisoning

Detection of coproporphyrin in urine is a characteristic finding in lead poisoning, due to inhibition of enzymes involved in heme synthesis.

Lead interferes with ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase, causing accumulation of porphyrin precursors that are excreted in urine.

In contrast, silicosis, byssinosis, and bagassosis are occupational lung diseases and are not associated with porphyrin metabolism abnormalities.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A vital layer, also known as “Schmutzdecke”, is seen in which one of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Slow sand filter

The Schmutzdecke (German for “dirty layer” or “vital layer”) is a biologically active layer that develops on the surface of a slow sand filter. It consists of algae, bacteria, protozoa, fungi, and organic matter and is responsible for the major purification of water by removing microorganisms and organic impurities.

• A. Air filter ✗

• Does not contain a Schmutzdecke.

• B. Rapid sand filter ✗

• Purification occurs mainly by physical filtration after coagulation and sedimentation.
• No biological layer (Schmutzdecke) is formed.

• C. Slow sand filter ✓

• The Schmutzdecke is its characteristic feature and provides biological purification.

• D. Reverse osmosis filter ✗

• Uses a semipermeable membrane under pressure; no biological layer is involved.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to BMW rules, in which color-coded bag should the object shown in the image be discarded?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Red

Understand the Biomedical Waste Management (BMWM) Rules, 2016 (amended) and identify the correct color-coded container for disposal of contaminated healthcare waste. The item shown is an IV fluid/TPN bag, which is a contaminated recyclable plastic item. Such plastic waste should be discarded in the red bag for disinfection (autoclaving/microwaving/hydroclaving) followed by recycling.

Why not the other options?

• A. Red: ✔ Correct. Used for contaminated recyclable plastic waste such as IV sets, tubing, catheters, urine bags, syringes (without needles), gloves, and IV fluid bags.
• B. Yellow: Used for incinerable waste such as human anatomical waste, soiled waste, microbiological waste, expired medicines, and pathological waste.
• C. Blue: Used for glassware and metallic implants, including glass vials and ampoules.
• D. White (Translucent): Used for sharps, including needles, blades, scalpels, and other metal sharps in puncture-proof containers.

| BMW Color Code | Waste Category

| -------------- | --------------

| Yellow | Human anatomical waste, soiled waste, microbiological waste, expired medicines

| Red | Contaminated recyclable plastics (IV sets, tubing, catheters, urine bags, gloves, IV fluid bags)

| White (Translucent) | Sharps (needles, blades, scalpels)

| Blue | Glassware (vials, ampoules) and metallic implants

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to the biomedical waste management guidelines, a cotton swab used for cleaning should be discarded in which type of bag?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Yellow non-chlorinated

Under Biomedical Waste Management Rules (2016 and amendments), items soiled with blood or body fluids such as used cotton swabs, gauze, and dressings are categorized as soiled waste.

Soiled waste is disposed of in the yellow non-chlorinated bag, which is meant for incineration or deep burial.

| Examples of Waste | Category

| ----------------- | --------

| Cotton swabs contaminated with body fluids | Yellow

| Dressings and bandages | Yellow

| Human tissues or organs | Yellow

| Microbiology lab waste | Yellow

Red bags are reserved for contaminated recyclable plastics, and chlorinated bags are no longer recommended due to environmental concerns.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Arrange the steps of the Disaster cycle in sequence.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Disaster impact – Response – Rehabilitation – Mitigation

The disaster cycle describes the continuous sequence of activities before and after a disaster. It begins with disaster impact, followed by response involving rescue and relief measures. It is a continuous cycle used in disaster preparedness programs such as those coordinated by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).

This is succeeded by rehabilitation and recovery, and finally mitigation, which aims to reduce the impact of future disasters through preparedness and risk reduction.

Expanded version of the same: Impact- Response- Rehabilitation-Reconstruction-Development-Prevention-Mitigation-Preparedness

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As an index of thermal comfort, the ‘Corrected Effective Temperature’ is considered to be an improvement over ‘Effective Temperature’. It deals with which of the following factors? I. Air velocity II. Humidity III. Mean radiant heat IV. Sweat rate Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. I, II and III

Corrected Effective Temperature (CET) is an improved index of thermal comfort that assesses the combined effect of air temperature, humidity, air velocity, and mean radiant temperature on human comfort. It is more accurate than Effective Temperature (ET) because it also incorporates the effect of radiant heat.

• Effective Temperature (ET): Based on air temperature, humidity, and air velocity.
• Corrected Effective Temperature (CET): ET + Mean Radiant Temperature (Radiant heat).
• Sweat rate is not a component of CET.
• CET is widely used to evaluate thermal comfort in homes, workplaces, hospitals, and industrial settings.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As per the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), the goal is to provide every rural household with a functional household tap connection that delivers at least how many litres of tap water per capita per day (lpcd)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 55

Under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), the goal is to provide every rural household with a Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) supplying at least 55 litres of water per capita per day (lpcd) of prescribed quality on a regular basis.

Therefore, B. 55 lpcd is correct.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following stages of modern sewage treatment plants: 1. Use of Grit chamber 2. Use of Primary sedimentation tank 3. Screening 4. Use of Sludge digester What would be the correct sequence of the above stages?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 3 → 1 → 2 → 4

Sewage treatment is the process of removing physical, chemical, and biological impurities from wastewater before its safe disposal or reuse. A modern sewage treatment plant follows a definite sequence of treatment steps: Screening → Grit Chamber → Primary Sedimentation Tank → Sludge Digester

• Stage 3: Screening

• Removes large floating materials such as rags, sticks, paper, plastics, and leaves using coarse and fine screens.

• Stage 1: Grit Chamber

• Removes heavy inorganic particles like sand, gravel, grit, and broken glass that could damage pumps and machinery.

• Stage 2: Primary Sedimentation Tank

• Allows suspended organic solids to settle as primary sludge, while scum floats and is removed.

• Stage 4: Sludge Digester

• Anaerobic digestion of sludge produces biogas (mainly methane) and stabilizes the sludge for safe disposal.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following statements about working of septic tanks: 1. They are recommended for large communities, rather than small communities. 2. There should be no air space between the level of liquid in the tank and the undersurface of the cover. 3. Liquid effluent from the outlet pipe is free from all pathogens. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. None of the statements

A septic tank is an on-site sewage disposal system used for individual houses and small communities where a centralized sewerage system is not available. It works by anaerobic digestion, where solids settle and decompose, while the liquid effluent is discharged for further treatment in a soak pit or dispersion trenches.

• 1. They are recommended for large communities\, rather than small communities. ✗

• Septic tanks are designed for individual households and small communities, not large populations.

• 2. There should be no air space between the level of liquid in the tank and the undersurface of the cover. ✗

• A septic tank should have an air space (about 30 cm) between the liquid level and the cover to allow gas accumulation and proper functioning.

• 3. Liquid effluent from the outlet pipe is free from all pathogens. ✗

• The effluent still contains pathogenic microorganisms and requires further disposal/treatment through a soak pit, leach field, or other methods.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During the Nalgonda technique of defluoridation of water, which of the following plays a major role in flocculation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Alum

Nalgonda technique is a cost-effective community method for defluoridation of drinking water, in which alum (aluminium sulfate) is the principal coagulant/flocculating agent that removes fluoride by forming flocs. Lime aids coagulation by adjusting pH, while bleaching powder is added for disinfection.

Why not the other options?

• A. Bleaching powder: Used for disinfection, not flocculation.
• C. Lime: Helps optimize pH and coagulation, but is not the primary flocculating agent.
• D. Activated charcoal: Used for adsorption of organic impurities, taste, and odor, not fluoride removal in the Nalgonda technique.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Horrocks’ apparatus was used to find out the dose of bleaching powder required to disinfect the water in a well. The 3rd cup in the Horrocks’ apparatus showed the distinct blue colour. How much bleaching powder (good quality) will be required to disinfect the well, for every 455 litres of water?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 6 grams

The Horrocks apparatus is used to determine the approximate amount of bleaching powder required to disinfect a well.

• The 3rd cup showing a distinct blue colour indicates that the required dose corresponds to 3 g of bleaching powder per 455 L (100 gallons) of water in the standard Horrocks calculation.
• For good-quality bleaching powder, the calculated quantity is multiplied by 2.

Therefore:

3 g × 2 = 6 g per 455 L

Hence, the correct answer is (d) 6 grams.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: How much illumination is recommended by the Illuminating Engineering Society for the general office work?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 400 lux

Illumination is the amount of light falling on a surface and is measured in lux (lx). Adequate illumination improves visual performance, reduces eye strain, and enhances work efficiency. According to the Illuminating Engineering Society (IES), the recommended illumination for general office work is 400 lux.

• General office work: 400 lux
• Corridors and staircases: 100 lux
• Classrooms: 150–300 lux
• Drawing/design work: 700–1000 lux
• Operation theatre: 1000–10,000 lux (shadow-free lighting)
• Direct sunlight: Approximately 100,000 lux

Units of Light

• Luminous flux: Lumen (lm)
• Illumination: Lux (lx) = Lumen/m²
• Luminous intensity: Candela (cd)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the logo, which is used for biomedical waste management.
options: [Option image — not included in this edition]
[Option image — not included in this edition]
[Option image — not included in this edition]
[Option image — not included in this edition]
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. [image not included in this edition]

The biohazard symbol (three interlocking crescents) on yellow containers is the universal logo for biomedical waste management in healthcare facilities.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a causality triage scenario, following a road traffic accident, whom would you treat first?
options: 60-year-old conscious patient with pants covered in blood
40-year-old female who is unconscious with laboured breathing
20-year-old female who is agitated with anxiety and increased breathing
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 40-year-old female who is unconscious with laboured breathing

In triage, priority is given based on immediacy of life-threatening conditions, following the ABCDE (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure) principle.

An unconscious patient with laboured breathing has a compromised airway and respiration, which are immediately life-threatening and require urgent intervention.

Patients who are conscious, crying, anxious, or bleeding but stable can be managed after stabilization of airway and breathing–threatened cases.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the Nalgonda technique for defluoridation of water, which of the following chemicals are used? Select the best combination. 1. Gypsum 2. Lime 3. Charcoal 4. Alum
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 2 & 4

The Nalgonda technique is a community-level method for Defluoridation of drinking water, developed in India.

It uses alum (aluminium sulphate) as a coagulant to precipitate fluoride and lime to aid floc formation and adjust pH.

The technique uses three main chemicals:

The process also involves rapid mixing, flocculation, sedimentation, and filtration, making it suitable for rural and semi-urban settings with high fluoride levels.

Steps in Nalgonda Technique

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Particulate matter 2.5 is an important component while calculating the AQI. If a person inhales a 2.5 particle, it gets deposited in which part of the airway?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Alveoli

PM2.5 particles have an aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 µm, allowing them to bypass upper airway defences.

They penetrate deep into the respiratory tract and are deposited in the alveoli, where gas exchange occurs.

This deep deposition explains their strong association with cardiopulmonary morbidity and mortality and their importance in AQI calculations.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The given instrument is used for:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Low air velocity

The instrument shown is a Kata thermometer, which is specifically used to assess low air velocity by measuring the cooling power of air.

Types of Kata Thermometers

It works by recording the time taken for alcohol in the thermometer to cool between two fixed temperature points, which reflects air movement in still environments.

Kata thermometers are commonly used in occupational health to evaluate ventilation in indoor workplaces where air flow is minimal.

A. Air pollution- Measured by instruments like high-volume air sampler.

B. Air humidity- measured using hygrometers or psychrometers.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The Langelier’s Saturation Index for water is used to assess which characteristic of water?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Water corrosion

Langelier’s Saturation Index (LSI) is used to assess the corrosive or scale-forming tendency of water.

The Langelier Saturation Index (LSI) is used to determine whether water will:

• Corrode pipes, or
• Form scale deposits (calcium carbonate).

Thus it helps evaluate the corrosive nature of water.

It is calculated using parameters such as:

• pH
• Alkalinity
• Calcium concentration
• Temperature
• Total dissolved solids (TDS)

| LSI Value | Meaning

| --------- | -------

| LSI < 0 | Water is corrosive

| LSI = 0 | Water is neutral/stable

| LSI > 0 | Water tends to form scale

A negative LSI indicates corrosive water, while a positive LSI suggests a tendency to form scale due to calcium carbonate precipitation.

It does not assess microbiological contamination, chemical pollutants like nitrates, or radioactivity.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The method of combined disposal of refuse and night soil is known as:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Composting

Composting is the combined biological disposal of refuse (solid waste) and night soil (human excreta) through controlled aerobic and anaerobic decomposition by microorganisms. It converts organic waste into stable, nutrient-rich manure (compost) that can be safely used as a soil conditioner.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Dumping: Simple open disposal of waste without treatment; unhygienic and environmentally unsafe.
• B. Controlled tipping (Sanitary landfill): Waste is compacted and covered with soil daily but does not involve combined disposal of night soil.
• C. Incineration: Waste is destroyed by high-temperature burning; suitable for infectious and hazardous waste, not for combined disposal of refuse and night soil.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The seating arrangement between the doctor and patient is illustrated below. Which of the following statements is correctly describes the risk of transmission of airborne droplet infections in this setting?
options: Setting 1 is better (low risk) for doctor
Setting 2 is better (low risk) for doctor
Setting 1 and Setting 2 both are high risk
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Setting 2 is better (low risk) for doctor

Consultation room layout and airflow direction influence the transmission of airborne and droplet infections. The doctor should sit near the source of fresh air (window), while the patient should sit downstream, so that airflow moves from the doctor toward the patient and then out of the room, minimizing the doctor’s exposure to infectious aerosols.

Why not the other options?

• A. Setting 1 is better (low risk) for doctor: Incorrect; airflow carries respiratory droplets from the patient toward the doctor, increasing exposure.
• B. Setting 1 is better in winters: Incorrect; the principle of airflow direction remains the same irrespective of season.
• D. Setting 1 and Setting 2 both are high risk: Incorrect; Setting 2 reduces the doctor’s risk by optimizing airflow.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The statement, “Health is a dynamic equilibrium between man and environment and disease a maladjustment of the human organism to environment” explains which one of the following concepts of health?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Ecological

The ecological concept of health defines health as a dynamic equilibrium between the individual and the environment. Disease occurs when this balance is disturbed, leading to maladjustment between the human organism and its environment. This concept emphasizes the interaction of host, agent, and environment, which forms the basis of modern epidemiology.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Biomedical concept:

• Defines health as the absence of disease.
• Focuses on biological causes and medical treatment, largely ignoring social and environmental factors.

• C. Psychosocial concept: Emphasizes the influence of psychological, social, cultural, economic, and political factors on health.
• D. Holistic concept: Integrates physical, mental, social, environmental, and spiritual well-being, representing the broadest concept of health.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016, human anatomical waste is to be carried in which colour plastic bags?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Yellow

Under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016, human anatomical waste (human tissues, organs, body parts, fetus, and placenta) is segregated into yellow non-chlorinated plastic bags and disposed of by incineration, plasma pyrolysis, or deep burial (where permitted).

High-Yield Pearls

• Yellow Bag: Human/animal anatomical waste, placenta, fetus, soiled waste, microbiology waste, expired medicines.
• Red Bag: Contaminated recyclable plastics (IV sets, tubing, catheters, gloves).
• White Container: Sharps (needles, scalpels, blades).
• Blue Container: Glassware, vials, ampoules.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What are the reasons for choosing coliform organisms as indicators of faecal pollution of water rather than the waterborne pathogens directly? I. They are present in great abundance in the human intestine and excreted in great numbers in faeces. II. They have lower resistance to forces of natural purification. III. They survive less than the pathogens. IV. They are easily detected by culture methods. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. I and IV

The following statements are correct:

• I. They are present in great abundance in the human intestine and excreted in great numbers in feces: Coliforms, especially E. coli, are normal intestinal flora and are shed in large numbers, making them reliable indicators of fecal pollution.
• IV. They are easily detected by culture methods: Coliforms can be identified rapidly using simple and inexpensive methods such as the Most Probable Number (MPN) test and membrane filtration.

Why are II and III incorrect?

• II. They have lower resistance to forces of natural purification: An ideal indicator organism should have resistance similar to or greater than many pathogens, so that its absence suggests water safety.
• III. They survive less than the pathogens: Indicator organisms should survive at least as long as enteric pathogens, making this statement incorrect.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the most appropriate disposal mechanism for expired medications in biomedical waste management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Incineration

Expired or discarded pharmaceuticals are preferably disposed of by high-temperature incineration, which ensures complete destruction of the drugs and prevents environmental contamination or misuse. It is the recommended method under Biomedical Waste Management Rules for pharmaceutical waste.

Why not the other options?

• A. Autoclaving: Used for infectious biomedical waste, not pharmaceutical waste.
• B. Deep burial: Reserved for specific anatomical or infectious waste in limited settings; not recommended for expired medicines.
• D. Landfill: Not preferred because pharmaceuticals may leach into soil and groundwater, posing environmental hazards.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the proper disposal method for a damaged vaccine vial according to biomedical waste management protocols?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: A. Puncture proof blue bin

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which is the most economical method to disinfect 20 litres of water at the household level after a disaster?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Chlorine tablet

During disasters and emergencies, chlorination is the most economical, practical, and effective method for household-level disinfection of drinking water. Chlorine tablets are inexpensive, easy to transport, simple to use, and effective against most waterborne pathogens.

After adding the tablet, the water should be allowed to stand for at least 30 minutes before consumption.

Why not the other options?

• B. Alum: Used for coagulation and sedimentation (removing turbidity), not for disinfection.
• C. Fluorine: Used for prevention of dental caries, not for water disinfection.
