questions.text: Which of the following indicators are considered for computing “Physical Quality of Life Index” (PQLI)? I. Infant mortality II. Life expectancy at age one III. Literacy IV. Per capita income Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. I, II and III

The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) was developed by Morris D. Morris (1979) to measure a country’s quality of life based on social and health indicators, rather than economic performance. It evaluates the actual outcomes of development using three indicators, each scored from 0 to 100, with the average giving the PQLI score (0–100). The three components of PQLI are:

• I. Infant mortality rate (IMR): Reflects the quality of maternal and child health services and overall health status.
• II. Life expectancy at age one: Measures the expected survival of a child who has reached one year of age, thereby excluding the influence of infant mortality.
• III. Literacy: Usually based on the adult literacy rate, representing the educational status of the population.

Why is IV incorrect?

• IV. Per capita income: Per capita income is not included in PQLI. It is an economic indicator and is used in indices such as the Human Development Index (HDI), but PQLI intentionally excludes income to focus on physical quality of life.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following indicators stand consolidated in Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI)? 1. Infant mortality 2. Life expectancy at age one 3. Per capita income 4. Literacy Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2 and 4

The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) was developed by Morris D. Morris (1979) to measure the physical well-being of a population, independent of economic indicators. It is calculated using three indicators:

• Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)
• Life Expectancy at Age One
• Basic Literacy Rate

Per capita income is NOT included in PQLI.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a High-risk group for HIV?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Long distance truck drivers (LDTD)

High-risk groups for HIV are those with direct high-risk sexual or parenteral exposure, such as IDU, MSM, and CSW, due to needle sharing or unprotected sex.

Long-distance truck drivers are classified as a bridge population, not a core high-risk group, as they facilitate transmission between high-risk groups and the general population.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the best indicator to measure the burden of disease?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. DALY

Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) is the standard measure of the overall burden of disease. It combines the impact of premature mortality and disability into a single metric.

DALY = Years of Life Lost (YLL) + Years Lived with Disability (YLD)

A higher DALY indicates a greater burden of disease.

Why not the other options?

• A. HALE (Health-Adjusted Life Expectancy): Measures the average number of years a person is expected to live in good health.
• B. QALY (Quality-Adjusted Life Year): Measures the effectiveness of healthcare interventions by combining quantity and quality of life.
• D. Sullivan Index: Measures disability-free life expectancy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct for incidence rate? 1. It is useful for taking action to control a disease. 2. Rising incidence rates may indicate ineffectiveness of the current control programmes. 3. Fluctuation in incidence rate may indicate a change in aetiology of disease. Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2 and 3

Incidence rate measures the occurrence of new cases of a disease in a population at risk over a specified period of time. It is the best measure of the risk of developing a disease and is widely used to assess disease trends, evaluate control programs, and identify changes in disease occurrence.

• 1. It is useful for taking action to control a disease. ✓

• Incidence reflects current transmission and occurrence of new cases, making it valuable for planning and evaluating disease control measures.

• 2. Rising incidence rates may indicate ineffectiveness of the current control programmes. ✓

• An increase in incidence may suggest failure of preventive or control measures, poor vaccination coverage, or emergence of new risk factors.

• 3. Fluctuation in incidence rate may indicate a change in aetiology of disease. ✓

• Changes in incidence may result from:

• Emergence of new risk factors
• Environmental or behavioral changes
• Improved diagnostics or surveillance
• Change in the disease’s etiology

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding prevention of Zika virus infection?
options: Early administration of NSAIDs reduces viremia and prevents complications
Consistent condom uses and avoidance of pregnancy during periods of active transmission are recommended
Routine immunization with a licensed live-attenuated Zika vaccine is effective in endemic regions
Plasmapheresis is indicated to prevent neurological complications of Zika virus infection
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Consistent condom uses and avoidance of pregnancy during periods of active transmission are recommended

Prevention of Zika virus infection focuses on avoiding mosquito bites and preventing sexual transmission, as the virus can persist in semen.

Use of condoms during intercourse and avoiding pregnancy during active transmission periods are recommended to prevent congenital Zika syndrome. Major concern arises because infection during pregnancy can cause congenital Zika syndrome, including:

• Microcephaly
• Brain malformations
• Developmental abnormalities

There is no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral treatment for Zika, and management is supportive only.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding a case-control study is incorrect?
options: It is typically a prospective study
It proceeds from effect to cause
Recall bias is an important limitation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. It is typically a prospective study

• A case-control study begins by identifying individuals who have a particular disease or outcome (cases) and comparing them with individuals without the disease (controls). Investigators then assess and compare their previous exposure to suspected risk factors.
• Thus, the classical direction of inquiry is:

• Disease/Effect → Previous exposure/Cause

• Case-control studies are conventionally described as retrospective studies because they usually look backward from an established outcome to determine prior exposure. Therefore, describing a case-control study as prospective is incorrect in the conventional exam context.

Why are the other statements correct?

• B. Proceeds from effect to cause: Correct. Subjects are selected according to outcome/disease status, and previous exposures are investigated.
• C. Recall bias is a major problem: Correct. Cases may remember previous exposures differently from controls, resulting in recall bias.
• D. Cost-effective: Correct. Case-control studies are generally quicker and less expensive than cohort studies and require fewer participants.

High-Yield Comparison:

| Feature | Case-Control Study | Cohort Study

| ------- | ------------------ | ------------

| Starts with | Disease/outcome | Exposure

| Direction | Effect → Cause | Cause → Effect

| Classical description | Retrospective | Prospective or retrospective

| Best suited for | Rare diseases | Rare exposures

| Main measure | Odds ratio | Relative risk

| Important bias | Recall bias | Loss to follow-up

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following steps is not included in WHO's STEP approach?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: A. Therapeutic assessment

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following best explains the relationship among Prevalence (P), Incidence (I) and Duration (D) of a disease, given the assumption that the population is stable?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. P = I × D

The relationship between Prevalence (P), Incidence (I), and Duration D. in a stable population (where disease incidence and population size remain constant) is:

• Prevalence = Incidence × Average Duration of Disease
•

P = I × D

•

A. I = P × D ✗: Incorrect relationship.

• B. D = P × I ✗: Incorrect formula.
• C. I = P + D ✗: No epidemiological basis.
• D. P = I × D ✓: Correct formula under steady-state conditions.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following terms is an “all-or-none phenomenon” and is best described as termination of all transmission of infection by extermination of the infectious agent?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Disease eradication

Disease eradication is the permanent worldwide reduction to zero of the incidence of infection caused by a specific infectious agent, such that no further intervention is required. It is an “all-or-none phenomenon”, meaning a disease is either completely eradicated globally or it is not. Once eradication is achieved, routine control measures and vaccination are no longer required (except for laboratory containment).

Why not the other options?

• A. Disease control:

• Reduction of disease incidence, prevalence, morbidity, or mortality to an acceptable level through continuous public health measures.
• Ongoing interventions are required.

• B. Disease elimination:

• Reduction of disease transmission to zero in a defined geographical area, but continued surveillance and preventive measures are necessary because reintroduction is possible. ⭐

• D. Disease surveillance:

• Continuous collection, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination of health data for planning and evaluating public health interventions.
• It is not a disease outcome.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: While planning a health research study, which of the following represents the correct sequence of initial steps? 1. Selection of study population 2. Formulation of research objectives 3. Identification of research problem 4. Selection of study design
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 3 → 2 → 4 → 1

1. Identification of the research problem
2. Formulation of the research question
3. Review of literature
4. Formulation of hypothesis/ research objectives
5. Selection of study design
6. Selection of study population and sampling method
7. Finalization of research setting
8. Development of study tools and data collection methods
9. Pilot study / Pretesting
10. Data collection
11. Data analysis and interpretation
12. Report writing and dissemination of results

Health research follows a systematic scientific process.

Before collecting any data, researchers must clearly define:

1. What problem is being studied
2. What exactly the study aims to achieve
3. How the study will be conducted
4. Who will be included in the study

This logical progression ensures valid results and efficient research planning.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 28-year-old male is positive for SARS-COV-2. A total of 30 people have been in contact with the patient and show no symptoms or signs of COVID-19. What is the time duration for which they must be quarantined?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Maximum incubation period

Quarantine is the limitation in freedom of movement of healthy contacts of cases, who have been exposed for a period that lasts as much as the maximal incubation period of the disease.

The incubation period is the time interval between the invasion of the infectious agent and the appearance of the first symptom or signs in the body. It is termed as the latent period in non-infectious diseases.

* It is a primary level of prevention, under specific protection.

* Types of quarantine

* Absolute: complete limitation of movement

* Modified: selective partial limitation of movement

* Segregation: observation of a group of persons in a population after separation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 45-year-old healthy man with a history of small streaks of blood in his stools is being sent for a colonoscopy to screen for colon cancer. This type of prevention is _______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Secondary

Colonoscopies for early detection/screening of colon cancer are an example of secondary prevention.

Early diagnosis (including screening) and treatment are the components of secondary prevention. Some examples of secondary prevention are as follows:

* Papanicolaou (Pap) smear for early detection of cervical cancer

* Mammography, for early detection of breast cancer

* Colonoscopies, for early detection of colon cancer

* Blood Pressure Screening

Secondary prevention measures focus on the sub-clinical stage and the early clinical stage, such as dysplasia in this case. These measures enable early detection and prompt effective intervention to correct departures from a state of health.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A male had a vasectomy 1 month ago and the couple asks the doctor if they have to take any precautions while having sex. What advice should be given?
options: Oral contraceptive pills for 1 month for the woman
Hormonal treatment given for 2 more months for the man
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Use condoms for 3 months

The best advice is to use condoms for 3 months as the sperms are stored in the reproductive tract for upto 3 months.

Vasectomy

* Vasectomy consists of dividing the vas deferens and disrupting the passage of sperms.

* It is done through a small incision in the scrotum, under local anaesthesia. The sterility is not immediate. The sperms are stored in the reproductive tract for up to 3 months. The couple must therefore abstain from intercourse during this period or use other methods of contraception.

* Approximately, 20 ejaculates clear the semen of all sperms. Two semen analysis reports must confirm the absence of sperms before the man can be declared sterile.

* No- scalpel technique has been now adopted. One single incision is made with a special forceps and skin stitch is not required. Clips and plugs can be applied over the vas instead of cutting. Vasectomy is cheaper than tubectomy

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A non alcoholic factory worker in a groundnut factory developed hepatocellular carcinoma. What is the most probable cause in this worker who has been working there for a long time?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Aflatoxins

Aflatoxin is the most probable cause in this patient as he is working in a groundnut factory.

Aflatoxins:

* These are a type of mycotoxins produced by Aspergillus species of fungi, such as A. flavus (secretes B1) and A. parasiticus (secretes B1, B2, G1 and G2)

* Frequently present in moldy foods, like groundnuts, corn, and peas.

* These toxins are highly toxic to animals and birds, as well as to human beings.

* Known to cause hepatomas in lower animals, and carcinogenic effects in humans have also been seen.

Risk factors for HCC

* HBV, HCV, aflatoxin, alcohol

* Hereditary hemochromatosis, α1AT deficiency, Wilson disease, metabolic syndrome, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

Other options:

BOAA (Beta oxalyl amino alanine) is the toxic compound causing Lathyrism.

Sanguinarine is the toxic compound causing epidemic dropsy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher is studying the difference in the incidence of asthma in children who are exposed to second-hand smoke and those who are not. If he wishes to express the additional incidence of asthma in the exposed children as a percentage, which of the following should he use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Attributable risk

The researcher may use attributable risk to express the increased incidence of asthma in the exposed children.

Attributable risk (AR) is the difference in incidence rates of disease (or death) between an exposed group and the non-exposed group. It is often expressed as a percentage. The terms "risk difference" or "cumulative incidence difference" refers to attributable risk.

Other Options:

Option B: Relative risk (RR) is the ratio of the incidence of the disease (or death) among exposed and the incidence among non-exposed.

Option C: Population-attributable risk is the incidence of the disease (or death) in the total population minus the incidence of disease (or death) among those who were not exposed to the suspected causal factor. Population attributable risk is measured by multiplying attributable risk with the population prevalence of exposure.

Option D: Odds ratio is a measure of the strength of association between a risk factor and outcome in case-control studies.

questions.text: A researcher who was studying on Plasmodium species decided to visit the malaria-endemic place in Odisha after 2 days to do his clinical study for 5 weeks. Which of the following drugs need to be taken as prophylaxis before visiting the malaria-endemic place?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Doxycycline

Doxycycline needs to be taken as prophylaxis by the researcher before going to the malaria-endemic place.

Pearl PF0981: National Strategic Plan for Malaria Elimination 2017 - 2022

* The National Strategic Plan (NSP) for Malaria Elimination (2017-22) was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare under NVBDCP, which is based on the National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016 – 2030).

* The NSP focuses mainly on the districts which function as the operational units.

Accordingly all the districts are classified into the following four categories

Category of districts
Definition

Category 0: Prevention of re-establishment phase
Includes all districts in which no incidence of malaria was reported in last three years.

Category 1: Elimination phase
District in which annual parasite incidence (API), is less than one per 1000 population.

Category 2: Pre elimination phase
Districts with API in between one and two per 1000 population.

Category 3: Intensified control phase
Districts having API more than two.

The above classification is more operational than the classification mentioned in the NFME which is state focussed.

The goals of NSP strategy are phased elimination of malaria in India. The National Framework for Malaria Elimination (NFME) in India has set 2030 as goal for eliminating malaria, and the goals of NSP in consonance with overall goals.

The goals of NSP 2017 – 2022 are:

* Eliminate malaria in category 1 (API < 1) districts by 2020, and category 2 (API 1 - 2) districts by 2022.

* Reduce transmission in category 3 districts to stabilize API at less than 1 by 2022

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was done to assess nutritional status among young children in rural and urban areas. 40 children in rural and 30 children in urban areas were malnourished. Which of the following tests of significance is the most appropriate in this case?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Chi Square test

The most appropriate test of significance, in this case, is the chi-square test. It is used to compare qualitative data between 2 groups with independent measures.

In this question,

* Nutritional status (nourished or malnourished) is a qualitative measure.

* Residence (Urban or rural) is again a qualitative measure.

* Further, only these TWO variables are being compared. Therefore, the chi-square test is the most appropriate test of significance.

The Chi-Square test (χ2) is a non-parametric(non-numeric) test and it is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.

* It is a test of proportions and associations.

* A Chi-square distribution is usually positively skewed but it approaches a normal distribution as its degrees of freedom increase.

* If the frequency of any of the cells of the categorical table is <5, then Fisher’s exact test can also be used.

Other options:

Option B: The paired t-test compares paired data or pre-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. If a study were to compare BP in a group of patients before and after treatment, then paired t-test would be used. It is also a test done for quantitative variables.

Option C: Standard error of the mean measures how much discrepancy is likely in a sample's mean compared with the population mean. It is not a test for statistical significance.

Option D: The analysis of variance test (ANOVA) is used to test the difference between means of two or more than two groups. Hence it is used in studies with quantitative data. If a study was done to compare the heights of boys in different classes in a school, ANOVA would be used.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to Sustainable Development Goals, which of the following statement is false ?
options: End the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and combat hepatitis
Reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 (per 100,000 live births)
Reduce the neonatal mortality rate to as low as 25 (per 1,000 live births)
Reduce under-5 mortality to as low as 25 (per 1,000 live births)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Reduce the neonatal mortality rate to as low as 25 (per 1,000 live births)

The statement "Reduce the neonatal mortality rate to as low as 25 (per 1,000 live births)" is false, and the true statement is "Reduce the neonatal mortality rate to as low as 12 (per 1,000 live births)".

SDG (Sustainable Development Goals) comprises 17 goals and 170 targets for Agenda 2030.

* The MDGs came to an end in December 2015 and were replaced by the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

* 17 SDGs take their place and as of 1st January 2016, the SDGs of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development officially came into force.

* The five P's of the new agenda are People, Planet, Prosperity, Peace, and Partnership.

Health is positioned in one comprehensive goal SDG 3.

* Target 3.1: To reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 (per 100,000 live births)

* Target 3.2: To reduce neonatal mortality and under-5 mortality by as low as 12 and 25 (per 1,000 live births) respectively.

* Target 3.3: To end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, and neglected tropical diseases and combat hepatitis, water-borne diseases, and other communicable diseases.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: After how many days is the polymorphic rash of Varicella not contagious?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. After crust formation over lesions

Chicken pox or Varicella caused by Varicella zoster virus becomes non-contagious after the lesions have crusted.

* Varicella zoster virus is an α Herpes virus (Human Herpes Virus 3).

* Over half of primary infections occur before the age of 5 and 85% before puberty.

* The lesions are polymorphic - present at different stages in each site.

* In 2–4 days, a dry crust forms and soon separates, to leave a shallow pink depression which, in the absence of secondary infection, heals without scarring.

* Most common complication is secondary bacterial infection.

* Varicella confers lasting immunity and second attacks are uncommon.

* In histopathology, keratinocytes show ballooning degeneration creating multinucleated giant cells called Tzanck cells.

Characteristics of rash of chicken pox

* Superficial

* Pleomorphic

* Centripetal

* Unilocular

* Symmetrical

* Spares palms and soles, affects flexor surfaces and axilla

* Rapid evolution

* Dew drop on Rose-petal appearance

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following are minimum standards for sanitation of schools and its environment in India except:
options: Combined doors + windows area = 25 % of floor space area
One urinal for 10 students and one latrine for 25 students
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. One urinal for 10 students and one latrine for 25 students

One urinal per 60 students and one latrine per 100 students is the standard.

Healthful school environment: Suggested minimum standards for sanitation of schools and its environment in India includes:

* Location: Away from noisy surroundings; kept fenced.

* Site: 5 acres for primary schools; 10 acres for higher elementary schools.

* Structure: Exterior walls 10 inch thick and heat resistant.

* Class room: 1 class room per 40 students maximum; Per capita space > 10 sq. feet

* Furniture: Single desks of ‘minus (–) type’.

* Doors and windows: Doors and windows area> 25% of floor area

* Color: Inside color of walls should be white.

* Lighting: Natural light from left side.

* Water supply: Safe and potable and continuous supply through taps.

* Lavatory: 1 urinal per 60 students and 1 latrine per 100 students.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following are pillars of primary health care except _____.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Health education

Health education is not a pillar or principle of primary health care. It is, however, an element of primary health care.

Pearl PF1537: Elements and Principles of Primary Health Care

A. Elements of Primary Health Care

(Mnemonic: ELEMENTS)

* Education about health problems and their prevention and control

* Locally endemic diseases – prevention and control

* Essential drugs

* Maternal and child health care

* Expanded programme of immunization against vaccine preventable diseases

* Nutrition and proper food supply

* Treatment of common diseases and injuries

* Safe water and sanitation

B. Principles/Pillars of Primary Health Care

* Equitable distribution

* Community participation

* Intersectoral coordination

* Appropriate technology

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As a medical officer posted in rural service, you have been asked to supervise the various preventive measures being taken in your region against malaria. According to the program whose logo is shown below, you would be correct to advise all of the following except:
options: Two rounds of spraying with DDT should be done to provide protection during the entire transmission season.
Long Lasting Insecticide Nets (LLIN) should be provided in areas with Annual Parasite Index ≥ 5.
Indoor Residual Sprays are not suitable for vector control in rural areas.
In case of DDT resistance, 3 rounds of spraying with Malathion should be done to provide protection during the entire transmission season.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Indoor Residual Sprays are not suitable for vector control in rural areas.

Under the Integrated vector management initiative, Indoor Residual Sprays are the main methods of vector control in rural areas.

National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) is the nodal agency for the prevention of control of the following vector-borne diseases:

* Kala-azar (also called visceral leishmaniasis)

* Malaria

* Dengue

* Filariasis

* Japanese encephalitis

* Chikungunya.

Integrated Vector Management:

* For adult mosquitoes:

* Indoor residual Sprays are used. It is the main method of vector control in rural areas.

* DDT is the insecticide of choice.

* Two rounds of spraying are done with DDT and in DDT-resistant areas, three rounds of spraying are done with Malathion (if DDT-resistant).

* For the larvae: Larvivorous fish and larvicides are used. This is the main method of vector control in urban areas.

* For personal protection:

* Insecticide-treated bed nets are supplied in areas with Annual Parasite Index (API) ≥ 2.

* Long-Lasting Insecticide Nets (LLIN) are provided in areas with API ≥ 5.

The Drug distribution centers only dispense anti-malarial drugs under the NVBDCP for Malaria.

Important points about the organization for the anti-Malaria program:

* Central Government: Supplies DDT and larvicides.

* State government: Procures the Indoor Residual Sprays (IRS) for the districts.

* District Malaria Office: Key unit for the implementation of the program.

* District Malaria Officer: Has direct responsibility for IRS spraying operations and is assisted by one Assistant Malaria Officer and Malaria Inspectors.

* Medical officer of the PHC:  Has the overall responsibility for the surveillance and laboratory services.

* Multi-Purpose Workers and ASHAs: Carry out surveillance and case detection in the community.

* Drug Distribution Centres: Only dispensing anti-malarial drugs.

* Fever Treatment Depots: Dispense the anti-malarial drugs and collect the blood slides.

Pearl PF1014: Insecticides

Contact poisons

* Natural: Pyrethrum, rotenone, derris, nicotine, mineral oils

* Synthetic:

* Organo-chlorine compounds: DDT, methoxychlor, HCH, lindane, chlordane, heptachlor, dieldrin, aldrin, toxaphene, kepone, mirex.

* Repellants: Benzyl benzoate, indalone, meta-diethyltoluamide, dimethyl phthalate, ethyl hexanediol.

* Organo-phosphorus compounds: Chlorthion (aryl), diazinon (aryl), demethoate, malathion (alkyl), fenthion, parathion (aryl), trichlorfon (alkyl), runnel, abale, naled, chlorpyrifos, fenitrothion, dicapthon.

* Carbamates: Carbaryl, dimetilan, propoxur, pyrolan.

* Synthetic pyrethroids: Prothrin, resmethrin, bioresmethrin, permethrin, proparthin, tetramethrin

* Stomach poisons: Paris green, sodium fluoride.

* Fumigants: Hydrogen cyanide, methyl bromide, sulphur dioxide, carbon disulphide.

Specific Insecticides
Comments

DDT (Dichloro-diphenyl-thrichloroethane)
Insecticidal properties were discovered by Swiss scientist, Paul Muller. Most widely used insecticide. Attacks nerves of insects but doesn’t cause immediate death. White amorphous powder. Contains 70 – 80% of para-para isomers, which is the most active fraction of DDT. Has residual action up to 18 months. Used as a residual spray.Least toxic organo-chlorine compound.

HCH (hexachlorocyclo-hexane)
Synthesized by Michael Faraday. Normal HCH contains 13 – 16% of gamma isomer. Gamma-HCH or lindane has 99% gamma isomer.Short residual action – 3 months.

Malathion
Least toxicity of all organophosphorus compounds. Used as an ultra-low volume spray.

Fenthion
Also called baytex. Used as a residual spray.

Pyrethrum
Vegetable origin – Chrysanthemum cinerariafolium. Nerve poison and is excellent as a space spray.No residual action.Synergistic action with DDT as space spray.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: At what point in time is the population assessed for calculation of crude death rate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1st July

Crude death rate is a mortality indicator, which uses the mid-year population as its denominator. The mid year population is always attributed as population on 1st July of any year.

Pearl PF0954: Crude Death Rate

Crude death rate:

* The crude death rate is the simplest measure of mortality.

* It is the number of deaths (from all causes) per 1000 estimated mid-year population in one year, in a given place.

* Crude death rate =  (Number of deaths per year)/(Mid-year population) x 1000

* Disadvantage: lacks comparability for communities with populations that differ in age, sex, race, etc.

* Currently, the crude death rate in India is 6.3.

Note: Crude death rate according to SRS in the year 2018 is 6.2

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the given logo below?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Bureau of Indian Standards

The given logo is of the Bureau of Indian Standards.

BIS is the National Standard Body of India established under the BIS Act 2016 for the harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods.

BIS has been providing traceability and tangibility benefits to the national economy in a number of ways – providing safe reliable quality goods; minimizing health hazards to consumers; promoting export and import substitutes; controlling over proliferation of varieties etc. through standardization, certification and testing.

Other options:

Option A: The Food Corporation of India implements the objectives of the National Food Policy:

* Effective price support operations for safeguarding the interests of poor farmers

* Distribution of foodgrains throughout the country for Public Distribution System (PDS)

* Maintaining a satisfactory level of operational and buffer stocks of foodgrains to ensure National Food Security

* Regulate market price to provide foodgrains to consumers at a reliable price

Option C: AGMARK is a certification mark employed on agricultural products in India, assuring that they conform to a set of standards approved by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection, an agency of the Government of India.

Option D: Goods and Services Tax (GST) is an indirect tax (or consumption tax) used in India on the supply of goods and services. It is a comprehensive, multistage, destination-based tax.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the type of study from the following design:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Case control study

The above study design is typical of a Case control study.

* A case control study uses individuals as the unit.

* The study proceeds from effect to cause and is done after the exposure and outcome have occurred.

* This is the first approach to test causal hypothesis and uses controls to support or refute an inference.

* A nested case control study is a case control study nested in a cohort study and it is a type of cohort study which moves in the forward direction.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a triage system, highest priority and dead patients are respectively colour coded by
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Red and black

Highest priority patients are coded red and dead patients are coded black.

* Triage consists of rapidly classifying the injured on the basis of the severity of their injuries and the likelihood of their survival with prompt medical intervention.

* Triage is the only approach that can provide maximum benefit to the greatest number of injured in a major disaster situation.

Pearl PF1015: Triage Colour Coding

Triage system consists of four colour codes:

Color code

Red

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Komal, a 2-year-old girl is brought to the clinic with a high fever, cough, red eyes, and rash. Parents say that the rash started on the forehead and behind the ears, then subsequently spread to the neck and body. On examination, a confluent maculopapular rash is noted as shown below. Which of the following is false regarding this child's condition?
options: The period of infectivity is 3 days before and 5 days after the appearance of rash
The most common cause of death is subacute sclerosing panencephalitis
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. The most common cause of death is subacute sclerosing panencephalitis

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of measles. The most common cause of death is pneumonia (Hecht's giant cell pneumonia).

Measles (rubeola) is caused by RNA paramyxovirus. The infection is spread via droplets, with a secondary attack rate ≥of 90%. The patients are infectious from 3 days before to 5 days after the appearance of the rash. The rash appears on the 4th day of the fever. It starts from the retro auricular region. Koplik spots and Warthin–Finkeldey giant cells are pathognomonic.

Measles can lead to subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) as a late complication.

Measles can be prevented by administering live attenuated, Edmonston–Zagreb strain or combined MMR given at 9 months of age.

Pearl PF0095: Viral infections associated with rash

Viral infection
Rash characteristics

Chickenpox
Appears 1st day of fever, centripetal, pleomorphic, dewdrops on rose petal appearance

Measles
Appears on the 4th day over the face and retroauricular origin

Rubella
Rash on day 1 over the face

Erythema infectiosum

Rash on cheeks (slapped cheek appearance), moves to trunk and extremities

Exanthem subitum
Macules or maculopapular rash

Infectious mononucleosis
Associated with maculopapular rash

Pearl PF0096: Skin rashes: 1st to 6th diseases

1st disease

Measles

2nd disease

Scarlet fever

3rd disease

Rubella

4th disease

Duke’s disease

5th disease

Erythema infectiosum

6th disease

Roseola infantum

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: New Cholera which is a notifiable disease, should be reported to World Health Organisation within ?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 24 hours

Cholera is notifiable to the WHO by the National Government within 24 hours of its occurrence.

The number of cases and deaths due to cholera are to be reported daily and weekly till the area is declared free of cholera.

An area is declared free of cholera when twice the incubation period, 10 days, has elapsed since the death, recovery, or isolation of the last case.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The best way to plot the changes in the incidence of a disease in a given area is by:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Line graph

Line graphs or line diagrams are the best way to plot the changes in the incidence of a disease in a given area.

Pearl PF0302: Graphical Representation of Data

1. Histogram

* A histogram, by definition, is a graphical representation of frequency distribution that contains rectangles and shows the underlying frequency of a set of continuous, quantitative data.

* The X or horizontal axis is called the abscissa which usually has the group scores or class intervals of the variables/data and the Y or vertical axis is called the ordinate which usually shows the frequencies at which these variables appear.

* The following is a histogram of cholesterol levels from the Framingham Heart Study.

2. Bar Chart

* It is also called a bar graph.

* It is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data as they are not quantitative and usually qualitative.

* The difference between a bar graph and a histogram is that the rectangles are separated by spaces representing data that forms discrete categories instead of continuous groups.

* Bar graphs can be simple, multiple or component bar graphs.

3. Pie Charts

* Pie charts are also used for nominal or ordinal data.

* The categorical data are represented as segments of a circle.

4. Frequency polygons

* Frequency polygons are used for mainly ratio and interval scale data.

* In a frequency polygon, the mid-points of each class interval are joined together by straight lines.

5. Ogive

* A frequency polygon which is drawn to represent cumulative frequency distributions form a typical S-shaped curve which is called an ogive. It referred to as a cumulative frequency diagram.

6. Line chart

* It is also called a line diagram or line graph.

* Its best use is to show the trend of events or change over passage of time.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: There has been a gradual decrease in the number of polio cases as compared to the previous years. This trend is called _____
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Secular

* The secular trend describes the occurrence of disease over a prolonged period, usually years.

* Even though it may have short term fluctuations, there is a tendency of the disease occurrence to change consistently in a particular direction or a definite movement in one direction.

* The secular trend is influenced by the degree of immunity in the population and possibly nonspecific measures such as improved socioeconomic and nutritional levels among the population.

* The examples of secular trend includes, coronary heart disease, lungcancer and diabetes, which have shown a consistent upward tren in incidence as well as prevalence, in the developed countries in the past 50 years.

* Similarly there has been a consistent decline in the diseases such as tuberculosis, typhoidfever, diphtheria, and polio.

Other options:

* Option a: Seasonal trend: This trend reflects seasonal changes in disease occurrence following changes in environmental conditions that enhance the ability of the agent to replicate or be transmitted.

* Option b: Cyclic trends: Some diseases occurs in cycles spread over short periods of time which may be, days, weeks, months or years.

* Option c: Periodic trend: It includes both seasonal and cyclic trends.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is used to obtain consensus forecasts among a large number of people?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Delphi method

Delphi method is a systematic interactive forecasting method, which is used to obtain a consensus forecast, i.e., to determine the degree of agreement on a topic. This can help in setting priorities or selecting alternatives in planning. This method uses questionnaires, which are answered by experts in two or more rounds.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following foods has the least iron content?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Milk

The least iron content among the given foods is in milk.

The iron content of milk is low in all mammalian species(iron content of breast milk is around 0.2 mg/dl, which is well utilized).

There are two forms of iron:

1. Haem-iron which is better absorbed than non-haem iron is seen in liver, meat, poultry, and fish.

2. Foods containing non-haem iron are those of vegetable origin- cereals, green leafy vegetables, legumes, nuts, oilseeds, jaggery, and dried fruits.

The bioavailability of non-haem iron is poor owing to the presence of phytates, oxalates, carbonates, phosphates, and dietary fiber which interfere with iron
absorption.

Other foods that inhibit iron absorption are milk, eggs, and tea.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is helpful in predicting the virulence of a disease?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Case fatality rate

The case fatality rate represents the killing power (or virulence) of the disease.

Case fatality rate = Total number of deaths due to a particular disease X 100 / Total number of cases due to the same disease

The case-fatality rate is thus the proportion of people with a particular disease who die from that disease. It is a measure of the severity of the disease, the deadliness of an outbreak, and may be used to evaluate any public health measures implemented.

Due to changes in the agent, host, and environmental factors in different epidemics, the case fatality rate for the same disease may vary in different epidemics. It is typically used in acute infectious diseases. Eg: Food poisoning, measles, cholera, etc.

The case-fatality rate is not a true rate, but actually a proportion. Hence, the term case-fatality ratio is often preferred.

Pearl PF0955: Case Fatality Rate

* Case fatality rate =  (Total number of deaths due to a particular disease)/(Total number of cases due to the same disease)x 100

* It is a good indicator of severity or killing power of a disease.

* It is used mostly in acute and infectious diseases.

* No time interval is used.

* Case fatality rate is closely related to virulence.

* Limitation of CFR is that its usefulness for chronic diseases is limited because the period from onset to death is variable.

* It is expressed in percentage.

* CFR is an incidence proportion and not a true rate.

* CFR may vary for the same disease in different epidemics.

*

Case fatality of a few diseases:

* Rabies - 100% especially after symptoms manifest

* Ebola - 25 to 90%, average - 50%

* Yellow fever - 15 to 50%

* Chicken pox - 0.001%

* Diseases with a high case fatality rate: Tetanus, Rabies, Botulism, Ebola.

* Diseases with a low case fatality rate: Leprosy, Trachoma, Lymphatic filariasis.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the ultimate desired state towards which objectives and resources are directed?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Goal

Goal is the ultimate desired state towards which objectives and resources are directed. It is not constrained by time or resources.

Objective is the planned end point of all activities. It is a precise point. Whereas, target refers to a discrete activity and permits the concept of degree of achievement.

Mission describes the cause of existence of the programme.

Plan is a blueprint for taking action.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements is false regarding the given image?
options: It is inserted by withdrawal technique
The copper in this device has a surface area of 380 square mm
It is used in emergency contraception
It has a life-span of 5 years
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. It has a life-span of 5 years

The given image is CuT 380 A as it has copper in both the stem as well as the horizontal arms and it has the highest life span of 10 years.

Copper T-380A (Paragard):

It is named so for the 380 mm2 of copper surface area. A higher surface area of copper results in higher contraceptive efficacy.

It has a plastic T-shaped core with copper placed around the vertical stem and horizontal arms. A silver core within the copper sheath is included to prevent fragmentation of the copper, extending the lifespan of the Copper T-380A.

The frame is connected to a monofilament thread that protrudes through the cervical canal into the upper vagina. This facilitates easy removal and allows the user to ensure that the IUD remains in the uterus.

If an IUCD is inserted within 5 days after coitus, it serves as an emergency contraceptive and is more effective than levonorgestrel/ulipristal acetate regimens.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: WHO defines blindness as visual acuity less than ______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 3/60

According to WHO, 'Blindness' is defined as visual acuity of less than 3/60, or a corresponding visual field loss to less than 10°, in the better eye with the best possible correction.

Presenting visual acuity in the range of worse than 6/18 to 6/60 is defined as moderate visual impairment. Presenting visual acuities from 3/60 (including 3/60) to worse than 6/60 is classified as severe visual impairment.

Distance vision impairment:

* Mild –visual acuity worse than 6/12 to 6/18

* Moderate –visual acuity worse than 6/18 to 6/60

* Severe –visual acuity worse than 6/60 to 3/60

* Blindness –visual acuity worse than 3/60

National Programme for the Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI). The levels of eye care, according to NPCBVI are:

* Primary level: Sub-district level hospitals, community health centers, mobile ophthalmic units, upgraded PHCs, link workers, Panchayats.

* Secondary level: District hospitals, NGO eye hospitals

* Tertiary levels: Regional institutes of Ophthalmology, medical colleges.

The goal is to reduce the prevalence of blindness to 0.3% by 2020.

questions.text: A 30-year-old woman presents with complaints of greenish frothy vaginal discharge for 1 month and a burning sensation in her vaginal area for the past 5 days. There is no history of fever. Vitals are within normal limits. On speculum examination, you are able to see the below finding. Which of the following kits would you prescribe to this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Green kit

The given clinical scenario and the image showing  strawberry cervix is suggestive of Trichomoniasis and the green kit containing Tablet Secnidazole 2 gm, to be taken orally as a single dose is recommended in its treatment.

Trichomoniasis: Infection of the female genital tract with the Trichomonas vaginalis protozoan

Trichomoniasis characteristically causes a copious, frothy, offensive yellow-green discharge with vaginal soreness or irritation and urinary frequency.

The vagina looks red and inflamed. The inflamed cervix looks like a strawberry with punctate hemorrhagic spots.

Management: The CDC recommends one of the following treatment regimens.

* Metronidazole 2 g orally in a single dose (Standard treatment) or Secnidazole/Tinidazole 2 g orally in a single dose

* The alternative regimen includes Metronidazole 500 mg orally twice a day for 7 days

* Metronidazole gel does not reach therapeutic levels in the urethra and perivaginal glands. Because it is less efficacious than oral metronidazole, it is not recommended.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A research study is being conducted on patients in rehabilitation where the impact of addiction among young adults was assessed on their subsequent divorce. Among two groups of study subjects, divorced and non-divorced, the history of alcohol or drug use was assessed. What kind of study is being done here?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Case control study

The above study design is typical of a case-control study. Here the divorced group acts as a case study group while the non-divorced group acts as a control group.

* A case-control study uses individuals as the unit.

* The study proceeds from effect to cause and is done after the exposure and outcome have occurred.

* This is the first approach to test causal hypotheses and uses controls to support or refute an inference.

* A nested case-control study is a case-control study nested in a cohort study and it is a type of cohort study which moves in the forward direction.

Pearl PF0958: Types of Epidemiological Study Designs

Types of Epidemiological Study Designs

The flow chart below gives a glance into the types of epidemiological study designs and where they are generally used.

Note: Descripitve study is used to formulate aetiological hypothesis of a disease. Whereas analytical study is used to test the hypothesis (i.e to accept or reject the hypothesis).

Pearl PF1701: Case Control Study

In a case-control study, progression is from effect (disease) to cause (exposure) as the outcome or disease has already occurred. It is also called a retrospective study.

Design of case-control study:

* Steps of case control study:

* Selection of cases and controls

* Matching

* Measurement of exposure

* Analysis in the form of exposure rates, risk ratio, and odds ratio

* Advantages of case control study:

* Easy to carry out, rapid and inexpensive

* Requires few subjects, no risk to subjects

* Used to investigate rare diseases

* Different etiological factors can be studied and risk factors can be identified

* No attrition problems, minimal ethical problems

* Disadvantages of case control study:

* Relies on memory or past records giving rise to bias

* Selection of appropriate control groups is difficult

* Incidence cannot be measured

* Does not distinguish between causes and associated factors

* Not suited for evaluation of therapy or prophylaxis

* Representativeness of the cases and controls is often inadequate

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the image.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Lepromatous leprosy

The given image depicts lepromatous leprosy in the infiltrated stage of the disease.

In lepromatous leprosy, the earliest clinical manifestations are dermal.

The early features include:

* Numerous, ill-defined, shiny macules

* Anhidrosis

* Normal sensation

* Nasal symptoms - stuffiness, discharge, epistaxis

* Peripheral oedema due to capillary stasis

Early nerve involvement is asymptomatic. Peripheral nerves are affected first. In the late stages, even facial and corneal nerves can be involved. Loss of sensation begins as patchy and later becomes extensive. Stocking and glove anesthesia is a late manifestation. The affected skin can become dry and ichthyotic.

The late stage of lepromatous leprosy gives rise to the following features:

* Leonine facies - infiltration of skin folds

* Madarosis - loss of eyelashes eyebrow hair

* Rat-bitten ear - repeated ulceration and healing

* Saddle nose deformity - breakdown of nasal cartilage

Lepromatous leprosy develops in three stages:

* Early macular stage

* Infiltrated stage - induration due to dermal infiltration, marked in face and ear lobe

* Late nodulo-plaque stage - progress to papules, nodules, and plaques, which ulcerate.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a community of 5000, the crude birth rate is 25 per 1000 people. What is the number of pregnant females in this community?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 138

The number of pregnant females is 138.

Step 1: In the given question, the crude birth rate is 25 per 1000 people i.e 25 children are born from pregnant mothers for every 1000 people. Therefore there are 25 pregnant females per 1000 population.

Step 2: Since the total population is 5000, the total no of pregnant females = 25 x 5000/1000 = 125

Step 3: We should also consider the pregnancy wastage i.e 10% of total live births =10 x 125/100=12.5 (since some pregnancies may not result in live birth i.e abortions and stillbirths, a correction factor of 10% is to be added to avoid the underestimation of the number of pregnancies)

Step 4: Total pregnant females = total live birth + pregnancy wastage = 125+12.5=137.5 ,which is rounded off to 138.

Pearl PF1746: Fertility Indicators

Crude birth rate

* It is the simplest measure of fertility although its usage is unsatisfactory

* India, as per SRS bulletin 2018, had a birth rate of 20.0 per 1000 population

General Fertility Rate

* It is a better indicator of fertility than crude birth rate

* The demerit of this indicator is that not all women in the denominator are exposed to childbirth

Age-specific fertility rates is a more precise measure of fertility and is also a sensitive indicator of family planning achievement.

Total Fertility Rate

* It is the sum of all age-specific fertility rates multiplied by 5

* This measure gives the approximate magnitude of completed family size

Gross Reproductive Rate is the average number of girls that would be born to a woman if she experiences the current fertility pattern throughout her reproductive span, assuming no mortality.

Net Reproduction Rate

* It is a demographic indicator

* NRR of 1 is equivalent to approximately the 2 child norm

* If the NRR is less than 1, then the reproductive performance of the population is said to be inadequate

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a village with a given population, the total number of live births in a year is 4000. 40 newborns died within the first 7 days of life whereas 40 died due to various causes between 8 to 28 days of life. There were 50 deaths between the age of 1 month to 6 months of life and 30 of them died in utero. What is the neonatal mortality rate in this population?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 20

Neonatal mortality rate = Number of deaths of children under 28 days of age in a year x 1000/Total live births in the same year

The total live births in this scenario is = 4000 live births.

NMR = (40+40) x 1000/4000 = 20.

Note: Still births and deaths after 28 days of life are not considered in Neonatal Mortality Rate.

Correct answer: A. NHM

In Integrated child development services (ICDS), intersectoral coordination is seen with NHM(National Health Mission).

The ICDS overlaps with many of the programs of NHM of which the Anemia Mukt Bharat Scheme  is an example, where prophylactic iron and folic acid is given to children, adolescents, women of reproductive age, and pregnant women, irrespective of anemia

ICDS:

The blueprint for the scheme was prepared by the Department of Social Welfare in 1975. The Government of India decided to expand the project to cover 100 areas by 1978-79. Two major evaluations were conducted in 1978and 1982. The positive results of these evaluations formed the basis for the government's decision to accelerate the expansion of ICDS in 1982.

NACO(National AIDS Control Organization): prevents the transmission of HIV,  decreases the morbidity and mortality associated with it and minimize the socio-economic impact resulting from it.

NLEP(National Leprosy Eradication Programme) : is a centrally sponsored Health Scheme of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Govt. of India.

UNDP (United Nations Development Programme): It is the main source of funds for technical assistance. Its main objective is to help poorer nations develop their human and natural resources to their potential.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In rural areas, one ASHA worker is assigned to a population of ___ people.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1000

In rural areas, a population of 1000 should have at least 1 ASHA.

An Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) does not procure ORS, contraceptives, IFA tablets, etc. from the CHC for her community.

An ASHA acts as a depot holder for these essential supplies, hence making them readily available to her community. These include Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORS), Iron Folic Acid tablets (IFA), chloroquine, Disposable Delivery Kits (DDK), Oral Pills & Condoms, etc.

General norm:

* Must be a woman - married/divorced/widow (age group 25-45 years)

* Must be a resident of that village

* Formal education of up to 10th standard

* At least 1 ASHA for a population of 1000.

Relaxations in the general norm:

* If no candidate is available with a qualification of 10th standard, the requirement can be relaxed to 8th standard.

* In tribal, hilly, and desert areas, the norm can be relaxed to 1 ASHA per habitation.

Note: The States have been given the flexibility to relax the population norms as well as the educational qualifications on a case-to-case basis, depending on the local conditions as far as her recruitment is concerned. However, these are exceptions and not the general norm.

Pearl PF0294: ASHA

ASHA is an Accredited Social Health Activist.

An ASHA must be a woman, a resident of the village, 25 to 45 years old and have a formal education till 10th standard preferably if they are in good numbers. This may be relaxed upto 8th standard only if no suitable person with this qualification is available. She is part of the primary health care at the village level.

National norm: In rural areas, a population of 1000 should have at least 1 ASHA, but in remote areas, one ASHA per habitation is the norm. In urban areas, 1 ASHA worker is assigned to a population of 1000-2500. This norm is also mandated by each state, differently, according to their requirements.

Responsibilities of ASHA:

* Health education and awareness

* Reproductive and child health and family planning

* Facilitate the access to health services

* Promotion of sanitation and household toilet construction

* Provision of primary medical care for minor ailments

* Provider of DOTS

* Depot holder of essentials like ORS, iron and folic acid tablets, condoms, disposable delivery kits, etc.

* Dispersal of health information on her community to higher centres

* Some responsibilities are integrated with Anganwadi workers and Auxiliary Nurse Midwife

questions.text: In the following flowchart representing natural history of disease, The duration between point A to B is called as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Screening time

The period between the first possible time of detection (point A) and the first critical point of diagnosis (point B) is called Screening time.

The period between the first possible time of detection (point A) and the usual time of diagnosis (point C) is called lead time.

Pearl PF0975: Lead Time in Screening

Lead time is the advantage gained by screening which is the period between diagnosis by early detection and diagnosis by other means.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. National Planning Commission (NPC)

The government of India has established NITI (National Institution for Transforming India) Aayog to replace The National Planning Commission on 1st January 2015.

NITI Aayog will seek to provide a critical directional and strategic input into the development process.  It will provide Governments at the central and state, with relevant strategic and technical advice across the spectrum of key elements of policy.

Objectives:

*

evolve a shared vision of national development priorities, sectors, and strategies with the active involvement of States and foster cooperative federalism between states.

*

develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate these progressively at higher levels of government.

*

ensure that the interests of national security are incorporated in economic strategy and policy.

*

pay special attention to the sections of our society that may be at risk of not benefiting adequately from economic progress.

*

provide advice and encourage partnerships between key stakeholders and national and international like-minded think tanks, as well as educational and policy research institutions.

*

create a knowledge, innovation, and entrepreneurial support system through a collaborative community of national and international experts, practitioners, and other partners.

*

offer a platform for the resolution of inter-sectoral and inter departmental issues in order to accelerate the implementation of the development agenda.

*

maintain a state-of-the-art resource center, be a repository of research on good governance and best practices in sustainable and equitable development.

*

monitor and evaluate the implementation of programs and initiatives, including the identification of the needed resources so as to strengthen the probability of success and scope of delivery.

*

focus on technology up-gradation and capacity building for the implementation of programs and initiatives.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Positive predictive value is most affected by _____
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Prevalence

If the prevalence of a disease in a population is high, the more accurate will be the positive predictive value of a screening test.

If the prevalence declines, the PPV will be low.

Predictive value is affected the most by prevalence. However, both sensitivity and specificity can change the predictive value.

Pearl PF0045: Validity of a Screening Test

* Validity/ Accuracy of a screening test depends upon the sensitivity, specificity, and predictive accuracy of the test.

* It represents the closeness to a true value/ actual value.

* These are the inherent properties of a screening test.

* PPV and NPV are dependent on the Prevalence of disease.

* Sensitivity & Speciifity are independent of prevalence of disease.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Revised A nurse got an accidental prick from a needle used for an HIV+ patient. Which single test would lead to a confirmatory diagnosis in her?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Western blot assay

The single test that would lead to a confirmatory diagnosis in this patient is Western blot assay.

The Western blot assay detects specific antibodies against various HIV proteins in the patient's blood sample. It is considered highly specific and is used to confirm the presence of HIV antibodies after a positive screening test, such as an ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay). The Western blot assay helps differentiate between true HIV infection and false-positive results that may occur with screening tests.

ELISA even though is done as a 2-test protocol, one single test is not considered a positive case. The two-test protocol for the diagnosis of HIV needs two ELISA tests to be positive. (i.e. If the initial ELISA is positive, a second ELISA is carried out. If the second ELISA is also positive, only then, the case is reported to be positive).

Investigations involved in HIV testing strategies:

* ELISA/ rapid tests

* Confirmatory tests with high specificity like Western Blot and line immunoassays are used in indeterminate/ discordant cases of rapid tests.

In India, NACO provides Western Blot Confirmatory testing only to resolve indeterminate results on previous serological testing and not for routine confirmation after a positive result on screening tests. The drawbacks of Western Blot include low rates of detection during acute HIV infection and misclassification of HIV-2 infection.

Other options:

p24 antigen:

* The p24 antigen is a viral protein that is detectable in the blood during the early stages of HIV infection.

* It can be detected within a few days to a few weeks after infection before antibodies are produced.

* While a positive p24 antigen test suggests HIV infection, it is not considered a confirmatory test on its own and is often used in combination with other tests.

PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction):

* PCR is a sensitive molecular test that can detect the genetic material (RNA or DNA) of the HIV virus in a person's blood.

* It can detect HIV at an early stage, even before antibodies are produced.

* PCR is commonly used for early diagnosis in infants born to HIV-positive mothers or in cases where early detection is crucial, such as occupational exposures.

HIV ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay):

* The ELISA is a screening test that detects antibodies produced by the immune system in response to HIV infection.

* It is highly sensitive and widely used as an initial test for HIV.

* However, a positive ELISA result needs to be confirmed by additional tests, such as the Western blot assay, to differentiate between true infection and false-positive results.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The full form of the Urban HEART programme is __.
options: Urban Health Equity Assessment and Response Tool
Urban Health Evaluation Assessment and Response Tool
Urban Health Equity Assessment and Response Technique
Urban Health Evaluation Assessment and Response Technique
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Urban Health Equity Assessment and Response Tool

Urban HEART stands for Urban Health Equity Assessment and Response Tool and facilitates the process of addressing health inequities across the world.

Urban HEART guides local policymakers and communities through a standardized procedure of gathering relevant evidence and planning efficiently for appropriate actions to tackle health inequities.

Three main approaches applied to measure and tackle inequities in health are:

* targeting disadvantaged population groups or social classes

* narrowing the health gap

* reducing inequities throughout the whole population.

Core elements of Urban HEART:

* sound evidence

* intersectoral action for health

* community participation

Urban HEART is expected to achieve the following:

* local and national authorities equipped with relevant evidence to inform important decisions related to prioritization and resource allocation

* communities mobilized and empowered to promote health equity

* multiple sectors engaged in addressing common goals, including the promotion of health equity

* people living in cities with better health and social status, and reduced inequities in health between population groups.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The students of a boarding school eat from the same canteen. One of the students developed abdominal pain, jaundice, and fever following which other students also presented with similar symptoms. Which of the following investigations should the Medical Officer of the area check for to reach a diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. IgM for Hepatitis A

The given scenario is of a Hepatitis A outbreak that is spread via the fecal-oral route and the investigation of choice is IgM for Hepatitis A.

Hepatitis A:

Modes of transmission

* Fecal-oral route: This is the major route of transmission. It can occur directly (handshake after toilet) or indirectly via contaminated food, water, or milk.

* Parenteral route: This is very rare and occurs during the viral dissemination phase. It occurs during the prodromal phase and not when patients are symptomatic and admitted to the hospital. As a result, healthcare workers are not at increased risk.

* Sexual transmission may occur in individuals practicing oro-anal methods (usually homosexual men). It however would not cause an outbreak.

Incubation period:

* 10 to 50 days (usually 14-28 days). Isolation is not an effective measure to control outbreaks as the shedding of the virus is maximum during the early stages of illness when clinical illness may not have started and many patients are asymptomatic yet continue to shed the virus.

Clinical spectrum:

* The onset of jaundice is preceded by gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, anorexia, and mild fever.

* Jaundice may appear within a few days of the prodromal period, but anicteric hepatitis is more common.

* Hepatitis A resolves completely in 98 percent of cases but relapse of symptoms is noted in 3-20 percent of cases

Diagnosis:

* Laboratory diagnosis of hepatitis A can be obtained by

* Demonstration of HAV particles or specific viral antigens in the feces, bile, and blood.

* Anti-HAV appears in the lgM fraction during the acute phase, peaking about 2 weeks after the elevation of liver enzymes. ELISA is the method of choice for measuring HAV antibodies.

Prevention and containment:

* Control of reservoir: Use of 0.5 percent sodium hypochlorite has been strongly recommended as an effective disinfectant

* Control of transmission: personal and community hygiene. Hand hygiene before food and after the toilet is highly recommended.

* 1 mg/L of free residual chlorine can cause the destruction of the virus in 30 minutes at pH values of 8.5 or less. Hence adequate chlorination can be helpful.

* Patients with chronic liver disease are at increased risk for fulminant hepatitis A and should be vaccinated. The use of the hepatitis A vaccine should be considered for pre-exposure(for travelers) and post-exposure(close contacts of affected individuals)prophylaxis.
