questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The thickness of lead apron to prevent radiation is?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 0.5mm

The thickness of lead apron is 0.5mm. They will reduce the intensity of scattered X-rays by over 90% and shud be worn by all workers regularly associated with X-ray procedures.

Lead is the most common agent used in modern construction because of it's ability to provide radiation shielding. Lead can effectively attenuate certain kinds of radiation because of its high density and atomic number.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: There is a group of 200 hypertensive patients. First group of 100 patients is given medical advice whereas a second group of 100 patients is advised lifestyle changes. Which of the following tests of significance is used to compare the blood pressure after 3 months ?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Un- paired t test

The unpaired t-test is used to test the difference between two groups or means when the samples are independent of each other. Here, the blood pressure of the two groups who are given different interventions is being compared, which are independent of each other.

Pearl PF0591: Tests of Significance

How to choose which test to use?

* See the variable. Are the variables quantitative or qualitative?

* If the variables are qualitative (nominal), then Chi square test is used.

* If the variables are quantitative, then see whether 2 groups are being tested, or more than 2 groups.

* If 2 groups are being tested, then T tests are used. In that, if the same group is tested before and after, paired T test is used. Otherwise, unpaired T test is used.

* If more than 2 groups are being tested, then use ANOVA.

The tests:

1. T Tests

* Unpaired t tests

* Also known as the student’s t test, independent t test, two-samples t test.

* It's the most commonly used t test and it tests the difference between two groups (the means of 2 groups) independent of each other and indicates how significant the differences are.

* Paired t tests

* "Pairs before marriage are not the same after!"

* So remember paired test is mainly used in comparison of a before and after scenario

* Also known as correlated t test, dependent samples t test.

* It is mainly used on dependent samples For example, the cholesterol level of a person before and after using a specific drug.

* It can also be used when you put the same condition under test using different items or things. For example, same crash safety tests for different cars.

* T scores

* The t score is referred to as the ratio of the difference between two groups and the difference within the groups.

* The smaller the t score, the more similarity there is between two groups and vice versa.

2. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)

* The analysis of variance test (ANOVA) is used to test the difference between two or usually more than two groups (means) and here the inferences are made by analyzing the variances.

3. Chi-Square Test

* The Chi-Square test (χ2) is a non-parametric(non-numeric) test and it is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.

* It is a test of proportions and associations.

* A Chi-square distribution is usually positively skewed but it approaches a normal distribution as its degrees of freedom increases.

* If the frequency of any of the cells of the categorical table is <5, then Fisher’s exact test is used.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which agency collects data and publishes large scale surveys continuously regarding morbidity, family planning, vital events?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. National Sample Survey

The National Sample Survey collects data and publishes large-scale surveys continuously regarding morbidity, family planning, vital events.

The National Sample Survey(NSS), headed by a Director-General, is responsible for the conduct of large-scale sample surveys in diverse fields all over India.

Data are collected through national household surveys on various socio-economic subjects. Besides these surveys, NSS collects data on rural and urban prices and plays a significant role in the improvement of crop statistics through supervision of the area enumeration and crop estimation surveys of the State agencies.  It also maintains a frame of urban area units for use in sample surveys in urban areas.

The four types of survey methods are :

* Health interview (face-to-face) survey

* Health examination survey

* Health records survey

* Mailed questionnaire survey

The cause of death is noted by the Sample registration system (SRS), the Death certificate, and via lay reporting

Other Options:

Option A: Civil Registration System also known as Vital Registration System, is managed under the Ministry of Home Affairs by the Office of the Registrar General of India. Birth and death registration in India is undertaken by this system and is registered within 21 days.

Option C: Sample Registration System, a Biannual system conducted every 6 months, and assess indicators such as crude birth rate, death rate, Infant mortality rate, Maternal mortality rate, and so on.

Option D: Central Bureau of Health functions as the national health data repository, responsible for the collection, analysis, and dissemination of health statistics to support evidence-based policy and planning.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following diseases are included in the scheme, which has the logo as given below?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. CVD, Cancer, Diabetes, Stroke

The logo shows the NPCDCS scheme that has separate components for cancer and other non-communicable diseases like diabetes, cardiovascular disease and stroke.

The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS) has specialized facilities in district hospitals.

It has been implemented in over 100 districts in 21 states.

At the subcentre level under NPCDCS, screening and referral is done.

NOTE: Non-alcoholic fattly liver disease (NAFLD) has been integrated with NPCDCS in 2021.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following fertility indicator can change with changes in age-specific mortality rates?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Net reproduction rate

Net reproduction rate can change with changes in age-specific mortality rates. General fertility rate, total fertility rate, and gross reproduction rate are not dependent on age-specific mortality rate.

Net reproduction rate (NRR) is defined as the number of daughters a newborn girl will bear during her lifetime assuming fixed age-specific fertility and mortality rate.

India is aiming for an NRR of 1 as it is equivalent to the two-child norm. If the NRR is less than 1, then the population growth of a community is said to be inadequate.

Pearl PF1746: Fertility Indicators

Crude birth rate

* It is the simplest measure of fertility although its usage is unsatisfactory

* India, as per SRS bulletin 2018, had a birth rate of 20.0 per 1000 population

General Fertility Rate

* It is a better indicator of fertility than crude birth rate

* The demerit of this indicator is that not all women in the denominator are exposed to childbirth

Age-specific fertility rates is a more precise measure of fertility and is also a sensitive indicator of family planning achievement.

Total Fertility Rate

* It is the sum of all age-specific fertility rates multiplied by 5

* This measure gives the approximate magnitude of completed family size

Gross Reproductive Rate is the average number of girls that would be born to a woman if she experiences the current fertility pattern throughout her reproductive span, assuming no mortality.

Net Reproduction Rate

* It is a demographic indicator

* NRR of 1 is equivalent to approximately the 2 child norm

* If the NRR is less than 1, then the reproductive performance of the population is said to be inadequate

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is a rabies free area ?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Lakshadweep

In the following options, Lakshadweep is a rabies-free state as water is a natural barrier to rabies.

Rabies occurs in more than 150 countries and territories. A number of carnivorous and bat species serve as natural reservoirs and dogs are the primary sources of infection.

While some countries have achieved "rabies-free" status by vigorous campaigns of elimination, in others the disease has never been introduced. A "Rabies-free"
area has been defined as one in which no case of indigenously acquired rabies has occurred in man or any animal species for 2 years.

Geographic boundaries seem to play an important role here. Water appears to be the most effective natural barrier to rabies.

In India, the Union Territory of Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar islands are free of the disease. Other areas of the world include Australia, China, Taiwan, Cyprus, Iceland, Ireland, Japan, Malta, New Zealand, the U.K., and the islands of the Western Pacific.

Note: A recent initiative by the Worldwide Veterinary Services called the  'Mission Rabies Project' is ongoing in the state of Goa and other parts of India to eradicate the disease. On June 23, 2021 the state of Goa declared that they have not reported a single case of rabies in the past 3 years.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Zika virus is transmitted by:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Aedes aegypti

Zika virus may be transmitted by the bite of infected Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus.

The symptoms of Zika virus disease include fever, rash, conjunctivitis, muscle and joint pain, malaise, or headache. These symptoms are mild and usually last for 2-7 days.

It can spread via:

* Mosquito bites

* Bloodstream

* Unsafe sexual practices

* Vertical transmission

Zika virus infection during pregnancy may lead to microcephaly or congenital Zika syndrome.

The complications include:

* Guillain-Barré syndrome

* Encephalitis

* Meningitis

* Myelitis

* Life span of mosquitoes is around 8 to 34 days.

* Their morphology consists of a head with a proboscis, a pair of palpi and a pair of antennae; a thorax and an abdomen.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A couple has given birth to their first child. Based on the nuclear family cycle, which phase is the family entering into?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Extension

The phase of a nuclear family cycle from the birth of their first child to the birth of their last child is called extension.

Pearl PF0595: The Family as a Social Organization

* A family is a group of biologically related individuals living together under the same roof and eating from a common kitchen.

* It is the most primary and basic unit of all societies.

* The basic and arbitrary model of a family cycle has six phases:

* Types of families:

* A nuclear family or elementary family consists of only the married couple and their offspring while they are dependants.

* The term new family is applied when nuclear families are younger than 10 years and consist of parents and children.

* A joint family or extended family consists of a number of married couples and their children who live together in the same household with usually the men being related by blood. All property in joint families is held in common with the family income going into a common pocket. A senior male member is usually the head of the family who makes decisions.

* A three generation family is one where there are representatives from three different generations in one house.

* A communal family is one in which all the members play a part in its management.

* Functions of the family:

* Residence (patrilocal and matrilocal)

* Division of labour

* Reproduction and raising children

* Socialization and social care

* Economic functions

* Problems families are those that lag behind the rest of the community in terms of standard and quality of life of its members.

* Broken families are those in which the parental or family system has been disrupted by separation, divorce or death.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A diabetic patient comes to you for advice regarding his diet. You advise him to include foods with a low glycemic index in the diet. Which of the following would you advise him for the same?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Papaya

The patient should be advised to take papaya since it has a low glycemic index.

The Glycemic index (GI) is the area under the two-hour blood glucose response curve (AUC) following ingestion of a fixed portion of test carbohydrate as a proportion of the AUC of the standard (glucose or white bread).

The classification of foods according to Glycemic index (GI) is as follows,

* Low GI foods (GI = 55 or less): Most fruits and vegetables (except potatoes, watermelon, and sweet corn), whole grains, pasta foods, beans, and lentils.

* Moderate GI foods (GI = 56 to 69): Sucrose, basmati rice, and brown rice.

* High GI foods (GI = 70 or more): Corn flakes, baked potatoes, white bread, candies, and syrupy foods.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A patient presents to an ESI hospital for treatment. Under the ESI Act, he/she is treated under which benefit ?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Medical benefit

Under the ESI Act, medical benefit is not given as a cash benefit. It is provided in the form of consultations, investigations and treatment by means of the ESI hospitals or ESI dispensaries.

Pearl PF0292: ESI ACT, 1948

Scope: It is applicable to all factories in India excluding

* Defense

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study to determine the association between maternal smoking during pregnancy and low birth weight is being carried out. It involves obtaining smoking histories from pregnant women during their antenatal visits and then subsequently assessing the birth weight of their babies soon after delivery. What type of study is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Prosprective Cohort

The study of choice is a prospective cohort study.

A prospective cohort study is a study in which the outcome has not yet occurred at the time that the investigations begin. They begin in the present and continue into the future.

This study is a prospective cohort study because the subjects (pregnant women) were categorized on the basis of exposure or lack of exposure to a risk factor -smoking during pregnancy. They were followed to determine if the outcome- the low birth weight of the babies occurred or not.

The design of a prospective cohort is shown below.

A retrospective cohort study is when both the exposure and outcome have occurred before the investigations and study is undertaken. An example would be if the charts in a hospital from the previous year were reviewed, and mothers classified as smokers or nonsmokers based on records. The records are then followed through time and then the birth weight of the children in both groups are compared. It is also called a historical cohort study, a prospective study in retrospect, or a non-concurrent prospective study.

In a case-control study of the same, low birth weight infants would be selected as the cases and normal birth weight babies as the controls. The frequency of maternal smoking would then be compared in the two groups.

In cross-sectional studies, exposure and outcome are measured at the same point in time.

Pearl PF0220: Cohort Study

* A cohort study progresses from cause to effect, as exposure has occured but not disease.

* It is also known as forward-looking study, incidence study, prospective study, and longitudinal study.

* Design of a Cohort Study

* Types

* Prospective cohort studies (concurrent cohort studies)

* Retrospective cohort studies (historical cohort study)

* Combination cohort studies

* Steps

questions.text: According to the biomedical waste disposal guidelines, the used cotton swabs should be disposed of in the __ colored bag.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Yellow

The used cotton swabs are disposed of in the yellow-coloured bags after use.

The biomedical waste management rule applies to all those who collect, receive, store, dispose and treat biomedical waste. The wastes are categorised and segregated at the point of generation of waste. A colour coding system with 4 colours namely yellow, red, white, and blue is used for waste segregation.

The segregated waste is then disposed of by various methods. They are:

* Incineration - this is a dry oxidation process done using high temperatures. The types are rotary kiln, pyrolytic incinerator, and single chamber incinerator.

* Chemical disinfection - chemicals are added to waste to kill or inactivate the microorganisms. Mostly used for treating liquid wastes.

* Wet and dry thermal treatment - shredded infectious waste is exposed to high temperature, high-pressure steam and it resembles an autoclave sterilization process.

* Microwave irradiation - microorganisms are killed using high-frequency microwaves. Its efficiency should be checked routinely.

* Land disposal - either municipal disposal sites or sanitary landfills are used.

* Inertization - waste is mixed with cement and other substances before disposal to reduce toxicity.

Disposal by deep burial is permitted only in rural areas that lack common bio-medical treatment facilities. Permission from the concerned authority is needed and guidelines issued by the central pollution control board should be followed.

Cytotoxic and biohazard materials will have separate non-washable and visible symbols as shown below:

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to WHO, what is the minimum number of antenatal visits?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 8

According to WHO, the minimum number of antenatal visits is 8.

The WHO increased the minimum number of antenatal visits from 4 to 8 visits to reduce perinatal mortality.

WHO suggests the first visit at 12 weeks of gestation followed by visits at 20,26,30,34,36,38,40 weeks of gestation.

The ideal number of antenatal visits is 12-14.

The antenatal visits should ideally be:

* From 36 weeks - Weekly

* From 28-36 weeks - Two weekly

* From 28 weeks - Monthly

Note:

The minimum number of antenatal visits according to MCH(Maternal and Child Health Program) is 4.

The vitamin A dose for an 8 months old baby with clinical signs of deficiency is 100,000 IU orally.

Treatment of children with Vit A deficiency:

* 100,000 IU orally or 50,000 IU IM for a child < 12 months and

* 200,000 IU of vitamin A orally or 100,000 IU by intramuscular injection for a child above 12 months.

The same dose of Vitamin A is repeated the next day and on the 14th day.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During your rural posting, you are asked to educate a small, uneducated village about the importance of routine antenatal care for pregnant mothers. You want to deliver some statistical data to emphasize its importance. Which of the following is the best way to do so?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pictogram

Pictogram is the best method of presenting data among people, who cannot understand orthodox charts.

In this method, small pictures or symbols are used to present the data. Fractions of the picture are used to represent numbers smaller than the value of a whole symbol. Basically, pictograms are a form of bar charts.

Other options

Option B- Line diagrams are mainly used to show the trend of events in a given period of time. For example trend of dengue cases in Asia during 2018-21.

Option C- Histogram is a pictorial diagram of a frequency distribution that consists of a series of blocks. The frequencies are given along the vertical axis and class intervals on the horizontal axis. The area of each block obtained is proportional to frequency.

Option D- Frequency polygon is the diagrammatical representation of frequency distribution obtained by joining the midpoints of the histogram blocks.

Pearl PF0302: Graphical Representation of Data

1. Histogram

* A histogram, by definition, is a graphical representation of frequency distribution that contains rectangles and shows the underlying frequency of a set of continuous, quantitative data.

* The X or horizontal axis is called the abscissa which usually has the group scores or class intervals of the variables/data and the Y or vertical axis is called the ordinate which usually shows the frequencies at which these variables appear.

* The following is a histogram of cholesterol levels from the Framingham Heart Study.

2. Bar Chart

* It is also called a bar graph.

* It is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data as they are not quantitative and usually qualitative.

* The difference between a bar graph and a histogram is that the rectangles are separated by spaces representing data that forms discrete categories instead of continuous groups.

* Bar graphs can be simple, multiple or component bar graphs.

3. Pie Charts

* Pie charts are also used for nominal or ordinal data.

* The categorical data are represented as segments of a circle.

4. Frequency polygons

* Frequency polygons are used for mainly ratio and interval scale data.

* In a frequency polygon, the mid-points of each class interval are joined together by straight lines.

5. Ogive

* A frequency polygon which is drawn to represent cumulative frequency distributions form a typical S-shaped curve which is called an ogive. It referred to as a cumulative frequency diagram.

6. Line chart

* It is also called a line diagram or line graph.

* Its best use is to show the trend of events or change over passage of time.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: For a population of 10,000, what does a sex ratio of more than 1000 mean?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Males are less than 5000

For a population of 10000, if the sex ratio is more than 1000, it means males are less than 5000 i.e., less than half the population.

The sex ratio refers to the number of females per 1000 males. An ideal sex ratio would be 1000 which indicates the population comprises an equal number of males and females.

Sex ratio >1000 indicates that there are more females than males in a population. Sex ratio <1000 indicates that there are fewer females compared to males in the population.

Pearl PF0985: Sex Ratio

* It is the number of females per 1000 males.

* According to a census in 2011, the sex ratio in India was 940 females per 1000 males.

* Kerala currently holds a favorable sex ratio with values of 1084 females per 1000 men.

* The sex composition of the population is affected by the differentials in mortality conditions of males and females, sex-selective migration and the sex ratio at birth.

* A very low sex ratio indicates male-child favoritism.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Highest Sodium content is present in which of the following foods:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Canned soup

Highest Sodium content is present in Canned Soup.

Packaged, processed, store-bought, and restaurant foods have highest amount of sodium in the form of salt added as a preservative to the canned foods.

Other options: Sugar cane, Barley, Fresh fruit juices all have less sodium content when compared to canned soup.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: If Bajra is mixed with black seeds, what is used to separate them?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 20 % salt water

20% saltwater is used to separate bajra from black grains or seeds. They can also be removed by hand-picking and air floatation.

Note:

Food items like bajra, rye, sorghum, and wheat have a tendency to house the ergot fungus called Claviceps purpurea.The safe limit for ergot alkaloids in grains is 0.05 mg per 100 grams.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a normal curve, what is the percentage of the distribution that falls within one standard deviation of the mean?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 68%

According to the empirical rule of normal distributions, 68% of the distribution falls within 1 standard deviation of the mean.

In a normal curve, the area on either side of the mean will include :

Approximately 68% of the distribution falls within ±1 standard deviations of the mean.

Approximately 95% of the distribution falls within ±2 standard deviations of the mean.

Approximately 99.7% of the distribution falls within ±3 standard deviations of the mean.

Pearl PF0301: Normal Distribution

* Normal distribution is the most widely used continuous distribution.

* It is also called bell curve (bell shaped) or Gaussian distribution after a mathematician named Karl Friedrich Gauss.

* The following is an image of three different types of normal distributions.

* Normal distributions are defined by two parameters: the mean and the standard deviation.

* The mean, median and mode are all equal in a normal distribution.

* All normal distributions are symmetric and have bell-shaped density curves with a single peak.

* Exactly half of the values are to the left of the centre and the other half to the right.

* The total area under the curve is 1.

* The density of a normal distribution is more around the centre and less around the tails.

* There is no skew in the curve.

* Looking at the figure below, we can understand the empirical rule of a normal distribution which states that:

* Approximately 68% of the distribution falls within one standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 1 SD).

* Approximately 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 2 SD).

* Approximately 99.7% of the distribution falls within three standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 3 SD).

* Many data like blood pressure, heights, IQ scores, etc. form a normal distribution.

* A standard normal distribution is a normal distribution with a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Lung malignancy is most commonly associated with?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Asbestosis

Asbestosis is most commonly associated with mesotheliomas,  pleural malignancy.

Asbestos-related diseases include:

* Localized fibrous plaques or diffuse pleural fibrosis

* Pleural effusion

* Parenchymal interstitial fibrosis (asbestosis)

* Lung carcinoma

* Mesotheliomas

* Laryngeal, ovarian and colon carcinomas

Asbestosis:

* Asbestosis is a type of pneumoconiosis that occurs after 5-10 years of exposure to asbestos. However, once established, it progresses even in the further removal of the worker from its contact. Asbestosis affects the basal part of the lung causing diffuse peribronchial fibrosis.

* Asbestos is of 2 types, i.e

* Serpentine

* Amphibole

* Sputum shows asbestos bodies, which are asbestos fibres coated with fibrin.

* They present with cough and exertional dyspnoea and predominantly affect the lower lobes of the lung, in contrast to other forms of pneumoconiosis, which affect the upper lobes.

* Pulmonary function testing in asbestosis typically shows a restrictive pattern with a decrease in both lung volumes and diffusing capacity.

* X-ray shows peripheral reticular opacities predominantly in the lower zones.

* HRCT shows:

* traction bronchiectasis

* subpleural fibrotic lines

* honeycomb pattern

* irregular opacities

* The complications that can occur are

* Pulmonary fibrosis

* Carcinoma of the lung

* Malignancy of the gastrointestinal tract

* Mesothelioma of the pleura

Preventive measures:

* Using a safer type of asbestos, like chrysolite and amosite

* Substituting other insulants like glass fibre, mineral wool, calcium silicate, plastic foams, etc

* Dust control

* Periodic examination of workers

* Continuing research

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Re-infection with which of the following will lead to catastrophic symptoms even in the presence of antibodies?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Dengue

Re-infection with Dengue virus will lead to catastrophic symptoms even in the presence of antibodies.

The DENV-1/DENV-2 sequence of infection has a 500-fold risk of DHF than primary infection.

DENV-3/DENV-2 sequence has a 150-fold risk and DENV-4/DENV-2 has a 50-fold risk of DHF.

This shows that multiple infection with different serotypes of the dengue virus leads to severe forms of dengue such as DHF/DSS.

Recent update: Dengvaxia is the WHO endorsed first ever vaccine for dengue fever, which is currently licensed in twenty countries.

Other options: Re-infection with Yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis and Zika will not cause catastrophic symptoms in the presence of antibodies.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The best method of teaching an urban slum about ORS is ________.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Demonstration

The best method of teaching an urban slum about ORS is by demonstration.

* Demonstration is a carefully prepared presentation on how to perform a certain task or skill or procedure.

* It shows the step by step process of a task.

* Demonstration arouses interest and incites ‘learning by doing,’ and ‘seeing is believing’ philosophies.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The minimum requirements of a health worker job are given: should be a woman, a resident of the village, 25 to 45 years old, and have a formal education till 10th standard. What is this health worker called?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. ASHA worker

The requirements of being a woman, a resident of the village, 25 to 45 years old, and having a formal education till 10th standard is for an ASHA(Accredited Social Health Activist) worker.

An ASHA is a trained female community health activist and a resident woman of the village with a formal education of at least up to 10th grade. . This may be relaxed upto 8th standard only if no suitable person with this qualification is available. She should preferably be in the age group of 25 to 45 years (married/divorced/widow) and have qualities such as good communication skills and leadership skills. The general norm of selection recommends having one ASHA for 1000 population, but in tribal, hilly, and desert areas, the norm could be relaxed to one ASHA per habitation.

Roles of ASHA:

* To create awareness and provide information to the community on determinants of health such as nutrition, basic sanitation, and hygienic practices.

* To counsel women on birth preparedness, the importance of safe delivery, breastfeeding and complementary feeding, immunization, and contraception.

* To counsel women on the prevention of common infections including reproductive tract infections/sexually transmitted infections.

* To mobilize the community and help them in accessing health and health-related services.

* To arrange and escort pregnant women and children requiring treatment/admission to the nearest pre-identified health facility.

* To inform the sub-centre/primary health centre about the births and deaths in her village and any unusual health problems/disease outbreaks in the community.

* To promote the construction of household toilets under the total sanitation campaign.

Other options:

Option A: An Anganwadi worker is a community-based health worker in India, primarily responsible for providing maternal and child health services, nutrition, and education. They work under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) program to support the well-being of children and mothers.

Option B: A nurse is a healthcare professional responsible for providing patient care, administering medications, and assisting with treatment plans. They play a crucial role in promoting health, preventing illness, and supporting recovery across various healthcare settings.

Option C: A midwife is a trained professional who specializes in assisting women during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period. They provide prenatal care, support during labour, and postnatal care for both the mother and newborn.

Pearl PF0294: ASHA

ASHA is an Accredited Social Health Activist.

An ASHA must be a woman, a resident of the village, 25 to 45 years old and have a formal education till 10th standard preferably if they are in good numbers. This may be relaxed upto 8th standard only if no suitable person with this qualification is available. She is part of the primary health care at the village level.

National norm: In rural areas, a population of 1000 should have at least 1 ASHA, but in remote areas, one ASHA per habitation is the norm. In urban areas, 1 ASHA worker is assigned to a population of 1000-2500. This norm is also mandated by each state, differently, according to their requirements.

Responsibilities of ASHA:

* Health education and awareness

* Reproductive and child health and family planning

* Facilitate the access to health services

* Promotion of sanitation and household toilet construction

* Provision of primary medical care for minor ailments

* Provider of DOTS

* Depot holder of essentials like ORS, iron and folic acid tablets, condoms, disposable delivery kits, etc.

* Dispersal of health information on her community to higher centres

* Some responsibilities are integrated with Anganwadi workers and Auxiliary Nurse Midwife

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births is called ___.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Maternal mortality ratio

Maternal mortality ratio is defined as the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births during a given time period.

Other options:

Infant mortality rate (IMR) is defined as the ratio of infant deaths registered in a given year to the total number of live births in the same year.

Maternal mortality rate is the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 women of reproductive age in a given time period.

Pearl PF0987: Maternal Mortality Ratio

Maternal death is defined as the death of a woman while pregnant or within 42 days of termination of pregnancy, irrespective of the duration and site of pregnancy, from any cause related to or aggravated by the pregnancy or its management but not from accidental or incidental causes.

* Maternal mortality ratio is the number of maternal deaths in a given period per 100,000 live births during the same period.

* MMR = Number of maternal deaths in a period x 100,000 (or 1000)/Number of live births in the same period

* Main global causes of maternal deaths are severe bleeding, indirect causes (anemia, malaria, heart diseases), infections, unsafe abortions, eclampsia, obstructed labor and other direct causes like ectopic pregnancy, anesthesia related complications, etc.

* In India, the most common causes of maternal deaths are hemorrhage (leading cause), sepsis, obstructed labor, hypertensive disorders, etc.

Pearl PF0988: Perinatal Mortality Rate

* The term ‘perinatal mortality’ includes both late fetal death (stillbirths) and early neonatal deaths.

* Babies chosen for inclusion in perinatal statistics should be above a minimum birth weight (1000g at birth). If the birth weight is not available, a gestation period of at least 28 weeks should be used (as the weight at 28 weeks corresponds to 1000g). If both are not available, then crown to heel length of at least 35cm should be used.

* Generally, the PMR = Late fetal deaths and early neonatal deaths weighing over 1000g at birth x 1000/Total births(live+dead) weighing over 1000g at birth.

* The PMR is the yard-stick of obstetric and pediatric care before and around the time of birth.

* The PMR of India (2016) is 24 per 1000 births.

* The main causes of perinatal mortality are intrauterine and birth asphyxia, low birth weight, birth trauma, and intrauterine/neonatal infections.

Please note that the actual perinatal period commences from the 22nd week of life, but at that time the fetus weighs only about 500g.

Therefore, only for statistical calculations and international comparisons, to calculate the perinatal mortality rate, the period from the 28th week of life is taken, as then the baby weighs about 1000g. As mentioned, babies included in the perinatal statistics must weigh above 1000g.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: When quarantine was introduced in the 14th century for plague, how many days were people who were suspected to have the infection quarantined for?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 40 days

In the 14th century, quarantine was used for plague and the suspects were quarantined for 40 days.

The idea of quarantine when it was initially introduced was that, the disease would remain dormant in the quarantine period and die out. But the 40 day period caused inconveniences and was based on a lack of scientific knowledge regarding the causation and spread of the disease.

Quarantine is the restriction on the movement of people, animals, and goods that may have been exposed to a communicable disease. It is intended to prevent the spread of communicable diseases.

Quarantine is distinct from medical isolation, in which those confirmed to be infected with a communicable disease are isolated from the healthy population.

It is a primary level of prevention and falls under specific protection measures. The various types of quarantine are:

* Absolute - Complete limitation of movement

* Modified - Selective partial limitation of movement

* Segregation - Observation of a group of persons in a population after separation

Note:

With respect to the COVID-19 pandemic, home quarantine is advised when a person comes in contact with a COVID-19 positive patient.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following indicators is the best to know the overall burden of disease?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Disability Adjusted Life Years (DALY)

DALY is the best measure of the overall disease burden in a defined population and the effectiveness of interventions.

DALY (Disability Adjusted Life Years):

* It can measure both mortality and disability together.

* One DALY can be considered a lost year of a "healthy" life.

* The sum of these DALYs across the population, or the burden of disease, can be thought of as a measurement of the gap between current health status and an ideal health situation where the entire population lives to an advanced age, free of disease and disability.

DALYs for a disease or health condition are calculated as the sum of the Years of Life Lost (YLL) due to premature mortality in the population and the Years Lost due to Disability (YLD) for people living with the health condition or its consequences:

Calculation

DALY = YLL + YLD

The YLL basically corresponds to the number of deaths multiplied by the standard life expectancy at the age at which death occurs. The basic formula for YLL (without yet including other social preferences discussed below), is the following for a given cause, age, and sex:

YLL = N x L

where:

* N = number of deaths

* L = standard life expectancy at the age of death in years

Prevalence YLD

YLD = P x DW

where:

* P = number of prevalent cases

* DW = disability weight

Other options:

Option A: QALY is a disability rate indicator. It is based on the number of years that would be added to life due to medical intervention. A utility value of 1.0 is given for each year of perfect health and 0 for death. It is the measure of the disease burden which includes both quality and quantity of life.

Option B: HALE (health adjusted life expectancy) is an indicator that estimates the number of years a newborn is expected to live in full health based on the current rates of ill health and mortality. HALE is calculated using the life expectancy at birth with an adjustment for time spent in poor health. It was known as DALE (disability-adjusted life expectancy) previously.

Option D: DFLE (disability-free life expectancy) is an indicator that estimates the average number of years an individual is expected to live free of disability if the current pattern of mortality and disability continues to apply. It is also known as active life expectancy and is calculated by:

DFLE = Life expectancy - Duration of disability

Pearl PF0951: QALY vs. DALY

QALY and DALY are disability indicators used as measures of health in a population.

Measures health loss in quality of life

1 = Perfect health

0 = Death

Expressed as 0 or 1 where,

0 = Perfect health

1 = Death

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for the device shown in the image below?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Vaginal bleeding of unknown etiology

The device shown in the image is of a CuT 380 A(IUD) and vaginal bleeding of unknown etiology is an absolute contraindication.

Contraindications for IUD usage include:

Absolute contraindications

Relative contraindications

• Suspected pregnancy
• PID
• Vaginal bleeding of unknown etiology
• Carcinoma cervix /uterus/adnexa /other pelvic tumors

• Anemia
• Menorrhagia
• History of PID since the last pregnancy
• Purulent cervical discharge
• Distortions of the uterine cavity due to fibroids
• Uterine malformations
• An unmotivated person

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is responsible for maintaining data about births and deaths in India?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Sample registration system

The Sample Registration System is responsible for maintaining data about births and deaths in India.

SRS was initiated in the mid-1960s to provide reliable estimates of birth and death rates at the National and State levels. It is a dual-record system where there is continuous registration of births and deaths and a 6-month independent survey by an investigator-supervisor. It provides reliable health information, age-specific fertility and mortality rates, infant mortality,under-five and adult mortality.

Other options:

Lay reporting is defined as the collection of information, its use, and its transmission to other levels of the health system by non-professional health workers.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is used to reduce the selection bias in a clinical trial?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Randomization

Randomization is done to reduce the clinical error and selection bias in a study.

Randomization:

* Randomization is a statistical procedure wherein the population is grouped into study and control groups.

* It is done so to know whether any intervention is needed to be given or not.

* This is done to reduce the bias and to allow comparability between the individuals.

* Randomization is the "heart" of a control trial.

Pearl PF0964: Randomized Control Trials

Randomized controlled trials are a type of experimental studies.

General Design of an RCT

Steps of an RCT

* Drawing up a protocol

* Selecting reference and experimental population

* Randomization

* Manipulation or intervention

* Follow-up

* Assessment of outcome

Types

* Clinical trials

* Preventive trials

* Risk factor trials

* Cessation experiments

* Trial of etiological agents

* Evaluation of health services

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following terms refers to instilling a particular point of view in people’s minds and inhibiting their independent thought?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Health propaganda

The act of instilling a particular point of view in people’s minds and inhibiting their independent thought is referred to as Health propaganda.

When information is used to spread a particular systemized doctrine it is called health propaganda.

The difference between health education (option A) and health propaganda is given below:

Health education
Health propaganda

Knowledge
Actively acquired
Instilled in the mind

Skills
Actively acquired
Instilled

Primitive desires
Disciplined
Aroused

Action
Reflective behaviour; trained to use judgement before acting
Reflexive behaviour; Aims at impulsive action

Emotion
Does not appeal to emotion but appeals to reason
Appeals to emotion

Behaviour
The process is behaviour centred
The process is information centred

Four approaches to health education:

* Regulatory approach: Governmental intervention, direct or indirect, designed to alter human behavior. It may range from prohibition to imprisonment.

* Service approach: Providing all health services needed by people at their doorstep on the assumption that people would use them to improve their own health.

* Health education approach: People must be educated through planned learning experiences on what to do, and be informed, educated, and encouraged to make their own choices for a healthy life.

* Primary health care approach: Full participation and active involvement in planning and delivery of health services based on principles of primary health care viz community involvement and intersectoral coordination.

Other options:

Option C: Health awareness is a crucial component of public health strategies aimed at promoting positive health behaviors and reducing the burden of disease through education and preventive measures.

Option D: Health promotion is a mode of intervention in primary prevention and is the process of enabling people to increase control over and improve health. Health promotion may be achieved through health education, environmental modification, nutritional interventions, or lifestyle changes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: You are a doctor in a village. A 1 yr old child who is not taking feeds, presents with fever and cough for 2 days. On examination, he is calm, with a respiratory rate of 51 breaths/min, and stridor is present. According to IMNCI (Integrated management of neonatal and childhood illnesses), how is he classified?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Severe Pneumonia

This child is classified as having a very severe disease/severe pneumonia.

Signs of very severe disease are:

* Stridor in a calm child

* Not able to drink

* Convulsions

* Abnormally sleepy or difficult to wake

* Severe malnutrition.

In any of these cases, an urgent referral is very important.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A government plans to outline tobacco control laws. What is the level of prevention here?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Primary prevention

Creating tobacco control laws is a method of primary prevention.

Making tobacco control laws targets smokers who are already exposed to risk of smoking, who have not yet developed any disease. This aims to reduce smoking which is essentially a reduction of risk factor which is a primary prevention stratergy.

Primary prevention is defined as an action taken prior to the onset of disease, whose aim is to prevent the disease from occuring. Its target population is healthy individuals. It commonly institutes activities that limit risk exposure or increase the immunity of individuals at risk to prevent a disease from progressing in a susceptible individual. They approaches can be as follows:

* Population (mass) strategy where the target group is the whole population

* A high-risk strategy where the target group is limited to the people who are most at risk of developing a particular disease.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A pregnant woman with a 2-year-old child gives a history of completing required antenatal vaccinations during her previous pregnancy. Which of the following would you recommend for her current pregnancy?
options: Give a booster dose of TT
Give a booster dose of Td
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Give a booster dose of Td

In the given scenario of a mother who was vaccinated in her previous pregnancy 2 years ago, a booster dose of Td (tetanus and adult diphtheria) is recommended.

All pregnant women must be vaccinated with 0.5 ml, intramuscular Td in the upper arm to prevent neonatal and maternal tetanus.

* Unimmunized women should receive two doses of Td vaccine with the first dose given as early as possible. The second dose should have at least one month gap and be given at least 3 weeks before delivery to allow sufficient time for developing antibodies.

* Previously immunized women just require a booster Td if the current pregnancy occurred within 3 years of last pregnancy and 2 Td doses were received.

The guidelines recommend replacing TT with Td vaccine for all age groups, including pregnant women and isolated tetanus toxoid is no longer recommended.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A primigravida delivers a healthy baby via normal delivery. After how many hours should she initiate breastfeeding?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Within 1 hour

In this scenario of a healthy mother and infant, breastfeeding should be started within 1 hour.

Breastmilk is the ideal and exclusively food for infants in the first 6 months. It reduces the infant mortality rate, neonatal hypocalcaemia and hypomagnesemia hence  should be started as soon possible.

The standard essential newborn care include:

* Maintain the airway and breathing

* Maintain the body temperature and prevent hypothermia

* Initiate breastfeeding within one hour

* Cleaning of baby and care to prevent infection

* Cord care and care of the eyes

* Administering vitamin K

* Performing a thoroiugh examination.

Pearl PF0003: Baby-friendly hospital initiative (revised 2018)

Ten steps to successful breastfeeding (Revised 2018)

Critical management procedures

1  a. Comply fully with the International Code of Marketing of Breast-milk Substitutes and relevant World Health Assembly resolutions.

b. Have a written infant feeding policy that is routinely communicated to staff and parents.

c. Establish ongoing monitoring and data-management systems.

2. Ensure that staff has sufficient knowledge, competence, and skills to support breastfeeding.

Key clinical practices

3. Discuss the importance and management of breastfeeding with pregnant women and their families.

4. Facilitate immediate and uninterrupted skin-to-skin contact and support mothers to initiate breastfeeding as soon as possible after birth.

5. Support mothers to initiate and maintain breastfeeding and manage common difficulties.

6. Do not provide breastfed newborns any food or fluids other than breast milk, unless medically indicated.

7. Enable mothers and their infants to remain together and to practice rooming-in 24 hours a day.

8. Support mothers to recognize and respond to their infants’ cues for feeding.

9. Counsel mothers on the use and risks of feeding bottles, teats, and pacifiers.

10. Coordinate discharge so that parents and their infants have timely access to ongoing support and care.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was conducted to compare MMR vaccine history in children with autism and children without autism. What kind of study is being done here?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Case control study

The above study design is typical of a case-control study. Children with autism are cases and children without autism are controls.

Case-control study is a type of obesrvational study used to test a hypothesis. Here the study subjects are divided into cases- those having the disease of interest and controls- those without the disease of interest.  Odds ratio is a measure of strength of the association between risk factor and outcome in these studies.

Other options:

Option A: Cross-sectional study is based on a single examination of a cross-section of population at one point in time and the results can be projected on the whole population.

Option B: Cohort study divides subjects into those with exposure and without exposure. This study gives relative risk which is the ratio of the incidence of the disease (or death) among exposed and the incidence among non-exposed. If this study were to divide children based on those who recieved MMR vaccine and those who did not recieve it to find out any association with autism, it would be called a cohort study.

Option D: A clinical trial is a type of experimental or interventional study. They are mainly concerned with evaluating therapeutic agents, mainly drugs.

Pearl PF1701: Case Control Study

In a case-control study, progression is from effect (disease) to cause (exposure) as the outcome or disease has already occurred. It is also called a retrospective study.

Design of case-control study:

* Steps of case control study:

* Selection of cases and controls

* Matching

* Measurement of exposure

* Analysis in the form of exposure rates, risk ratio, and odds ratio

* Advantages of case control study:

* Easy to carry out, rapid and inexpensive

* Requires few subjects, no risk to subjects

* Used to investigate rare diseases

* Different etiological factors can be studied and risk factors can be identified

* No attrition problems, minimal ethical problems

* Disadvantages of case control study:

* Relies on memory or past records giving rise to bias

* Selection of appropriate control groups is difficult

* Incidence cannot be measured

* Does not distinguish between causes and associated factors

* Not suited for evaluation of therapy or prophylaxis

* Representativeness of the cases and controls is often inadequate

Pearl PF0957: Odds Ratio

* Odds ratio is a measure of the strength of association between risk factor and outcome in case control studies.

* Odds ratio can be arrived at from case control studies.

* It is also known as cross product ratio.

* A representation of the odds ratio (OR) is given in the picture below:

Odds ratio calculation (OR) = (a/b)/(c/d) = ad/bc where,

Cancer

Exposure

Yes
No

Yes
a
b

No
c
d

* If the frequency of exposure is higher among cases, the OR will exceed 1, which indicates increased risk.

* If the frequency is lower, then it will be <1, which can indicate possible protection.

* If the OR is 1, then there is no association of risk with exposure or that the event is equally likely in both groups.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A surveyor visits a household consisting of a 35-year-old man, his wife who is 6 weeks pregnant and a 3-year-old child. The man's brother along with his wife is currently visiting them for a month owing to winter vacation. What type of family would the surveyor classify the household?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Nuclear family

A surveyor would label this house as a nuclear family.

The nuclear or elementary family consists of the married couple and their children while they are still regarded as dependents. This nuclear family has visitors who neither live permanantly in the same household or hold a common property which are characters of a joint or extended family.

The joint or extended family consists of a number of married couples and their children who live together in the same household and hold the property in common. The senior male member of the family is considered as the head.

Third generation family consists of three generations that are direct descents, living in the same house. It occurs usually when young couples continue to live with their parents and have their own children.

Pearl PF1702: The Family as a Social Organization

* A family is a group of biologically related individuals living together under the same roof and eating from a common kitchen.

* It is the most primary and basic unit of all societies.

* The basic and arbitrary model of a family cycle has six phases:

Phase

Beginning

End

1

Formation

Marriage

Birth of 1st child

2

Extension

Birth of 1st child

Birth of last child

3

Complete extension

Birth of last child

1st child leaves home

4

Contraction

1st child leaves home

Last child leaves parental home

5

Completed contraction

Last child leaves parental home

Death of 1st spouse

6

Dissolution

Death of 1st spouse

Death of survivor

* Types of families:

* A nuclear family or elementary family consists of only the married couple and their offspring while they are dependants.

* The term new family is applied when nuclear families are younger than 10 years and consist of parents and children.

* A joint family or extended family consists of a number of married couples and their children who live together in the same household with usually the men being related by blood. All property in joint families is held in common with the family income going into a common pocket. A senior male member is usually the head of the family who makes decisions.

* A three generation family is one where there are representatives from three different generations in one house.

* A communal family is one in which all the members play a part in its management.

* Functions of the family:

* Residence (patrilocal and matrilocal)

* Division of labour

* Reproduction and raising children

* Socialization and social care

* Economic functions

* Problems families are those that lag behind the rest of the community in terms of standard and quality of life of its members.

* Broken families are those in which the parental or family system has been disrupted by separation, divorce or death.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An 8 weeks pregnant woman, working in an industry consults a doctor. According to the ESI act, what is the duration of maternity leave that she can get?
options: 28 weeks, starting from 4 weeks after delivery
26 weeks, starting from 8 weeks before delivery
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 26 weeks, starting from 8 weeks before delivery

According to ESI act, this pregnant woman is entitled to a leave of 26 weeks, starting 8 weeks preceding the expected date of delivery.

According to The Employees State Insurance Act and its amendments, pregnant ladies can receive benefits in cash for confinement/miscarriage or sickness arising out of the same or premature birth of a child or miscarriage. This includes maternity leave for

* 26 weeks of which not more than 8 weeks shall be preceding the expected date of her delivery.

* 6 weeks in case of miscarriage.

* 30 days for sickness arising out of being in the family way, premature delivery or medical termination of pregnancy.

* Women having 2 or more surviving children shall be allowed maternity leave of 12 weeks of which not more than 6 weeks should be before the expected date of her delivery.

Pearl PF1924: ESI ACT, 1948

Employees State Insurance Act, 1948 (Revised in 2019)

Scope: It is applicable to all factories in India excluding:

* Defence

* Railway

* Mines

Finance Contribution

* It covers all employees getting income up to Rs.21,000/- per month.

* Employee – 0.75% of his daily wage.

* Employer – 3.25% of the employees' daily wage.

* Medical benefit – 1/8th by the state government and 7/8th by the ESI Corporation.

Benefits

To the Employees

* Medical Benefit- full medical care is provided free of cost in case of sickness, employment injury, and maternity.

* Sickness Benefit- is given at 70% of average daily wages for a duration of 91 days in one year. In order to qualify for sickness benefit, the worker is required to contribute for 78 days in a period of 6 months.

* Extended sickness benefit – 80% of the daily wages for a duration of 2 years, for 34 specified diseases such as TB, leprosy, malignant diseases, diabetes, Parkinson's, myasthenia gravis, glaucoma, coronary artery disease, etc.

* Enhanced sickness benefit – at full wages for sterilization procedure; for a duration of 7 days post-vasectomy and 14 days post tubectomy.

* The total amount payable is double the standard sickness benefit rate, that is, equal to full wages.

* Maternity Benefit – benefit is payable at full wages for 26 weeks (6.5 months) for pregnancy, 6 weeks following a miscarriage, and 30 days for sickness arising out of pregnancy. It also covers the premature birth of a child born to an insured woman.

* Dependance Benefit– in case of death, as a result of employment injury, the dependents of an insured person are eligible for periodical payments. Pension at the rate of 90% of the wages is payable, shared by dependants in a fixed ratio, on monthly basis in accordance with the prescribed share. An eligible son or daughter is entitled to the dependant's benefit up to the age of 18; the benefit is withdrawn if the daughter marries earlier.

* Disablement Benefits–

* Temporary disability- at 90% daily wages as long as the person is disabled.

* Permanent disability- lifetime pension. It also covers occupational diseases.

* Funeral Benefit – a maximum of Rs.15,000/-.

* Rehabilitation Benefit- on payment of Rs.10, the insured person and his/her family continue to get medical treatment after permanent disablement or retirement.

To the Employers

* Exemption from Workman Compensation Act.

* Exemption from Maternity Benefit Act.

* Income tax rebate on the amount contributed towards the scheme.

* Exemption from payment of medical allowance to employees and their dependants, or arranging for their medical care.

* Healthy-work force.

Pearl PF1016: The Factories act, 1948 and The Maternity Act, 2017

The Factories act,1948

* The act defines factory as an establishment employing 10 or more workers where power is used, and 20 or more workers where power is not used.

* Age of employment –  prohibition children of < 14 years from working.

* Adolescents between 15 – 18 years

* Can be employed  only in certain industries and  work between 6 AM – 7 PM

* They should not be made to work for more than four and a half hours

* They are allowed to take leave once in every 15 days and have an accumulated leave of up to 40 days

* Hours of work for adults: maximum hours of work for an industrial worker should be not more than 48 hours per week, not exceeding 9 hours a day, if working overtime then it should be no more than 60 hrs per week

* Per capita space availability: For factories established after 1948 – min 500cuft / person

* Safety and Welfare measures:

* > 1000 Workers – Safety officer

* > 500 Workers – Welfare officer

* > 250 Workers – Canteen

* > 50 Workers- Crèche*

The Maternity Act, 2017 is a landmark law which has enhanced the duration of paid maternity leave:

* Working mothers- 12 weeks to 26 weeks

* Working mothers, already with 2 surviving children - 12 weeks

* Adopting mother and commissioning mothers- 12 weeks from the date on which the child is being handed over to the mother.

*for fifty women worker after the 1976 amendment.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Confidentiality is maintained in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Counselling

Confidentiality is always maintained during counselling.

Confidentiality is defined as the state of being private- maintaining the patients’ privacy by restricting access to personal and confidential information. It is always implied between the doctor and his patient. The doctor is obliged to keep secret, all that he comes to know concerning the patient in the course of his professional work.

It assumes that without confidentiality, patients will not reveal everything during a consultation, especially intimate details, due to which the clinical history may be deficient or even misleading. The responsibility of the attending physician in this regard is very great because he has the confidence of the patient. The patient will discuss and listen more readily, making counselling more easier if they are assured that the conversations will be kept confidential.

An example of this is counselling individuals with HIV/ AIDS. With a confidential dialogue between a person and a counsellor enables the person to explore the risk of HIV infection, cope with stress and make personal decisions to deal with the disease.

Group discussions, panel discussions and seminars are group approaches to health education and would not involve the question of confidentiality.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During a vaccination drive, a male patient asks the presiding doctor if the recommended vaccine can lead to impotency. What type of barrier will the doctor be addressing?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Cultural barrier

The doctor in this case is trying to address the cultural barrier.

This individual thinks that vaccination can cause impotency. This may be due to his understanding, beliefs or knowledge towards vaccination which are all part of cultural barrier.

A failure in communication between educators and the community affects health education, counselling and motivating people. They can be of the following types:

* Physiological barrier due to difficulties in hearing, expression

* Psychological barriers like emotional disturbances, neurosis, levels of intelligence, language or comprehension difficulties.

* Environmental barriers like noise, invisibility, congestion

* Cultural barriers include illiteracy, levels of knowledge and understanding, customs, beliefs, religion, attitudes, economic and social class differences, language variations, and cultural difficulties.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Eligible couple registers are maintained at which of the following centres?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Sub-centre

Eligible couple registers are maintained at sub-centres by Female health workers(FHW).

A sub-centre provides an interface with the community at the grass-root level, providing all the primary health care services. They can be categorised into

* Type A without facilities for conducting delivery

* Type B (MCH sub-centre) with facilities for conducting delivery.

1 FHW in type A and 2 FHWs in type B along with 1 Male health worker(MHW) are essential to provide services at the sub-centre level.

• Universal Immunization Program
• Detection of non communicable diseases

• National Health Programmes

• RNTCP

• Environmental sanitation including chlorination of water and proper waste disposal

• Record and report vital events

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Giving class in a village for wound care after a dog bite by enacting it is which mode of health communication?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Demonstration

The best method of giving a class in a village for wound care after a dog bite is by demonstration.

A demonstration is a group approach to health communication where the audience is educated on how to follow the advice by enacting it. Here the procedure is carried out step by step before an audience or the target group. It can bring about behavioural change in practices by arousing interest.

Other options:

Option A: A lecture is an oral presentation of facts, thoughts and ideas with help of chalk and board. Its effectiveness depends to a large extent on the speaker's ability and the comprehension of listeners. It would not be an effective tool in teaching a procedure like wound care.

Option B: Group discussion involves members interacting in a face-to-face situation. A group leader initiates the subject, encourages everyone to participate, takes discussion in the proper manner, and sums up the discussion in the end.

Option C: Flash card is a card that has words, numbers, or pictures on it that helps to learn. They are a form of visual aids in communication.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Hand washing during COVID-19 is what level of prevention?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Primary prevention

Hand washing during COVID-19 is a method of Primary prevention.

COVID-19 is an infectious respiratory illness caused by the coronavirus. Infection control measures like immunization, hand washing, personal hygiene and public health measures such as sanitation serve as a holistic primary prevention strategy.

Primary prevention is defined as an action taken prior to the onset of a disease, whose aim is to prevent the disease from occurring. Its target population is healthy individuals. It commonly institutes activities that limit risk exposure or increase the immunity of individuals at risk to prevent a disease from progressing in a susceptible individual. The approaches can be as follows:

* Population (mass) strategy where the target group is the whole population

* A high-risk strategy is where the target group is limited to the people who are most at risk of developing a particular disease.

The highest birth rate is seen in stage I of the demographic cycle.

Demographic cycle of a country represents a population’s shift from high mortality and high fertility to low mortality and low fertility.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: How much per cent of GNP does WHO recommend being spent on the healthcare sector?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 5%

The WHO has set the target of at least 5% expenditure of each country's GNP on healthcare

India spends about 1% of its GNP on health and family welfare. The National Health Policy, 2017 aims to increase public health expenditure from 1.15% of GDP to around 2.5% by 2025.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Infectivity is also known as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Secondary attack rate

Infectivity is also known as the secondary attack rate.

Infectivity is the ability of an infectious agent to cause a new infection in a susceptible host. In diseases that are directly transmitted, it is measured by the secondary attack rate, which is the proportion of susceptible individuals that develop the infection after exposure to a primary case. It measures the communicability of the disease.

Secondary attack rate (SAR) = (Number of exposed persons developing the disease within the incubation period x 100)/ (Total number of susceptible close contacts).

Once a person gets infected, the time interval between invasion and appearance of the first sign or symptom is called as incubation period. During incubation, the agent multiplies in the host and builds up till it is sufficient to present as a disease.

As it is difficult to precisely calculate the incubation period, the gap in time between the onset of the primary case and the secondary case is used to calculate the incubation period. This is called serial interval.

Pearl PF1806: Case Fatality Rate

* Case fatality rate =  (Total number of deaths due to a particular disease)/(Total number of cases due to the same disease)x 100

* It is a good indicator of severity or killing power of a disease.

* It is used mostly in acute and infectious diseases.

* No time interval is used.

* Case fatality rate is closely related to virulence.

* Limitation of CFR is that its usefulness for chronic diseases is limited because the period from onset to death is variable.

* It is expressed in percentage.

* CFR is an incidence proportion and not a true rate.

* CFR may vary for the same disease in different epidemics.

*

Case fatality of a few diseases:

* Rabies - 100% especially after symptoms manifest

* Ebola - 25 to 90%, average - 50%

* Yellow fever - 15 to 50%

* Chicken pox - 0.001%

* Diseases with a high case fatality rate: Tetanus, Rabies, Botulism, Ebola.

* Diseases with a low case fatality rate: Leprosy, Trachoma, Lymphatic filariasis.

Pearl PF0956: Morbidity Measurements in Epidemiology

Morbidity Measurements in Epidemiology

Incidence rate = ( Number of new cases of a disease in a specified period of time/Population at risk during that time ) x 1000

Incidence rate of spells of sickness = ( Number of spells of sickness starting in a specified period /Mean number of people exposed to that risk in the specified time ) x 1000

Attack rate = ( Number of new cases of a disease in a specified period of time /Total population at risk during the given time ) x 100

Secondary attack rate = ( Number of exposed persons developing the disease within the range of the incubation period/Total number of exposed or susceptible contacts ) x 100

Prevalence = ( Number of all cases (new+old) of a specified disease at a given point in time/ Estimated population at the same point in time ) x 100

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Revised A patient comes with a history of category 3 dog bites. He received prophylaxis for a monkey bite 6 months back. What is the next step in management? RIG- Rabies immunoglobulin
options: Wound cleaning+ rabies vaccine on day 0 & 3
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Wound cleaning+ rabies vaccine on day 0 & 3

This patient should receive 2 doses of vaccine on days 0 & 3 as he has received a prior course of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) > 3 months ago.

In India, monkeys are known to transmit rabies. Hence the national rabies control program advises a full course of PEP for monkey bites. This patient who was bitten by a monkey 6 months back would have received PEP for rabies.

Management of a new dog bite in a previously immunized individual with either pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) or post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) is as follows:

* Category I: Wound treatment only

* Category II/ III:

* Wound treatment with soap and running water for 15 min and apply antiseptic

* Receive Anti-rabies vaccine (ARV) 2 doses ID (0.1 ml, 1 site)/ 2 doses IM (1 VIAL, 1 site) on days 0 and 3.

Rabies immunoglobulin is not given for any category in case they have completed a full course of PEP.

*Note: In developing countries like India, the vaccination status of animals alone, doesn't play a significant role in determining the initiation of prophylaxis in humans.

Pearl PF1934: Rabies vaccines and immunoglobulins schedules

According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India:

WHO category II or III exposures should receive post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) immediately.

One intradermal (ID) dose is 0.1 mL of vaccine and one intramuscular (IM) dose is an entire vial of vaccine, irrespective of the vial size.

Should a vaccine dose be delayed for any reason, the PEP schedule should be resumed (not restarted).

Rabies Immunoglobulin(RIG):

* Passive immunization

* Single-dose; after initiation of PEP and not beyond 7 days after the first dose of vaccine

* Max dose: hRIG - 20IU/kg , eRIG - 40IU/kg body weight

* Vaccines should never be withheld regardless of the availability of RIG.

* Alternatives for RIG- WHO recommends monoclonal antibodies (mAb) as a 'cocktail' containing at least two antibodies against the rabies virus.

Administration of RIG:

* RIG should be administered into or around the wound site or sites.

* The remaining RIG, if any, should be injected IM at a site distant from the site of vaccine administration.

* RIG may be diluted to a volume sufficient for all wounds to be effectively and safely infiltrated.

Prioritization of RIG allocation (numbered according to priority order):

* Multiple bites

* Deep wounds

* Bites to head, neck, and hands

* Patients with severe immunodeficiency

* Confirmed/probable rabies in biting animal

* Bites, scratches, and exposure of mucous membranes caused by a bat

Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)

PrEP is considered in the following conditions:

* High-risk groups- laboratory staff, wildlife wardens, veterinarians, animal handlers, and travelers to endemic regions.

* Remote, rabies-endemic areas where access to PEP is difficult

* Areas where dog bite incidence is >5% per year

* Areas where vampire bat rabies is known to be present.

Pre-exposure rabies vaccination consists of two intramuscular (IM) or two intradermal (ID) doses. These are given on days 0 and 3.

* Adults - the vaccine should always be administered in the deltoid area of the arm

* Young children (under 1 year of age)- Administration into the anterolateral area of the thigh is recommended.

* Rabies vaccine should never be administered in the gluteal area. Administration in this manner will result in lower neutralizing antibody titers.

For exposed or re-exposed patients who can document previous completion of PEP the following guidelines would be applicable:

* Proper wound management should be done.

* There is no need for the administration of RIG.

* One site ID or IM vaccine administration on days 0 and 3.

Only adequate wound washing would be required in case of re-exposure where the animal bite victim has documented proof of complete PEP within the last three months.

The following cases are treated as fresh cases and given full PEP:

* Those who have previously received full post-exposure treatment with neural tissue vaccines (NTV) or vaccines of unproven potency

* Those who cannot document complete PEP or PrEP treatment

questions.text: School health service should include all the following except
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Doctor on premises

School health service includes all the above except the presence of a doctor on school premises.

School health service programs function to promote positive health, prevent diseases, diagnose, treat and follow up on defects.

The health appraisal services of the program are administered by doctors in PHCs. Teachers are trained to do daily inspection, first aid and emergency care whenever necessary and a doctor's presence on school premises is not required.

The main aspects of this program includes:

* Screening of general health assessment of anaemia/nutritional status, visual acuity, hearing problem, dental check-up, physical disabilities, learning disorders, behaviour problems, etc.

* Prevention of communicable diseases through immunization

* Providing a healthful school environment

* Nutritional services

* First-aid and emergency care

* Education of handicapped children

* Health education

* Maintenance and use of school health records

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Sickness absenteeism of workers in the industry is used to evaluate__________
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Health of the worker

Sickness absenteeism of workers in the industry is used to evaluate the health of the workers.

Sickness absenteeism refers to employees' self-reported absence from work due to health problems. The apparent cause for sickness absenteeism may or may not be due to actual sickness. These include

* Economic causes: reporting sick to avail a sick leave with pay

* Social causes: obligations such as weddings, and festivals

* Medical causes: due to occupational accidents

* Non-occupational causes: nutritional disorders, alcoholism and drug addiction.

Absenteeism is an index used in industries to assess the state of health of workers and their physical, mental and social well-being. Interventions to reduce sickness absenteeism should focus on areas, such as periodic medical checkups, monitoring work schedules, improving employees’ job satisfaction, and reducing workplace stress.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. >10 sq. ft.

Per capita space for students in classroom should be >10 sq. ft.

Healthful school environment includes

* Location: Properly approachable roads and away from noisy surroundings

* Site: 5 acres for primary schools; 10 acres for higher elementary schools.

* Structure: Exterior walls 10 inch thick and heat resistant.

* Class room: 1 class room per 40 students maximum; Per capita space > 10 sq. feet
