questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During his posting in the surgery department, an intern noticed that after a surgical procedure, the nursing staff placed used syringes (without needles) and IV fluid bottles in a separate tray. The tray was marked with a distinct logo that indicated the waste collected could be recycled. Which among the following logos will be seen on a trolley designated for this type of waste?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2

The logo seen on a trolley containing used syringes (without needles) and IV fluid bottles should be the recyclable logo, which is represented by “2” in the given image. This symbol indicates that the waste materials collected are suitable for reprocessing and recycling after appropriate disinfection and treatment.

Recyclable waste in healthcare, according to biomedical waste guidelines, includes items like IV fluid bottles, syringes without needles, plastic tubing, catheters, urine bag, vacutainers(needles removed) and gloves.

Other options:

Option A: Image 1 represents the Bio-hazard and is used for infectious and contaminated biomedical waste

Option C: Image 3 represents the Radiation hazard and is used for radioactive waste

Option D: Image 4 represents the Electrical hazard

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During the assessment of drinking water from a village tank. Which of the following parameters is not within the acceptable limits for safe drinking water?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Cadmium- 0.3 mg/L

The guideline value for cadmium in drinking water is established at 0.3 µg/L. Therefore cadmium level of 0.3 mg/L is higher than the permissible limit.

Cadmium is released into the environment through wastewater, fertilizers, and air pollution, and contamination in drinking water may also occur from galvanized pipes and metal fittings. Since cadmium accumulates in the kidneys and has a very long biological half-life in humans (10–35 years), exceeding the safe limit poses significant health risks. Absorption of the cadmium compound is dependent on the solubility of the compound.

Other options:

Option A: Fluoride content of 1.5mg/L or above in water leads to dental fluorosis. Levels lower than that value is within the acceptable limits for safe drinking water.

Option B: The Maximum permissible limit of nitrate is 50 mg/L.

Option C: Water with concentrations of Total Dissolved Solids(TDS) below 1000 mg/L is generally acceptable to the consumers.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a group, the mean blood glucose level is 105 mg/dL with a standard deviation of 10 mg/dL. Assuming a normal distribution, what is the expected range of blood glucose values for approximately 95% of the population? SD-Standard deviation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 85–125 mg/dL

The expected range of blood glucose values for approximately 95% of the population will be 85–125 mg/dL.  For a normal distribution, ~95% of observations lie within ±2 SD of the mean.

To determine the range within two standard deviations in a normal distribution, we use the formula:

Range Mean ±2 × Standard Deviation (SD)

Given data: Mean = 105, Standard Deviation = 10

So, Range  = Mean +/- 2 SD.

Calculation:
Lower limit=105−(2×10)=105−20= 85

Upper limit=105+(2×10)=105+20=125

Hence, the range of blood pressure of 95% of the population will be 85–125 mg/dL.

Pearl PF0301: Normal Distribution

* Normal distribution is the most widely used continuous distribution.

* It is also called bell curve (bell shaped) or Gaussian distribution after a mathematician named Karl Friedrich Gauss.

* The following is an image of three different types of normal distributions.

* Normal distributions are defined by two parameters: the mean and the standard deviation.

* The mean, median and mode are all equal in a normal distribution.

* All normal distributions are symmetric and have bell-shaped density curves with a single peak.

* Exactly half of the values are to the left of the centre and the other half to the right.

* The total area under the curve is 1.

* The density of a normal distribution is more around the centre and less around the tails.

* There is no skew in the curve.

* Looking at the figure below, we can understand the empirical rule of a normal distribution which states that:

* Approximately 68% of the distribution falls within one standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 1 SD).

* Approximately 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 2 SD).

* Approximately 99.7% of the distribution falls within three standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 3 SD).

* Many data like blood pressure, heights, IQ scores, etc. form a normal distribution.

* A standard normal distribution is a normal distribution with a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Complete extension

The given scenario corresponds to the complete extension phase in the family cycle, which is the period from the birth of the last child to the time when the first child leaves home.

Pearl PF1702: The Family as a Social Organization

* It is the most primary and basic unit of all societies.

* The basic and arbitrary model of a family cycle has six phases:

* Types of families:

* A nuclear family or elementary family consists of only the married couple and their offspring while they are dependants.

* The term new family is applied when nuclear families are younger than 10 years and consist of parents and children.

* A joint family or extended family consists of a number of married couples and their children who live together in the same household with usually the men being related by blood. All property in joint families is held in common with the family income going into a common pocket. A senior male member is usually the head of the family who makes decisions.

* A three generation family is one where there are representatives from three different generations in one house.

* A communal family is one in which all the members play a part in its management.

* Functions of the family:

* Residence (patrilocal and matrilocal)

* Division of labour

* Reproduction and raising children

* Socialization and social care

* Economic functions

* Problems families are those that lag behind the rest of the community in terms of standard and quality of life of its members.

* Broken families are those in which the parental or family system has been disrupted by separation, divorce or death.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a study to see the effect of a new antihypertensive drug, two groups were made, one group was given the new drug, and the other group was given a different drug. Their mean BP was compared later. Which kind of statistical study is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Unpaired T test

The test of choice to measure the difference in means between two groups in a study, with one group being a control is Unpaired T test.

In this scenario, two groups are being compared hence, Student's t test/ Unpaired t test will be used. If 2 groups are being tested, then T tests are used. In that, if the same group is tested before and after, paired T test is used. Otherwise, unpaired T test is used.

Other options:

Option A: The chi-square test is used to compare qualitative data between 2 groups with independent measures.

Option B: The analysis of variance test (ANOVA) is used to test the difference between two or usually more than two groups (means) and here the inferences are made by analyzing the variances.

Option D: Paired t-test compares paired data or pre-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. This doesn't apply here as the groups are not paired.

Pearl PF0591: Tests of Significance

How to choose which test to use?

* See the variable. Are the variables quantitative or qualitative?

* If the variables are qualitative (nominal), then Chi square test is used.

* If the variables are quantitative, then see whether 2 groups are being tested, or more than 2 groups.

* If 2 groups are being tested, then T tests are used. In that, if the same group is tested before and after, paired T test is used. Otherwise, unpaired T test is used.

* If more than 2 groups are being tested, then use ANOVA.

The tests:

1. T Tests

* Unpaired t tests

* Also known as the student’s t test, independent t test, two-samples t test.

* It's the most commonly used t test and it tests the difference between two groups (the means of 2 groups) independent of each other and indicates how significant the differences are.

* Paired t tests

* "Pairs before marriage are not the same after!"

* So remember paired test is mainly used in comparison of a before and after scenario

* Also known as correlated t test, dependent samples t test.

* It is mainly used on dependent samples For example, the cholesterol level of a person before and after using a specific drug.

* It can also be used when you put the same condition under test using different items or things. For example, same crash safety tests for different cars.

* T scores

* The t score is referred to as the ratio of the difference between two groups and the difference within the groups.

* The smaller the t score, the more similarity there is between two groups and vice versa.

2. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)

* The analysis of variance test (ANOVA) is used to test the difference between two or usually more than two groups (means) and here the inferences are made by analyzing the variances.

3. Chi-Square Test

* The Chi-Square test (χ2) is a non-parametric(non-numeric) test and it is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.

* It is a test of proportions and associations.

* A Chi-square distribution is usually positively skewed but it approaches a normal distribution as its degrees of freedom increases.

* If the frequency of any of the cells of the categorical table is <5, then Fisher’s exact test is used.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In which of the following data sets can information on registration of births, deaths, infant mortality rate (IMR), abortions, pregnancies, marriages, and contraception use be found?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. National health family survey

NFHS is a large-scale, nationally representative survey conducted in India that provides information on fertility, family planning, reproductive health, infant and child mortality, maternal health, and use of contraception. It also includes data on abortions, pregnancies, and marriage patterns.

Other options:

Option A:Civil registration system: mainly records vital events such as births and deaths

Option B:Census of India is the systematic process of collecting, compiling, analyzing and disseminating demographic, social and economic data pertaining to every person in the country at a particular time, conducted every 10 years.

Option D:National Medical Commission is responsible for functions such as framing policies, ensuring quality of medical education, maintaining the National Register of medical practitioners, regulating fees in private colleges, and promoting equitable access to healthcare professionals across India.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Long-term use of combined oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) provides protection against which of the following cancers except?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Cervical

Long-term use of combined oral contraceptives increases the risk of cervical cancer, especially in women with persistent HPV infection, while offering protection against ovarian, endometrial, and colorectal cancers.

Mode of Action of Combined Oral Pills:

The primary mechanism of action of combined oral pills is to prevent the release of the ovum from the ovary by blocking pituitary secretion of gonadotropin required for ovulation. In addition, the progestogen component makes the cervical mucus thick and scanty, thereby inhibiting sperm penetration. Progestogens also reduce tubal motility and delay the transport of sperm and ovum to the uterine cavity.

Benefits of Combined Pills:

* Highly effective in preventing pregnancy when taken as prescribed (almost 100% effective).

* Protection against other diseases such as benign breast disorders, including fibrocystic disease and fibroadenoma, ovarian cysts, iron-deficiency anaemia, pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy.

* Can be safely used in large family planning programmes, making them important for population control efforts.

Adverse Effects of Combined Pills:

* Cardiovascular effects: Increased risk of myocardial infarction, cerebral thrombosis, and venous thrombosis, especially with advancing age and smoking.

* Metabolic effects: Elevation of blood pressure, changes in serum lipids (increase in LDL, decrease in HDL), altered carbohydrate metabolism with elevated blood glucose and insulin.

* Liver disorders: Risk of hepatocellular adenoma and gallbladder disease; cholestatic jaundice can occur in some users.

* Effects on lactation and fertility: Reduced breast milk quantity and premature cessation of lactation; slight delay in return of fertility after discontinuation.

* Other risks: Possible ectopic pregnancies with progestogen-only use, and potential concerns regarding foetal development if taken inadvertently during pregnancy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Measles vaccine is classified under which type of vaccine?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Live vaccine

Measles vaccine is a live attenuated vaccine prepared from live or wild organisms grown in culture and attenuated to retain immunogenicity. It is available as a freeze-dried product and recommended only in the live attenuated form for safe and effective immunization.

The vaccine is supplied as a freeze-dried product, reconstituted with sterile diluent, and one dose of 0.5 ml contains ≥1000 viral infective units of the vaccine strain. The reconstituted vaccine is generally injected subcutaneously, but it is also effective when administered intramuscularly.

It should be stored at 2–8°C after reconstitution and used within 4 hours, since it loses about 50% potency after 1 hour at 20°C. When administered, measles vaccine induces seroconversion in 95–98% of recipients after a single dose, ensuring strong immunity.

The first dose (MCV1) is given at 9 completed months, with a second dose (MCV2) at 15–18 months to ensure full coverage.Reaching all children with 2 doses of measles containing vaccine (MCV) should be the standard for all national immunization programmes. In countries with high measles risk, MCV is also given as part of outbreak control or supplementary doses up to 5 years of age. It is often used in combination vaccines like MR (measles-rubella), MMR (measles-mumps-rubella), and MMRV (measles-mumps-rubella-varicella).

Adverse Reactions :

* After vaccination, a mild “measles-like illness” (fever and rash) may occur in 5–10 days, lasting for 1–2 days.

* Other reactions include minor upper respiratory infections, mild diarrhea, or fever that resolves in 1–3 days.

* Toxic Shock Syndrome (TSS) can occur if the vaccine vial is contaminated or used beyond 4 hours after reconstitution, leading to severe symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhea, high fever, and even death within 48 hours.

Contraindications:

* immunosuppression (e.g., HIV-infected persons with evidence of severe immunosuppression).

* Pregnancy – should be avoided for at least 4 weeks following MMR vaccination.

Persons with moderate or severe acute illness should postpone vaccination until recovery.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: On January 1, 2024, a community with a population of 10,000 had 100 existing cases of tuberculosis (TB). During the year, 30 patients were cured and 10 patients died. Additionally, 20 new TB cases were reported, of which 5 were cured before December 31, 2024. What is the incidence of TB at the end of the year and the prevalence of TB for the year?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 2/1000,12/1000

Incidence is the number of new cases occurring in a defined population during a period of time. Here, 20 new TB cases occurred in 2024 in a population of 10,000, so:

* Incidence = (Number of cases of a disease in a specified period of time/Population at risk during that time) x 1000

* incidence = (20/10,000) × 1000 = 2/1000

Prevalence is the proportion of all cases, old and new, present during a specified period. At the end of 2024, the community had 100 old cases plus 20 new cases, giving a total of 120 cases. So:

* Prevalence = (Number of all cases of a specified disease at a given point in time/Estimated population at the same point in time)

* prevalence = (120/10,000) × 1000 = 12 per 1000

Pearl PF0953: Incidence and Prevalence

Incidence in Epidemiology:

* Incidence is the number of new cases occurring in a defined population during a period of time.

* Incidence = (Number of cases of a disease in a specified period of time/Population at risk during that time) x 1000

* Incidence rate is expressed in person-time units, usually per 1000 per year.

* It provides insight into the effectives of health services and programs.

* Incidence rate of spells of sickness =  (Number of spells of sickness starting in the specified period/Mean number of people exposed to that risk in the specified time) x 1000

* It is generally used for acute illnesses.

* Special types of incidence rates:

* Attack rate: It is used when there is a risk for a limited period of time.

* Secondary attack rate: It is the number of exposed persons developing the disease within the range of incubation period following exposure to a primary case.

* Incidence can be determined from cohort studies and longitudinal studies.

Prevalence in Epidemiology:

* Prevalence is the proportion of all cases, old and new, of a particular disease at a given point in time or over a period of time in a given population.

* It is a proportion, not a rate or ratio.

* It can be determined from cross-sectional studies.

* Types:

* Point prevalence is the prevalence at a point in time. Usually, prevalence is point prevalence unless otherwise specified.

* Period prevalence is the prevalence over a period of time.

* Prevalence is always expressed in percentage.

* Prevalence = (Number of all cases of a specified disease at a given point in time/Estimated population at the same point in time) x 100

* It is useful to determine the magnitude of health problems.

Relationship between Incidence and Prevalence:

* Prevalence depends upon incidence and duration.

* Prevalence = Incidence x Mean Duration

* Longer the duration of the disease, greater the prevalence.

* In acute diseases,because of rapid recovery/death prevalence will be relatively lower than incidence.This is because in some diseases (eg. food poisoning), the disease is so short lived, there are no "old cases".

* In chronic diseases like TB, prevalence will be higher than incidence.

* If a new treatment for a disease is effective, incidence does not change but prevalence decreases as duration of disease decreases.

* If treatment only prevents death but doesn’t cure the disease, it may cause a paradoxical increase in prevalence.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following indicators is used to calculate both Human Development Index (HDI) and Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI), according to WHO?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Literacy

Literacy is used in the measurement of both HDI and PQLI.

The components of the Human Development Index (HDI) include life expectancy at birth, literacy, and standard of living.

Human Development Index (HDI) is a measure of a country's average achievements in three dimensions of human development:

* A long and healthy life, as measured by life expectancy at birth

* Knowledge (literacy), as measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling, and

* A decent standard of living, as measured by GNI (gross national income) per capita

HDI values range from 0 to 1, with 1 as the maximum value.

Life expectancy at 1 year, literacy, and infant mortality rate are components of the Physical quality of life index (PQLI).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is a facility offered by Ayushman AROGYA mandirs?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Essential drugs

Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (formerly Health & Wellness Centres) are mandated to provide free and essential medicines as part of comprehensive primary healthcare services.

Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are envisaged to deliver an expanded range of services that go beyond Maternal and child health care services to include care for non-communicable diseases, palliative and rehabilitative care, Oral, Eye and ENT care, mental health and first-level care for emergencies and trauma, including free essential drugs and diagnostic services.

Ayushman Arogya Mandir represents a shift from a selective model of healthcare to one that offers a comprehensive package of services, including preventive, promotive, curative, rehabilitative, and palliative care. The scheme has two complementary components. The first aims to establish 1,50,000 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs to provide universal, free, and comprehensive primary health care, with an emphasis on wellness and expanded services delivered closer to communities. The second component is the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), which offers health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakhs per year to more than poor and vulnerable families for secondary and tertiary level treatments.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is classified as Medical Eligibility Criteria 1( MEC-1) for the use of oral contraceptive pills(OCPs)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. HIV

According to the WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use (MEC), HIV falls under category 1, meaning OCPs can be used in any circumstance.

Combined oral contraceptives contain estrogen (ethinylestradiol/mestranol) and progestins (levonorgestrel, norethisterone, desogestrel). Their primary mode of action is inhibition of ovulation: estrogen suppresses FSH to prevent follicular growth, while progestins suppress LH to block ovulation. This negative feedback on the hypothalamo-pituitary axis prevents the mid-cycle gonadotropin surge.

Additionally, they act by producing a non-receptive endometrium, thickening cervical mucus to block sperm penetration, and possibly altering tubal motility to prevent fertilization. Progestins also counteract estrogen’s proliferative effect on the endometrium, reducing the risk of hyperplasia and controlling withdrawal bleeding.

WHO category 1- Indication of OCPs

* Age: Menarche to 40 years

* Postabortion

* Anemia (iron deficiency, malaria)

* HIV or AIDS (additional to condom use)

* GTN following normal hCG level

* History of ectopic pregnancy

* Endometriosis, uterine fibroid, ovarian or endometrial cancer

* Dysmenorrhea, DUB

* Pelvic inflammatory disease

* Epilepsy

* Thyroid disease

* Varicose veins

* Tuberculosis

* Benign breast disease

Contraindications of OCPs :

A. WHO Category–2 (advantages outweigh

the risks)

• Age ≥ 40 years
• Smoker < 35 years
• History of jaundice
• Mild hypertension
• Gallbladder disease
• Diabetes
• Sickle cell disease
• Headache
• Cancer cervix

Absolute (WHO category 4)

A. Circulatory diseases (past or present)

• Arterial or venous thrombosis
• Severe hypertension
• History of stroke
• Heart disease: Valvular, ischemic
• Diabetes with vascular complications
• Migraine with focal neurologic symptoms

B. WHO Category–3 (risks outweigh advantages)

• Unexplained vaginal bleeding
• Hyperlipidemia
• Liver tumors (benign)
• Breastfeeding (postpartum 6 weeks to 6 months)
• Heavy smoker (> 20 cigarettes/day)

B. Diseases of the liver

• Active liver disease, jaundice
• Liver adenoma, carcinoma

C. Others

• Pregnancy
• Breastfeeding (postpartum 6 weeks)
• Major surgery

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Who is primarily responsible for registering eligible couples for family planning, maintaining their records, and distributing oral contraceptives under the national health system?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Multipurpose worker(female)

According to the national health system, the Multipurpose worker(female)/ANM is primarily responsible for registering couples for family planning, maintaining records, and distributing oral contraceptives at the sub-centre level.

The Health Worker Female (ANM) is instructed to utilize information from the eligible couple register and child register for the family planning programme. She maintains the eligible couple registers and updates them regularly. In addition, she distributes conventional contraceptives and oral contraceptives to couples, provides facilities to depot holders, and helps prospective acceptors in availing family planning services. Other responsibilities include:

* Provide a continuous supply of contraceptives through depot holders.

* Assist and accompany prospective acceptors to higher centers for family planning services when required.

* Offer follow-up services, manage side effects, give treatment for minor complications, and refer cases needing higher care.

* Establish and guide depot holders for contraceptive distribution in the community.

Other options:

Option A: ASHA is an Accredited Social Health Activist. Even though ASHA workers are sometimes involved in maintaining list of eligible couples and distribution of contraceptives, among other responsibilities, the registration of eligible couples is primarily done by the female multipurpose worker

Option C: Village Health Guide (VHG) was a national community health worker initiative launched in 1977 in India, aiming to deploy locally selected volunteers—most often women—trained to deliver basic preventive, promotive, and limited curative services at the village level.

Option D: Anganwadi workers are community-based functionaries under the ICDS scheme responsible for health check-ups, including growth chart maintenance, immunization, supplementary nutrition, health education, and preschool education. They also provide referral services, acting as the primary link between the community and health services for young children and women.

Pearl PF0294: ASHA

ASHA is an Accredited Social Health Activist.

An ASHA must be a woman, a resident of the village, 25 to 45 years old and have a formal education till 10th standard preferably if they are in good numbers. This may be relaxed upto 8th standard only if no suitable person with this qualification is available. She is part of the primary health care at the village level.

National norm: In rural areas, a population of 1000 should have at least 1 ASHA, but in remote areas, one ASHA per habitation is the norm. In urban areas, 1 ASHA worker is assigned to a population of 1000-2500. This norm is also mandated by each state, differently, according to their requirements.

Responsibilities of ASHA:

* Health education and awareness

* Reproductive and child health and family planning

* Facilitate the access to health services

* Promotion of sanitation and household toilet construction

* Provision of primary medical care for minor ailments

* Provider of DOTS

* Depot holder of essentials like ORS, iron and folic acid tablets, condoms, disposable delivery kits, etc.

* Dispersal of health information on her community to higher centres

* Some responsibilities are integrated with Anganwadi workers and Auxiliary Nurse Midwife

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 45-year-old man living in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh presents with the following lesions on his teeth. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Fluorosis

The above image along with the endemic area of Andhra Pradesh is diagnostic of Dental fluorosis.

Dental fluorosis (also termed mottled enamel) is an extremely common disorder, characterized by hypomineralization of tooth enamel caused by ingestion of excessive fluoride during enamel formation.

Fluorosis occurs when drinking water contains excess amounts of fluorine, in the range of 3-5mg/L. It is endemic in parts of India- Andhra Pradesh (Nellore, Nalgonda, Prakasam), Punjab, Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu.

Mechanism:

* In the extra-cellular environment of maturing enamel, an excess of fluoride ions alters the rate at which enamel matrix proteins (amelogenin) are enzymatically broken down and the rate at which the subsequent breakdown products are removed.

* Fluoride may also indirectly alter the action of protease via a decrease in the availability of free calcium ions in the mineralization environment.

* This results in the formation of enamel with less mineralization.

* This hypomineralized enamel has altered optical properties and appears opaque and lustreless relative to normal enamel.

Classification:

The two main classification systems which are used in the grading of severity of dental fluorosis are Dean’s system and TF system.

Symptoms correspond to levels of fluoride intake:

* Dental fluorosis: (1.5mg/L) Occurs if excess fluoride is ingested during the period of tooth calcification, i.e. in the first 7 years of life. Best seen on the upper incisors and almost exclusively affects only permanent teeth. It causes mottling on dental enamel, the appearance of chalky-white patches on the teeth, and loss of shine in the early stages. The white spots progressively turn yellow and can even become brown-black. The loss of enamel gives a corroded appearance.

* Skeletal fluorosis: (3-6mg/L) Occurs due to the heavy deposition of fluoride in the skeleton. Fluorosis stimulates osteoblastic activity, fluorapatite crystals are laid down in bone and these are usually resistant to secondary osteoclastic resorption. This leads to calcium retention, osteosclerosis, and osteophytosis. Ossification of ligaments and fascial attachments is characteristic.

* Crippling fluorosis: (>10mg/L) Can lead to permanent disability.

Genu valgum and osteoporosis of the lower limb are seen in a newer form of fluorosis in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. It is seen in people consuming jawar (sorghum), as it promotes greater retention of ingested fluoride.

Interventions for Fluorosis

* Change the drinking water source with a lower fluoride content (0.5 to 0.8 mg/L). Running surface water contains lower quantities of fluorides than groundwater sources.

* Chemical treatment in a water treatment plant can be moderately expensive. The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute, Nagpur developed a technique for removing fluoride by a chemical treatment called the Nalgonda technique.

* Fluoride supplements should not be prescribed for children who drink fluoridated water.

* The use of fluoride toothpaste in areas of endemic fluorosis is not recommended for children up to 6 years of age

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 50 year old male who was working in the dye industry with exposure to aniline dyes presented with bladder problems. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Transitional cell carcinoma

Since the person has chronic exposure to dyes , especially aniline dyes the most probable cancer in this patient is transitional cell carcinoma or bladder cancer.

Bladder cancer is caused by aromatic amines, which are metabolised in the body and excreted in the urine. Bladder carcinoma is associated with aniline dye exposure – benzidine , b-naphthylamine ,auramine, magenta.

Risk factors for carcinoma bladder are:

* Transitional cell carcinoma:

* Cigarette smoking is the main etiological factor

* Occupational exposure to chemicals: Naphthyline, benzidine, acrolein, aniline dyes, hydrocarbons

* Dye, petroleum, rubber, leather and printing industry workers

* Schistosoma hematobium

* Drugs: phenacetin, chlornaphazine, cyclophosphamide

* Pelvic irradiation

* Squamous cell carcinoma:

* Bladder diverticula

* Chronic irritation: chronic UTI, long term indwelling catheters, urinary calculi

* Schistosoma hematobium

Pearl PF0897: Etiological Factors for Bladder Carcinoma

Cigarette smoking

Exposure to aryl amines, particularly 2-
naphthylamine and related compounds (e.g., in diesel exhaust, in paint products)

Schistosoma haematobium infestation

Long-term use of analgesics (phenacetin)

Heavy-dose long-term use of cyclophosphamide

Radiotherapy

Congenital bladder exstrophy

Inherited cancer syndromes:

• Lynch syndrome
• Heriditary retinoblastoma
• Costello syndrome

Acquired genetic mutations in FGFR3, HRAS, P53, RB genes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A worker in a groundnut factory developed food poisoning after he ate some stale groundnuts which were stored in the factory. What is the most probable cause in this person?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Aflatoxins

Aflatoxin is the most probable cause in this patient as he had some stale groundnuts in which mycotoxins from Aspergillus fungi can be present.

Aflatoxins:

* These are a type of mycotoxins produced by Aspergillus species of fungi, such as A. flavus (secretes B1) and A. parasiticus (secretes B1, B2, G1 and G2)

* Frequently present in moldy foods, like groundnuts, corn, and peas.

* These toxins are highly toxic to animals and birds, as well as to human beings.

* Known to cause hepatomas in lower animals, and carcinogenic effects in humans have also been seen.

Other options:

BOAA (Beta oxalyl amino alanine) is the toxic compound causing Lathyrism.

Sanguinarine is the toxic compound causing epidemic dropsy.

options: Online food eaters and Non online food eaters

Correct answer: C. Obese and Non-obese persons

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Analyze the graphs given below on different occupational groups and the chance of developing fever amongst each group. Which of the following groups has the highest chance of developing fever?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. White collar jobs

The given image shows a component bar graph(A) and a pie chart(B). The pie chart shows the different groups and their percentage among the total workers, whereas the component bar graph shows the chance of them developing a fever. The highest chance of developing a fever is around 90% , which is seen among white-collar jobs as evident from the component bar graph.

The chance of developing fever in other groups are Industrial workers-50%, Farmers- 50% and Houseweives-around 20%. If the question was on the group having the highest proportion among the total workers, then it would be industrial workers, from the pie graph.

Component bar graph:

The bars can be divided into two or more parts where each part represents a certain item, proportional to the magnitude of that particular item (males and females in this image).

It is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data.

The difference between a bar graph and a histogram is that the rectangles are separated by spaces representing data that forms discrete categories instead of continuous groups. Frequency polygon and Ogive can be constructed using a histogram, not a component bar chart

Pearl PF0302: Graphical Representation of Data

1. Histogram

* A histogram, by definition, is a graphical representation of frequency distribution that contains rectangles and shows the underlying frequency of a set of continuous, quantitative data.

* The X or horizontal axis is called the abscissa which usually has the group scores or class intervals of the variables/data and the Y or vertical axis is called the ordinate which usually shows the frequencies at which these variables appear.

* The following is a histogram of cholesterol levels from the Framingham Heart Study.

2. Bar Chart

* It is also called a bar graph.

* It is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data as they are not quantitative and usually qualitative.

* The difference between a bar graph and a histogram is that the rectangles are separated by spaces representing data that forms discrete categories instead of continuous groups.

* Bar graphs can be simple, multiple or component bar graphs.

3. Pie Charts

* Pie charts are also used for nominal or ordinal data.

* The categorical data are represented as segments of a circle.

4. Frequency polygons

* Frequency polygons are used for mainly ratio and interval scale data.

* In a frequency polygon, the mid-points of each class interval are joined together by straight lines.

5. Ogive

* A frequency polygon which is drawn to represent cumulative frequency distributions form a typical S-shaped curve which is called an ogive. It referred to as a cumulative frequency diagram.

6. Line chart

* It is also called a line diagram or line graph.

* Its best use is to show the trend of events or change over passage of time.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: New A pregnant lady presented to the casualty after she was scratched by a street dog while she was walking on the streets an hour ago. She has only some minor abrasions with no bleeding. What treatment should be offered to her?
options: No treatment as she is pregnant now
Local wound cleaning and rabies vaccine
Local wound cleaning, Rabies vaccine and Immunoglobulins
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Local wound cleaning and rabies vaccine

This case is classified under WHO category II since there was no bleeding present at the site of the dog bite and she has to be given Rabies vaccine along with local wound cleaning.

Since Rabies is a lethal disease, there is no contraindication for post-exposure prophylaxis following high-risk exposures, even in pregnancy, infancy, immunocompromised patients, and even in children with AIDS/HIV.

Note:

Patients taking chloroquine have to be given the vaccine intramuscularly as there is a reduced response to the intradermal route.

For pre-exposure prophylaxis, previous allergic reaction to any components of the vaccine is a contraindication.

Pearl PF1934: Rabies vaccines and immunoglobulins schedules

According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India:

WHO category II or III exposures should receive post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) immediately.

One intradermal (ID) dose is 0.1 mL of vaccine and one intramuscular (IM) dose is an entire vial of vaccine, irrespective of the vial size.

Should a vaccine dose be delayed for any reason, the PEP schedule should be resumed (not restarted).

Rabies Immunoglobulin(RIG):

* Passive immunization

* Single-dose; after initiation of PEP and not beyond 7 days after the first dose of vaccine

* Max dose: hRIG - 20IU/kg , eRIG - 40IU/kg body weight

* Vaccines should never be withheld regardless of the availability of RIG.

* Alternatives for RIG- WHO recommends monoclonal antibodies (mAb) as a 'cocktail' containing at least two antibodies against the rabies virus.

Administration of RIG:

* RIG should be administered into or around the wound site or sites.

* The remaining RIG, if any, should be injected IM at a site distant from the site of vaccine administration.

* RIG may be diluted to a volume sufficient for all wounds to be effectively and safely infiltrated.

Prioritization of RIG allocation (numbered according to priority order):

* Multiple bites

* Deep wounds

* Bites to head, neck, and hands

* Patients with severe immunodeficiency

* Confirmed/probable rabies in biting animal

* Bites, scratches, and exposure of mucous membranes caused by a bat

Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)

PrEP is considered in the following conditions:

* High-risk groups- laboratory staff, wildlife wardens, veterinarians, animal handlers, and travelers to endemic regions.

* Remote, rabies-endemic areas where access to PEP is difficult

* Areas where dog bite incidence is >5% per year

* Areas where vampire bat rabies is known to be present.

Pre-exposure rabies vaccination consists of two intramuscular (IM) or two intradermal (ID) doses. These are given on days 0 and 3.

* Adults - the vaccine should always be administered in the deltoid area of the arm

* Young children (under 1 year of age)- Administration into the anterolateral area of the thigh is recommended.

* Rabies vaccine should never be administered in the gluteal area. Administration in this manner will result in lower neutralizing antibody titers.

For exposed or re-exposed patients who can document previous completion of PEP the following guidelines would be applicable:

* Proper wound management should be done.

* There is no need for the administration of RIG.

* One site ID or IM vaccine administration on days 0 and 3.

Only adequate wound washing would be required in case of re-exposure where the animal bite victim has documented proof of complete PEP within the last three months.

The following cases are treated as fresh cases and given full PEP:

* Those who have previously received full post-exposure treatment with neural tissue vaccines (NTV) or vaccines of unproven potency

* Those who cannot document complete PEP or PrEP treatment

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Orthotolidine test is used to determine ________
options: Free and combined chlorine in water
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Free and combined chlorine in water

Orthotolidine (OT) test is used to determine free and combined chlorine in water.

Pearl PF0273: Chlorination of Water

* Chlorination is widely used for large scale purification of water and for drinking water.

* It is bactericidal and moderately virucidal but not sporicidal, except in high doses.

* Alongside its anti-pathogenic attributes, it oxidizes iron, manganese and hydrogen sulphide. It also destroys some taste and odor producing components. It controls algae and slime organisms and aids in coagulation.

* Action of chlorine:

* Hydrochloric acid and hypochlorous acid are formed when chlorine is added to water. Hypochlorous acid ionizes to form hydrogen and hypochlorite ions.

* H2O + Cl2 → HCl + HOCl
HOCl → H + OCl

* The disinfecting action of chlorine is predominantly due to hypochlorous acid. Hypochlorous acid is the most effective form of chlorine and it is almost 70 – 80 times more effective than hypochlorite ions.

* Chlorine acts best in water that has a pH of around 7.

* Principles of chlorination:

* The water to be disinfected must be clear of turbidity as turbidity impedes efficient chlorination.

* The chlorine demand of water is the difference between the amount of chlorine added to the water and the amount of residual chlorine remaining at the end of a specific period of contact (usually 60 minutes) at a given temperature and pH of the water. This has to be estimated before chlorination is done.

* The point at which the chlorine demand of water is met is called the breakpoint. It is beyond this that residual free chlorine begins to appear.

* Contact period of free chlorine for at least one hour is required to kill bacteria and viruses.

* Minimum recommended concentration of free chlorine is 0.5 mg/litre for one hour. Free residual chlorine provides a margin of safety against microbial contamination that occurs in storage or transport.

* The sum of the chlorine demand of the specific water plus free residual chlorine of 0.5 mg/litre constitutes the correct dose of chlorine to be applied.

* Methods of chlorination

* Chlorine gas: It is the first choice as it is cheap, quick and efficient in action and easy to apply. Special chlorinating equipments like Paterson’s chloronome are used for application of chlorine gas.

* Chloramines: These loose compounds of chlorine and ammonia give more persistent forms of residual chlorine. They have slow action and thus are not widely used.

* Perchloron or high test hypochlorite (H.T.H.): It is a calcium compound that has 60 – 70% of available chlorine.

* Break point chlorination:

* The point at which the chlorine demand of water is met is called the breakpoint.

* Free chlorine (HOCl and OCl) appears when chlorine is added beyond the breakpoint.

* In other words, at the breakpoint, if chlorine is added, then all the combined chlorines have been completely destroyed and free residual chlorines begin to appear.

* This corresponding dosage to achieve appearance of free residual chlorine is called breakpoint dosage and this method is called breakpoint chlorination.

* It is also called controlled superchlorination

* Superchlorination followed by dechlorination is used to disinfect highly polluted waters whose quality fluctuates greatly.

* Orthotolidine (OT) test:

* It is a test for chlorination and determines free and combined chlorine in water, rapidly and accurately.

* The reagent used is analytical grade Orthotolidine dissolved in 10% solution of hydrochloric acid.

* When added to water which contains chlorine, it turns yellow with varying intensity. This is faster in the presence of free chlorine and slower in the presence of combined chlorines.

* Orthotolidine - arsenite (OTA) test:

* This is a modification of the OT test which nullifies the errors caused due to interfering substances like iron, nitrites, manganese, etc.

* It determines free and combined chlorines separately.

Surveillance: There are factors which determine occurrence and distribution of diseases and other conditions of ill health. These factors are continuously scrutinised in surveillance. Monitoring is one of the essential components of surveillance concept.

Objectives of surveillance are:

* To provide information about changing health trends

* To provide feedback which can change health policy

* To provide public health disaster warnings

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The average number of children a woman would have if she were to pass through her reproductive years bearing children at the same rates as the women in her age group is called as __?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Total fertility rate

The average number of children a woman would have if she were to pass through her reproductive years bearing children at the same rates as the women in her age group is called as total fertility rate.

Pearl PF0245: Fertility Indicators

* Crude birth rate

* It is the simplest measure of fertility although its usage is unsatisfactory.

* It is the number of live births per 1000 estimated mid-year population in a given year.

* Birth rate = No. of live births during the year x 1000/Estimated mid-year population

* India, as per SRS bulletin 2018, had a birth rate of 20.0 per 1000 population

* General Fertility Rate

* It is the number of live births per 1000 women in the reproductive age group (15 - 49 years) in a given year.

* GFR = Number of live births in an area in a year x 1000/Mid-year population of women in the reproductive age in the same area in the same year.

* It is a better indicator of fertility than crude birth rate

* The demerit of this indicator is that not all women in the denominator are exposed to childbirth

* Age-specific fertility rates

* It is the number of live births in a year to 1000 women in any specified age group.

* It is a more precise measure of fertility and is also a sensitive indicator of family planning achievement.

* ASFR = Number of live births in a particular age group x 1000/Mid-year female population of the same age group.

* Total Fertility Rate

* It represents the average number of children a woman would have if she were to pass through her reproductive years bearing children at the same rates as the women in each age group now.

* It is the sum of all age specific fertility rates multiplied by 5.

* This measure gives the approximate magnitude of completed family size.

* Gross Reproductive Rate

* It is the average number of girls that would be born to a woman if she experiences the current fertility pattern throughout her reproductive span, assuming no mortality.

* Net Reproduction Rate

* It is the number of daughters a newborn girl will bear during her lifetime assuming age-specific fertility and mortality rates.

* NRR is a demographic indicator.

* NRR of 1 is equivalent of approximately the 2 child norm.

* If the NRR is less than 1, then the reproductive performance of the population is said to be inadequate.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The following diagram charts the population change over years from 1983 to 1989 in a given place. What is the statistical diagram used here?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Component bar graph

The given image shows a component bar graph or a component bar chart. The bars can be divided into two or more parts where each part represents a certain item, proportional to the magnitude of that particular item (males and females in this image).

It is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data.

The difference between a bar graph and a histogram is that the rectangles are separated by spaces representing data that forms discrete categories instead of continuous groups. Frequency polygon and Ogive can be constructed using a histogram, not a component bar chart

Pearl PF0302: Graphical Representation of Data

1. Histogram

* A histogram, by definition, is a graphical representation of frequency distribution that contains rectangles and shows the underlying frequency of a set of continuous, quantitative data.

* The X or horizontal axis is called the abscissa which usually has the group scores or class intervals of the variables/data and the Y or vertical axis is called the ordinate which usually shows the frequencies at which these variables appear.

* The following is a histogram of cholesterol levels from the Framingham Heart Study.

2. Bar Chart

* It is also called a bar graph.

* It is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data as they are not quantitative and usually qualitative.

* The difference between a bar graph and a histogram is that the rectangles are separated by spaces representing data that forms discrete categories instead of continuous groups.

* Bar graphs can be simple, multiple or component bar graphs.

3. Pie Charts

* Pie charts are also used for nominal or ordinal data.

* The categorical data are represented as segments of a circle.

4. Frequency polygons

* Frequency polygons are used for mainly ratio and interval scale data.

* In a frequency polygon, the mid-points of each class interval are joined together by straight lines.

5. Ogive

* A frequency polygon which is drawn to represent cumulative frequency distributions form a typical S-shaped curve which is called an ogive. It referred to as a cumulative frequency diagram.

6. Line chart

* It is also called a line diagram or line graph.

* Its best use is to show the trend of events or change over passage of time.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Infant parasite rate

The infant parasite rate provides the most sensitive index for recent transmission of malaria in a locality.

Infant Parasite Rate is defined as the percentage of infants showing malarial parasites in their blood films.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The present day strategy of initial screening of women for cervical cancer in a primary health centre is:
options: Visual inspection after application of freshly prepared solution 5% acetic acid solution
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Visual inspection after application of freshly prepared solution 5% acetic acid solution

The present day strategy of initial screening of women for cervical cancer is by visual inspection after application of freshly prepared solution 5% acetic acid solution.

Visual inspection with acetic acid is naked-eye examination of the uterine cervix, after application of 5% acetic acid and interpreting the result after one minute. This is a simple and inexpensive test for the detection of cervical precancerous lesions and early invasive cancer.

* Detection of well defined circum- orificial acetowhite areas or ulceroproliferative growth on the cervix will provide VIA or VIAM positive.

* In the district hospital treatment should be based on single visit colposcopy approach.

* Biopsy and Colposcopy are done to ensure that there are cytological and histological backup for the interventions.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The school health programs are managed by which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Primary health center

The school health programs are managed by the primary health centre (PHC).

The School Health Committee (1961) in India recommended that the school health services should be a part of the general health services. Since the general health services are administered through PHCs, school health programs are also managed by the PHCs under their jurisdiction.

The School Health Committee advocated the formation of school health committees at the village level, block level, district level, state level, and national level. The National School Health Council will be an advisory and coordinating body.

PHCs provide the following school health services:

* Screening of general health assessment of anemia/nutritional status, visual acuity, hearing problem, dental check-up, physical disabilities, learning disorders, and behavior problems, etc.

* Basic medicines for common ailments

* Deworming

* Mid-day meal

Note: National Programme for Mid-Day Meal in Schools has recently been renamed Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The term demographic bonus is denotes______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Decline in dependency ratio

The term demographic bonus denotes the decline in dependency ratio due to declining fertility.

A decline in the dependency ratio especially young age dependency ratio has been identified to be a key factor underlying the rapid economic development.

Demographic burden refers to an increase in the total dependency ratio, mostly caused by increased old-age dependency ratio.

Dependency ratio:

* Adults ≥65 years and children from 0 – 14 years are considered dependents.

* The total dependency ratio is the ratio of the combined dependent population to those in the age group of 15 – 65 years.

* Total dependency ratio = (children 0-14 years age + population above 65 years age) x 100/Total population in the age group of 15 – 64 years).

* It is also called societal dependency ratio.

* The total dependency ratio can also be divided into young age dependency ratio and old age dependency ratio.

* As of 2016, the dependency ratio of India is 52%.

* The potential support ratio is the inverse of the old age dependency ratio. It is the number of persons aged 15 to 64 per one older person aged 65 or more.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Two vacccines - Measles and the pentavalent vaccine are used during an immunisation programme. Which of these vaccines has to be discarded?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Measles

Open vial policy is not applicable for BCG, JE, Measles vaccines and Rota virus.

All open vials of BCG, measles and JE must be destroyed after 48 hours or before next session, whichever is earlier.

Open vial policy  is applicable for DPT, TT, hepatitis B vaccine, OPV and liquid pentavalent vaccine.

Pearl PF2122: Open Vial Policy

Open vial policy allows for reuse of partially used multidose vials of applicable vaccines under the Universal Immunization Programme in subsequent sessions up to 4 weeks subject to certain conditions and thereby reducing vaccine wastage.

It is applicable only for DPT, TT, hepatitis B vaccine, OPV, liquid pentavalent vaccine, rotavirus vaccine(new version with the VVM on the side), and JE vaccines (inactivated). It is not applicable to BCG and measles vaccines.

Vaccine vials opened in session-site can be used in more than one session up to four weeks if expiry date has not passed, if storage and transport was appropriate, no contamination has occurred in vial septum, asepsis in withdrawing was practiced and if vaccine vial monitor has not reached discard point.

Open vials should not be submerged in water. All open vials should have a record of date and time of opening. At the end of a session, all vaccines should be returned to the cold chain point and segregated as re-usable and non-reusable. All open vials of BCG, measles must be destroyed after 48 hours or before next session, whichever is earlier.

In case of any adverse events following immunization, all open vials should not be discarded until investigation is complete. All vials must be transported in zipper bags in the vaccine carrier and recorded in stock register. Ice packs used should be well sealed.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the health insurance package provided for an eligible family per year, in the Ayushman Bharat scheme?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 5 Lakhs per family per year

Under the Ayushman Bharat scheme Government provides health insurance cover of upto 5 Lakhs per family, per year.

Ayushman Bharat-National Health Protection Mission: To build a comprehensive need-based health care service. Dr R.S. Sharma is the Chief Executive Officer of the AB- NHPM.

Components: The target of the two initiatives mentioned below are to build a New India 2022.

* Creation of 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centres- These centres will provide Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC), covering both maternal and child health services and non-communicable diseases, including free essential drugs and diagnostic services. The first Health and Wellness Centre was launched by the Prime Minister at Jangla, Bijapur, Chhatisgarh on 14 April 2018.

* The second component is the National Health Protection Mission (NHPM) which provides health protection cover to poor and vulnerable families. The Health and Wellness Centres will play a critical role in creating awareness about AB-NHPM, screening for non-communicable diseases, follow-up of hospitalisation cases among others.

Beneficiary Level:

* Government provides health insurance cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 per family per year.

* More than 10.74 crore poor and vulnerable families (approximately 50 crore beneficiaries) covered across the country.

* All families listed in the SECC database as per defined criteria will be covered. No cap on family size and age of members.

* Priority to girl child, women and and senior citizens.

* Free treatment available at all public and empaneled private hospitals in times of need.

* Covers secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.

* 1,350 medical packages covering surgery, medical and day care treatments, cost of medicines and diagnostics.

* All pre-existing diseases covered. Hospitals cannot deny treatment.

* Cashless and paperless access to quality health care services.

* Hospitals will not be allowed to charge any additional money from beneficiaries for the treatment.

* Can reach out for information, assistance, complaints and grievances to a 24X7 helpline number - 14555

Ayushman Bharat Diwas is being celebrated across the country on April 30.

On 12 December 2012, the United Nations General Assembly endorsed a resolution urging countries to accelerate progress toward universal health coverage (UHC) – the idea that everyone, everywhere should have access to quality, affordable health care - as an essential priority for international development. International Universal Health Coverage Day aims to raise awareness of the need for strong and resilient health systems and universal health coverage

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the largest fund for population and reproduction-related programs?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. UNFPA

United Nations Population Fund or formerly known as United Nations Fund for Population Activities(UNFPA), is the largest fund for sexual and reproductive health activities.

The goals of UNFPA are:

* To support reproductive health care for the women and the youth

* To help pregnant women, especially the ones who face maternal complications

* Provide access for all to modern contraceptives.

* Provide training for health workers to ensure childbirths are supervised by skilled attendants

* Prevention of gender-based violence and female genital mutilation

* Prevention of teen pregnancies and ending child marriage

* Delivery of safe birth supplies, dignity kits, and other materials to survivors of conflict and natural disaster

* Collection of data, census and analyze them for development and planning.

The Resources and Funding are divided into core resources and non-core resources.

Core resources are used to effectively provide essential sexual and reproductive health services to those in need and in crisis.

Non-core resources include thematic funds such as UNFPA Supplies, the Maternal and New-born Health Thematic Fund, the Humanitarian Action Thematic Fund, Population Data Thematic Fund, and other funds which are goal-based. Some of the others include regional, issue-based or multi-country programs and initiatives.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What phase of the demographic cycle is the low stationary phase of demographic cycle?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Phase 4

Phase 4 is called the low stationary phase in which birth rate and death rate are low and they cancel each other.

* It is the 4 th phase of the demographic cycle.

* Population fails to grow.

* Demographic gap is 0.

* Eg. Australia, UK, Denmark, Belgium and Sweden.

Pearl PF0983: Demographic Process and Cycle

* Demographic process

* Fertility

* Mortality

* Marriage

* Migration

* Social Mobility

* Demographic cycle

* Stage 1 : High stationary

* High birth rate and high death rate render the population stationary.

* Narrow demographic gap.

* Stage 2 : Early expanding

* Death rate declines and birth rate remains unchanged

* Demographic gap starts increasing and then becomes maximum

* Stage 3 : Late expanding

* Death rate decline further and birth rate falls

* India is in this stage, currently

* Demographic gap starts declining

* Stage 4 : Low stationary

* Low birth rate and low death rate renders the population stationary

* Narrow demographic gap

* Stage 5 : Declining

* Population begins to decline as birth rate is lower than death rate

* Demographic gap is negative

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which agency promotes health awareness in India?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Central Health Education Bureau

The Central Health Education Bureau(CHEB), under the Directorate General of Health Services is responsible for promoting health education in India.

The five divisions of CHEB are :

* Media and editorial division

* Health promotion and education

* School health education division

* Training Division

* Administrative Division

The objectives of CHEB are to :

* Interpret the plans, programmes and achievements of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

* Design, guide and conduct research in health behaviour, health education processes and aids.

* Produce and distribute type health education material in relation to various health problems and programmes.

* Train key health and community welfare workers in health education and research methods, evolve effective methodology and tools of training.

* Help schools and teacher training institutes for health education of the school population.

* Provide guidelines for the organizational set-up and functioning of health education units at the state, district and other levels.

* Offer technical help to official and non-official agencies engaged in health education work and coordinate their programmes.

* Collaborate with international agencies in promoting health education activities.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the initial step when an immunization survey is being conducted?
options: Completing the cluster and summary forms
Calculating the total fertility rate of the area
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Cluster identification

Among the following options, finding a cluster is the first step to be done in an immunization survey.

The five major steps of an immunization survey are as follows:

* Plan the survey

* Conduct the survey

* Tabulate data

* Analyse data

* Take action

1. Planning the survey includes selecting the children based on age groups, finding clusters among the population, and deciding how many interviewers are needed for the survey.

2. Conducting the survey includes the actual process in which interviewers visit houses and get information on the immunization status of the children or the clusters.

3. Data tabulation includes completing the cluster forms and summary forms that organize the data collected.

4. Analysis of the data procured occurs next which can evaluate immunization status and the reasons for immunization failure if any.

5. The last step includes taking action on the reports made by evaluating the data.

An immunization survey gives information on the total coverage of the population and areas where the immunization services can be improved. Actions can be done by increasing the immunization programs if the coverage is low or targeting a specific population or cluster to improve their immunization status.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following vaccines has faster seroconversion rate as compared to the incubation period of the disease?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Measles

In the following options, measles has faster seroconversion rates as compared to its incubation period.

The incubation period of measles when acquired naturally is 10 days from exposure to the onset of fever and up to 14 days from exposure to the appearance of the rash. When measles infection is artificially induced bypassing the respiratory tract (as with injection of live measles vaccine), the incubation period is somewhat shortened, averaging 7 days.

This is the reason that measles vaccines are given when a disaster or epidemic occurs.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which organization does not fund The National TB program of India?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. UNICEF

The funding for the National TB program of India is done by all, except option D, UNICEF.

The procurement of Anti TB drugs, equipment like microscopes, and diagnostics like CBNAAT cartridges are done mainly from the Domestic Budgetary Sources, that is the budget allocated by the Govt. of India for this program, World Bank, and The Global Fund.

The Central Medical Services Society (CMSS), an independent and autonomous body under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare procures the drugs and other materials through the DBS and World Bank funding.

However, The Global Fund is made use of by the Global Drug Facility which is administered and housed by the United Nations Office for Project Services.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which test uses the graph given below to assess the viral load in a test sample ?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Real time RTPCR

The image shows the Ct value(Cycle threshold) of Real-time RTPCR which can be used to assess the viral genetic load.

The image shows a graph with cycle number on the X-axis and relative fluorescence on the Y-axis. At 25.6 there is an exponential rise in the fluorescence which is the Ct value for the sample.

The cycle threshold (Ct) can be defined as the thermal cycle number at which the fluorescent signal exceeds that of the background and thus passes the threshold for positivity.

The first step for a real-time RTPCR is by extracting the viral RNA from the sample followed by purifying and concentrating it. They are then added to a mixture of primers, nucleotide bases, enzymes for the reaction, and fluorescently labeled probes (short stretches of nucleic acid which stick to the target ). The primers initially attach to the viral nucleic acid which is RNA and a complementary DNA strand is made using the nucleotides in the mixture. It is then subjected to repeated thermal cycles so that the copies of the viral targets are increased. The labeled probes stick to the viral genome and emit a fluorescent signal. An exponential rise occurs early when the viral load in the sample is high when compared to a less viral load.

A typical RT-PCR assay will have a maximum of 40 thermal cycles. The lower the Ct value the higher the quantity of viral genetic material in the sample.

A 3-point increase in Ct value is roughly equivalent to a 10-fold decrease in the quantity of viral genetic material. Low Ct values more likely indicate acute disease and high infectivity whereas high Ct values can be attributed to reduced viral load but might need clinical interpretation.

Note:

Ct values cannot be used to compare different types of assays nor does it provide information on the course of the illness. However, it can be used for clinical management in a hospital setting.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Panel discussion

The given premise best denotes a panel discussion.

In a panel discussion,

* 4 to 8 experts are allowed to have a discussion on a topic in front of an audience.

* No speeches or order is set beforehand.

* A moderator is present to regulate the discussion.

* The audience is invited to speak after the discussion and ask questions.

A workshop is a series of meetings with an emphasis on individual work within a group, with the use of external consultants or experts. It can be divided into small groups each with a chairman and recorder. Each individual solves a part of the problem and leaves the workshop with a plan of action.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 35-year-old man is unemployed because he is unable to walk after an accident. His unemployment is classified as a _______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Handicap

The patient here being unemployed can be classified as handicap, according to the concept given below.

Disease → Impairment → Disability → Handicap

* Impairment is any loss or abnormality in normal structure or function.

* Disability is the inability to carry out normal actions due to impairment.

* Handicap is experiencing disadvantages due to disability and inability to discharge obligations normally.

In the given example:

* Accident: Disease (or disorder)

* Loss of foot: Impairment (extrinsic or intrinsic)

* Cannot walk: Disability (objectified)

* Unemployed: Handicap (socialized)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 40 year old female with no comorbidities complaints of swelling in both her legs which was acute in onset . She also gives a history of loose stools. Her family members too has similar symptoms. On examination there was no signs of inflammation in both the legs. Detailed history revealed that mustard oil is a staple part of their diet . Which of the following substance is responsible for her condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Sanguinarine

The clinical presentation is suggestive of epidemic dropsy and Sanguinarine is the toxic compound responsible for this.

Epidemic Dropsy: Contamination of mustard oil with argemone oil.

* Toxic compound: Sanguinarine

* Mechanism of action : Sanguinarine interfers with the oxidation of pyruvic acid which inturn accumulates in the blood and causes symptoms.

* Clinical presentation :The patient presents with sudden onset, non inflammatory swelling of bilateral legs which is often associated with diarrhoea. Some patients can develop glaucoma. Dyspnea, cardiac failure and death can occur in later stages.

* Mortality rate - 5-50%

Tests to detect argemone oil:

* Nitric acid test

* Paper chromatography: most sensitive(can detect very low concentration of argemone oil)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: If a wide range of values are present in a community, what is the best measure of central tendency?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Median

The best measure of central tendency if there are a wide range of values is median.

If we take an example of a dataset of (1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 11, 41), we can see that 41 seems to be well away from the mean of 7.45 of the dataset.  If we eliminate this outlier, we can get a new dataset of (1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 11) with a median of 4.5 and a mean of 4.1. We see that the median only changed by 10% (went down to 4.5 from 5), while the mean decreased by 45%. Therefore, the median is less affected by outliers or extreme values.

The median is not sensitive to extreme values or outliers and thus it is the preferred measure of central tendency in a distribution with a wide range of values.

* The median is the central element in a distribution when all the elements are arranged in order.

* In a distribution that has an odd number of elements, the median is the middle value.

* In a distribution that has an even number of elements, the median is the average of the middle values, i.e., the arithmetic mean of the two middle values.

* The drawback of the median is that it doesn’t respond to the actual values of the elements but only to the number of values above or below it.

* The median is the same as the 50th centile.

* It is sometimes symbolized by Mdn.

* The median can be arrived at in ordinal, interval and ratio data scales.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The best way to plot trends in the incidence of diarrheal disease in a given area is by?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Line graph

Line graphs or line diagrams are the best way to plot trends in the incidence of a disease in a given area.

Pearl PF0302: Graphical Representation of Data

1. Histogram

* A histogram, by definition, is a graphical representation of frequency distribution that contains rectangles and shows the underlying frequency of a set of continuous, quantitative data.

* The X or horizontal axis is called the abscissa which usually has the group scores or class intervals of the variables/data and the Y or vertical axis is called the ordinate which usually shows the frequencies at which these variables appear.

* The following is a histogram of cholesterol levels from the Framingham Heart Study.

2. Bar Chart

* It is also called a bar graph.

* It is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data as they are not quantitative and usually qualitative.

* The difference between a bar graph and a histogram is that the rectangles are separated by spaces representing data that forms discrete categories instead of continuous groups.

* Bar graphs can be simple, multiple or component bar graphs.

3. Pie Charts

* Pie charts are also used for nominal or ordinal data.

* The categorical data are represented as segments of a circle.

4. Frequency polygons

* Frequency polygons are used for mainly ratio and interval scale data.

* In a frequency polygon, the mid-points of each class interval are joined together by straight lines.

5. Ogive

* A frequency polygon which is drawn to represent cumulative frequency distributions form a typical S-shaped curve which is called an ogive. It referred to as a cumulative frequency diagram.

6. Line chart

* It is also called a line diagram or line graph.

* Its best use is to show the trend of events or change over passage of time.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The given type of population pyramid indicates all except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Developed countries

The given image shows an age pyramid/population pyramid with a broad base and tapering top. The age pyramid is plotted as a younger age at the bottom and older age at the top. Hence this age pyramid represents a higher young population. This pyramid is typical of developing countries, and not developed countries.

This type of pyramid also indicates an increasing population because of high young population reflecting high fertility.

Pearl PF1861: Population Pyramid

* The age or population pyramid is used to represent the age/sex structure of a population.

* Below is the age pyramid of India (2017).

* The age pyramid of India has a broad base and a tapering top, as it is with most developing countries.

* As a nation develops the lower portion of the pyramid will start constricting and the upper portion will start increasing.

* Developed countries usually will have a bulge in the middle with a narrow base, as shown below in the age pyramid of Switzerland.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The major contributor to demographic burden is __________.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Increased old age dependency ratio

Demographic burden refers to an increase in the total dependency ratio, mostly caused by an increased old-age dependency ratio.

The term demographic bonus denotes the decline in dependency ratio due to declining fertility.

Note :

A decline in the dependency ratio especially the young age dependency ratio has been identified to be a key factor underlying the rapid economic development.

Pearl PF0983: Demographic Process and Cycle

* Demographic process

* Fertility

* Mortality

* Marriage

* Migration

* Social Mobility

* Demographic cycle

* Stage 1 : High stationary

* High birth rate and high death rate render the population stationary.

* Narrow demographic gap.

* Stage 2 : Early expanding

* Death rate declines and birth rate remains unchanged

* Demographic gap starts increasing and then becomes maximum

* Stage 3 : Late expanding

* Death rate decline further and birth rate falls

* India is in this stage, currently

* Demographic gap starts declining

* Stage 4 : Low stationary

* Low birth rate and low death rate renders the population stationary

* Narrow demographic gap

* Stage 5 : Declining

* Population begins to decline as birth rate is lower than death rate

* Demographic gap is negative

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which amongst the following can be used to treat kesari dal toxicity?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Vitamin C

Vitamin C in doses of 500-1000 mg can be used for the prevention and treatment of lathyrism (kesari dal toxicity).

Lathyrism is a paralyzing disease of humans and animals. It is due to the consumption of khesari dal or Lathyrus sativus. When the husk is removed, it looks similar to red gram or Bengal gram. It is mostly consumed by poor agricultural laborers because it is relatively cheap. Lathyrism is more prevalent in parts of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, and Bihar. The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act in India has banned Lathyrus sativus in all forms (whole/ split/ flour).

In humans, it is referred to as neurolathyrism because it affects the nervous system. It is characterized by gradually developing spastic paralysis of the lower limbs. Beta-oxalyl amino alanine (BOAA) is the toxic compound causing this disease. It is water-soluble and can be removed by the following methods:

* Soaking pulses in hot water and discarding the water

* Overnight soaking in lime water, followed by boiling

* Parboiling - for large-scale detoxification
