questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following demographic indicators is used to compare the life expectancy of two different countries?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. HDI

The demographic indicator used to compare the life expectancy of two different countries is Human Development Index(HDI).

Human Development Index (HDI) is a measure of a country's average achievements in three dimensions of human development. The components include:

* A long and healthy life, as measured by life expectancy at birth

* Knowledge (literacy), as measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling, and

* A decent standard of living, as measured by GNI (gross national income) per capita.

HDI values range from 0 to 1, with 1 as the maximum value.

Life expectancy at 1 year, literacy and infant mortality rate are components of the Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the most common cause of macrocytic anemia?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Alcohol

Alcohol is the most common cause of macrocytic anaemia.

Macrocytic anemia can be megaloblastic anemia and non-megaloblastic anemia. Alcohol causes non megaloblastic macrocytic anemia.

Other causes of macrocytic anaemia:

* Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency

* Bone marrow disorders

* Liver disease

* Drug-induced

* HIV

* Multiple myeloma

* Complication of bariatric surgery

Megaloblastic anemia is a type of macrocytic anemia with impaired nucleic acid metabolism. Nuclear maturation lags behind cytoplasmic maturation. The causes include:

* Vitamin B12 deficiency

* Folate deficiency

* Drugs (Methotrexate)

Vitamin B12 or cobalamin is a water-soluble vitamin that is derived from animal products such as red meat, dairy, and eggs. Other causes of B12 deficiency includes

* Malabsorption (Pernicious anemia)

* Total or partial gastrectomy

* Ileal resection

* Tropical sprue

Clinical features of cyanocobalamin and folate deficiency (megaloblastic anemia) include:

* Anorexia, weight loss, diarrhea, or constipation

* Oral manifestations: glossitis, angular cheilosis

* Mild fever in more severely anemic patients

* Jaundice (unconjugated)

* Reversible melanin skin hyperpigmentation

* Bruising (thrombocytopenia) and infections (low leucocyte count)

* Complications in pregnancy: recurrent fetal loss and neural tube defects

* Cardiovascular disease: cerebrovascular, peripheral vascular, and coronary heart disease with deep vein thrombosis

* Neurologic manifestations: Bilateral peripheral neuropathy or degeneration of the posterior and pyramidal tracts of the spinal cord (SACDSC). Seen in only B12 deficiency.

* Psychiatric disturbances

* RR = 1 indicates no association.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding the fifth stage of the demographic cycle?
options: Birth rate falls below death rate
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Birth rate falls below death rate

In stage 5 of the demographic cycle, the birth rate falls below the death rate.

In this stage, the death rate attains a low stable rate while the birth rate keeps declining. Thus, the curve of the birth rate will cross the curve of the death rate in a graph of the demographic cycle and falls further below.

The demographic gap is negative and the population is declining. So, this stage is known as the declining stage.

* Demographic gap starts increasing and then becomes maximum

* Stage 3 : Late expanding

* Death rate decline further and birth rate falls

* India is in this stage, currently
