questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 15-year-old girl presents to you with her mother, reporting abdominal discomfort and is found to be 12 weeks pregnant based on a positive urine pregnancy test. As a medical professional, what would be your initial course of action?
options: Get consent from mother for P/V
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Inform police

Any pregnancy in a minor (<18 years) is legally considered statutory rape, regardless of consent. Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 (POCSO Act), healthcare professionals are mandated to report suspected sexual offences involving minors. Failure to report such cases is a punishable offence.

In this question, pregnancy in a 13-year-old is classified as a medico-legal case under the POCSO Act, as the girl is a minor and sexual activity is presumed to be an offence.

The first legal obligation of the medical professional is to inform the police, irrespective of consent or clinical findings.

Clinical examination and consent procedures follow after mandatory reporting, ensuring legal protection for the child and the healthcare provider.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 3-year-old child has a long-standing history of rickets and malnutrition. The child’s growth is below the 5th percentile, and there has been no exposure to sunlight. Which of the following national programs specifically addresses nutritional deficiencies among children below 6 years of age?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. ICDS Program

The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) programme is the primary national initiative addressing nutrition, growth, and development of children below 6 years of age.

The child in the question:

• Age 3 years
• Has malnutrition and rickets
• Falls under preschool age group (<6 years)

ICDS directly addresses these issues through nutrition supplementation and health services delivered via Anganwadi centres.

Target Beneficiaries of ICDS

Thus, ICDS is the primary national program for child nutrition below 6 years.

It provides supplementary nutrition, growth monitoring, health check-ups, immunization support, and nutrition education through Anganwadi centres.

Programs like Mid-Day Meal target school-age children, while Anemia Mukt Bharat and NNAPP focus on anemia rather than comprehensive early childhood nutrition.

Six Services Under ICDS

These services are delivered through Anganwadi centres

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 30-week primigravida c/o reduced vision at night. She has been avoiding papaya, mango, and other fruits throughout her pregnancy as she thinks they could be abortifacients. It is the primary duty of which of the following workers to provide counselling and information to the patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. ASHA

The woman has night blindness due to vitamin A deficiency, caused by dietary misconceptions during pregnancy.

Providing health education, counselling, and correcting food myths at the community and household level is the primary role of ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 70-year-old patient with a history of progressive vision loss is scheduled for cataract surgery under the National Program for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment. Which of the following is NOT an accurate guideline or inclusion criterion for cataract surgery within this national program?
options: Patients requiring cataract surgeries are selected and asked to report to base hospital
Perform more small incision cataract surgery
To do surgery in rural area with make shift hospital/Ots
To perform surgeries in fixed facility surgery by shifting patients from rural area
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. To do surgery in rural area with make shift hospital/Ots

Under the National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI), cataract surgeries are emphasized to be performed in fixed, well-equipped facilities to ensure asepsis, quality, and patient safety.

The program focuses on:

• Cataract surgery
• Refractive error correction
• Eye screening programs
• Strengthening ophthalmic infrastructure

Cataract remains the leading cause of blindness in India, accounting for a large proportion of avoidable blindness.

Current approach emphasizes:

Thus, makeshift operation theatres are no longer recommended.

Patients from rural areas are mobilized and transported to base hospitals rather than conducting surgeries in makeshift or temporary operating theatres.

The program promotes small incision cataract surgery (SICS) with standardized protocols to reduce complications and improve outcomes.

OPTION C. Surgery in rural areas with makeshift OT- Temporary operating theatres were used earlier in cataract camps, but are now discouraged due to risk of infection and poor surgical conditions.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A city has a total population of 70,00,000, of which 30% resides in slum areas. According to the existing Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), how many Urban Primary Health Centers (Urban PHCs) should be established to cater to the slum population?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 42

As per IPHS norms, one Urban PHC caters to \~50,000 slum population.

Slum population = 30% of 70,00,000 = 21,00,000.

According to IPHS / NUHM guidelines:

Required Urban PHCs = 21,00,000 ÷ 50,000 = 42. Thus, 42 Urban PHCs are needed to adequately serve the slum population.

Urban PHCs were strengthened under the National Urban Health Mission (NUHM). Urban poor populations often face:

• Overcrowding
• Poor sanitation
• Limited healthcare access
• Higher communicable disease burden

Thus, more densely distributed health centres are required.

Urban Health Facility Structure (NUHM)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A male patient who was diagnosed with tuberculosis has successfully completed the full course of treatment. Subsequent to finishing both the intensive and continuation phases, the initial sputum examination was conducted. The results of this examination were negative. What is the current condition of the patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Cured

Under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP), treatment outcomes are defined based on:

• Completion of therapy
• Sputum examination results

A patient is classified as “cured” when they have completed the full course of anti-tubercular treatment and have documented bacteriological negativity at the end of treatment.

| Outcome | Definition

| ------- | ----------

| Cured | Bacteriologically confirmed TB + completed treatment + negative sputum

| Treatment completed | Completed treatment but no sputum result available

| Treatment failed | Sputum positive at end of treatment

| Lost to follow-up | Treatment interrupted ≥ 1 month

In this case, the patient completed both the intensive and continuation phases, and the post-treatment sputum examination is negative, fulfilling the criteria for cure.

“Treatment completed” is used only when bacteriological confirmation is unavailable at the end of therapy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A pregnant woman in her second trimester with anemia has been receiving iron and folic acid supplementation under the Anemia Mukt Bharat Program. Which additional supplement should be included to enhance the effectiveness of the treatment?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Albendazole

Under the Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) strategy, deworming with Albendazole is an essential adjunct to iron and folic acid (IFA) supplementation in pregnant women (after the first trimester). Treating intestinal helminthic infections improves iron absorption, reduces chronic blood loss, and enhances the response to IFA therapy.

Why not the other options?

• A. Albendazole: ✔ Correct. Given as a single 400 mg dose after the first trimester in endemic areas as part of AMB.
• B. Vitamin A: Not routinely recommended during pregnancy due to the risk of teratogenicity with high doses.
• C. Green leafy vegetables: Beneficial dietary advice but not the additional programmatic intervention under AMB.
• D. Non-vegetarian food: Improves dietary iron intake but is not a component of the AMB supplementation strategy.

Note: Anemia Mukt Bharat Program 2018 -

| Age Group | Iron (mg) | Folic Acid (mcg) | Frequency | Remark

| --------- | --------- | ---------------- | --------- | ------

| 6–59 months children | 20 mg elemental | 100 mcg | Biweekly | Bottle (50 mL)

| 5–9 years children | 45 mg elemental | 400 mcg | Weekly | Pink color tablet

| 10–19 years adolescents | 60 mg elemental | 500 mcg | Weekly | Blue color tablet

| 20–49 years women (NPNL) | 60 mg elemental | 500 mcg | Weekly | Red color tablet

| Pregnant and lactating mothers | 60 mg elemental | 500 mcg | Daily | Red color tablet

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A pregnant woman visits a Primary Health Centre (PHC) for routine antenatal care. The healthcare provider conducts antenatal check-ups, administers immunizations, counsels on breastfeeding and family planning, and provides essential maternal and child health (MCH) services. Which of the following personnel is primarily responsible for delivering these services at the PHC level?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM)

The Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM) is the frontline female health worker responsible for delivering maternal and child health (MCH) and reproductive health services in the public healthcare system. ANMs are posted at Sub-centres and also work at Primary Health Centres (PHCs).

Their key responsibilities include:

• Antenatal, intranatal, and postnatal care
• Immunization of mothers and children
• Family planning counseling and services
• Growth monitoring of children
• Health education and nutrition counseling
• Basic management of common illnesses and referral of high-risk cases

ANMs play a central role in implementing national programs such as the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) and RMNCH+A services.

Why not the other options?

• A. Pharmacist: Responsible for dispensing medicines, maintaining drug stocks, and ensuring rational drug use. Does not routinely provide MCH services.
• B. ASHA worker: An Accredited Social Health Activist is a community-based volunteer, not a regular salaried PHC employee. She mobilizes the community, promotes institutional deliveries, facilitates immunization, and links people to health services but does not independently provide comprehensive MCH care.
• C. Staff Nurse: Provides nursing care, assists in inpatient and emergency services, and supports obstetric care, but the designated frontline MCH worker is the ANM.

High-yield pearl

| Health worker | Primary role

| ------------- | ------------

| ANM | Maternal & child health, immunization, family planning, antenatal care

| ASHA | Community mobilization, home visits, health education, referral

| Staff Nurse | Nursing care, inpatient and labour room services

| Pharmacist | Drug dispensing and inventory management

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A public health officer wants to assess environmental iodine deficiency in a district. Which indicator should be used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Neonatal hypothyroidism prevalence

Park lists four criteria for assessing Iodine Deficiency Disorders (IDD) in a community: goitre prevalence, urinary iodine excretion, neonatal hypothyroidism, and thyroid function tests (T4/TSH). Among these, neonatal hypothyroidism is specifically described as the indicator of "environmental iodine deficiency" — because the neonatal thyroid has minimal iodine reserve, it is the most sensitive tissue to a deficient environment, and neonatal TSH reflects iodine status at the time of birth rather than years of past exposure. The cut-off: if >3% of neonates have TSH >5 mIU/L on cord/heel-prick blood, environmental iodine deficiency exists in that population. It also carries a direct public-health meaning — risk of brain damage in the community.

Other options:

• A. Serum thyroxine → an individual diagnostic test, poor sensitivity for community surveys; often normal in mild deficiency.
• B. Goitre prevalence → indicator of chronic/past iodine deficiency; goitre persists for years even after iodine repletion ("goitre lags"). Used for grading endemicity (>5% in 6–12 yr children = endemic).
• D. Urinary iodine excretion → best indicator of current dietary iodine intake / recent nutritional status (median <100 µg/L = deficiency). Reflects intake, not the disease burden of environmental deficiency.

Pearl:

• Goitre = past deficiency
• Urinary iodine = present intake
• Neonatal hypothyroidism = environmental deficiency + brain damage risk.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A woman earning ₹20,000 undergoes a tubectomy. How many days of leave is she entitled to?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 14 days

Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (as amended), a woman who undergoes a tubectomy operation is entitled to 2 weeks (14 days) of paid leave immediately following the procedure.

• The salary mentioned (₹20,000) does not change the duration of leave.

Why not the other options?

• A. 4 days: Incorrect; no such provision exists.
• B. 7 days: Incorrect; 7 days is not the leave entitlement for tubectomy under the Maternity Benefit Act.
• D. 10 days: Incorrect; the statutory leave is 14 days.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Aarogya Mandir (Ayushman Arogya Mandir) provides community-level awareness and promotive services in multiple domains. Which of the following is NOT included in its scope?
options: Promotion of balanced diet and nutrition counselling
Household hygiene practices including washing and ironing of clothes
Preventive, promotive, and basic curative health services
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Household hygiene practices including washing and ironing of clothes

Ayushman Arogya Mandir focuses on health promotion, nutrition, safe water, and basic health services; domestic activities like laundry are outside its scope.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following are the components of Anemia Mukt Bharat Programme except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 6 departments

The Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) strategy is structured around 6×6×6 framework, which includes 6 target beneficiary groups, 6 interventions, and 6 institutional mechanisms.

The 6 Beneficiary Groups

The program targets populations most vulnerable to anemia:

1. Children (6–59 months)
2. Children (5–9 years)
3. Adolescents (10–19 years)
4. Women of reproductive age (15–49 years)
5. Pregnant women
6. Lactating mothers

The 6 Interventions of Anemia Mukt Bharat:

1. Prophylactic Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) Supplementation: Age-appropriate dosage for children (6-59 months), children (5-9 years), adolescents (10-19 years), women of reproductive age (15-49 years), pregnant women, and lactating women.
2. Periodic Deworming: Administering anthelmintic drugs (Albendazole) to children, adolescents, and pregnant women to eliminate parasitic worms.
3. Intensified Year-Round Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) Campaign: Promoting healthy eating habits (Solid Body, Smart Mind), including iron-rich foods and delayed cord clamping (by 3 minutes) at birth.
4. Testing and Treatment of Anemia: Using digital, non-invasive methods (digital haemoglobinometer) for testing and point-of-care treatment.
5. Mandatory Provision of Iron & Folic Acid Fortified Foods: Ensuring IFA-fortified foods are available in all government-funded public health programs.
6. Addressing Non-Nutritional Causes of Anemia: Targeting anemia in endemic areas caused by malaria, hemoglobinopathies, and fluorosis.

The 6 Institutional Mechanisms

These ensure proper implementation and monitoring:

1. Inter-ministerial coordination
2. National Anaemia Mukt Bharat Unit
3. Convergence with other programs
4. Supply chain management
5. Digital monitoring
6. Capacity building and training

Understanding the structural pillars of AMB helps distinguish program design elements from implementation personnel.

*This is a MCQ of 2024 - This has now been proposed to be updated to 7X7X7 in 2026-

What's new in 7×7×7

| Layer | 7th addition

| ----- | ------------

| Beneficiary group | Low Birth Weight (LBW) babies, 0–6 months — to break the intergenerational cycle of anemia at the earliest stage

| Intervention | "Eating Right" approach — daily conscious consumption of diversified, iron-rich diets

| Institutional mechanism | Digitally integrated Monitoring & Evaluation framework for end-to-end accountability

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An 18-year-old girl has a low hemoglobin level. What is the recommended therapeutic dose of iron-folic acid?
options: 45 mg elemental iron + 400µg folic acid once daily
60 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid twice daily
100 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid once daily
100 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid twice daily
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 60 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid twice daily

All children between 10-19 years of age diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia should receive therapeutic iron-folic acid (IFA) supplementation, which is higher than the prophylactic dose. In many Indian public health/PSM examination questions, the recommended therapeutic regimen for school-aged children with anemia is:

• 60 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid twice daily for 3 months, followed by reassessment of hemoglobin.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) mobilizes pregnant women for antenatal check-ups, encourages families to attend Village Health, Sanitation and Nutrition Day (VHSND) sessions, promotes immunization, and conducts health education within the community. These activities primarily reflect which principle of Primary Health Care (PHC)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Community participation

Community participation is one of the four fundamental principles of Primary Health Care (PHC) as outlined in the Alma-Ata Declaration (1978). It emphasizes the active involvement of individuals, families, and the community in planning, implementing, and utilizing health services.

ASHA workers are community-based health activists who:

• Mobilize people to attend Village Health, Sanitation and Nutrition Day (VHSND) sessions
• Promote antenatal care and institutional deliveries
• Encourage childhood immunization
• Provide health education on nutrition, sanitation, and family planning
• Serve as a link between the community and the health system

These responsibilities primarily foster community ownership and participation, making community participation the best answer.

Why not the other options?

• B. Equitable distribution: Refers to ensuring equal access to essential health services for all sections of the population, especially underserved groups. Although ASHAs help improve access, their defining role in VHSNDs is community mobilization.
• C. Intersectoral coordination: Involves collaboration between sectors such as health, education, sanitation, nutrition, agriculture, and rural development. While VHSNDs involve multiple sectors, the ASHA's primary function is to engage the community.
• D. Appropriate technology: Refers to the use of simple, scientifically sound, affordable, and locally acceptable technologies, such as ORS, home-based newborn care, and rapid diagnostic tests.

High-yield pearl

Four principles of Primary Health Care (Alma-Ata):

1. Equitable distribution – Health care for all, with emphasis on underserved populations.
2. Community participation – Active involvement of the community in health programs.
3. Intersectoral coordination – Collaboration among health and non-health sectors.
4. Appropriate technology – Affordable, practical, evidence-based interventions.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Assuming that a pregnancy was confirmed, the ASHA informed Mrs. M that she should take iron and folic acid (IFA) supplementation for a minimum of X days during her pregnancy period, under the Government’s Anaemia Mukt Bharat Programme. Which one among the following best represents X?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 180

Under the Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) Programme, pregnant women are advised to take daily iron–folic acid (IFA) supplementation for a minimum of 180 days during pregnancy.

• IFA tablet: 60 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid
• Duration during pregnancy: ≥180 days
• Supplementation is continued for 180 days postpartum as well.

Therefore, X = 180 days → C.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following advices to be given by the ASHA to Mrs. M, assuming pregnancy has been confirmed, regarding personal hygiene measures: 1. Minimum 12 hours sleep at a stretch at night 2. Avoid resting immediately after mid-day meals 3. Avoid intake of extra fluids to avoid constipation 4. Avoid taking purgatives like castor oil to relieve constipation How many of the four advices listed above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Two

Let’s assess each advice:

1. Minimum 12 hours of sleep at a stretch at night — Incorrect

• Pregnant women generally require adequate rest and sleep, but 12 hours of continuous nighttime sleep is not a standard recommendation.

2. Avoid resting immediately after mid-day meals — Correct

• Avoiding lying down immediately after meals helps reduce indigestion and heartburn during pregnancy.

3. Avoid extra fluids to prevent constipation — Incorrect

• Adequate fluid intake helps prevent constipation. Pregnant women should be encouraged to maintain adequate hydration.

4. Avoid purgatives such as castor oil for constipation — Correct

• Castor oil and other strong purgatives should be avoided during pregnancy because they can stimulate intestinal contractions and potentially cause uterine contractions.

Therefore, 2 statements are correct → B. Two.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following organizations of importance in the history of international health: 1. The Health Organization of the League of Nations 2. The Pan American Sanitary Bureau 3. The United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration 4. The World Health Organization Which one of the following represents the correct chronological order (from the oldest to the newest) of the establishment of these organizations?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2 → 1 → 3 → 4

The correct chronological order is:

1. Pan American Sanitary Bureau (PASB) → 1902
2. Health Organization of the League of Nations → 1923
3. United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration (UNRRA) → 1943
4. World Health Organization (WHO) → 1948

Therefore:

1902 → 1923 → 1943 → 1948

→ D. 2 → 1 → 3 → 4

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following staff: 1. Medical Officer 2. Pharmacist 3. Anaesthetist 4. Health Educator Of them, who are routinely posted to a PHC?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2 and 4

As per the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), a Primary Health Centre (PHC) serves as the first point of contact between the community and a medical officer. It is staffed with essential healthcare personnel to provide preventive, promotive, curative, and basic public health services.

• 1. Medical Officer ✅

• Routinely posted at every PHC to provide outpatient care, emergency services, maternal and child health services, and supervise public health activities.

• 2. Pharmacist ✅

• Responsible for dispensing medicines, maintaining drug inventory, and managing the pharmacy.

• 3. Anaesthetist ❌

• Not routinely posted at a PHC.
• Anaesthetists are usually available at Community Health Centres (CHCs) and higher-level hospitals where surgical services are provided.

• 4. Health Educator ✅

• Conducts health education, IEC/BCC activities, and community awareness programmes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following statements with regard to Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC): I. Early detection and special care of pre-term newborns is one of the major objectives of HBNC. II. ANM is the main person involved in the delivery of HBNC. III. Supporting the family for adoption of healthy practices helps achieve the key objectives of HBNC. IV. The primary aim of HBNC is to improve newborn survival. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. I, III and IV only

Home-Based Newborn Care (HBNC) is a Government of India initiative under the National Health Mission (NHM) that provides essential newborn care through scheduled home visits by ASHAs during the first 42 days of life. The programme aims to improve newborn survival through early identification of illness, timely referral, promotion of healthy newborn care practices, and family counselling.

• Primary aim: Improve newborn survival and reduce neonatal mortality.
• Main service provider: ASHA, not ANM.
• Key objectives:

• Early detection and management/referral of sick and preterm/LBW newborns
• Promote exclusive breastfeeding
• Ensure warmth (prevention of hypothermia)
• Cord and eye care
• Support families in adopting healthy newborn care practices

• HBNC home visits:

• Institutional delivery: 6 visits (Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42)
• Home delivery: 7 visits (Days 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following statements with regard to selection of Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) under NRHM: 1. ASHA must be a woman preferably in the age group of 18 to 25 years. 2. ASHA must have had formal education up to at least class ten. 3. ASHA must be a resident of the village. 4. ASHA may be a married, widowed or divorced woman. Which of the statements given above are correct with regard to process of selection of ASHA?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 3 and 4 only

The Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) is a community-based female health volunteer introduced under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) (now National Health Mission, NHM) to act as a link between the community and the public health system.

• 1. ASHA must be a woman preferably in the age group of 18 to 25 years. ✗

• The preferred age is 25–45 years, not 18–25 years.

• 2. ASHA must have had formal education up to at least class ten. ✗

• The minimum educational qualification is Class VIII (8th pass) (may be relaxed in tribal or difficult areas).

• 3. ASHA must be a resident of the village. ✓

• She should be a resident of the village to ensure community acceptance and accessibility.

• 4. ASHA may be a married\, widowed or divorced woman. ✓

• She is preferably married, widowed, or divorced, as these women are generally more acceptable and stable members of the community.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: DANIDA, the international aid agency of Denmark, is known for its assistance to which one of the India’s National Health programs?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. National Blindness Control Programme

DANIDA (Danish International Development Agency) is the international aid agency of Denmark and has provided significant financial and technical assistance to India’s National Programme for Control of Blindness (NPCB/NPCBVI), particularly for strengthening eye care services and cataract control.

Why not the other options?

• A. National AIDS Control Programme❌: Supported mainly by the World Bank, GFATM, UNAIDS, etc.
• C. National Tuberculosis Control Programme❌: Supported by WHO, World Bank, USAID, GFATM, etc.
• D. National Deafness Control Programme❌: Not associated with DANIDA.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Full form of JSSK is?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram

JSSK stands for Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram, a flagship maternal and child health initiative under the National Health Mission. The program ensures free and cashless services to pregnant women and sick newborns, including drugs, diagnostics, transport, and diet.

The main goals are to:

• Promote institutional deliveries
• Reduce maternal mortality
• Reduce neonatal mortality
• Remove out-of-pocket expenditure for pregnant women

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a health program, assessment of the fulfilment of objectives, achievement of targets, and short-term goals is carried out through which of the following methods?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Evaluation

Evaluation is the process of assessing whether a health program has achieved its stated objectives, targets, and short-term goals.

It focuses on measuring outcomes and impact after implementation, helping determine program effectiveness.

Monitoring vs Evaluation-

In contrast, monitoring is continuous and process-oriented, supervision ensures correct implementation, and planning precedes execution.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In an urban area in the state of Madhya Pradesh, a first-time pregnant woman visits a healthcare facility for her delivery following encouragement from an ASHA worker. What monetary advantages will they obtain under the Janani Suraksha Yojana?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1000 for mother and 400 for ASHA

Under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), cash incentives vary by state category (low-performing vs high-performing) and rural/urban area.

Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a safe motherhood intervention under the National Health Mission that promotes institutional deliveries through cash incentives.

The amount differs based on:

• High Performing States (HPS) vs Low Performing States (LPS)
• Urban vs rural areas

Madhya Pradesh is a low-performing state, and for an urban institutional delivery, the entitlement is ₹1000 to the mother and ₹400 to the ASHA.

The incentive aims to promote institutional deliveries and reduce maternal and neonatal mortality.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In RMNCHA+, all of the indicators in your area are in the Red zone. Which of the following statements is true? 1. Infant Mortality Rate in the area is <20% than the national average 2. Total Fertility Rate in the area is >20% than the national average 3. Children born with low birth weight are <20% than the national average 4. Care seeking for ARI is >20% than the national average
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2 only

RMNCHA+ (Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health) prioritizes districts using a color-coded system based on key health indicators. A Red zone indicates that the indicator is performing more than 20% worse than the national average, requiring urgent programmatic intervention.

• Red zone: Indicator is >20% worse than the national average.
• For adverse indicators (e.g., Total Fertility Rate, IMR, MMR, Low Birth Weight), higher values indicate poorer performance.
• For positive service coverage indicators (e.g., institutional delivery, immunization, care-seeking for ARI), lower values indicate poorer performance.
• Thus, a Total Fertility Rate >20% above the national average is classified as a Red zone indicator.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the context of the Family Health Education Model, which of the following is NOT considered an appropriate non-biological role of the family in health promotion?
options: Ensuring a clean and safe domestic environment conducive to health
Exercising strict surveillance and control over the sexual behaviour of adolescent family members
Providing physical and emotional care to members during episodes of illness
Transmitting health-related customs, practices, and beliefs across generations
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Exercising strict surveillance and control over the sexual behaviour of adolescent family members

Exercising strict surveillance and control over the sexual behaviour of adolescent family members- NOT part of accepted health education roles; modern public health emphasizes education, communication, and autonomy, not surveillance or control of sexual activity

Family is the basic unit of community health

⭐ Non-biological roles include:

• Environmental sanitation
• Emotional support
• Cultural transmission
• Care during illness

⭐ Health education programs often target families rather than individuals

⭐ Modern family health models emphasize guidance, support, and education rather than authoritarian control

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Mrs. M is a poor, migrant worker who has recently moved into a village along with her husband to work in the local brick kiln. The ASHA of that particular village visits her and comes to know that she has missed her last period. The last menstrual period (LMP) was on 6th January, while the ASHA visited her on 4th March of the same year. The lady has never delivered a child or had an abortion earlier. The ASHA talks to her and finds out that her age is 28 years, and measures that her height is 144 cm and weight is 52 kg. A blood test was performed and her haemoglobin was found to be 11.6 g/dL. From the data given in the case scenario, consider if the lady’s pregnancy would fall under a “high-risk” pregnancy on account of: 1. Her age 2. Her height and parity 3. Her haemoglobin level Mrs. M’s pregnancy qualifies as a “high-risk” pregnancy under which of the above parameters?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2

Consider the risk factors given in the case:

1. Age: Not a high-risk factor

• She is 28 years old.
• High-risk age groups are generally <18 years or ≥35 years.

2. Height and parity: High-risk → Correct

• Her height is 144 cm, which is below the commonly used high-risk cutoff of 145 cm.
• She is primigravida (G1P0). In this programme-based context, her short stature is the relevant high-risk criterion.

3. Hemoglobin: Not a high-risk factor in this case

• Hb = 11.6 g/dL, which is not anemia by the pregnancy cutoff of <11 g/dL.

Therefore, the pregnancy qualifies as high risk under parameter 2 → B.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Mrs. M is a poor, migrant worker who has recently moved into a village along with her husband to work in the local brick kiln. The ASHA of that particular village visits her and comes to know that she has missed her last period. The last menstrual period (LMP) was on 6th January, while the ASHA visited her on 4th March of the same year. The lady has never delivered a child or had an abortion earlier. The ASHA talks to her and finds out that her age is 28 years, and measures that her height is 144 cm and weight is 52 kg. A blood test was performed and her haemoglobin was found to be 11.6 g/dL. Which one among the following test kits available under the National Health Programme can the ASHA use for the confirmation of pregnancy in this case?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Nischay kit

The Nischay kit is a urine-based pregnancy test kit used under the National Health Programme for early detection/confirmation of pregnancy.

• Nischay kit → Pregnancy detection
• Nikshay → Tuberculosis-related programme
• Lakshya → Labour room/maternity quality-improvement initiative
• Abha → Digital health/health ID initiative

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Once the confirmation of the pregnancy is done, consider the following statements regarding the registration of pregnancy: 1. It is to be done as soon as possible, and within 12 weeks. 2. It is to be done as soon as possible, once 12 weeks are complete. 3. It is the primary responsibility of the ASHA. 4. It is the primary responsibility of the ANM. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1 and 4

1. Registration as soon as possible and within 12 weeks: Correct

• Pregnancy should be registered at the earliest, preferably during the first trimester and within 12 weeks.

2. Registration after 12 weeks: Incorrect

• Registration should not be delayed until 12 weeks are completed.

3. Primary responsibility of ASHA: Incorrect

• ASHA plays an important role in identifying, motivating and facilitating pregnant women to access services, but she is not primarily responsible for formal pregnancy registration.

4. Primary responsibility of ANM: Correct

• The ANM is primarily responsible for registration of pregnancy and provision/coordination of antenatal care services.

Therefore, statements 1 and 4 are correct → C.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The following table shows three broad components under which the objectives of the National Health Policy, 2017 can be grouped, along with an example of goal/objective under that component. How many of the pairs given below are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. All of the three pairs

The National Health Policy (NHP), 2017 groups its measurable targets into three broad components:

1. Health Status and Programme Impact → Increase life expectancy at birth from 67.5 to 70 years by 2025 ✓

• This is a health outcome indicator reflecting improvement in the overall health status of the population.

2. Health Systems Performance → More than 90% of newborns fully immunized by one year of age by 2025 ✓

• Immunization coverage is a health system performance indicator, reflecting the effectiveness of service delivery.

3. Health Systems Strengthening → Increase State sector health spending to more than 8% of their budget by 2020 ✓

• Increasing government health expenditure strengthens infrastructure, workforce, and service delivery, making it a health systems strengthening target.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The given image is the logo for which of the following health programs?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. National Leprosy Eradication Program

The logo shown corresponds to the National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP), which focuses on early detection, complete treatment with MDT, disability prevention, and stigma reduction.

The program aims to interrupt transmission and achieve elimination of leprosy as a public health problem.

Other programs like IDSP, NTEP, and NHM have distinct logos and broader or disease-specific mandates, making NLEP the correct identification here.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has launched a programme to meet the challenge of high prevalence of anaemia amongst adolescent boys and girls. Consider the following statements in relation to the key interventions being undertaken: I. It entails supervised weekly administration of 100 mg elemental iron and 500 μg folic acid. II. These weekly iron-folic acid supplements are administered by using a fixed day approach. III. It entails supervised administration of Albendazole 400 mg every three months for control of helminth infestation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. I and II

The Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) Programme was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to reduce the high prevalence of iron deficiency anemia among adolescents (10–19 years).  The following statements are correct:

• I. It entails supervised weekly administration of 100 mg elemental iron and 500 μg folic acid: Adolescents receive one tablet containing 100 mg elemental iron and 500 μg folic acid once weekly under supervision.
• II. These weekly iron-folic acid supplements are administered by using a fixed day approach: The programme follows a fixed day every week (e.g., every Monday) to improve compliance and supervision.

Why is III incorrect?

• III. It entails supervised administration of Albendazole 400 mg every three months for control of helminth infestation: Under the WIFS programme, Albendazole 400 mg is administered every 6 months (biannually), not every 3 months.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The term “health worker” was first used by which committee?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Kartar Singh Committee

The Kartar Singh Committee (1973) introduced the concept and designation of the Multipurpose Health Worker (Health Worker) in India. It recommended integrating multiple vertical health programs at the peripheral level by creating:

• Male Health Worker (MPW-Male)
• Female Health Worker (MPW-Female)

It also recommended one Health Assistant (Male) and one Health Assistant (Female) to supervise health workers.

Why not the other options?

• A. Bhore Committee (1946): Proposed the comprehensive health service model and establishment of Primary Health Centres (PHCs), but did not introduce the term “health worker.”
• C. Mudaliar Committee (1962): Focused on strengthening existing PHCs and improving quality of health services.
• D. Jungalwalla Committee (1967): Recommended integration of health services, unified cadre, equal pay for equal work, and prohibition of private practice by government doctors.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The voluntary scheme under which any obstetrics and gynaecology specialist, lady doctor/MBBS doctor can volunteer themselves for providing safe motherhood service is called:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Vande Mataram Scheme

The Vande Mataram Scheme is a voluntary public-private partnership initiative under which private obstetricians & gynecologists, lady doctors, and MBBS doctors voluntarily provide safe motherhood services to pregnant women, especially on the 9th of every month, free of cost or at subsidized rates.

Why not the other options?

• A. Ayushman Bharat Scheme❌: Health insurance and Health & Wellness Centres.
• B. Mamta Scheme❌: State-specific maternal/child health incentive scheme (not a national voluntary PPP for doctors).
• C. Janani Suraksha Scheme (JSY)❌: Cash incentive scheme to promote institutional deliveries.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under the Ayushman Bharat Program, identify the new designated name of the Sub-centre, as shown in the image below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Ayushman Aarogya Mandir

Under the Ayushman Bharat Programme, the former Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs) at Sub-centres and Primary Health Centres (PHCs) have been redesignated as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) to provide comprehensive primary health care (CPHC), including preventive, promotive, curative, rehabilitative, and palliative services.

Why not the other options?

• A. Health and Wellness Centre: This was the previous designation; it has now been renamed Ayushman Arogya Mandir.
• C. Subcentre Type-B: Refers to a classification of subcentres, not the new designated name under Ayushman Bharat.
• D. Subcentre Type-A: Also a classification based on workload/population, not the new nomenclature.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under the Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948, if the sickness of an insured person is duly certified by an Insurance Medical Officer, periodical cash payment benefit is payable for a maximum period of how many days in any continuous period of 365 days, as Sickness Benefit?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 91 days

The Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Act, 1948 provides Sickness Benefit as a cash compensation to insured persons who are temporarily unable to work due to certified illness. The benefit is payable at approximately 70% of wages for a maximum of 91 days in two consecutive benefit periods (365 days), provided the insured person fulfills the required contribution conditions.

High-Yield Pearls

• Sickness Benefit: Cash benefit at \~70% of wages. ⭐
• Maximum duration: 91 days in a continuous period of 365 days. ⭐
• Requires certification by an Insurance Medical Officer.
• Available only if the insured person has made the prescribed contributions during the relevant contribution period.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under the National Health Mission (NHM), the RMNCH+A strategy has been formulated to provide quality health care to various vulnerable age groups. Which of the following is a component of the RMNCH+A strategy? 1. Adolescent health 2. Family planning 3. Geriatric health 4. Maternal health 5. Infant Health
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2, 4, 5

RMNCH+A stands for Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health, covering the life-cycle approach from adolescence through childhood, including family planning. The “+” represents linkages with other health services like family planning, nutrition, gender issues & universal immunization. The strategy was introduced to provide continuum of care from adolescence → pregnancy → childbirth → childhood.

Geriatric health is not part of RMNCH+A; hence the included components are adolescent health, family planning, maternal health, and infant/child health.

Major Programs Under RMNCH+A-

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan, the beneficiaries are being provided with a minimum package of antenatal care including certain investigations and drugs on a fixed day of every month. Which day of the month is specified for this purpose?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 9th day of the month

The Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) was launched by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare in 2016 to ensure that every pregnant woman receives at least one comprehensive antenatal check-up by a physician or specialist during the second or third trimester. The programme is conducted on a fixed day—the 9th of every month—at designated government health facilities.

• PMSMA is observed on the 9th of every month.
• Target beneficiaries: All pregnant women in the 2nd and 3rd trimester (after the first trimester).
• Provides a minimum package of antenatal care, including:

• Clinical examination
• Blood pressure measurement
• Weight monitoring
• Fetal assessment
• Laboratory investigations (Hb, urine sugar/protein, blood grouping, etc.)
• Iron-folic acid and calcium supplementation
• Tetanus/Td immunization
• Counselling on nutrition, birth preparedness, breastfeeding, and danger signs.

• High-risk pregnancies are identified, line-listed, and referred for appropriate management. ⭐
• High-risk pregnancies are marked with a red sticker on the Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card for easy identification.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under WIFS (Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplementation) program, what is the weekly dose of Iron Folic Acid that is given to Adolescents 10-19 years of age?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Iron – 100 mg, Folic acid – 500 mcg

Under the Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) programme, adolescents aged 10–19 years receive Iron 100 mg + Folic acid 500 µg once

weekly.

Standard Weekly Dose in WIFS

Target Groups under WIFS

Additional Components of WIFS

• Deworming is done using Albendazole.
• This higher weekly dose is designed to prevent and control iron deficiency anemia during the rapid growth phase of adolescence.
• The programme is implemented through schools and Anganwadi centres, along with biannual deworming to improve iron absorption.
• According to Anemia Mukt Bharat (which is followed now instead of WIFS), adolescents get 60mg elemental iron + 500 ug folate; since the question specifically asks WIFS, we go with those values.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the name of the online portal used for delivering mental healthcare services via telephone and other digital platforms for mental disorders such as schizophrenia, under the National Mental Health Programme?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Tele-manas

Tele-MANAS is the national digital mental health platform launched under the National Mental Health Programme to provide telephonic and online mental health services.

It offers 24×7 toll-free counseling, referral, and follow-up care for conditions including schizophrenia, depression, anxiety, and substance use disorders.

| Feature | Details

| ------- | -------

| Services | Telephonic counselling and psychiatric support

| Coverage | Available across India

| Target conditions | Depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, substance abuse

| Access | Toll-free helpline

Other portals like NIKSHAY (TB), U-WIN (immunization), and Quinitin are unrelated to mental health services.

| Option | Program

| ------ | -------

| A. NIKSHAY | Portal for tuberculosis patient management

| B. Tele-MANAS | ✔ Tele mental health services

| C. Quinitin | Not a recognized national health portal

| D. U-WIN | Digital platform for immunization tracking

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which committee first recommended the concept of comprehensive health services?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Bhore Committee

The Bhore Committee (Health Survey and Development Committee, 1946) was the first committee in India to recommend the concept of comprehensive health services. It emphasized that preventive, promotive, curative, and rehabilitative services should be integrated and made available to all individuals irrespective of their ability to pay.

The Bhore Committee recommended:

• Comprehensive health care ⭐
• Integration of preventive and curative services
• Establishment of Primary Health Centres (PHCs)
• Health care accessible to every citizen

Why not the other options?

• B. Kartar Singh Committee (1973): Introduced the Multipurpose Health Worker (MPW) scheme.
• C. Mudaliar Committee (1962): Recommended strengthening existing PHCs and referral services.
• D. Shrivastav Committee (1975): Recommended Village Health Guides and community participation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which disease the girl is related to and what's her name?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Sapna, Leprosy

Sapna is the national IEC mascot for leprosy under India’s leprosy control programme.

She is used in public awareness campaigns to promote early detection, treatment compliance, and stigma reduction related to leprosy.

Sapna is used in:

• Posters
• School awareness materials
• Community education campaigns

Her messages focus on:

Other diseases like TB, malaria, and HIV have different mascots or IEC symbols, making Sapna–Leprosy the correct association.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which infection is most commonly transmitted during the third trimester of pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Toxoplasmosis

Toxoplasmosis shows an increasing rate of transplacental transmission with advancing gestational age, being most commonly transmitted in the third trimester.

However, infections acquired earlier in pregnancy cause more severe fetal disease, while third-trimester infections are more frequent but often milder.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following are correct regarding activities under the Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) programme? 1. Administration of supervised weekly iron-folic acid supplements of 100 mg elemental iron and 500 μg folic acid. 2. Administration of supervised weekly iron-folic acid supplements of 60 mg elemental iron and 0.5 mg folic acid. 3. Biannual deworming with albendazole. 4. Annual deworming with albendazole. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1 and 3

The Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) Programme is a Government of India initiative aimed at reducing the burden of iron deficiency anemia among adolescents (10–19 years) through weekly iron-folic acid supplementation and biannual deworming.

Why is B correct?

• 1. Administration of supervised weekly iron-folic acid supplements of 100 mg elemental iron and 500 μg folic acid. ✅

• WIFS recommends one tablet containing 100 mg elemental iron and 500 μg (0.5 mg) folic acid once weekly.

• 2. Administration of supervised weekly iron-folic acid supplements of 60 mg elemental iron and 0.5 mg folic acid. ❌

• 60 mg elemental iron is recommended for pregnant women under ANC programs, not under WIFS.

• 3. Biannual deworming with albendazole. ✅

• Albendazole 400 mg is administered twice yearly (every 6 months) to reduce helminthic infestation and improve iron absorption.

• 4. Annual deworming with albendazole. ❌

• WIFS recommends biannual, not annual, deworming.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following are included as a “Deficiency” under the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK)? I. Hypothyroidism II. Vitamin A deficiency III. Anemia IV. Vitamin D deficiency Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. II, III and IV

The Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) is a national child health screening and early intervention program launched under the National Health Mission (NHM). It aims for early identification and management of the “4 Ds” in children from birth to 18 years of age:

• Defects at birth
• Deficiencies
• Diseases
• Developmental delays including disabilities ⭐

Under the “Deficiencies” category, common nutritional deficiencies screened include Vitamin A deficiency, Vitamin D deficiency, Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), and anemia.

Why is D correct?

• I. Hypothyroidism ✘

• Congenital hypothyroidism is classified under Defects at Birth, not Deficiencies.

• II. Vitamin A deficiency ✔

• Included under the Deficiencies component of RBSK.

• III. Anemia ✔

• Nutritional anemia is one of the major deficiencies screened under RBSK.

• IV. Vitamin D deficiency ✔

• Included among nutritional deficiencies screened under the program.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following does not indicate a syndromic approach treating sexually transmitted infection in males?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Lower abdominal pain

The syndromic approach for STI management in males is based on presenting symptom complexes such as urethral discharge, genital ulcer disease, and inguinal swelling (bubo).

Lower abdominal pain is a syndrome used for females, not males. It usually indicates Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID).

Lower abdominal pain is a key syndrome in female STIs, often indicating pelvic inflammatory disease, and is not part of male STI syndromic management.

Syndromic management prioritizes immediate treatment without laboratory confirmation to prevent complications and transmission.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a component of School Health under Ayushman Bharat Program?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Monthly IFA supplementations

Under the School Health Programme of Ayushman Bharat, services include periodic health check-ups, biannual deworming with albendazole, and menstrual hygiene support, including sanitary napkin distribution.

Iron–folic acid supplementation under this program follows the Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) strategy, not monthly dosing.

Therefore, monthly IFA supplementation is not a component of School Health under Ayushman Bharat.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a part of a Primary Health Centre?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Physiotherapist

A Primary Health Centre (PHC) is the first point of contact between the community and a medical officer in the public health system. As per the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), the core PHC staff include a Medical Officer, Pharmacist, and Laboratory Technician. A Physiotherapist is not a routine member of the PHC team.

A Physiotherapist is generally posted at higher-level health facilities such as Community Health Centres (CHCs), Sub-District Hospitals, or District Hospitals, not at a standard PHC.

Why not the other options?

• A. Pharmacist: Essential PHC staff responsible for dispensing medicines.
• B. Laboratory Technician: Performs basic laboratory investigations at the PHC.
• C. Medical Officer: In-charge of the PHC and provides clinical and public health services.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the challenge faced in the operationalization of the concept of Universal Health Coverage (UHC)?
options: Universal Health Coverage aims to provide free health care services to all, regardless of the available resources in the country
Universal Health Coverage aims to provide services despite having unregulated and fragmented healthcare delivery systems
Universal Health Coverage prioritizes the safety of resources in a low-resource setting
Universal Health Coverage targets primary health care delivery based on the needs of the population
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Universal Health Coverage aims to provide services despite having unregulated and fragmented healthcare delivery systems

Universal Health Coverage (UHC) means all individuals and communities receive the health services they need without suffering financial hardship.

UHC includes access to health promotion, disease prevention, treatment, rehabilitation, palliative care.

A major challenge in implementing Universal Health Coverage (UHC) is delivering equitable and continuous care within unregulated and fragmented healthcare systems, where services are split between public and private sectors.

Such fragmentation leads to inefficiencies, variable quality, and gaps in continuity of care, making universal access difficult.

In contrast, UHC is based on resource prioritization and need-based primary health care, not on unlimited or unsafe use of resources.

UHC in India

India’s move toward UHC includes initiatives such as:

• Ayushman Bharat
• Health and Wellness Centres
• Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY)

These programs aim to improve access, affordability, and quality of care.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the primary objective for usage of health index by NITI Aayog?
options: Raise funding to the private hospitals
Rank the state according to health status
Assess the efficiency of the government hospital
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Rank the state according to health status

The Health Index developed by NITI Aayog, in collaboration with MoHFW and World Bank, is primarily used to rank States and Union Territories based on their health performance.

It assesses indicators related to health outcomes, governance, and key inputs/processes, enabling inter-state comparison and competitive federalism.

The index is not meant for hospital-level efficiency assessment or district identification, but for tracking and incentivizing overall state-level health improvements.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following strategies were encouraged by the UNICEF under its ‘GOBI Campaign’? I. G for growth charts to better monitor child development II. O for oral rehydration to treat all mild and moderate dehydration III. B for better and continuous evaluation of children up to 5 years of age IV. I for immunization against measles, diphtheria, polio, pertussis, tetanus and tuberculosis Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. I, II and IV

The GOBI Campaign was introduced by UNICEF in 1983 under the leadership of James P. Grant to reduce child mortality through four simple, cost-effective interventions.

GOBI stands for:

• G – Growth Monitoring (using growth charts)
• O – Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) for diarrheal dehydration
• B – Breastfeeding (not “better and continuous evaluation”)
• I – Immunization against the six vaccine-preventable diseases (TB, DPT, Polio, Measles)

Therefore:

• Statement I. G for growth charts to better monitor child development: Correct
• Statement II. O for oral rehydration to treat all mild and moderate dehydration: Correct
• Statement III. B for better and continuous evaluation of children up to 5 years of age: Incorrect (B stands for Breastfeeding)
• Statement IV. I for immunization against measles, diphtheria, polio, pertussis, tetanus and tuberculosis: Correct

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following illnesses is not covered under the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Childhood cancer

RBSK — 4 Ds

• The Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) provides screening and early intervention for children from birth to 18 years for the 4 Ds:

| 4 Ds | Important conditions screened

| ---- | -----------------------------

| 1. Defects at birth | Neural tube defects, Down syndrome, cleft lip/palate, congenital heart disease, congenital cataract, congenital deafness, clubfoot, developmental dysplasia of hip

| 2. Deficiencies | Anemia, vitamin A deficiency, vitamin D deficiency/rickets, severe acute malnutrition, goitre

| 3. Diseases | Skin conditions, dental caries, rheumatic heart disease, tuberculosis, reactive airway disease, convulsive disorders, otitis media

| 4. Developmental delays & disabilities | Vision and hearing impairment, motor delay, cognitive delay, language delay, autism spectrum disorder, learning disorders, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder

High-yield point

• Childhood cancer is NOT included in the standard RBSK 4-D screening list.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following most appropriately describes the “tracking” phenomenon of blood pressure?
options: Continuous monitoring of blood pressure on any individual to keep a track of blood pressure for early diagnosis of hypertension
Persistence of rank order of blood pressure in individuals as they grow older
Keeping a track of the prevalence of hypertension in a community
Tracking of twins for change in blood pressure to see the effect of genetic makeup
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Persistence of rank order of blood pressure in individuals as they grow older

• "Tracking" in epidemiology refers to the phenomenon whereby an individual's relative position (rank/percentile) within a population distribution of a measurement tends to persist over time as the population as a whole ages. In the context of blood pressure, this means that a child or adolescent whose BP is in the higher percentile of their peer group tends to remain in a similarly high percentile as they grow into adulthood — even as the absolute BP values of everyone in the cohort rise with age.
• Significance:

• Tracking underlies the rationale for early identification of children/adolescents with high-normal or elevated BP, since those with higher BP early in life are more likely to become hypertensive adults.
• It's a key concept in longitudinal/cohort studies of chronic disease risk factors (also applies to BMI, cholesterol, and other continuous variables).

Why not the other options?

• A. Continuous monitoring of blood pressure on any individual to keep a track of blood pressure for early diagnosis of hypertension: Describes serial/continuous BP monitoring for diagnosis — not "tracking" in the epidemiological sense; this is simply longitudinal measurement.
• C. Keeping a track of the prevalence of hypertension in a community: Describes surveillance of hypertension prevalence at a population level — a public health monitoring activity, not "tracking" of individual rank.
• D. Tracking of twins for change in blood pressure to see the effect of genetic makeup: Describes a twin study design used to estimate heritability — a different research methodology, not the tracking phenomenon.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which scheme provides pension to people aged 65 years and above who are below the poverty line?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Indira Gandhi National Pension Scheme

The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) is a component of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) and provides a monthly pension to elderly persons belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households.

Under the scheme:

• Beneficiaries must belong to BPL households.
• Pension is provided to elderly individuals (currently 60 years and above under the revised scheme; earlier exam questions often mention 65 years based on the older eligibility criteria).
• The Central Government provides financial assistance, with many states adding their own contribution.

Why not the other options?

• A. Rajiv Gandhi National Pension Scheme: No such old-age pension scheme exists.
• C. Atal Pension Yojana (APY): A contributory pension scheme for workers, not specifically for BPL elderly.
• D. Pradhan Mantri Pension Scheme: Not the name of the BPL old-age pension scheme.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which statement most accurately refers to the requirements for initiating an urban community health center?
options: Caters to a population of 1-1.5 lakh
Referral centre for 2- 3 primary health centers
No sub-district and district hospitals present in the area
Should have a 100-bed facility in metro cities
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Should have a 100-bed facility in metro cities

An Urban Community Health Centre (UCHC) under IPHS is designed to function as a secondary-level healthcare facility in urban areas.

In metro cities, UCHCs are recommended to have a 100-bed capacity to cater to higher patient load and referral needs.

Population norms and referral linkages differ from rural CHCs, and the presence of district hospitals does not preclude establishment of UCHCs.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: World Health Organisation (WHO) considers blindness as a major public health problem. As per WHO, what is the definition of blindness?
options: Visual acuity <6/60 after correction in better eye
Visual acuity <3/60 after correction in better eye
Visual acuity <6/60 without correction in better eye
Visual acuity <3/60 without correction in better eye
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Visual acuity <3/60 after correction in better eye

As per WHO definition, blindness is defined as best corrected visual acuity less than 3/60 in the better eye, or a corresponding visual field loss.

WHO Classification

• Normal vision: ≥ 6/18
• Visual impairment: < 6/18 to ≥ 3/60
• Severe visual impairment: < 6/60 to ≥ 3/60
• Blindness: < 3/60

(All based on best-corrected visual acuity in the better eye)

India runs the National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI) to reduce avoidable blindness.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A homogenous sample of 4 groups was taken as shown below. The height and weight of each group had a correlation coefficient of 0.6. What will be the total coefficient of correlation of the whole group?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Equal to 0.6

In a homogenous sample or population, the total coefficient of correlation (r) will be the average of the individual correlation coefficients. Therefore in the given condition, it will be the same as 0.6

The given scattergram shows the correlation coefficient of height and weight of 4 homogenous samples. Averaging methods are appropriate when several different samples are independently drawn from the same or a homogenous population and the interest is in aggregating those values.

Therefore the total correlation coefficient of the whole group will be:

r = (sum of correlation coeffiecient of each sample) ÷ (total no. of samples)

= (0.6 + 0.6  + 0.6 + 0.6) ÷ 4 = 2.4 ÷ 4

= 0.6

Note: A correlation between 2 variables does not demonstrate any causal relationship between those variables, no matter how strong it is. Correlation is merely a measure of a statistical association between the variables. Therefore inferring a causal relationship between two variables on the basis of a correlation is a common and fundamental error.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A nurse keeps the bins as shown in the image in the hospital ward. Which of the following items would go into the black bin?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Glove paper cover

Glove paper cover is a general solid waste that is to be collected in the black bin.

All non-infectious general wastes like food waste, paper waste, and mineral water bottles should be discarded in black bins.

Soiled linen bedsheets contaminated by blood or body fluids should be disposed in the yellow bin. All plastic recyclable wastes are discarded in red bins (gloves and contaminated gloves).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to WHO, which of the following are components of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
options: Life expectancy at birth, literacy and standard of living
Life expectancy at 1 year, literacy and standard of living
Infant mortality rate, literacy and standard of living
Life expectancy at 1 year, literacy and infant mortality rate
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Life expectancy at birth, literacy and standard of living

The components of the Human Development Index (HDI) include life expectancy at birth, literacy, and standard of living.

Human Development Index (HDI) is a measure of a country's average achievements in three dimensions of human development:

• A long and healthy life, as measured by life expectancy at birth
• Knowledge (literacy), as measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling, and
• A decent standard of living, as measured by GNI (gross national income) per capita.

HDI values range from 0 to 1, with 1 as the maximum value.

Note- Life expectancy at 1 year, literacy and infant mortality rate are components of the Physical quality of life index (PQLI).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Administration of which of the following vaccines is associated with the risk of intussussception?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Rotavirus vaccine

Rotavirus vaccine is associated with a potential risk of intussusception, especially when the first dose of these vaccines is given to infants aged >12 weeks. Because of this risk, the rotavirus vaccine is not a part of catch-up immunization programs, as the age of the child is difficult to ascertain in such programs.

Rotavirus vaccines are oral, live attenuated vaccines and are of 3 types:

1. Rotarix (human monovalent) vaccine is administered in 2 oral doses:

• First dose: At 6 weeks, no later than 12 weeks (due to the risk of intussusception).
• Second dose: With a gap of 4 weeks from the first dose, to be given by 16 weeks and no later than 24 weeks.

2. RotaTeq (pentavalent bovine-human reassortant) vaccine is administered in 3 oral doses at 2, 4, and 6 months. The first dose is given between 6-12 weeks and subsequent doses within a 4-10 weeks gap. All the 3 doses should be given before 32 weeks.
3. Rotavac (monovalent liquid frozen) vaccine is administered in 3 oral doses, 4 weeks apart at 6,10 and 14 weeks. It should not be administered to children more than 8 months of age.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All the following tests are related to pasteurization of milk except
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Iodine test

All the above tests are related to the pasteurization of milk except the iodine test. It is done to test if milk is adulterated with starch or cereal flour.

The iodine test is done by adding 2 drops of iodine solution containing potassium iodide and iodine to 1ml of milk. The appearance of a blue color indicates that the milk is adulterated with starch. A control sample of milk that is not adulterated with starch will develop a slightly yellowish color.

Pasteurization can be done by the following methods,

• Holder/Vat method: 63-66 °C for 30 minutes and then quickly cooled to 5°C.
• HTST method (High-temperature short time): 72°C for at least 15 seconds, and then cooled rapidly to 4°C.
• UHT method (Ultra-high temp): Rapidly heated to 125 °C for a few seconds, then cooled and bottled as quickly as possible.

Tests in pasteurization:

• Phosphatase test: It is based on the fact that raw milk contains phosphatase enzyme which gets destroyed at temperatures corresponding to the standard time and temperature required for pasteurization.
• Standard plate count: It is used to determine the bacteriological quality of pasteurized milk.
• Coliform count: The presence of coliform organisms in pasteurized milk indicates either improper pasteurization or post-pasteurization contamination.
• Methylene blue reduction test is an indirect method for the detection of microorganisms in milk. This test is carried out on the milk accepted for pasteurization. Definite quantities of methylene blue are added to 10 ml of milk at a uniform temperature of 37°C. The milk is considered satisfactory if it fails to reduce the methylene blue dye in 30 minutes under standard conditions.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Arrange the following causes of neonatal mortality from maximum to the least (according to the verbal autopsy report 2010-2013 data).

1. Prematurity and low birth weight
2. Birth injuries and birth asphyxia
3. Congenital anomalies
4. Sepsis
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1>2>4>3

According to verbal autopsy report 2010-2013 data, the correct sequence of causes of neonatal mortality from maximum to least is prematurity and low birth weight> birth injuries and birth asphyxia> sepsis> congenital anomalies. (1>2>4>3)

Neonatal deaths are deaths that occur during the neonatal period, that is between birth and 28 completed days after birth. It is calculated by using the following formula:

Neonatal mortality rate = Number of deaths of children under 28 days of age in a year x 1000/Total live births in the same year

Important causes of neonatal mortality include ( from maximum to least)

• Prematurity & low birth weight
• Birth asphyxia & birth trauma
• Neonatal pneumonia
• Other non-communicable diseases
• Sepsis
• Congenital anomalies
• Diarrhoeal diseases
• Injuries
• Tetanus

Note: Recent 2020 SRS (Sample Registration System) report shows the following:

• Neonatal mortality rate to be 20.
• Infant mortality rate to be 28.
• Under 5 mortality rate to be 32.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
As per the verbal autopsy report 2010-2013, arrange the most common cause of death among 1-4-year-old children in descending order:

1. Diarrhea
2. Pneumonia
3. Malaria
4. Injuries
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2 > 1 > 4 > 3

According to the verbal autopsy report of 2010-2013, the most common cause of death among 1-4 year old children in descending order is Pneumonia > Diarrhea > Injuries > Malaria.

According to the Verbal autopsy report 2010-2013, the top 5 causes of death among children aged 1-4 years are:

1. Pneumonia
2. Diarrheal diseases
3. Injuries
4. Other non-communicable diseases
5. Malaria

1-4 year mortality rate also known as the child death rate is the number of deaths of children aged 1-4 years per 1000 children in the same age group in a given year. It thus excludes infant mortality. It is given by the formula,

1-4 year mortality rate (child death rate) = (no. of deaths of children aged 1-4 years during a year x 1000) / Total no. of children aged 1-4 years at the middle of the year.

It is a more refined indicator of the social situation than the infant mortality rate as it reflects adverse environmental health hazards like malnutrition, poor hygiene, infections, and accidents. It is not affected by perinatal hazards. In the 1-4 year group, second year is the period with the highest risk of death (mainly due to childhood infections like measles, whooping cough, diphtheria, diarrhea, and ARI), after which the rates decline progressively.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Certain new vaccines are being studied in the market and their efficacies are compared and presented in the image as shown below. Which of the newer vaccines can be used with the same efficacy as compared to the previous vaccine?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. C, D and E

Vaccines C, D, and E can be used with the same efficacy as compared to the previous vaccine, as their confidence interval lies within the zone of equivalence.

In a classical randomized controlled trial (RCT), the aim is to evaluate a difference between two drugs by proving the superiority of the new drug over the standard drug. However, an equivalence study is carried out with the aim of showing there are no significant differences in the efficacy between the new drug and the standard drug.

To define 'no significant differences' the limit of equivalence (δ) must be defined first. δ must be set as superiority margin (+δ) and non-inferiority margin (-δ), so that they are clinically appropriate and the differences can be tolerated as clinically irrelevant. To conclude equivalence the confidence interval (CI), i.e., the whisker (tail) of the box-whisker plot must lie within the zone of equivalence.

Therefore in the given question, vaccines C, D, and E have CI in the zone of equivalence and thus have the same efficacy as the previous vaccine. Vaccines F and G lie outside the zone of equivalence but well within +δ, making them superior to the previous vaccine. Vaccines A and B lie outside the zone of equivalence but well within -δ, making them non-equivalent and at the same time non-inferior to the previous vaccine. If the CI of any vaccine includes or crosses the -δ limit, they will be considered inferior to the standard vaccine.

Note: A superiority trial is done to show that the new drug is superior to the standard drug. A non-inferiority trial is done to show that the new drug is not worse than the standard drug. This is done for newer interventions or drugs that may be less costly, less invasive, and have fewer side effects.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Compared to a pregnant female, a lactating female would require a higher level of nutrient supplementation for which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Calcium

According to the Recommended daily allowance (RDA) guidelines set by the National Institute of Nutrition (NIN), the requirement of calcium intake is increased in a lactating woman (1200mg/d) when compared to that of a pregnant woman (1000mg/d). Calcium intake of 1200mg/d is advised in postmenopausal women as well.

The RDA of vitamin A is increased by 50mcg in lactation as compared to pregnancy. But the increased vitamin A demand is met from the diet and it is not given as a supplement nutrient. Vitamin A supplements are given only when there is vitamin A deficiency.

The RDA of iron and folic acid is decreased during lactation compared to pregnancy.
