• Autonomy: The patient is conscious and capable of expressing her wishes. Her preferences must take priority over family demands.
• Beneficence & Non-maleficence: Avoid futile, burdensome interventions that offer no survival benefit.
• Shared decision-making: Requires a family meeting to discuss prognosis, goals of care, and patient values (comfort vs life-prolongation).

The correct step is to convene a family meeting, clarify the patient’s goals, address anxiety, and then decide on palliative or hospice care with informed consent.

A. Discharge patient saying nothing more can be done- This is abandonment of care and unethical.

B. Listen to daughter and be aggressive- Aggressive treatment that provides no benefit is medically futile. Patient autonomy must be respected.

D. Give placebo to reduce anxiety- Giving placebo without disclosure is unethical and deceptive.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Arrange the following international health organizations in the correct sequence shown in the video.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. WHO – UNICEF – NLEP – ICDS

The video shows the logos in the following order:

1. WHO (World Health Organization): United Nations' specialized agency for international public health.
2. UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund): Focuses on child health, nutrition, immunization, education, and welfare.
3. NLEP (National Leprosy Eradication Programme): Government of India programme aimed at eliminating leprosy.
4. ICDS (Integrated Child Development Services): India's flagship programme providing supplementary nutrition, immunization, preschool education, and health services to children under 6 years and pregnant/lactating women.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As per the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the target “3.4” refers to which one of the following?
options: By 2030, reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 per 100,000 live births
By 2020, halve the number of global deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents
By 2030, reduce by 1/3rd premature mortality from non-communicable diseases through prevention and treatment, and promote mental health and well-being
Strengthen the prevention and treatment of substance abuse, including narcotic drug abuse and harmful use of alcohol
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. By 2030, reduce by 1/3rd premature mortality from non-communicable diseases through prevention and treatment, and promote mental health and well-being

SDG 3.4 aim:

• By 2030, reduce by one-third premature mortality from non-communicable diseases through prevention and treatment and promote mental health and well-being.

Why not the others?

• A. By 2030, reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 per 100,000 live births: SDG 3.1 — Reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to <70 per 100,000 live births by 2030.
• B. By 2020, halve the number of global deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents: SDG 3.6 — Reduce global deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents.
• C. By 2030, reduce by 1/3rd premature mortality from non-communicable diseases through prevention and treatment, and promote mental health and well-being: SDG 3.4 — Correct. Focuses on NCDs + mental health.
• D. Strengthen the prevention and treatment of substance abuse, including narcotic drug abuse and harmful use of alcohol: SDG 3.5 — Strengthen prevention and treatment of substance abuse, including narcotic drug abuse and harmful alcohol use.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As per the basic model of a nuclear family life cycle, consider the following phases: 1. Contraction 2. Dissolution 3. Extension 4. Formation Which one of the following best represents the correct sequence of phases in a normal nuclear family?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 4 → 3 → 1 → 2

The family life cycle describes the predictable stages through which a nuclear family progresses from its formation to its eventual dissolution. Understanding these stages helps in planning appropriate maternal, child, and geriatric health services.

The normal sequence of phases in a nuclear family is: Formation → Extension → Contraction → Dissolution

• Formation: Begins with marriage and establishment of a new family.
• Extension: Family expands with the birth and upbringing of children.
• Contraction: Children become independent, leave home, marry, and start their own families (“empty nest” phase).
• Dissolution: Ends with the death of one or both spouses, marking the end of the family unit.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As per the POCSO Act, who is defined as being entitled to protection under the law?
options: Girl child less than 16 years age
Girl child less than 18 years age
Any child less than 16 years age
Any child less than 18 years age
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Any child less than 18 years age

Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, a child is defined as any person below 18 years of age, irrespective of gender.

The Act provides gender-neutral protection against sexual offences and mandates child-friendly procedures during reporting, investigation, and trial.

This uniform age definition ensures comprehensive legal protection for all minors.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following management methods/techniques: 1. System analysis 2. Organizational design 3. Personnel management 4. Information systems Which of the above methods/techniques are based on behavioural sciences?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2, 3 and 4

The behavioural science approach to management applies principles of psychology, sociology, anthropology, and organizational behavior to improve the effectiveness of individuals and organizations. It emphasizes human behavior, motivation, leadership, communication, and teamwork in achieving organizational goals.

• 1. System analysis ✗

• System analysis is based on the systems approach, focusing on organizational processes, workflows, and interrelationships rather than human behavior.

• 2. Organizational design ✓

• Organizational design involves structuring roles, authority, communication, and teamwork, all of which are based on behavioral science principles.

• 3. Personnel management ✓

• Personnel management deals with recruitment, motivation, performance appraisal, leadership, and employee welfare, making it a core application of behavioral sciences.

• 4. Information systems ✓

• Modern Management Information Systems (MIS) incorporate behavioral aspects such as communication, decision-making, user interaction, and organizational behavior, and are therefore considered part of the behavioral science approach in management.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following statements: • Statement 1- Contemplation – A person who smokes is thinking of quitting smoking • Statement 2- Precontemplation – A person is considering starting morning walks and the benefits to their health • Statement 3- Maintenance phase – A person quit smoking one year back and has not smoked since then • Statement 4- Action phase – A person with obesity says they can’t do anything, as it runs deep in their family
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Statement 1 and 3 are correct

The Stages of Change (Transtheoretical Model):

A behavioral change framework (Prochaska & DiClemente) describing readiness to change across sequential stages.

Stages of Change

• Precontemplation

• No intention to change
• Unaware / denial / resistance
• Example: “Smoking isn’t a problem for me.”

• Contemplation

• Aware of problem, thinking about change
• Ambivalence present
• Example: “I should quit, but it’s hard.”

• Preparation

• Intends to act soon
• Small initial steps taken
• Example: “I’ll quit next month; I’ve reduced cigarettes.”

• Action

• Active behavior change
• High effort and risk of relapse
• Example: Recently stopped smoking

• Maintenance

• Sustained change (>6 months)
• Focus on preventing relapse
• Example: Abstinent for months, avoiding triggers

• Relapse

• Return to old behavior
• Common and part of the cycle

Contemplation involves awareness and thinking about change (Statement 1 correct), while precontemplation reflects lack of intent to change; considering health benefits fits early contemplation rather than denial. (hence statement 2 is incorrect)

Maintenance refers to sustained behaviour change for >6 months, as in quitting smoking for one year (Statement 3 correct).

The action phase involves active behaviour change; expressing helplessness reflects precontemplation, making Statement 4 incorrect.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following steps of a planning cycle: 1. Assigning priorities among the problems 2. Evaluation 3. Selecting best programme 4. Operating the programme Which among the following is the correct sequence of steps?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1 → 3 → 4 → 2

Health planning is a systematic process of identifying health problems, setting priorities, selecting the best interventions, implementing them, and evaluating outcomes. The planning cycle ensures that health programs are evidence-based, efficient, and continuously improved.

The correct sequence of the given steps is: 1 → 3 → 4 → 2

• 1. Assigning priorities among the problems ✓

• After identifying health problems, priorities are set based on magnitude, severity, feasibility, and available resources.

• 3. Selecting best programme ✓

• Alternative strategies are evaluated, and the most appropriate intervention/programme is selected.

• 4. Operating the programme ✓

• The selected programme is implemented.

• 2. Evaluation ✓

• The programme is monitored and evaluated to determine whether the objectives have been achieved and to guide future planning.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Despite substantial improvements in immunization coverage, institutional deliveries, and healthcare accessibility under the rural health program, these indicators continued to lag considerably behind those observed in urban populations. Which of the following pillars of primary health care is most likely to be exploited?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Equitable distribution

Equitable distribution is a core principle of Primary Health Care (PHC), ensuring that essential health services are available and accessible to all segments of the population, irrespective of geographic location or socioeconomic status. Persistent disparities between rural and urban health indicators, despite overall improvements, reflect a failure to achieve equitable distribution of healthcare.

Why not the other options?

• A. Appropriate technology: Refers to the use of scientifically sound, affordable, and locally acceptable technologies; it does not address rural–urban disparities in access.
• B. Community participation: Involves active involvement of the community in planning and implementing health programs but does not primarily explain unequal service distribution.
• C. Intersectoral coordination: Refers to collaboration between sectors such as health, education, sanitation, and nutrition to improve health outcomes; it is not the main issue highlighted in the question.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During a health education session, people cannot understand your few technical words during the chat, and it’s a miscommunication. This is which type of barrier?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Semantic barrier

A semantic barrier arises when words, symbols, or language used by the communicator are not understood by the audience.

Use of technical or medical jargon during health education can lead to misunderstanding and ineffective communication.

Example:

If a health worker says “hypertension”, people may not understand unless it is explained as “high blood pressure.”

Overcoming semantic barriers requires using simple language, local terms, and culturally appropriate expressions to ensure message clarity.

| Barrier | Main Problem | Medical Example

| ------- | ------------ | ---------------

| Cultural | Difference in beliefs/customs | Refusal of blood transfusion for religious reasons

| Physiological | Physical disability | Deaf patient cannot hear instructions

| Psychological | Emotional/mental factors | Anxiety causing misunderstanding

| Semantic | Language/jargon issue | Patient confused by medical terminology

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: For Health Education, the Motivation Model has its 1st Step as Awareness. Its 2nd Step is Motivation. Its 3rd Step is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Action

In the Motivation Model of Health Education, behaviour change proceeds in a stepwise manner.

After awareness (knowledge of the health issue) and motivation (desire to change), the third step is action, where the individual actually adopts the desired health behaviour.

This model emphasizes moving from knowledge to practice, which is the ultimate goal of health education.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: ICER is used as an Economic model in which of the following Health Management Techniques:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cost effectiveness analysis

In health economics, decision makers often need to determine which health intervention provides the best value for money. One important method used for this purpose is Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (CEA). It compared the cost of an intervention along with the health outcomes achieved.

ICER (Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio) is a key measure in cost-effectiveness analysis, used to compare the additional cost per additional unit of health outcome (e.g., cost per life-year or QALY gained) between two interventions. ICER is used for evaluating vaccination programs, cancer screening programs, new drug therapies, public health interventions.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify the communication method in which speakers present one after another on a specific health topic, followed by a summary from the chairperson, but without any discussion among the speakers.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Symposium

A symposium is a communication method in which multiple speakers present sequentially on different aspects of a single topic.

Each speaker delivers an individual presentation, and the session concludes with a summary by the chairperson, without interaction or discussion among the speakers.

| Feature | Description

| ------- | -----------

| Speakers | Multiple experts

| Presentation | Sequential

| Interaction | No discussion among speakers

| Role of chairperson | Summarizes at the end

| Method | Main Feature

| ------ | ------------

| Symposium | Sequential expert presentations

| Panel discussion | Experts discuss among themselves

| Seminar | Presentation + discussion

| Workshop | Practical skill training

In contrast, panel discussions involve interaction, seminars include audience participation, and workshops emphasize hands-on training.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the 18th century, the East India Company engaged in the illicit trade of a specific substance with China, which played a significant role in the historical trade dynamics. What was the substance that the company smuggled into China during this time?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Opium

During the 18th and early 19th centuries, the British East India Company smuggled opium from India into China to counterbalance the trade deficit caused by Chinese tea exports. During the 18th and early 19th centuries, the British East India Company controlled opium production in India, particularly in:

• Bengal
• Bihar
• United Provinces (present-day Uttar Pradesh)

The Opium Trade Triangle

The opium produced in India was illegally exported to China, where it was widely consumed. This trade became one of the largest narcotics trades in history.

This illicit trade led to widespread opium addiction in China and eventually triggered the Opium Wars, reshaping global trade and colonial policies.

The episode is a classic example of how commercial interests influenced public health and international relations.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the broad planning of a health program, which sequence of steps is most appropriate? 1. Evaluation 2. Execution 3. Planning 4. Delegation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Planning, Execution, Evaluation

Health program management follows a systematic sequence of Planning → Execution (Implementation) → Evaluation. Planning identifies health needs, sets objectives, and allocates resources; execution implements the planned activities; and evaluation assesses whether program objectives have been achieved and provides feedback for future planning.

Why not the other options?

• B. Planning → Delegation → Evaluation: Delegation is a management function within implementation, not a major phase of program planning.
• C. Execution → Delegation → Evaluation: Incorrect because planning must precede execution.
• D. Execution → Planning → Delegation: Incorrect sequence; implementation cannot begin before planning.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the following table, the end results of planning are qualified by brief characteristics. How many of the pairs given below are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Only one of the pairs

In health planning and management, goals, objectives, and targets are distinct terms with different characteristics.

Why is only Pair 2 correct?

• 1. Goal – Always constrained by time ✗

• A goal is a broad, general statement of the desired end result.
• It is not necessarily time-bound and allows varying degrees of achievement.

• 2. Objective – Precise; either achieved or not achieved ✓

• An objective is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART).
• It is a precise statement with a definite endpoint and is considered either achieved or not achieved.

• 3. Target – Permits the concept of degree of achievement ✗

• A target is a quantified, time-bound level of achievement (e.g., 90% immunization by 2025).
• It is also precise and is generally regarded as achieved or not achieved, rather than permitting broad degrees of achievement.
• The concept of “degree of achievement” is more applicable to goals.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Sterilization technique for the tip of disposable glass pipette is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Autoclaving and 70% ethanol

The most effective sterilization technique for the tip of disposable glass pipettes is autoclaving combined with 70% ethanol.

Autoclaving uses: 121°C, 15 psi,15–20 minutes. This method destroys all microorganisms including spores.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The Panchayati Raj is a three-tier structure of rural local self-government in India with the three levels being village, block and district. Consider the following bodies: I. Gram Sabha II. Gram Panchayat III. Nyaya Panchayat IV. Panchayat Samiti Which of the above bodies are present at the village level?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. I, II and III

The Panchayati Raj System is the three-tier system of rural local self-government in India, established through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 to promote decentralization of power and democratic participation at the grassroots level. The three tiers are:

• Village level → Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, Nyaya Panchayat
• Block (Intermediate) level → Panchayat Samiti
• District level → Zila Parishad

The following bodies are present at the village level:

• I. Gram Sabha

• The general body of all registered voters in a village.
• It is the foundation of the Panchayati Raj System and exercises overall supervision of the Gram Panchayat.

• II. Gram Panchayat

• The executive body at the village level.
• Headed by the Sarpanch (Pradhan) and responsible for implementing developmental and welfare activities.

• III. Nyaya Panchayat

• A village-level judicial body (where constituted by the state) that settles minor civil and criminal disputes.
• It is not constitutionally mandatory, but traditionally functions at the village or group-of-villages level.

Why is IV incorrect?

• IV. Panchayat Samiti

• It functions at the Block (Intermediate) level, not at the village level.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: To visit an industry to audit whether the benefits under the Employees State Insurance Act are being properly provided, which of the following benefits should be available to the insured person, or other dependents as the case may be? 1. Medical benefit 2. Sickness benefit 3. Funeral expenses 4. Rehabilitation allowance Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2, 3 and 4

The Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Act, 1948 provides comprehensive social security benefits to insured workers and their dependents.

Why are the statements correct?

• 1. Medical benefit✔️: Comprehensive medical care for the insured person and eligible family members.
• 2. Sickness benefit✔️: Cash compensation during certified sickness.
• 3. Funeral expenses✔️: Lump-sum payment to the eldest surviving family member or the person performing the funeral.
• 4. Rehabilitation allowance✔️: Includes vocational and physical rehabilitation benefits for insured persons with disablement.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What are the components of attitude?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Cognition, behavior, affective

Attitude is a learned predisposition to respond consistently toward an object, person, or situation. It comprises three interrelated components, collectively known as the ABC model of attitude:

• Affective: Feelings or emotions toward an object (e.g., liking or disliking vaccination).
• Behavioral: The tendency or intention to act in a particular way (e.g., getting vaccinated).
• Cognitive: Knowledge, beliefs, or thoughts about the object (e.g., believing vaccines prevent disease).

Why not the other options?

• B. Affective, responsive, social: “Responsive” and “social” are not recognized components of attitude.
• C. Knowledge, income status, education: Income and education are determinants, not components of attitude.
• D. Social, confidence, knowledge: Social and confidence are not core components of the ABC model.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the use of secondary prevention in Colorectal cancer?
options: Vaccine to reduce transmission of cancer
For early diagnosis and improved prognosis and treatment
To screen for cancer before onset of disease
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. For early diagnosis and improved prognosis and treatment

| Level of Prevention | Aim

| ------------------- | ---

| Primary prevention | Prevent occurrence of disease

| Secondary prevention | Early detection and early treatment

| Tertiary prevention | Reduce disability and complications

Secondary prevention aims at early detection of disease after its onset but before symptoms become advanced.

In colorectal cancer, this includes screening methods like fecal occult blood testing, sigmoidoscopy, or colonoscopy to detect cancer at an early, treatable stage.

Early diagnosis through secondary prevention leads to better prognosis and more effective treatment, distinguishing it from primary prevention (risk reduction) and tertiary prevention (palliation).

Early detection allows:

| Benefit | Explanation

| ------- | -----------

| Early treatment | Tumor removed before spread

| Better prognosis | Higher survival rates

| Reduced mortality | Early-stage cancers are curable

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which among the following are characteristics of health education, rather than propaganda? 1. Knowledge actively acquired, rather than instilled. 2. Appeals to emotion, rather than reason. 3. Behaviour centred, rather than information centred. 4. Arouses and stimulates primitive desires, rather than disciplines them. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1 and 3

Health education is a planned learning process that helps individuals and communities voluntarily adopt healthy behaviors through understanding, motivation, and participation. Unlike propaganda, it emphasizes reason, active learning, and behavior change rather than emotional manipulation.

• 1. Knowledge actively acquired\, rather than instilled. ✓

• Health education encourages active participation, critical thinking, and self-learning.

• 2. Appeals to emotion\, rather than reason. ✗

• This is a feature of propaganda, which relies on emotional appeal rather than rational understanding.

• 3. Behaviour centred\, rather than information centred. ✓

• The ultimate goal of health education is behavior change, not merely providing information.

• 4. Arouses and stimulates primitive desires\, rather than disciplines them. ✗

• This is also a characteristic of propaganda, not health education.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which legislation is responsible for ensuring the security and confidentiality of medical records?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. DPDP

The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 is the Indian legislation that governs collection, processing, storage, and protection of personal data, including medical records, ensuring confidentiality and data security.

HIPAA is a US law about data protection, while MTP and PCPNDT regulate specific medical practices, not data protection.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following international agencies, which agency has been assisting India in development of friendly models of sanitization?
options: CARE (Cooperative for Assistance and Relief Everywhere)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Ford Foundation

The Ford Foundation has historically assisted India in the development and promotion of sanitary latrine models and rural sanitation programmes, contributing to the evolution of appropriate (“user-friendly”) sanitation technologies and community-based sanitation initiatives.

Why not the other options?

• A. SIDA ❌: Primarily supports broader health, water, and development programmes.
• B. DANIDA ❌: Best known in India for its support to the National Programme for Control of Blindness (NPCB).
• D. CARE ❌: Mainly works in nutrition, maternal-child health, disaster relief, and community development.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one among the following terms best fits the description “the entire gamut of preventive, therapeutic and rehabilitative services for the protection of society from antisocial, criminal or deviant conduct of man”?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Social defence

Social defence refers to the entire range of preventive, therapeutic and rehabilitative measures aimed at protecting society from antisocial, criminal or deviant behaviour.

• A. Social delinquency: Refers to antisocial or delinquent behaviour itself.
• B. Social defence — Correct: Encompasses prevention, treatment and rehabilitation of individuals exhibiting antisocial or deviant behaviour.
• C. Social pathology: Study of social problems and dysfunctional social behaviour.
• D. Social survey: Systematic collection of information about a population or social group.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following management techniques helps in standardising the methods of performing jobs?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Work Sampling

Work sampling is a work measurement and management technique used to analyze how workers spend their time during a job. By making random observations of work activities, it helps identify inefficiencies and standardize the best method of performing a job, thereby improving productivity.

• A. Systems Analysis ✗

• Studies the functioning of an entire system and its components to improve overall efficiency.
• Does not standardize individual job methods.

• B. Decision Making ✗

• Refers to selecting the best course of action from available alternatives.
• It is a managerial function, not a method for standardizing work.

• C. Work Sampling ✓

• Uses random observations to determine how time is utilized.
• Helps establish standard methods, improve workflow, and increase efficiency.

• D. Personnel Management ✗

• Deals with recruitment, training, motivation, and appraisal of employees.
• It is not used to standardize job performance.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which type of graph is used to illustrate studies on healthcare and disease prevalence in a population?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Ishikawa diagram/Fish bone diagram

The Kaoru Ishikawa (fish-bone) diagram is used to systematically analyse and illustrate the multiple determinants and contributing factors affecting health outcomes and disease prevalence in a population.

The structure resembles a fish skeleton:

• Head of fish → problem or outcome
• Bones → major categories of causes
• Smaller branches → contributing factors

In public health research, it helps map biological, environmental, social, and health-system factors influencing disease burden.

Bar diagrams and histograms display data distribution, while regression models are analytical tools rather than illustrative diagrams.

A. Bar diagram- Bar diagrams show comparisons between categories, such as disease rates across regions.

B. Histogram- Histograms display frequency distribution of continuous variables.

Example: age distribution of patients.

C. Multiple regression model- This is a statistical analysis technique, not a graphical representation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Why was the “Health for All” (HFA) goal eventually replaced by the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) and later the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?
options: HFA was only meant for Communicable diseases
HFA was only meant for low socioeconomic/developing countries
HFA failed to achieve the original targets
HFA was only meant for Non-communicable diseases
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. HFA failed to achieve the original targets

Health for All (HFA) initiative, launched by the WHO following the Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) with the goal of achieving “Health for All by the year 2000,” was replaced by the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) and later the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) because its original targets were not achieved globally. The MDGs and SDGs adopted broader, measurable, and time-bound health and development targets.

Why not the other options?

• A. HFA was only meant for communicable diseases: Incorrect. HFA addressed comprehensive primary health care, not just communicable diseases.
• B. HFA was only meant for low socioeconomic/developing countries: Incorrect. it was a global initiative applicable to all countries.
• D. HFA was only meant for non-communicable diseases: Incorrect. HFA covered all aspects of health, including communicable diseases, maternal and child health, nutrition, and health promotion.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 9-month-old baby with diarrhea is feeding well and is thirsty. Skin pinch when done returns in 2 seconds. What is the treatment?
options: 200-400 ml of ORS to be given in the first four hours.
400-700 ml of ORS to be given in the first four hours.
700-900 ml of ORS to be given in the first 4 hours.
In addition to the usual fluid intake, 100-200 ml should be given after each loose stool.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 400-700 ml of ORS to be given in the first four hours.

According to the IMNCI classification, the baby has some dehydration and comes under Plan B. The amount of ORS given is 75ml/kg body weight.

Here, the weight of the child is not specified. Hence, 400-700 ml of ORS at home is to be given in the first four hours according to the age of the child. The below table shows the amount of ORS to be given according to the age of the child.

The four rules of home treatment are:

• Give extra fluid
• Give zinc supplements (1 tablet per day for 14 days, dissolved in a small amount of ORS or breast milk or clean water)
• Continue breastfeeding
• Counsel the mother to return if there is blood in stools and if the child is feeding poorly

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to the WHO, what percentage of immunization coverage is needed for eradication of measles?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 96%

According to the WHO, eradication of measles requires achieving an immunization coverage of at least 96% of children under 1 year of age.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Cytotoxic and expired drugs are disposed by:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Incineration

Cytotoxic and expired drugs are collected in a yellow bag and then disposed of by incineration.

Expired cytotoxic drugs are to be returned to the manufacturer and subjected to incineration, encapsulation, or plasma pyrolysis. Other discarded medicines can be disposed by incineration.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a screening test for DM out of 1000 population, 90 were positive. However, a gold standard test for DM was done of which 100 were positive. Calculate the sensitivity of the screening test?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 90/100

The screening test only identified 90 people as positive for diabetes, while the gold standard test identified 100 people. This means that out of the 100 confirmed, 90 have been identified as truly positive by the screening test and 10 are falsely negative. Therefore,

• True positive = 90
• False negative = 100-90= 10
• Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN) =90/(90+10) = 90/100 = 90%

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a well-designed cancer study, similar remission rates were obtained for a new treatment (33.2%) and the usual treatment (32.2%), with the p-value being 0.04. Which of the following statements is true regarding the study?
options: Both the treatments are equally effective
Neither of the treatments is effective
The new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment
The information given is not adequate to compare the efficacy of the treatments
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. The new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment

As the p-value is 0.04, we can conclude that the new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment.

Even though both treatments have similar rates of remission, a valid statistical test is required to determine the difference in their effectiveness. Statistically, p-value < 0.05 implies that the alternate hypothesis is true.

In this scenario, we can consider:

• Null hypothesis: Both the treatments are equally effective (in other terms, there is no difference between the effect of the two treatments).
• Alternative hypothesis: New treatment is more effective than the usual treatment.

As the p-value is 0.04, which is statistically significant (<0.05), the null hypothesis is rejected and the alternative hypothesis is accepted. Hence the new treatment is more effective than the usual treatment.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
In order to reach the demographic goal of NRR=1, the couple protection rate should exceed?

NRR: Net reproduction rate
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 60%

In order to reach the demographic goal of NRR=1, the couple protection rate (CPR) should exceed 60%. This coincides with every couple having 2 children.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Kala-Azar is endemic in all these areas except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Assam

Kala-Azar is not endemic in Assam. It is endemic in the following states in 54 districts:

• Uttar Pradesh
• West Bengal
• Bihar
• Jharkhand

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The Chadah committee recommended all of the following except:
options: One basic health worker per 10,000 population
Responsibility of PHCs in malaria eradication
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. One PHC for 50,000 population

The recommendation of one PHC for a 50,000 population was given by Kartar Singh Committee.

The recommendations given by the Chadah Committee of 1963:

• PHC at the block level
• One basic health worker per 10,000 population
• Responsibility of PHCs in malaria eradication

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The dose of iodine for lactating women in India according to the recommended dietary allowance is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 280 μg/day

According to the National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) 2020 guidelines, the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for dietary iodine in lactating women in India is 280 μg/day.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The incidence of a disease is 4 per 1000 of the population with an average duration of 2 years. What is the prevalence?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 8/1000

The prevelance in the given situation is 8/1000 population.

Prevalence is given by the formula :

Prevalance = Incidence x Mean Duration

Prevalence = 4/1000 x 2 = 8/1000 population

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The probability that infection will occur among susceptible persons following contact with an infectious person within the incubation period is known as the_______.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Secondary attack rate

The probability that infection will occur among susceptible persons following contact with an infectious person within the incubation period is called secondary attack rate.

It is calculated by the following formula:

Secondary attack rate (SAR) = (Number of exposed or susceptible persons developing the disease within the incubation period x 100)/(Total number of close or exposed contacts that are susceptible)

Primary cases are usually excluded from the numerator and denominator.

Secondary attack rate measures the communicability of the disease.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the ratio of the incidence of the disease in the exposed to that of the non-exposed?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Relative risk

The ratio of incidence of disease or death among exposed to that among the non-exposed is called relative risk (RR).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the unit of observation in ecological studies?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Population

In ecological studies, the unit of observation is the population or community.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What should be the minimum interval between the administration of two live vaccines?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 4 weeks

The minimum interval between the administration of two live vaccines is 4 weeks.

This is because decreasing the interval between two doses may interfere with the antibody response and protection. Thus, live vaccines can either be given on the same day according to the schedule or 4 weeks apart.

Note: In Park 27th ed. the minimum interval between two live vaccines is given as 3 weeks. However, several other standard sources including CDC and UNDP suggested an interval of 4 weeks. When both are given in options, it is recommended to mark 4 weeks as the correct answer.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What value of BMI is considered as 'lethal' in men?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. < 13

A body mass index (BMI) of 13 or less is considered lethal in men.

However, females can survive even at a lower BMI up to 11.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which article of the Indian Constitution confers Right to Life to the citizens of India?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Article 21

The Right to Life is given in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.

Option A: Article 11 defines the right of the parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.

Option C: Article 23 defines the prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labor.

Option D: Article 25 defines the freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following does not cause hardness of water?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Calcium carbonate

Calcium carbonate does not cause hardness of water. Hardness of water is caused by bicarbonates and sulphates of calcium and magnesium.

There are two types of hardness of water:

• Temporary (carbonate) hardness is due to bicarbonates of calcium and magnesium.
• Permanent (non-carbonate) hardness is due to sulphates, chlorides and nitrates.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a method of direct transmission of communicable diseases?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Droplet nuclei

Airborne transmission by droplet nuclei is not a method of direct transmission of diseases.

It is a method of indirect transmission of diseases.

Droplet nuclei are tiny particles of size 1-5 microns range that may be formed by either due to evaporation of droplets coughed or sneezed into the air or are formed from aerosols.

These droplet nuclei remain airborne for long periods of time and can transmit diseases like tuberculosis, influenza, chickenpox, measles, Q fever and other respiratory infections.

Droplet transmission, vertical transmission, and contact with soil are methods of direct transmission of diseases.

Differences between droplet and droplet nuclei are summarised below:

DROPLET NUCLEI
DROPLET

Indirect transmission
Direct transmission

It is the residue from evaporated droplets
It is produced while coughing, sneezing, talking

<5microns in diameter
≥5 microns in diameter

No need for close contact for transmission
Requires closeness and direct contact for transmission

Diseases transmitted: chickenpox, measles etc.
Diseases transmitted: diphtheria, meningococcal meningitis etc.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not used in the assessment of body fat?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Breslow index

Breslow's staging is used for the staging of malignant melanoma, not for the assessment of body fat.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is true about Factories Act?
options: Children under 14 years of age must not be employed in factories
A child of 16 years can be employed only between 6 AM and 8 PM
The maximum working hours for an adult is 72 hours per week
A child of 16 years can work till 5 hours per day
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Children under 14 years of age must not be employed in factories

Factories act prohibits children of <14 years from being employed.

Children between 15–18 years can be employed only in certain industries and work only between 6 AM–7 PM. They should not be made to work for more than four and a half hours.

The maximum working hours for an adult industrial worker should be not more than 48 hours per week, not exceeding 9 hours a day; if overtime is paid, then it should be not more than 60 hrs per week.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is true for non-parametric tests?
options: ANOVA is an example of a non parametric test
It is used for skewed distributions
It involves the assumption that the data has a normal distribution
It cannot be used for small sample sizes
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. It is used for skewed distributions

Non-parametric tests are tests that do not assume that the data is normally distributed. Thus, they are used for skewed (asymmetric) distributions {skewed either to the lesser side (left-sided skewed) or towards the greater side (right-sided skewed)}.

The chi-square test is an example of a non-parametric test that is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.

ANOVA is an example of a parametric test.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 4-year-old male child developed sore throat and difficulty in swallowing and mild fever. On examination, the clinical picture shown below is seen. Which of the following sentences is false regarding the vaccine that could have prevented this condition?
options: Its administered on the anterolateral aspect of thigh
A prior adverse reaction with temperature above 37 degrees is a contraindication
Cellular pertussis component in the vaccine is not recommended after 7-years of age
The diphtheria toxoid dose in adults is much lesser than the pediatric dose
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. A prior adverse reaction with temperature above 37 degrees is a contraindication

The image shows a dirty white pseudomembrane classic of diphtheria. A prior adverse reaction with a temperature above 37 is not a contraindication.

Precautionary measures are taken when the temperature is above 40 degrees, but it is not considered a contraindication for subsequent doses of DPwT.

Anaphylaxis is a contraindication for subsequent vaccination with diphtheria, pertussis, or tetanus vaccine. Encephalopathy following vaccination is a contraindication for pertussis vaccine. DT is given for successive doses.

Events such as inconsolable cry, fever more than 40.5°C, seizures with or without fever are considered as precautions, and not contraindications for DTwP.

The cellular component of pertussis is not recommended after 7 years.

• Unvaccinated child 5-7 years: Give DPT 1, 2 and 3 at 1-month intervals. Administer booster dose of DPT at a minimum of 6 months
after administering DPT-3 up to the age of 7 years.
• Unvaccinated child above 7 years: Administer Tdap (Tetanus and diphtheria toxoids and acellular pertussis) at 0, and Td (Tetanus, Diphtheria vaccine) at 1 and 6 months, respectively.

The adult dose of diphtheria toxoid is almost 12 times lesser in comparison with the pediatric dosage.

Note: IAP guidelines state that "temperature more than >40.5°C is a precaution and not contraindication". Park's 27th Ed states that "temperature above 40°C is a contraindication to DPT". This topic is controversial, however, IAP guidelines are commonly followed by practitioners.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A paradoxical carrier is defined as:
options: A person who sheds pathogens during incubation period
A carrier who acquired pathogen from another carrier
A person who acquired pathogen from patient
A patient who became a carrier
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. A carrier who acquired pathogen from another carrier

A paradoxical carrier is a carrier that acquired a pathogen from another carrier.

Incubatory carriers are those who shed the infectious agents during the incubation period of the disease.

Convalescent carriers are those who continue to shed the disease agent during the period of convalescence.

Healthy carriers are those who had a subclinical infection and developed a carrier state without suffering from overt disease.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A resident doctor sustained a needlestick injury while sampling blood of a patient who is HIV positive. A decision is taken to offer him post-exposure prophylaxis. Which one of the following would be the best recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Lamivudine + Tenofovir + Dolutegravir for 4 weeks

Triple therapy with tenofovir 300mg, lamivudine 300mg, and dolutegravir 50mg for 4 weeks is recommended for HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).

Steps to be undertaken after a needlestick injury are:

• Wash the wound and skin with water and soap. Do not scrub and avoid antiseptics.
• Assess exposed individual:

• Check baseline viral markers
• Monitor for acute seroconversion illness within 3-6 weeks after exposure
• If testing is positive, refer to ART center

• Assess exposure source and determine the risk of transmission
• Counseling and support
• Initiate PEP at the earliest - preferably < 2 hours and ideally < 72 hours
• 28-day prescription with drug information
• HIV test at 3 months after exposure

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to IMNCI, a 6-month-old child is said to have pneumonia if the child has fast breathing with a respiratory rate more than:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 50

Three key clinical signs are used to assess a sick child with cough or difficult breathing:

• Respiratory rate (RR): distinguishes children who have pneumonia from those who do not. Children are classified as pneumonia if:

• > 50/min RR for infants 2 months to 12 months
• > 40/min RR for children 12 months to 5 years of age

• Lower chest wall indrawing indicates severe pneumonia
• Stridor indicates those with severe pneumonia requiring hospital admission.

The following image gives the IMNCI classification for cough/difficulty in breathing in children.

Signs of severe pneumonia are :

• Not able to drink
• Persistent vomiting
• Convulsions
• Lethargic or unconscious
• Stridor in a calm child
• Severe malnutrition

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Cross product ratio can be arrived from:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Case control study

Cross product ratio (Odds ratio) can be obtained from the case-control study.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: If a patient tests positive for a disease, which of the following represents the probability of her actually having the disease?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Positive predictive value

Positive predictive value implies the probability of a person with a positive test, actually having the disease.

It is the ability of a test to detect true positive(TP) out of total positive(TP+FP) and it is directly proportional to the prevalence of a disease.

PPV= TP/TP+FP

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a normal curve, what is the percentage of distribution of one standard deviation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 68%

Approximately 68% of a normal distribution falls within ±1 standard deviations of the mean. This is as per the empirical rule of a normal distribution.

Approximately 95% of the distribution falls within ±2 standard deviations of the mean.

Approximately 99.7% of the distribution falls within ±3 standard deviations of the mean.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In controlled tipping, the amount of land required for the trench method to be practiced for a population of 10,000 is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1 acre

In controlled tipping, one acre of land is required by the trench method to be practiced for a population of 10,000.

It is also known as a sanitary landfill. It is the most satisfactory method of refuse disposal where suitable land is available. In this method, waste material is placed in a trench or other prepared area. Then, it is adequately compacted and covered with earth at the end of the day.

Methods used in controlled tipping are:

• Trench method: Done in places where level ground is available
• Ramp method: Well suited where the terrain is moderately sloping
• Area method: Used for filling land depressions, disused quarries, and clay pits

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the following natural history of disease flowchart, point A to C is called as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Lead time

Lead time is the period between the first possible time of detection (point A) and the usual time of diagnosis (point C).

Screening time is the time difference between the first point of diagnosis and the critical point of diagnosis.

Diagnosis of a disease before the critical point has a good outcome and reduces the severity by reversing the disease process. Diagnosis beyond the critical point treatment would be unsuccessful and/or permanent damage would have occurred.

Screening must be done in conditions where there is a considerable time lag between the onset of disease and the usual time of diagnosis. That is conditions with a long lead time.

Generation time is defined as the interval of time between the onset of infection by a host and the maximal infectivity of that host.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The following diagram charts the population change over years from 1983 to 1989 in a given place. What is the statistical diagram used here?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Component bar graph

The given image shows a component bar graph. It is used to represent data in which the total magnitude is divided into different subsets or components.

A bar chart or bar graph is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data. They can be simple, multiple or component bar graphs.

The image given below shows a multiple bar graph showing the human losses of world war II by country. In a multiple bar chart, 2 or more sets of data are shown simultaneously.

A bar chart can be distinguished from a histogram because the rectangles are separated by the spaces. This indicates that the data forms discrete categories.

In a histogram, the rectangles are not separated by spaces as the data represented forms a continuous set instead of discrete groups.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The principal unit of administration in India is ______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. District

• The principal unit of administration in India is the district under a Collector.
• Under districts are the sub-divisions, tahsils or talukas, municipalities or corporations, villages, panchayats, etc.
• As of the 2019 census, there are 725 districts in India.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The risk of genetic diseases in consanguineous marriage between first cousins is?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 4-8%

The risk of genetic diseases in consanguineous marriage between first cousins is 4-8%.

The risk of genetic diseases in non-consanguineous marriage is 2-4%.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The test of choice to measure the difference in means between two groups in a study, with one group being a control is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Unpaired T test

The test of choice to measure the difference in means between two groups in a study, with one group being a control is unpaired T test.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The test of significance done for two or more proportions:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Chi- square test

Chi-Square(χ2) test is a test used for proportions and associations.

It is a non-parametric (non-numeric) test and it is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Triage is done during disaster management to ensure treatment of casualties is done properly. What is true about triage done at the disaster site?
options: Green labels are for those who need to be transported on priority
Moribund patients receive the lowest priority
Most commonly used system is three color code system
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Moribund patients receive the lowest priority

Moribund patients receive the lowest priority.

This is because despite paying quite a lot of attention, the benefit is still questionable.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the best way to plot the changes in incidence of a disease in a given area over time?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Line graph

Line graphs or line diagrams are the best way to plot the changes in the incidence of a disease in a given area over time.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the dosage of vitamin A given for a 2-year-old baby with keratomalacia?
options: 2,00,000 IU immediately, followed by same dose after 24 hours
1,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose after 1 week
1,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose after 24 hours and after a week
2,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose 24 hours later and after 2 weeks
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2,00,000 IU immediately, followed by the same dose 24 hours later and after 2 weeks

The recommended vitamin A dosage for a 2-year-old child with keratomalacia is 2,00,000 IU given immediately, followed by the same age-specific dose 24 hours later and after 2 weeks.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is false about Rubella infection?
options: It is a type of droplet infection
Infection in early pregnancy causes a milder form of disease in the fetus
Fetus affected in late pregnancy may have only deafness
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Infection in early pregnancy causes a milder form of disease in the fetus

Earlier the rubella infection occurs in pregnancy, greater is the damage to the foetus.

The major determinant of the extent of fetal infection in congenital rubella syndrome is the gestational age at which fetal transmission occurs.

Rubella infection in 1st trimester can cause:

• Abortions
• Still birth
• Skin lesions - blueberry muffin rash
• Congenital rubella syndrome

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is false regarding confounding factor?
options: It can be reduced by matching
It is associated individually with both cause and effect
It is distributed equally in both study and control groups
It is associated with the exposure of the study
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. It is distributed equally in both study and control groups

A confounding factor is a factor that is associated with both exposure and diseases and is distributed unequally in study and control groups. It can be reduced by matching.

For example, if the study is that a sedentary lifestyle can lead to coronary artery diseases, then age can act as a confounding factor as it is individually linked to both sedentary lifestyle and coronary artery diseases.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a personal protective equipment?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Lab coat

A lab coat is not a personal protective equipment.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) are:

• Gloves – protect hands.
• Gowns/ aprons – protect skin and clothing.
• Masks protect the mouth/nose and respirators protect the respiratory tract from airborne infectious agents.
• Goggles – protect eyes.
• Face shields – protect face, mouth, nose, and eyes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is part of the concurrent list of the Indian Constitution?
options: Fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Adulteration of food

Adulteration of food is included under the concurrent list.

The legislative section of the seventh schedule is divided into three lists:

• Union list - a list of 100 items on which the parliament has exclusive power to legislate
• State list - a list of 61 items on which the state government has exclusive power to legislate
• Concurrent list - a list of 52 items on which both central and state governments have the power to legislate

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the best level of prevention of breast cancer?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Early diagnosis and treatment

Early diagnosis and treatment is the best level of prevention of breast cancer. It is a secondary level of prevention.

The earlier a disease is diagnosed and treated, the better is the prognosis. The occurrence of secondary cases or any long term disability can be prevented. This is of particular importance in chronic diseases.

Early diagnosis and treatment is not as effective and economical as primary prevention. However, it may be critically important in reducing the high morbidity and mortality in diseases such as essential hypertension, cancer cervix and breast cancer.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following parameters would you use to check the efficiency of the surveillance system for malaria under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Annual Blood Examination Rate

The Annual Blood Examination Rate (ABER) is used to check the efficiency of the surveillance system for malaria. It takes into account the number of slides examined for the population under surveillance.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Varicella

Varicella vaccine is contraindicated in pregnant women as it is a live vaccine.

The live attenuated varicella virus vaccine is currently recommended for children between 12 to 18 months of age who have not had chickenpox.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 24-month-old child weighing 11 kg was brought to the pediatric OPD. He had a respiratory rate of 38/min. On examination, chest indrawing was observed. What is the next step of management?
options: Urgent referral to the tertiary care centre immediately
Administer IV antibiotics and ask the patient to be brought after 24 hours
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Oral amoxicillin for five days

From the given clinical picture, it appears that the child has pneumonia as diagnosed from the presence of chest indrawing. The next best step of management is to give oral amoxicillin for five days and send the child home.

This is based on the revised WHO classification and treatment of childhood pneumonia at health facilities. Pneumonia with general danger signs like inability to drink, persistent vomiting, convulsions, lethargic or unconscious, stridor in a calm child or severe malnutrition needs antibiotics with urgent referral to higher centre.

The following image distinguishes the previous and revised classification and treatment of the childhood pneumonia.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A patient comes with a history of clean-cut injury which is not lacerated. He says that he received his last dose of tetanus vaccination about 10 years ago. What should be given next?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Single dose tetanus toxoid

A single dose of tetanus toxoid is given as the wound is clean and the last dose was received more than 10 years ago.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A person wants to study about the relationship between smoking and lung cancer, so he collects data about people diseased with lung cancer from government hospitals and the number of cigarette packets sold at the same time period. Which type of study is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Ecological

The type of study described is an ecological study as the unit of study is the population. The number of cigarette packets sold at the same time is data about the population.

Option A: The unit of study in a cross-sectional study is an individual.

Option C: There is no experiment done here. Hence, it is not experimental study.

Option D: Quasi-experiments are nonrandomized, pre-post intervention studies done when it is not feasible or ethical to conduct a randomized controlled trial. The unit of study is therefore patients or individuals and not population.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was done to assess nutritional status among young children in rural and urban areas. 30 children in rural and 20 children in urban areas were malnourished. Which of the following tests of significance is the most appropriate in this case?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Chi Square test

The most appropriate test of significance, in this case, is the chi-square test. It is used to compare qualitative data between 2 groups with independent measures.

Option B: Paired t-test compares paired data or pre-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. This doesn't apply here as the groups are not paired.

Option C: The standard error of the mean is calculated for quantitative data, with a measure of central tendency as mean.

Option D: ANOVA is used to compare more than 2 groups.

questions.subject: Community Medicine

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As per NCEP- ATP III, which of the following is not a criterion for metabolic syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. High LDL

As per NCEP- ATP III, high LDL is not included in the definition criteria of metabolic syndrome.

Metabolic syndrome is present if three or more of the following five criteria are met, which is given by NCEP-ATP III (National Cholesterol Education Program and Adult Treatment Panel III). It includes:

• Central obesity: waist circumference >102 cm (M), >88 cm (F)
• Hypertriglyceridemia: triglyceride level ≥ 150 mg/dL
• Low HDL cholesterol: <40 mg/dL and <50 mg/dL for men and women, respectively.
• Hypertension: blood pressure ≥130 mmHg systolic or ≥ 85 mmHg diastolic.
• Fasting plasma glucose level: ≥100 mg/dL or previously diagnosed type 2 diabetes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a population study, the value of the mean is 200. If the standard deviation is 20, 68% of the population will lie between?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 180- 220

68% of the population will lie between 180- 220.

In a normal distribution curve, 68% of the values lie within the mean +/- 1 standard deviation and the mean=median=mode. Since the mean = 200 and the standard deviation = 20:

68% of population will lie between Mean +/- 1SD, that is, 200 +/- 20 = 180-220

95% of population lies between Mean+/-2SD, 200+/- 2*20 = 160- 240

99% of population lies between Mean+/-3SD, 200+/- 3*20 = 140- 260

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In Sustainable Development Goal 3, the target 3.1 aims to reduce the Maternal Mortality Ratio by 2030 to ____ (per 1 lakh live births):
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. <70

In Sustainable Development Goal 3, the target 3.1 aims to reduce the Maternal Mortality Ratio by 2030 to <70 per 1 lakh live births.

There are 17 global goals and 169 targets set for 2030 as part of the official Sustainable Development Goals of the Agenda 2030.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Monetary benefit is measured in which of the following analyses?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cost benefit analysis

The monetary benefit is measured in a cost-benefit analysis.

In cost-benefit analysis, the economic benefits of any program are compared with the cost of the program. The benefits are expressed in monetary terms to determine whether a given programme is economically sound and to select the best out of several alternate programmes.

The main drawback with this technique is that the benefits in the health field, as a result of a particular programme, cannot always be expressed in monetary terms. We generally express the benefit in terms of births or deaths prevented, or illness avoided or overcome.

In cost-effective analysis, the benefit is expressed in terms of results achieved. (Eg: number of lives saved or number of days free from disease).

Input-output analysis: how much input is needed to produce a unit amount of output. In the health field, input refers to all health service activities which consume resources (manpower, money, materials, and time); and output refers to useful outcomes such as cases treated, lives saved, or inoculations performed.

Network analysis: a network is a graphic plan of all events and activities to be completed in order to reach an end objective.

Management Methods in Health Programmes:

Methods based on behavioral sciences

Quantitative methods

Organisational design

Communication

Information systems

Management by objectives (MBO)

Cost-Effective analysis

Cost–Accounting

Input–Output analysis

Model

Systems analysis

Sulfur dioxide, lead, and particulate matter

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Attributable risk

The difference between the incidence of disease among exposed and incidence among non-exposed is given by attributable risk.

Attributable risk is often expressed as a percentage.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Coefficient of variation

The variation in one data set is compared with that of another data set using the coefficient of variation (CV). It measures the relative variability by using the mean and standard deviation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following compounds is predominantly responsible for the disinfecting property of bleaching powder?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Hypochlorous acid

The disinfectant property of bleaching powder is predominantly due to the action of hypochlorous acid. It is 70-80 times more effective than hypochlorite ions.

Bleaching powder, also known as chlorinated lime (CaOCl2), has 33 per cent of chlorine in it. When chlorine is added to water, there is the formation of hydrochloric and hypochlorous acids. The hydrochloric acid is neutralized by the alkalinity of the water. The hypochlorous acid ionizes to form hydrogen ions and hypochlorite ions, as follows:

H2O + Cl2 → HCl + HOCl

HOCl → H + OCl

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of prospective screening?
options: Cervical Pap smear in a 40 year old patient
Neonatal screening of a new-born baby for hypothyroidism
Screening of immigrants to a country
Urine for sugar screening in a 40 year old man
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Screening of immigrants to a country

Screening of immigrants to a country is an example of prospective screening.

Screening of disease is done to detect unrecognized disease or defect, in apparently healthy individuals, by means of rapidly applied tests, examinations, or other procedures.

The difference between prospective and prescriptive screening is given below:

Prospective screening
Prescriptive screening

Definition
People screened for others benefit
People screened solely for their own benefit

Essential purpose
Disease control
Case detection

Request for screening
Specific request from the authority
Request from physician

Example

• Immigrants for infectious diseases like tuberculosis syphilis, yellow fever, etc;
• HIV screening during antenatal visits, sex workers.
• Screening of blood donors.

• Neonatal screening for hypothyroidism.
• Pap smear for detection of cervical cancer.
• Testing of urine sugar for diabetes mellitus.

Note: Most common neonatal disease to be screened for is neonatal hypothyroidism.
