questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is calculated with the following information?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Maternal Mortality Rate

The given expression is used for calculating the maternal mortality rate. The maternal mortality rate is expressed as the "number of maternal deaths in a given period per 100,000 women in reproductive age during the same time period".

Other options:

Option B: The maternal mortality ratio is the "number of maternal deaths during a given period per 100,000 live births during the same time".

Option C: The death rate in reproductive women is expressed as the "number of deaths among women aged 15-49 years during a given period per 1,000 women of the same age group during the same time period.

Option D: The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is expressed as the "average number of children a woman would have over her lifetime if she were to experience the current age-specific fertility rates throughout her reproductive years (typically ages 15-49).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the communication barrier if interpretation of a words are understood in a different manner?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Semantic barrier

The communication barrier that occurs when the interpretation of words is understood differently is called a semantic Barrier.

Semantic barriers arise from misunderstandings due to differences in the meaning of words, phrases, or symbols. These barriers can cause confusion and misinterpretation, leading to ineffective communication.

example: In a public health campaign, "herd immunity" may be misunderstood by some as meaning they don’t need vaccination or as related to animals. This confusion can reduce vaccination rates and is a perfect example of a semantic barrier.

other options:

Option A: Linguistic Barrier: This barrier occurs when the language or dialect used in communication is not understood by one or more parties. It can include differences in language, vocabulary, or grammar, making it difficult to convey the intended message.

Option C: Psychological Barrier: Psychological barriers involve emotions, attitudes, or mental states that affect communication. These could include stress, fear, anger, or low self-esteem, which can hinder the ability to send, receive, or interpret messages accurately.

Option D: Cultural Barrier: Cultural barriers arise when differences in cultural backgrounds, beliefs, values, or practices lead to misunderstandings. These barriers can affect how messages are interpreted and can lead to miscommunication if cultural contexts are not considered.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which among the following diseases will be the best representation of the submerged portion?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Influenza

The best representation of the submerged portion of the iceberg phenomenon would be influenza, as it often has a large number of asymptomatic or mild cases that go undetected, especially in milder seasons.

Tetanus (option A), chickenpox(option C), rabies (option D) and measles are typically acute and severe, with most cases being symptomatic and well-recognized when they occur. They do not show the iceberg phenomenon.

Iceberg phenomenon is shown by:

• Polio
• Influenza
• Rubella
• Mumps
• Japanese Encephalitis
• Diphtheria
• Hepatitis A and B
• Tuberculosis
• Diabetes
• Malnutrition
• Hypertension

Note: If a disease has more number of subclinical infections, it shows the iceberg phenomenon of disease depicted in the image below.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Which of the following are components of the physical quality of life index (PQLI)?

1. Infant mortality rate
2. Life expectancy at birth
3. Literacy rate
4. Life expectancy at 1 year of age
5. Under 5 mortality rate
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1,3 and 4

Infant mortality rate, literacy rate, and life expectancy at 1 year of age are the components of the physical quality of life index (PQLI).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following are not included in the School Health Programme under Ayushman Bharat?
options: Monthly IFA tablets for all children
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Monthly IFA tablets for all children

Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplementation is included in School Heath Programme not monthly IFA tablets for all children.

The Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) program is a school health program that provides iron and folic acid (IFA) tablets which aims to reduce the prevalence of anemia in school going children.

The school health programs are managed by the primary health center (PHC).

The School Health Committee (1961) in India recommended that the school health services should be a part of the general health services administered through PHCs. Formation of school health committees at the village, block, district, state, and national levels was recommended. The National School Health Council was created as an advisory and coordinating body.

PHCs provide the following school health services:

• Screening and general assessments for

1. Anemia/nutritional status
2. Visual acuity and hearing problems
3. Dental check-up
4. Physical disabilities
5. Learning disorders and behavior problems

• Basic medicines for common ailments
• Immunization
• Micronutrient management (vitamin A, iron, and folic acid)
• Deworming
• Mid-day meal
• Provison of sanitary napkins

Note: National Programme for Mid-Day Meal in Schools has recently been renamed Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is true about longevity dividend?
options: The intervention can delay the onset of the disease
Small amounts of damage is accumulated over time
The older you are the more prone you are to disease
Economic and health benefit for the society
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. The intervention can delay the onset of the disease

The intervention can delay the onset of the disease (Statement 1) is true about longevity dividend.

The longevity dividend is a horizontal approach to public health which is based on a broader strategy which means to foster health for all generations. This can be done by developing a new model for health promotion and disease prevention. The longevity-dividend model aims to prevent or delay the root causes of disease and disability by decimating the one major risk factor which is biological aging.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following options best defines the correct sequence of the phases of the demographic cycle?
options: High expanding→ Early stationary → Late expanding → Low stationary → Declining
High stationary → Early expanding → Late expanding → Low stationary → Declining
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. High stationary → Early expanding → Late expanding → Low stationary → Declining

The correct sequence of the phases of the demographic cycle is High stationary → Early expanding → Late expanding → Low stationary → Declining.

India is currently in the "late expanding" stage which is the third stage in the demographic cycle where declining death rates and declining birth rates are seen.

Another important concept of the demographic cycle is the demographic gap which is the difference between birth rate and death rate. The demographic gap is maximum in the early-expanding phase, characterized by a high birth rate and low death rate. As the demography of the country transitions to the late-expanding phase, both birth rate and death rate falls causing a decreasing demographic gap. Although the birth rate is falling in the late-expanding phase, it is still higher than the death rate, which causes the population to increase.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which vaccine will be placed at zone 3 in the device shown below?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. OPV

The image shown in the question is of an ice-lined refrigerator (ILR). The OPV vaccines are stored in the zone 3 that corresponds to the lowest

ILRs are the main method of vaccine storage in primary health centers. They are an important part of the cold chain and they maintain a temperature of 2 to 8 °C for the storage of vaccines.
They have different temperature zones for different vaccines. The upper zone is for freeze-sensitive vaccines like cholera, hep B, rotavirus(liquid), etc while the lower zone is for heat-sensitive vaccines like OPV, measles, etc.

All vaccines are kept in the basket provided with ILR. Vaccines like OPV, BCG, measles, and JE can be kept at the bottom of the basket while, DPT, TT, Hep B, IPV, and pentavalent vaccines and diluents are kept in the upper part of the basket.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 2-year-old child is brought with complaints of not growing well. On examination, he weighs 8.1 kg, height 80 cm (WFL score between 0 and −2 SD), has a mid-arm circumference (MUAC) of 11.5 cm and both his palms are white. There is no edema of the feet. As per IMNCI, he will be classified as:
options: No acute malnutrition and severe anemia
Moderate acute malnutrition and severe anemia
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Moderate acute malnutrition and severe anemia

• Moderate acute malnutrition (MAM): MUAC = 11.5 cm in a 2-year-old. As per IMNCI, MUAC 11.0–11.9 cm indicates moderate acute malnutrition. There is no bilateral pedal edema, and WFL is between 0 and −2 SD.
• Severe anemia: Both palms are white/pale, which is classified as severe anemia under IMNCI.

Why not other options?

• A. No acute malnutrition + anemia: Incorrect because MUAC 11.5 cm indicates MAM.
• B. No acute malnutrition + severe anemia: Incorrect because the child has MAM.
• C. MAM + anemia: Incorrect because marked/pale palms (both palms) indicate severe anemia.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 25-year-old woman is a sedentary worker. She is a lactating mother with a 3-month-old child. Which one among the following is the best approximation of her energy requirement in terms of kilocalories per day?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 2500 kcal/day

Lactation substantially increases a woman’s energy requirements to support breast milk production. According to the ICMR/NIN Recommended Dietary Allowances (RDA), a sedentary lactating woman during the first 6 months postpartum requires approximately 2500 kcal/day.

• A. 1500 kcal/day ✗: Grossly inadequate for a lactating mother.
• B. 2250 kcal/day ✗: Lower than the recommended energy requirement during early lactation.
• C. 2500 kcal/day ✓: Appropriate energy requirement for a sedentary woman with a 3-month-old infant.
• D. 2830 kcal/day ✗: Higher than the recommended intake for a sedentary lactating woman.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A diabetic patient's fasting blood glucose level is found to be 160 mg/dL. What will you advise the patient regarding non-pharmacological management?
options: < 30% of the calories should come from fat
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. < 30% of the calories should come from fat

Solution - Standard Dietary Recommendations

| Component | Recommendation

| --------- | --------------

| Carbohydrates | 50–60% of calories

| Fat | < 30% of calories

| Protein | 15–20%

| Fiber | 25–40 g/day

| Salt | < 5 g/day

PRUDENT DIET– WHO Expert Committee

• Reduce total fat intake to 20–30% of total energy intake
• Limit saturated fat to <10% (ideal:<7%) of total energy intake
• Reduce dietary cholesterol to <100 mg per 1000 kcal/day
• Cholesterol: HDL ratio <3.5
• Increase complex carbohydrates
• Avoid alcohol consumption

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A lot of patients presented to PHC OPD with edema, ocular problems, cardiac failure. Several deaths were reported too. There was a common history of buying oil from a local grocery store. Drug inspector will use the following test to detect adulteration.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Paper chromatography test

The clinical picture suggests epidemic dropsy, caused by adulteration of edible oil with argemone oil.

Detection of argemone oil adulteration is best done using paper chromatography, which separates and identifies toxic alkaloids such as sanguinarine.

Sanguinarine causes:

• Capillary dilation
• Increased vascular permeability
• Edema and organ damage

Simple chemical tests like nitric acid or sulphuric acid are screening methods, but chromatography provides confirmatory evidence for regulatory action.

A) Nitrate test

❌ Used to detect nitrate contamination, not argemone oil.

B) Phosphatase test

❌ Used in milk pasteurization testing, not oil adulteration.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A particular community population has been consuming Maize as a staple diet for years. The vitamin deficiency most likely to be seen in this population is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Niacin

A maize-based staple diet is classically associated with niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency, leading to pellagra.

Maize is deficient in tryptophan and contains niacin in a bound, poorly absorbable form, especially when not processed by alkali treatment.

This results in the characteristic triad of dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia, making niacin deficiency the most likely outcome.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A person has been consuming contaminated bajra (pearl millet) for a prolonged period. Which of the following toxins is responsible for the resulting food adulteration–related disease?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Ergot toxin

Consumption of bajra (pearl millet) contaminated with Claviceps species leads to ergotism, caused by ergot alkaloids. Ergotism has historically been called “St. Anthony’s fire.”

Sources-

| Grain | Risk

| ----- | ----

| Rye | Most common

| Wheat | Possible

| Bajra (pearl millet) | Known contamination source

| Barley | Occasional

Ergot toxins produce vasoconstriction and neurotoxic effects, resulting in manifestations such as gangrene, convulsions, and paresthesia.

Other toxins like BOAA (lathyrism), sanguinarine (epidemic dropsy), and Fusarium toxins are linked to different staple foods and clinical syndromes.

| Food / Adulterant | Toxin | Disease

| ----------------- | ----- | -------

| Bajra / contaminated cereals | Ergot toxin | Ergotism

| Kesari dal | BOAA | Lathyrism

| Mustard oil | Sanguinarine | Epidemic dropsy

| Fungal cereals | Aflatoxin | Hepatotoxicity

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A poor farmer with a history of successive crop failure develops progressive spastic paraparesis, signs of upper motor neuron paralysis, and gait instability. Name the toxin responsible for this condition.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Beta-oxalyl-amino-alanine

The clinical picture describes neurolathyrism, a chronic neurological disorder seen in populations consuming Lathyrus sativus (khesari dal) during periods of famine or crop failure.

The causative neurotoxin is β-oxalyl-amino-alanine (BOAA), which leads to upper motor neuron damage and progressive spastic paraparesis.

BOAA acts as a neurotoxic excitatory amino acid.

Effects:

• Degeneration of upper motor neurons
• Damage to corticospinal tract
• Progressive spastic paralysis of lower limbs

Importantly:

• Sensory system remains normal
• Bladder control usually preserved

This condition is classically associated with poverty, drought, and dietary dependence on a single pulse, distinguishing it from mycotoxin-related illnesses.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to the Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) Guidelines, how much additional cereal-based food should be introduced to a 7-month-old breastfed infant at the initiation of complementary feeding?
options: ½ to full Katori 3 times a day
½ to full Katori 4 times a day
½ to full Katori 5 times a day
½ to full Katori 6 times a day
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. ½ to full Katori 3 times a day

As per IYCF guidelines, complementary feeding is initiated at 6 months while continuing breastfeeding. Complementary feeding is necessary because breast milk alone cannot meet the growing nutritional requirements after 6 months.

If complementary foods are delayed:

• Growth faltering
• Iron deficiency anemia
• Increased infection risk

may occur.

For a 7-month-old breastfed infant, the recommended quantity is ½ to 1 katori of cereal-based food given 3 times a day, along with breast milk.

Complementary foods should be:

The emphasis at this age is on meal frequency, energy density, and gradual increase in consistency, rather than large volumes, to ensure adequate nutrition and tolerance.

B. ½ to full Katori 4 times a dayFeeding frequency increases after 9 months, not at 6–8 months.

Complementary Feeding Frequency by Age

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An adult is weighing 80 kg and having a height of 1.6 metres. Under which category does the individual fall as per the WHO classification of BMI?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Obese class I

BMI is calculated as:

• BMI = Weight (kg) / Height² (m²) = 80 / (1.6)² = 80 / 2.56 = 31.25 kg/m²

According to the WHO classification:

• <18.5 → Underweight
• 18.5–24.9 → Normal
• 25.0–29.9 → Pre-obese
• 30.0–34.9 → Obese class I
• 35.0–39.9 → Obese class II
• ≥40 → Obese class III

Therefore, BMI = 31.25 kg/m² → Obese class I.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following with regard to Amino Acids: I. Essential amino acids are those that the body cannot synthesize and they must be obtained from dietary proteins. II. Not just the essential amino acids, non-essential amino acids are also needed by the body for synthesis of tissue proteins. III. Unless a protein contains all the essential amino acids in amounts corresponding to human needs, a protein is said to be biologically incomplete. IV. Animal proteins are rated superior to vegetable proteins. Of the above statements, how many are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. All four

Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins. They are classified into essential and non-essential amino acids based on the body’s ability to synthesize them. The biological value (BV) of a protein depends on its content of essential amino acids and their proportion relative to human requirements.

• Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized by the body and must be obtained from the diet.
• Non-essential amino acids can be synthesized by the body but are also required for protein synthesis and normal growth.
• A protein lacking one or more essential amino acids in adequate amounts is called a biologically incomplete protein.
• Animal proteins (milk, egg, meat, fish) are complete proteins with high biological value, whereas most vegetable proteins are incomplete.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Dietary fibres have:
options: Sometimes anabolic and sometimes catabolic effect, depending on the type
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. No metabolic effect

Dietary fiber (roughage) consists of non-digestible plant carbohydrates such as cellulose, hemicellulose, pectin, lignin, gums, and mucilage. Since humans lack the enzymes to digest fiber, it does not provide energy or participate directly in anabolic or catabolic metabolism. Therefore, it has no direct metabolic effect.

• Dietary fiber has no direct metabolic effect because it is not digested or absorbed. ⭐
• Soluble fiber (pectin, gums, mucilage):

• Lowers serum cholesterol
• Slows glucose absorption
• Improves glycemic control

• Insoluble fiber (cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin):

• Increases stool bulk
• Prevents constipation
• Reduces colonic transit time

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Egg proteins are considered to be the best among food proteins because: I. Of their biological value II. Of their digestibility III. They contain all the essential amino acids IV. Their calorie content is higher than proteins of vegetable sources Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. I, II and III

Egg protein is considered the reference (gold standard) protein because it has a high biological value, is highly digestible, and contains all the essential amino acids in optimal proportions required for human growth and tissue repair.

Why is B correct?

• I. High biological value ✅

• Egg protein has the highest biological value (\~100) among natural food proteins.

• II. High digestibility ✅

• Nearly 97–98% of egg protein is digested and absorbed.

• III. Contains all essential amino acids ✅

• Egg is a complete protein, providing all essential amino acids in adequate amounts.

• IV. Their calorie content is higher than proteins of vegetable sources ❌

• Calories depend on the amount of protein and fat, not on the protein source. Both animal and vegetable proteins provide 4 kcal/g.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a village, it is observed that several farmers have crossed gait and use a stick for support to stand up and walk. Due to poor yield from farms, they consume meals containing rice and pulses only. Supplementing their diet with which of the following vitamins could have prevented this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Vitamin C

The clinical picture describes lathyrism, seen in famine-affected villages where people consume Kesari dal (Lathyrus sativus) along with rice. The neurotoxin β-ODAP causes spastic paraparesis with scissoring (crossed) gait, forcing patients to use a stick for walking. Vitamin C supplementation reduces the neurotoxicity of the toxin and helps prevent lathyrism.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the case of a 7-year-old school-going child, which would be the most appropriate indicator to measure the current nutritional status?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Weight for height

In school-aged children (5–19 years), weight-for-height is the most appropriate indicator for assessing current nutritional status, as it reflects acute malnutrition (wasting) and is independent of age. Indicators such as birth weight, head circumference, and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) have limited utility in a 7-year-old child.

High-Yield Pearls

• Weight-for-height: Best indicator of current nutritional status (wasting/acute malnutrition).
• Height-for-age: Indicates chronic malnutrition (stunting).
• Weight-for-age: Reflects underweight but cannot differentiate between acute and chronic malnutrition.
• Birth weight: Assesses intrauterine growth, not current nutritional status.
• Head circumference: Useful only up to 2 years of age for monitoring brain growth.
• MUAC: Primarily used to screen acute malnutrition in children 6–59 months, not school-aged children.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Mustard oil adulteration is most commonly associated with the addition of which of the following oils?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Argemone oil

Mustard oil adulteration with Argemone oil is a classic cause of epidemic dropsy, a toxic condition caused by the alkaloids sanguinarine and dihydrosanguinarine present in Argemone mexicana seeds.

• Agreement oil closely resembles mustard oil in color and appearance, making it a common adulterant.
• Consumption causes epidemic dropsy, characterized by:

• Bilateral pitting edema of the legs
• Diarrhea
• Breathlessness
• Cardiac failure
• Glaucoma (may occur)
• Skin erythema and tenderness

Why not the other options?

• B. Castor oil: Used medicinally as a laxative; not the classic adulterant of mustard oil.
• C. Linseed oil: Used industrially and in paints; not associated with epidemic dropsy.
• D. Cottonseed oil: May be used as an edible oil but is not the classic adulterant responsible for epidemic dropsy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Observe the image below showing different food items. Identify the source of Thiamine.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. B

Thiamine (Vitamin B1) is abundantly present in whole grains and cereals, especially rice, particularly unpolished or parboiled rice.

It plays a key role in carbohydrate metabolism and nerve function, and deficiency leads to beriberi. Populations consuming predominantly polished rice are at higher risk of thiamine deficiency due to loss during milling. Rice contains thiamine mainly in the outer aleurone layer and germ.

Clinical Manifestations of Thiamine Deficiency-

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The “DASH diet” is a lifestyle modification for management of which of these conditions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hypertension

DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) is a dietary pattern specifically designed to prevent and treat hypertension. It has been shown to significantly reduce blood pressure and also lowers the risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, and chronic kidney disease.

• A. Cancer ✗: Although a healthy diet may reduce cancer risk, the DASH diet was not specifically developed for cancer management.
• B. Diabetes ✗: DASH can improve metabolic health, but its primary indication is hypertension.
• C. Anaemia ✗: DASH is not designed for the treatment of anemia.
• D. Hypertension ✓: DASH is the recommended dietary intervention for patients with hypertension and prehypertension.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The addition of Vitamin A to butter is an example of which of the following public health interventions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Food fortification

Food fortification is the deliberate addition of essential micronutrients to commonly consumed foods to prevent or correct nutrient deficiencies in the population. Addition of vitamin A to butter is an example of food fortification.

Why not the other options?

• A. Food adulteration: Addition of inferior or harmful substances to food, reducing its quality or safety.
• C. Food enrichment: Restoration of nutrients lost during food processing to their original levels (e.g., adding B vitamins to refined flour).
• D. Food addition: Not a recognized public health nutrition intervention.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The amount of iron lost per 28-day cycle in menstruating women is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 12.5 mg

Menstruating women lose approximately 12.5 mg of iron during each normal 28-day menstrual cycle, corresponding to an average menstrual blood loss of 30–40 mL. This increased iron loss explains the higher daily iron requirement in women of reproductive age compared to men.

• A. 5.5 mg ✗: Lower than the average iron loss during a normal menstrual cycle.
• B. 8.5 mg ✗: Incorrect; underestimates menstrual iron loss.
• C. 12.5 mg ✓: Average iron loss in a 28-day menstrual cycle.
• D. 15.5 mg ✗: Higher than the average; may occur in women with menorrhagia but is not the normal value.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The average daily dietary nutrient intake level sufficient to meet the nutrient requirements of nearly all (97-98%) healthy individuals in a particular life stage and gender group is known as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Recommended dietary allowance

The Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) is defined as the average daily intake level sufficient to meet the nutrient requirements of nearly all (97–98%) healthy individuals in a specific age and sex group.

It is derived from the Estimated Average Requirement (EAR) and includes a safety margin to cover individual variability.

RDA=EAR+2SD

In contrast, Adequate Intake is used when RDA cannot be determined, and dietary goals are population-level recommendations rather than individual requirements.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The most sensitive indicator of environmental iodine deficiency is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Urinary iodine excretion

Urinary iodine excretion (UIE) is the most sensitive indicator of current environmental iodine deficiency because more than 90% of ingested iodine is excreted in urine. It reflects recent iodine intake and is the preferred method for assessing the iodine status of a population.

• A. Prevalence of goitre ✗

• Goitre reflects long-term iodine deficiency and changes slowly after iodine supplementation.
• It is not a sensitive indicator of current iodine status.

• B. Prevalence of neonatal hypothyroidism ✗

• Used as an indicator of severe iodine deficiency, but is less sensitive than UIE for population surveillance.

• C. Prevalence of cretinism ✗

• Indicates very severe, longstanding iodine deficiency.
• It is a late manifestation and unsuitable for monitoring current iodine status.

• D. Urinary iodine excretion ✓

• Most sensitive and preferred indicator of environmental iodine deficiency in a community.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Under the ICDS program in India, what is the calorie and protein supplementation provided to a child aged 6-72 months?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 500 kcal, 12-15 grams

Under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, children aged 6–72 months receive supplementary nutrition providing 500 kcal and 12–15 g of protein per day for approximately 300 days per year to bridge the gap between dietary intake and nutritional requirements, thereby preventing protein-energy malnutrition.

Why not the other options?

• A. 200 kcal, 6–8 g: Inadequate for the ICDS recommendation for children aged 6–72 months.
• B. 300 kcal, 8–10 g: Lower than the recommended supplementary nutrition under ICDS.
• D. 600 kcal, 18–20 g: Exceeds the routine supplementation provided to normal children under ICDS.

The supplementation values for each group under ICDS Program:

| Beneficiary | Calories | Protein

| ----------- | -------- | -------

| Child 6–72 months (normal) | 500 kcal | 12–15 grams

| Malnourished children | 800 kcal | 20–25 grams

| Pregnant and lactating mother | 600 kcal | 18–20 grams

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the reference weight for an Indian woman (kg)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 55

Indian Reference male (man)

| Category | Description

| -------- | -----------

| Age and Weight | An Indian Reference man is between 19 and 39 years of age and weighs 65 kg

| Health Status | He is free from disease and physically fit for active work

| Work Activity | On each working day he is employed for 8 hours in an occupation that usually involves moderate activity

| Non-Work Activity |

| - Hours in bed | 8 hours

| - Sitting and moving around | 4-6 hours

| - Walking and active recreation/household duties | 2 hours

Indian Reference Female (Woman)

| Category | Description

| -------- | -----------

| Age and Weight | An Indian Reference woman is between 19 and 39 years of age and weighs 55 kg

| Health Status | She is free from disease and physically fit for active work

| Work Activity | On each day she may be engaged for 8 hours in general household work, in light industry, or other moderately active work

| Non-Work Activity |

| - Hours in bed | 8 hours

| - Sitting and moving around | 4-6 hours

| - Walking and active recreation | 2 hours

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which agency offers seeds and manure as part of applied nutrition programs in schools?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. UNICEF

The Applied Nutrition Programme (ANP) was initiated to improve the nutritional status of communities, especially school children, by promoting local food production and nutrition education.

The program was supported by UNICEF.

UNICEF supports applied nutrition programmes, including school nutrition initiatives that promote kitchen gardens by providing seeds and manure. School children were encouraged to grow vegetables in school gardens, improving availability of nutritious foods.

These programs aim to improve child nutrition, micronutrient intake, and food security through practical, school-based interventions.

Other agencies like WHO, UNDP, and CARE focus on broader health policy, development, or emergency nutrition rather than school garden support.

| Option | Role

| ------ | ----

| CARE | Known for food aid programs but not primary supporter of ANP seeds/manure

| UNDP | Focuses on economic development

| UNICEF | ✔ Supported applied nutrition programs and school gardens

| WHO | Focuses on health policy and disease control

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following amino acids, which is categorized as a nonessential amino acid?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Proline

Amino acids are classified as essential and nonessential based on whether they can be synthesized by the human body.

• Essential amino acids must be obtained from the diet.
• Nonessential amino acids can be synthesized in sufficient amounts by the body.

Proline is a nonessential amino acid because it is synthesized from glutamate in the body. It is important for collagen synthesis and wound healing.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Leucine: Essential, branched-chain amino acid (BCAA).
• B. Threonine: Essential amino acid.
• C. Tryptophan: Essential amino acid; precursor of serotonin, melatonin, and niacin (vitamin B3).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a criterion for defining severe acute malnutrition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Low Height for age

Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) is diagnosed using indicators of acute nutritional deficiency, namely weight-for-height Z score < −3 SD, MUAC <11.5 cm (in children 6–59 months), or bilateral pitting pedal edema.

It reflects severe wasting and acute nutritional deficiency. The diagnostic criteria are defined by the World Health Organization and used in programs like India’s Integrated Child Development Services and POSHAN Abhiyaan.

Low height-for-age indicates stunting, which reflects chronic malnutrition (stunting) rather than acute malnutrition and therefore is not included in SAM criteria.

Types of PEM-

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one among the following essential amino acids is usually the “limiting” amino acid in most of the pulses?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Methionine

Pulses (legumes) are an excellent source of plant protein and are rich in lysine, but they are relatively deficient in the sulfur-containing essential amino acid methionine, making it the limiting amino acid. This is why combining pulses with cereals provides a balanced amino acid profile and improves the overall biological value of dietary protein.

• Limiting amino acid in pulses: Methionine ⭐
• Limiting amino acid in cereals: Lysine ⭐
• Pulse + cereal combination (e.g., dal + rice, khichdi, idli, dosa) provides mutual protein supplementation, resulting in a high-quality protein. ⭐
• Pulses are rich in:

• Lysine
• Leucine
• Isoleucine

• Pulses are poor in:

• Methionine
• Cysteine

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following is the major contributor to the total energy intake, in terms of energy provided, in an average Indian diet?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Carbohydrates

Carbohydrates are the major source of energy in the average Indian diet, contributing approximately 60–70% of the total daily energy intake. They are the body’s preferred and most economical source of energy, providing 4 kcal/g.

High-Yield Pearls

• Carbohydrates provide 4 kcal/g and contribute 60–70% of total energy in a balanced Indian diet.
• Proteins provide 4 kcal/g and contribute about 10–15% of total energy.
• Fats provide 9 kcal/g and contribute about 20–30% of total energy.
• Vitamins do not provide energy; they function as regulators of metabolic processes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 10-week-old infant was taken to a primary health centre by his/her mother for vaccination. The infant has taken all the doses as per the recommended schedule of immunization at 6 weeks. The infant was prescribed pentavalent and rotavirus vaccine. After 3 days of getting the vaccine, the mother reported to the PHC that the infant has suffered an episode of epilepsy. On enquiring, it was found that the infant had a history of two epileptic episodes in the week prior to immunization, i.e. the 9th week. Considering the scenario, which one of the following statements is correct regarding this adverse event following immunization (AEFI)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. It is a coincidental event.

An AEFI (Adverse Event Following Immunization) is any untoward medical event occurring after vaccination, but it does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the vaccine.

In this case:

• The infant developed an epileptic episode 3 days after vaccination.
• However, the infant had already experienced two epileptic episodes during the week before vaccination.
• Therefore, the epilepsy was likely an underlying condition occurring independently of vaccination.

Hence, this is a coincidental AEFI.

Why not the others?

• A. Vaccine product-related: Would be caused by the intrinsic properties of the vaccine.
• B. Immunization error-related: Results from errors in vaccine handling, preparation, storage, or administration.
• C. Immunization stress-related: Related to anxiety/stress surrounding vaccination, such as syncope or hyperventilation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 2-month-old infant presents with persistent inconsolable crying lasting for 3 hours shortly after routine immunization. Which vaccine component is most commonly associated with this adverse effect?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Pertussis

Persistent inconsolable crying lasting ≥3 hours within 48 hours after immunization is a recognized adverse event most commonly associated with the whole-cell pertussis (wP) vaccine component of the DTwP vaccine.

This reaction is thought to result from the vaccine’s higher reactogenicity and is self-limiting. Although distressing, it is not associated with permanent neurological damage.

Other adverse effects of whole-cell pertussis vaccine:

• Fever
• Local pain, redness, and swelling
• Persistent inconsolable crying (≥3 hours)
• Hypotonic-hyporesponsive episode (HHE)
• Febrile seizures (rare)
• Encephalopathy (very rare)

Acellular pertussis (DTaP) vaccines are less reactogenic and are associated with fewer local and systemic adverse effects.

Why not the other options?

• A. Hepatitis B: Usually causes only mild local pain or low-grade fever.
• B. Inactivated polio vaccine (IPV): Generally well tolerated; significant crying is uncommon.
• D. Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib): Usually causes mild local reactions and occasional fever.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 2-year-old child has presented for vaccination, who has never been vaccinated earlier. As per the Universal Immunization Program, which among the following vaccines will be administered to the child on the first visit? 1. BCG vaccine 2. DPT-1 vaccine 3. Hepatitis B vaccine 4. Measles vaccine Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2 and 4 only

For a 2-year-old child who has never been vaccinated, the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) catch-up schedule recommends starting with:

• DPT-1 ✔️
• Measles/MR vaccine ✔️ (older questions may mention Measles vaccine)

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. BCG vaccine❌: Not given routinely after 1 year of age under UIP.
• 2. DPT-1 vaccine✔️: Start the primary DPT series.
• 3. Hepatitis B vaccine❌: Not included as a standalone vaccine in the UIP catch-up schedule for an unvaccinated 2-year-old in this exam context.
• 4. Measles vaccine✔️: Measles/MR vaccine should be administered.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 4-year-old unimmunized HIV-positive child on antiretroviral therapy for the last 2 years and weighing 15 kg is brought for vaccination. His records reveal a recent CD4 count of 750/mm³, with no evidence of any opportunistic infections in the past. Which of the following statements are applicable to this child? 1. Recombinant Hepatitis B vaccine can be safely administered. 2. MMR vaccine is always contraindicated. 3. BCG may be administered if chest radiograph is normal. 4. IPV is preferred over OPV. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1 and 4

1. Recombinant Hepatitis B vaccine: Correct

• Hepatitis B vaccine is a recombinant, non-live vaccine and can be safely administered to HIV-positive children.
• HIV-positive children should receive appropriate routine inactivated/recombinant vaccines.

2. MMR vaccine is always contraindicated: Incorrect

• MMR is a live attenuated vaccine, but it is not universally contraindicated in HIV.
• It can be given when the child is not severely immunocompromised. A good CD4 count supports its use.

3. BCG may be administered if chest radiograph is normal: Incorrect for the exam

• BCG is a live vaccine and is generally avoided in known HIV infection because of the risk of disseminated BCG disease.
• A normal chest X-ray does not establish adequate immune status for BCG administration.

4. IPV is preferred over OPV: Correct

• IPV is preferred in HIV-positive children because it is an inactivated vaccine and does not carry the risk associated with live OPV in an immunocompromised host.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 5-year-old girl has a greyish white membrane over tonsils and presented with bull-neck appearance. She has a 2-year-old brother who is fully immunized for his age. What should be given to the brother?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Penicillin

The clinical picture is suggestive of diphtheria in the index case. Standard Recommendations for Contacts

• Antibiotics:

• Penicillin (IM or oral) OR
• Erythromycin (alternative)

• Immunization:
• <3doses in contact: Complete the series
• >3 doses: Last received>5yrs- Give DPT booster; <5yrs: No additional vaccine

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A boys' hostel has an outbreak of fever cases with headache, followed by the development of pleomorphic rashes sparing palms and soles. What is the next best step in the management of suspected cases?
options: Isolate for 6 days after giving acyclovir, followed by VZIG within 72 hours of exposure
Isolate for 12 days after giving acyclovir, followed by VZIG within 48 hours of exposure
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Isolate for 6 days

The presentation of fever followed by pleomorphic rash sparing palms and soles in a closed setting like a hostel is suggestive of varicella (chickenpox).

The immediate management of suspected cases is isolation for 6 days after the appearance of rash (or until all lesions have crusted) to prevent transmission.

VZIG is not indicated for routine contacts and is reserved for high-risk susceptible individuals (e.g., immunocompromised, pregnant women) after confirmed exposure.

A. Acyclovir + VZIG + isolation- Not routine outbreak management.

B. Isolation for 12 days- Isolation usually \~6 days after rash onset until crusting.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A diagnostic test has a sensitivity of 80% and a specificity of 90%. If the prevalence of the disease is 1% in a population of 10,000, what is the positive predictive value?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 7.5%

PPV is the probability that a person with a positive test truly has the disease.

Population = 10,000

Disease prevalence = 1% = 100 diseased, 9,900 non-diseased

• True positives (TP) = 80% of 100 = 80
• False positives (FP) = 10% of 9,900 = 990

PPV = TP / (TP + FP)

= 80 / (80 + 990)

= 80 / 1070

= 7.5%

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A mother brought her 6-month-old infant baby to an Anganwadi worker Lata for advice regarding the vaccination of her child. The last vaccines he had received were OP V3, PENTA 3, TIP V2, and ROTA3 at 14 weeks of age. BCG and Hep B were given at birth. When is the next vaccination due?
options: MR vaccine at left arm intramuscularly and Vitamin A drops at the end of 9 months
MR vaccine at right arm subcutaneously and Vitamin A drops at the end of 8 months
MR vaccine at left arm intramuscularly and Vitamin A drops at the end of 8 months
MR vaccine at right arm subcutaneously and Vitamin A drops at the end of 9 months
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. MR vaccine at right arm subcutaneously and Vitamin A drops at the end of 9 months

What is due at 9 months-

• MR (Measles-Rubella) vaccine

o    Route: Subcutaneous

o    Site: Right upper arm

• Vitamin A

o    Dose: 1st dose (1 lakh IU) given orally

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A new test was developed for detection of COVID-19. What is the sensitivity of the test as per the information provided above?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 37.5%

Sensitivity is the ability of a diagnostic test to correctly identify individuals who truly have the disease (true positives). It answers the question:

“Among those who have the disease, how many test positive?”

Formula:

• Sensitivity = TP / (TP + FN) × 100

Where:

• TP (True Positive) = 60
• FN (False Negative) = 100

Calculation:

Sensitivity = 60 / (60 + 100) × 100

= 60 / 160 × 100

= 37.5%

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A person is relocating from Nigeria to the USA. While traveling from Nigeria to the USA, which of the following health certificates is required for entry?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 17-D Yellow fever vaccination certificate

Nigeria is a yellow fever endemic country, and international travel from such regions requires proof of vaccination.

The 17-D Yellow Fever vaccination certificate is mandated under International Health Regulations (IHR) for entry into several countries, including the USA.

Other vaccines like BCG, JE, or COVID are not universally required for international entry.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A population of 1000 people has 100 suffering from an early stage of disease. A new test correctly detects 90 of those with disease while identifying 50 additional subjects as false positives. What is the positive predictive value (PPV) of the test?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 64.50%

Positive Predictive Value (PPV) is the probability that a person with a positive test result truly has the disease.

Formula: PPV = TP / (TP + FP) × 100

In this question:

• True positives (TP) = 90
• False positives (FP) = 50

PPV = 90 / (90 + 50) × 100 = 90/140 × 100 = 64.3% ≈ 64.5%

• PPV answers: “If the test is positive, what is the probability that the person actually has the disease?”
• PPV increases with higher disease prevalence.
• PPV decreases as false positives increase.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A primary health centre provides nutritional counselling and treatment to 100 diabetic patients. To assess the effectiveness, the medical officer compares patients’ weights before and after the intervention. Which statistical test is most appropriate for this analysis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Paired t-test

The same 100 diabetic patients are assessed before and after the intervention, producing paired (dependent) continuous data. Data in paired tests are continuous variables.

The paired t-test evaluates whether the mean difference between two related measurements is statistically significant. It tests whether the intervention caused a significant change.

The paired t-test is used to compare the means of two related samples, making it the most appropriate test here.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A research study is designed to compare hemoglobin levels between two independent population groups. Which of the following statistical tests is most appropriate to determine whether the difference in mean hemoglobin levels between the two groups is statistically significant?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Unpaired t-test

When comparing the mean of a continuous variable (hemoglobin level) between two independent groups, the appropriate statistical test is the unpaired (independent samples) t-test.

Since the outcome variable is continuous, we use tests that compare means.

Concept of the Unpaired t-test

The unpaired t-test is used when:

• Comparing means of two independent groups
• Data is continuous
• Data follows approximately normal distribution

It evaluates whether the difference between the two-sample means is greater than expected by chance.

This test assesses whether the observed difference in means is likely due to chance, assuming approximate normal distribution and equal variances.

A. ANOVA test- used when comparing means of three or more groups Example: Comparing hemoglobin among three age groups.

B. Paired t-test- Used when two measurements come from the same subjects.

D. Chi-square test- Used for categorical data, not continuous data.

A paired t-test is used for related samples, ANOVA for more than two groups, and Chi-square for categorical data.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher has obtained the country-level data on the average Body Mass Index (BMI) and the average sugar intake for 100 countries. Which among the following will be best suited to present the relationship between BMI and sugar intake in the 100 countries?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Scatter diagram

A scatter diagram (scatter plot) is the best graphical method to study the relationship (correlation) between two quantitative (continuous) variables. Each observation is represented by a point on the graph, allowing visualization of the direction and strength of association.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Bar chart:

• Used to compare categorical data or frequencies between groups.
• Not suitable for showing the relationship between two continuous variables.

• B. Pie diagram:

• Used to display parts of a whole (proportions or percentages).
• Cannot demonstrate correlation.

• C. Frequency polygon:

• Used to display the distribution of a single continuous variable.
• Does not show the relationship between two variables.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was done on asthma and pollution. P value was found to be 0.03. What do you infer from this?
options: 3% probability that the result occurred due to chance alone
There is 95% confidence that the null hypothesis is true
The observed difference is not statistically significant
Null hypothesis is rejected at the probability of effect is less than 0.03
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 3% probability that the result occurred due to chance alone

A p-value of 0.03 means that there is a 3% probability of noting the result “by chance only”.

Since p < 0.05, the result is statistically significant, and the null hypothesis is rejected at the 5% significance level.

It does not indicate the probability that the null hypothesis is true, nor does it measure the size or importance of the effect.

⭐ p-value ≠ probability that hypothesis is true

⭐ p < 0.05 → statistically significant

⭐ p-value depends on sample size

Large samples may show significant results even for small effects.

⭐ Statistical significance ≠ clinical significance.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was undertaken to estimate the effect of a drug ‘D’ in three different groups – Plants, Animals, and Human beings. Samples were chosen randomly out of the three groups individually. This is a type of?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Stratified random sampling

Stratified random sampling involves dividing the population into distinct subgroups (strata) based on a specific characteristic and then selecting samples randomly from each stratum.

Here, plants, animals, and humans form separate strata, and random samples are taken independently from each group.

This method ensures adequate representation of all subgroups and improves the precision of comparisons across strata.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was undertaken to evaluate the association between the consumption of vegetarian/non-vegetarian food with certain diseases. The incidence of disease was evaluated in those two groups. Which statistical test should be applied to test significance?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Chi-square test

In the question there are two categorical variables:

Since both variables are qualitative, we use a test of association between proportions.

That test is the Chi-square test.

The variables studied are categorical—dietary habit (vegetarian/non-vegetarian) and presence or absence of disease.

The Chi-square test is used to assess the association between two categorical variables by comparing observed and expected frequencies.

t-tests are meant for comparison of means of continuous data, while Wilcoxon is a non-parametric alternative for paired or ranked data, making them inappropriate here.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was undertaken to evaluate the effect of Dietary modification on Serum cholesterol. A group of 100 people were chosen. Their mean cholesterol levels were measured before and after dietary modification. Which statistical test should be applied to test significance?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Paired student’s t-test

The variable measured is serum cholesterol, which is:

• Continuous data
• Expressed numerically (mg/dL)

Continuous data → usually analyzed using tests comparing means.

The study compares mean serum cholesterol levels measured before and after intervention in the same group of individuals, producing paired continuous data.

A paired Student’s t-test is appropriate to assess whether the mean difference before and after dietary modification is statistically significant. Chi-square and McNemar tests are used for categorical data, while odds ratio measures association rather than testing mean differences.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A surgical department of a premier medical college conducted a study on rates of post-operative wound infection. The results of the study were negative for the proposed hypothesis. What should the department do with the results?
options: Redo the study with a new hypothesis
Redesign the study and increase the sample size
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Report the negative results

Negative study results (i.e., failure to support the proposed hypothesis) are scientifically valuable and should always be reported and published. Reporting negative findings helps prevent publication bias, avoids unnecessary duplication of research, contributes to systematic reviews and meta-analyses, Promote transparency and research integrity and promotes evidence-based medicine.

A negative result does not mean the study has failed; it simply indicates that the hypothesis was not supported under the study conditions.

Why not the other options?

• A. Label them as worthless: Negative findings are valuable scientific evidence and should never be discarded.
• B. Redo the study with a new hypothesis: A new study may be justified later, but the current findings should still be reported.
• D. Redesign the study and increase the sample size: This may be considered if the study was underpowered, but it does not replace reporting the original results.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Administration of immunoglobulins interferes with the response to live vaccines, except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Oral typhoid vaccine

Immunoglobulin administration can interfere with the immune response to certain live attenuated vaccines, particularly measles- and rubella-containing vaccines, because passively transferred antibodies can neutralize the vaccine virus.

• A. Measles vaccine: Interference occurs
• B. Rubella vaccine: Interference occurs
• C. Oral typhoid vaccine: Correct; response is not significantly affected by immunoglobulin
• D. Mumps vaccine: Interference can occur because it is a live viral vaccine

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All are true about Rotaviral vaccine except:
options: Not given after 8 months of age
Given as monovalent and pentavalent vaccine
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Subunit vaccine

| Feature | Rotavac | Rotasil

| ------- | ------- | -------

| Type | Liquid vaccine (live attenuated) | Freeze-dried (lyophilized) vaccine (live attenuated)

| Valency | Monovalent (targets serotype GP9(11)) | Pentavalent (covers GP 1, 2, 3, 4, and 9)

| Dosage | 2.5 ml orally | 2.5 ml orally

| Administration Tool | 6 ml syringe without needle | 6 ml syringe without needle

| Dose Schedule | Two-dose schedule | Three-dose schedule

| Vaccine Vial Monitor | Number 30 | Number 30

• In India's Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), the rotavirus vaccine (RVV) is administered in a 3-dose series at 6, 10, and 14 weeks.
• Maximum Age for First Dose: 14 weeks and 6 days (15 weeks is the cutoff).
• Maximum Age for Last (3rd) Dose: 8 months (some brands recommend up to 1 year, but 8 months is standard for safety).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following are examples of passive immunity except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Toxoid

Passive immunity involves the transfer of preformed antibodies, providing immediate but temporary protection.

IgA (via breast milk), antitoxins, and monoclonal antibodies are all forms of passive immunization.

Antitoxin- Passive immunity.

Antitoxins contain preformed antibodies that neutralize toxins.

(Example: Tetanus antitoxin)

A toxoid stimulates the body to produce its own antibodies, which is active immunity, not passive.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following are types of polysaccharide vaccines except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Hepatitis B

Polysaccharide vaccines are vaccines made from the capsular polysaccharides of bacteria. These polysaccharides act as antigens, stimulating an immune response.

Hepatitis B is a recombinant subunit vaccine, not a polysaccharide vaccine. Polysaccharide vaccines include those for pneumococcus, meningococcus, and Haemophilus influenzae type B.

A. Haemophilus influenzae type B- Polysaccharide-based vaccine.

Originally developed as a capsular polysaccharide vaccine, later improved into conjugate Hib vaccine for better immunity in children.

B. Pneumococcal vaccine- Polysaccharide vaccine.

Example: PPSV23 (pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine). Protects against multiple serotypes of pneumococcus.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following vaccines may be administered to individuals aged 65 years and above, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Human papilloma virus vaccine

The HPV vaccine is primarily indicated for adolescents and young adults, as it is most effective before exposure to HPV, with recommended upper age limits well below 65 years.

In contrast, pneumococcal, Td, and varicella zoster vaccines are commonly recommended or beneficial in older adults, especially to reduce morbidity from age-related infections.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following variables are measured on nominal scale, except?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Severity of disease

A nominal scale classifies data into distinct categories without any inherent order, such as gender or vaccine status.

| Scale | Characteristics | Example

| ----- | --------------- | -------

| Nominal | Categories without order | Gender, blood group

| Ordinal | Categories with order | Disease severity

| Interval | Numeric scale with equal intervals | Temperature (°C)

| Ratio | Numeric with true zero | Height, weight

Pain (present/absent) can also be treated as nominal when not graded.

Severity of disease implies an ordered progression (mild, moderate, severe), which places it on an ordinal scale, not nominal.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following viral vaccines are types of Live vaccines except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Hepatitis B vaccine

Measles, rotavirus, and varicella vaccines are live attenuated viral vaccines that replicate in the host to produce immunity.

The Hepatitis B vaccine is a recombinant subunit vaccine containing purified HBsAg antigen produced in yeast cells, not a live virus.

Live vaccines are contraindicated in severe immunodeficiency, whereas recombinant vaccines like Hepatitis B are safe.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All the following viral vaccines are types of Live vaccines except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Hepatitis B vaccine

Viral vaccines can be live attenuated or inactivated/recombinant.

Live attenuated viral vaccines:

• Measles vaccine
• Rotavirus vaccine
• Varicella vaccine

Non-live (inactivated/recombinant) vaccine:

• Hepatitis B vaccine → recombinant subunit vaccine (HBsAg produced using yeast)

Key points:

• Live vaccines produce strong, long-lasting immunity
• They are contraindicated in immunocompromised individuals
• Recombinant vaccines are safer but may require booster doses

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An auxiliary nurse midwife is tasked with organizing a vaccination camp within a rural community. She has been provided with 2 vials that have been unsealed. Among these, one contains a pentavalent vaccine, while the other holds an MR vaccine. What options does she have in terms of effectively using these vials?
options: Use MR vaccine and discard pentavalent vaccine
Use pentavalent vaccine and discard MR vaccine
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Use pentavalent vaccine and discard MR vaccine

This scenario is governed by the Open Vial Policy (OVP) under the Universal Immunization Programme.

However, lyophilized (freeze-dried) vaccines must be discarded after reconstitution.

Pentavalent vaccine is a liquid, non-live, multi-dose vaccine that can be reused if the vial has been opened, provided cold chain is maintained, VVM is valid, expiry date not crossed, and aseptic technique was followed.

Exceptions to open vial policy: MMR, BCG, JE (Live), Yellow fever, COVID-19

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An eleven-month-old unimmunized child comes for immunization. Which vaccines should be given in this visit?
options: BCG, OPV, DPT and Hepatitis B vaccines
OPV, DPT and MR vaccines only
OPV, DPT, MR and Hepatitis B vaccines
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. OPV, DPT, MR and Hepatitis B vaccines

An 11-month-old unimmunized child should receive all age-appropriate catch-up vaccines in the same visit. These include:

• OPV
• DPT/Pentavalent (or DPT + Hepatitis B, depending on the schedule used)
• MR vaccine
• Hepatitis B

BCG is not routinely included in catch-up at this stage in standard examination-based catch-up schedules, making option D the best answer.

Why not the other options?

• A. BCG, OPV, DPT and Hepatitis B vaccines: No MR vaccine, which is due from 9 months onward.
• B. OPV, DPT and MR vaccines only: Omits Hepatitis B.
• C. BCG, DPT and MR vaccines: Omits OPV and Hepatitis B.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An unvaccinated pregnant woman comes for her first antenatal check-up. Which vaccine should be administered?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. TT

Pregnant women should be immunized against maternal and neonatal tetanus during antenatal care. Traditionally, Tetanus Toxoid (TT) was administered. Under the current Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) in India, Td vaccine (Tetanus-diphtheria) has replaced TT because it provides protection against both tetanus and diphtheria.

Current UIP Recommendation (India)

• Td-1: As early as possible during pregnancy.
• Td-2: At least 4 weeks after Td-1.
• If the woman has been adequately vaccinated in a previous pregnancy within the recommended interval, one Td booster is sufficient.

Why not the other options?

• A. DPT: Used in children; not recommended during pregnancy.
• C. DT: Pediatric vaccine for children who cannot receive pertussis vaccine.
• D. Pentavalent: Childhood vaccine (DPT + Hepatitis B + Hib), not used in pregnant women.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As per the National Immunization Schedule, PCV (Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine) is offered at:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 6 weeks, 14 weeks, 9 months

As per India’s National Immunization Schedule, PCV is given as:

• 6 weeks → PCV-1
• 14 weeks → PCV-2
• 9 months → PCV booster

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As per the Open Vial Policy, partially used multidose vials of which of the following vaccines can be used over more than one immunization session? 1. BCG vaccine 2. DPT vaccine 3. Hepatitis B vaccine 4. Measles vaccine Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2 and 3 only

The Open Vial Policy (OVP) of the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) allows certain opened multidose vaccine vials to be reused in subsequent immunization sessions for up to 28 days, provided they meet specific WHO-recommended storage and handling conditions. This policy helps reduce vaccine wastage without compromising safety.

• 1. BCG vaccine ✗

• BCG is a reconstituted vaccine and must be discarded within 4 hours of reconstitution or at the end of the immunization session.

• 2. DPT vaccine ✓

• DPT is covered under the Open Vial Policy and can be reused for up to 28 days if:

• Expiry date has not passed.
• Cold chain (2–8°C) has been maintained.
• Vial septum has not been contaminated.
• Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) is usable.

• 3. Hepatitis B vaccine ✓

• Hepatitis B vaccine is also covered under the Open Vial Policy and may be used for up to 28 days under the same conditions.

• 4. Measles vaccine ✗

• Measles vaccine is reconstituted and must be discarded within 4 hours of reconstitution or at the end of the session.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: At 6 weeks of life, a child developed a fever after DPT vaccination. And now child is 10 weeks due for vaccination. What should be done next?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Give DPT Vaccination

Mild adverse events following immunization, such as low-grade fever after DPT vaccination, are common and not a contraindication to subsequent doses.

• DPT vaccine can cause minor reactions like fever, irritability, and local pain
• These reactions do not warrant withholding or changing future doses
• True contraindications include severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) or encephalopathy after a previous dose

Clinical application:

• The child should continue the routine immunization schedule
• Subsequent doses of DPT should be given as planned

Key Distinction: True Contraindications vs. Precautions

| Reaction at 6 weeks | Action at 10 weeks

| ------------------- | ------------------

| Simple fever (<40.5°C) | ✅ Vaccinate normally

| Fever >40.5°C within 48h | ⚠️ Precaution — evaluate, likely still vaccinate

| Hypotonic-hyporesponsive episode (HHE) | ⚠️ Precaution

| Persistent inconsolable crying >3h | ⚠️ Precaution

| Encephalopathy within 7 days | ❌ TRUE contraindication — switch to DTaP/DT

| Anaphylaxis | ❌ TRUE contraindication

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: At a primary health center, a child received the BCG vaccine. On follow-up, the mother reports that no scar has developed at the vaccination site. Medical records confirm that the vaccine was administered. What should the medical officer advise the mother?
options: Reassure that nothing else is required
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Reassure that nothing else is required

Absence of a BCG scar does not indicate vaccine failure and does not correlate reliably with protection against tuberculosis.

As long as BCG vaccination is documented as given, revaccination is not recommended, regardless of scar formation.

Hence, the mother should be reassured, and no further intervention such as repeat BCG or Mantoux testing is required.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Calculate the median from the given set of observations: 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 4.5

With n = 8 (even), the median is the average of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th observations — that is, the 4th and 5th values:

2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8

• 4th observation = 4
• 5th observation = 5

Answer: 4.5

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following statements with regard to Ice-Lined Refrigerator (ILR) employed for storing vaccines at the sub-district level: I. These types of refrigerators are top-opening. II. Based on the temperature zone, the inside of ILRs can be divided into 3 parts. III. The upper part of ILR is cooler compared to the lower part. IV. Vaccines should never be kept directly on the floor of the ILR as they can get damaged. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. I and IV

An Ice-Lined Refrigerator (ILR) is the standard vaccine storage equipment used at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs), and sub-district health facilities under the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP). It maintains a temperature of +2°C to +8°C to preserve vaccine potency.

Why are I and IV correct?

• I. ILRs are top-opening refrigerators: Cold air is retained when the lid is opened, minimizing temperature fluctuations.
• IV. Vaccines should never be kept directly on the floor of the ILR: The floor is the coldest part due to the ice lining, and freeze-sensitive vaccines may be damaged if placed directly on it. Vaccines should always be stored in baskets.

Why are II and III incorrect?

• II. The inside of an ILR can be divided into 3 temperature zones: ILRs are generally considered to have two temperature zones (colder bottom and relatively warmer upper portion), not three.
• III. The upper part of the ILR is cooler than the lower part: The lower part is colder, while the upper part is relatively warmer because the ice lining is present along the walls and bottom.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following statements: 1. Hepatitis B vaccine has reduced efficacy if administered intramuscularly. 2. The maximum time allowed between reconstitution of MMR vaccine and use is 30 minutes. 3. Maternal antibodies do not interfere with cellular immune response to BCG vaccine. 4. DTwP is preferred to DTaP for primary immunization in most children. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 3 and 4

Immunization practices are based on vaccine characteristics, immune responses, and national recommendations. BCG induces a predominantly cell-mediated immune response that is not significantly affected by maternal antibodies, and DTwP is preferred over DTaP for routine primary immunization in most children because of its better effectiveness, longer duration of protection, and lower cost.

Why is D correct?

• 1. Hepatitis B vaccine has reduced efficacy if administered intramuscularly. ❌

• Hepatitis B vaccine is recommended to be administered intramuscularly (IM). Administration by the gluteal or subcutaneous route may reduce efficacy.

• 2. The maximum time allowed between reconstitution of MMR vaccine and use is 30 minutes. ❌

• Reconstituted MMR vaccine should generally be used within 4–6 hours (as per manufacturer recommendations) if stored appropriately, not within 30 minutes.

• 3. Maternal antibodies do not interfere with cellular immune response to BCG vaccine. ✅

• BCG induces T-cell-mediated immunity, which is not significantly affected by maternal antibodies, allowing vaccination at birth.

• 4. DTwP is preferred to DTaP for primary immunization in most children. ✅

• DTwP (whole-cell pertussis vaccine) is preferred in routine immunization programs because it provides stronger and longer-lasting immunity and is more cost-effective, despite higher reactogenicity.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Consider the following statements: Statement-1: In the National Immunization Program, BCG vaccine is given only on the left upper arm. Statement-2: This is done to maintain uniformity and for helping surveyors in verifying receipt of the vaccine. Which one of the following is correct?
options: Both Statement-1 and Statement-2 are correct and Statement-2 is the correct explanation for Statement-1.
Both Statement-1 and Statement-2 are correct and Statement-2 is not the correct explanation for Statement-1.
Statement-1 is true but Statement-2 is false.
Statement-1 is false but Statement-2 is true.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Both Statement-1 and Statement-2 are correct and Statement-2 is the correct explanation for Statement-1.

In India’s Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), the BCG vaccine is routinely administered intradermally over the left upper arm. This standardization ensures uniformity across the country and helps health workers and surveyors verify vaccination status by looking for the characteristic BCG scar during immunization surveys.

Why?

• Statement 1. In the National Immunization Program, BCG vaccine is given only on the left upper arm✔️: True. BCG is given in the left upper arm.
• Statement 2. This is done to maintain uniformity and for helping surveyors in verifying receipt of the vaccine✔️: True. The uniform site facilitates verification of vaccination during surveys and assessments.
• Statement-2 correctly explains Statement-1. ✔️

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Covaxin is a/an:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Inactivated whole virus vaccine

Covaxin (BBV152) is an inactivated whole-virion SARS-CoV-2 vaccine developed by Bharat Biotech in collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). It contains chemically inactivated SARS-CoV-2 virus with an Algel-IMDG adjuvant to enhance the immune response.

Why not the other options?

• A. Live attenuated vaccine❌: Contains weakened live virus; Covaxin is not live.
• C. Protein subunit vaccine❌: Example: Novavax (Covovax).
• D. Viral vector vaccine❌: Example: Covishield (ChAdOx1 nCoV-19) and Sputnik V.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Data arranged into two qualitative categories like 'Urban' and 'Rural' is best defined as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Nominal data

Categorical scales are divided into nominal (names only) and ordinal (order/ranking). Urban and Rural fall under nominal scale as they are qualitative classifications with no inherent order, measurement capability, or comparative relationship.

Data is divided into four levels of measurement:

| Type | Definition | Example

| ---- | ---------- | -------

| Nominal | Categories with no natural order — names/labels only | Urban/Rural, Male/Female, Blood groups, Religion

| Ordinal | Categories with natural order/ranking but unequal intervals | Mild/Moderate/Severe, Socioeconomic class I–V

| Interval | Ordered, equal intervals, no true zero | Temperature (°C), IQ score

| Ratio | Ordered, equal intervals, true zero exists | Height, Weight, Blood pressure, Age

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During an immunization session with 2 ANMs, a duration of 2 hours, and 40 vaccinations to be administered using a single vaccine carrier, which strategy would best minimize vaccine wastage and ensure effective session management?
options: Ask 1 ANM to make records and 1 ANM to give vaccination
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Ask 1 ANM to make records and 1 ANM to give vaccination

Efficient task allocation is essential for a successful immunization session. When two ANMs are available, assigning one ANM to vaccination and the other to registration, documentation, and beneficiary management improves workflow, minimizes delays, maintains the cold chain, and helps reduce vaccine wastage without requiring additional resources.

Why not the other options?

• A. Add 1 vaccine carrier: One properly packed vaccine carrier is adequate for 40 beneficiaries during a 2-hour session; an extra carrier is unnecessary.
• C. Add 1 hour and 1 vaccine carrier: Neither is required if the session is appropriately organized.
• D. Remove 20 children from the list: Reduces immunization coverage and is not an acceptable strategy.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: For the given Kaplan-Meier curve on the role of T-cells in the allograft rejection process, true statement is:
options: Only CD4 contributed to graft rejection significantly
Only CD8 contributed to graft rejection significantly
Both CD4 and CD8 protected against graft rejection significantly
Both CD4 and CD8 contributed to graft rejection significantly
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Both CD4 and CD8 contributed to graft rejection significantly

A Kaplan–Meier survival curve shows probability of survival over time. In transplant studies, it is used to evaluate graft survival under different immune conditions. Both CD4 and CD8 T-cells are crucial contributors to the allograft rejection process, and their combined depletion significantly prolongs graft survival.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Hepatitis B vaccine administered at birth is:
options: A combined vaccine of inactivated Polio and Hepatitis B
A monovalent vaccine of Hepatitis B
A fixed combination vaccine of Hib, Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. A monovalent vaccine of Hepatitis B

The birth dose of Hepatitis B vaccine given under the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) is a monovalent Hepatitis B vaccine. It should be administered within 24 hours of birth, irrespective of the mother’s hepatitis B status, to prevent perinatal (mother-to-child) transmission.

• A. A pentavalent vaccine ✗: Pentavalent vaccine is given at 6, 10, and 14 weeks, not at birth.
• B. A combined vaccine of inactivated Polio and Hepatitis B ✗: No such vaccine is used as the birth dose under UIP.
• C. A monovalent vaccine of Hepatitis B ✓: Correct. The birth dose is monovalent Hepatitis B vaccine.
• D. A fixed combination vaccine of Hib, Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B ✗: Such a combination is not part of the UIP birth schedule.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a 10-year-old school child, which of the following vaccines is given as a part of the school immunization program?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. TT/Td vaccine

Under the School Health Programme and Universal Immunization Programme, children around 10 years of age receive a Td (earlier TT) booster dose.

This booster maintains immunity against tetanus and diphtheria acquired from earlier childhood vaccinations.

Vaccines such as measles and rotavirus are given in infancy, while hepatitis B is part of the early childhood schedule, not routine school-age immunization.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a child diagnosed with Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID), which of the following vaccines is contraindicated?
questions.explanation:
