Correct answer: C. MMR vaccine

In Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID), live attenuated vaccines are contraindicated due to the risk of vaccine-derived infection.

Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) is a primary immunodeficiency disorder characterized by severe deficiency of T lymphocytes, impaired B-cell function and markedly weakened immune response.

Because these patients have severely impaired immunity, they cannot safely handle live attenuated vaccines, which contain weakened but still replicating organisms. Thus, live vaccines are contraindicated in SCID.

MMR is a live vaccine, whereas IPV, Hepatitis B, and DTaP are inactivated or toxoid vaccines and are safe.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a child who has not received any dose of DPT and OPV immunization, up to what age can these vaccines be given under the Universal Immunization Programme?
options: DPT up to 7 years of age and OPV up to 5 years of age
DPT up to 8 years of age and OPV up to 6 years of age
DPT up to 10 years of age and OPV up to 7 years of age
DPT up to 12 years of age and OPV up to 10 years of age
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. DPT up to 7 years of age and OPV up to 5 years of age

Under the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), catch-up vaccination is recommended for children who have missed routine immunization. A completely unimmunized child can receive DPT up to 7 years of age and OPV up to 5 years of age as part of the UIP catch-up schedule.

High-Yield Pearls

• DPT can be given up to 7 years of age under UIP catch-up vaccination.
• OPV can be given up to 5 years of age under UIP.
• After 7 years of age, Td (Tetanus-diphtheria) vaccine replaces DPT because the pertussis component is not routinely recommended in older children.
• OPV is not routinely administered after 5 years of age, except during Pulse Polio Immunization campaigns.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a given set of conditions, a screening test has 90% sensitivity and 90% specificity for screening a particular disease. The prevalence of the disease at the given time in that population is 10%. Which one of the following statements regarding positive predictive value of the test is correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. The positive predictive value is 50%.

Assume a population of 1000 people.

• Diseased = 10% of 1000 = 100
•

Non-diseased = 900

•

True positives = 90% of 100 = 90

• False positives = 10% of 900 = 90

PPV = TP / (TP + FP)

= 90 / (90 + 90)

= 50%

Therefore, the correct answer is D. 50%.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a normally distributed group of 100 students, the mean height is 105 cm and the standard deviation (SD) is 10 cm. Calculate the Standard error of mean range that covers approximately 95% of the values.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 103-107 cms

SEmean = SD / Square root of sample size

SEmean = 10/ 10 = 1cm

Hence,

Confidence interval for 95% population: mean +/- 2SE = 105 +/- 2cm

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a renal function study, the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) was found to follow a normal distribution with a mean of 126 ml/min. The range corresponding to ±2 standard deviations is 124–128 ml/min. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: 95% GFR values lie more than 126 ml/min
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 95% GFR values lie between 124-128 ml/min

In a normal (Gaussian) distribution, approximately 95% of observations lie within ±2 standard deviations (SD) of the mean. This is the basis of the 68–95–99.7 rule, which is commonly used to interpret biological and clinical data.

Why not the other options?

• A. 68% GFR values lie between 124–128 ml/min: 68% of observations lie within ±1 SD, not ±2 SD.
• B. 95% GFR values lie more than 126 ml/min: Incorrect. a normal distribution is symmetrical, with about 50% of values above and 50% below the mean.
• D. Study is not accurate: Incorrect. the data are consistent with a normal distribution.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a study involving 100 patients, which statistical test is most appropriate for comparing improvement in cholesterol levels after 3 months?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Paired t-test

A paired t-test is used to compare the means of a continuous variable measured twice in the same individuals (e.g., cholesterol levels before treatment and after 3 months). It determines whether the mean difference between paired observations is statistically significant.

Why not the other options?

• B. Unpaired t-test: Compares the means of two independent groups (e.g., treatment group vs control group).
• C. ANOVA: Compares the means of three or more groups.
• D. Chi-square test: Used to compare categorical variables or proportions, not continuous data.

| Statistical Test | Data Type | Used For | Example

| ---------------- | --------- | -------- | -------

| Paired t-test | Continuous | Compare two related means (same subjects before vs after) | BP before and after treatment, Cholesterol before and after 3 months

| Unpaired (Independent) t-test | Continuous | Compare two independent group means | Mean Hb in males vs females

| ANOVA (One-way) | Continuous | Compare ≥3 independent group means | Mean BP in three treatment groups

| Repeated Measures ANOVA | Continuous | Compare ≥3 measurements in the same individuals | BP at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months

| Chi-square test | Categorical | Compare proportions/association between categorical variables | Smoking vs lung cancer, Vaccine status vs disease

| Fisher’s Exact Test | Categorical | Chi-square alternative when expected cell count <5 | Small sample 2×2 table

| Pearson Correlation (r) | Continuous | Measure strength and direction of linear correlation | Height vs weight

| Linear Regression | Continuous | Predict one continuous variable from another | Predict BP from age

| Logistic Regression | Binary outcome | Identify predictors of a binary outcome | Risk factors for hypertension (Yes/No)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a study involving radiographic evaluations, two physicians independently assessed 100 chest X-rays. They calculated a Kappa statistic of 0.71 to measure inter-rater agreement. What does this Kappa value indicate about the level of agreement between the two doctors?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Substantial

The Kappa statistic measures inter-rater agreement beyond chance.

It is commonly used when:

• Two or more observers classify categorical data
• We want to evaluate reliability of diagnostic interpretation

Why Kappa is Needed? If two doctors read the same X-ray:

• Some agreement occurs by chance alone
• Simple percent agreement overestimates true reliability

Kappa adjusts for this chance agreement.

A Kappa value of 0.71 falls in the range of 0.61–0.80, which corresponds to substantial agreement.

Values above 0.80 indicate almost perfect agreement, while lower values reflect moderate to poor reliability.

Importance in Research

Kappa is used for:

• Diagnostic reliability studies
• Inter-observer variability analysis
• Questionnaire validation
• Clinical classification systems

Higher κ values indicate more reliable assessments.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a study, an investigator selected a group of children and divided them into two groups. The mean weight, height, and standard deviation (SD) for each group were measured and compared. Which statistical test of significance should be used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Unpaired t-test

The study compares the means of continuous variables (weight and height) between two independent groups of children.

For continuous variables comparing two independent groups, the correct test is: Unpaired Student’s t-test

An unpaired (independent samples) t-test is appropriate for testing whether the difference between the two-group means is statistically significant.

A paired t-test is used for related samples, Chi-square for categorical data, and ANOVA when comparing more than two groups.

| Situation | Statistical Test

| --------- | ----------------

| Continuous data, same group twice | Paired t-test

| Continuous data, two independent groups | Unpaired t-test

| Continuous data, >2 groups | ANOVA

| Categorical variables | Chi-square

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In countries with low levels of measles transmission, what should be the appropriate age for starting immunization with measles-containing vaccine (MCV)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 12 months

The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends that the age of the first dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) depends on the level of measles transmission in the country. In countries with low measles transmission, vaccination is started at 12 months of age, as maternal antibodies have largely disappeared, resulting in a better immune response.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A. 6 months: Reserved for outbreak situations or infants at high risk; this dose does not replace the routine first dose.
• B. 9 months: Recommended in countries with high measles transmission (including India under UIP) to provide early protection.
• D. 15–18 months: This is the age for the second dose (MCV2/MR2), not the first dose.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In which phase of clinical trials is drug dosing determined?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Phase 2

Phase 1 → Dose range determination

• First-in-human studies
• Finds:

• Maximum tolerated dose (MTD)
• Safe dose range

• Done mostly in healthy volunteers

Phase 2 → Optimal dose in patients

• Conducted in patients with disease
• Identifies:

• Effective dose (therapeutic dose)
• Dose-response relationship

• This is what you're referring to as “optimal drug dose”

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Malnutrition status is compared between children from two different villages. Which statistical test should be used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Chi-square test

• "Malnutrition status" is a categorical (qualitative) variable.

• Two independent groups are being compared.

• Chi-square compares proportions between categorical variables.

• It is used for contingency tables.

• Paired t-test compares means in paired observations.
• Unpaired t-test compares means of continuous variables.
• ANOVA compares means among three or more groups.
• Chi-square requires adequate expected cell frequencies.
• If expected counts are very small, Fisher's exact test is preferred.
• Categorical vs categorical = Chi-square test.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: On January 1, 2024, an area with a population of 10,000 had 100 TB cases. During the year, 30 patients were cured and 10 died. Twenty new TB cases were reported, and 5 of them were cured before December 31, 2024. What is the incidence of TB cases?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 2.02 per 1000 population

Incidence (new cases during 2024)

Only new TB cases count:

• New cases = 20
• Population at risk= 10,000-100 = 9900

Incidence (per 1000 population):

• Incidence = 20/9900 × 1000 = 2.02 per 1000

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Quartiles are measures of which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Locations

Quartiles and tertiles divide an ordered dataset into equal parts and indicate the position (location) of observations within the distribution.

Other measures of location include Deciles (divide data into 10 parts), Percentiles (divide data into 100 parts). These measures help describe the distribution pattern of data rather than its average or variability.

They are measures of location, not central tendency, dispersion, or correlation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Rotavirus vaccination is avoided during an episode of diarrhoea because:
options: It might compromise uptake of vaccine.
It could trigger an episode of intussusception.
Rotavirus vaccine is a live vaccine and hence may cause rotavirus diarrhoea and worsen the diarrhoeal episode.
Vomiting is a significant adverse effect of Rotavirus vaccine.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. It might compromise uptake of vaccine.

Rotavirus vaccine is a live attenuated oral vaccine administered to infants to prevent severe rotavirus gastroenteritis. It should be deferred in infants with moderate or severe acute diarrhoea or vomiting, as the illness may reduce intestinal uptake of the vaccine, leading to a suboptimal immune response. Vaccination can be given once the child has recovered.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• B. It could trigger an episode of intussusception: Rotavirus vaccine has a very small association with intussusception, but this is not the reason for postponing vaccination during an episode of diarrhoea.
• C. Rotavirus vaccine is a live vaccine and hence may cause rotavirus diarrhoea and worsen the diarrhoeal episode: Although it is a live attenuated vaccine, it does not cause clinically significant rotavirus diarrhoea in healthy infants.
• D. Vomiting is a significant adverse effect of Rotavirus vaccine: Mild vomiting may occur occasionally, but it is not the reason for delaying vaccination during acute diarrhoea.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Several randomized controlled trials evaluating a new drug are statistically pooled to obtain an overall estimate of treatment effect. This study is called:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Meta-analysis

• A meta-analysis combines data from multiple studies quantitatively.
• It increases statistical power by pooling sample sizes.
• Provides a more precise estimate of treatment effect.
• It is often performed after a systematic review.
• Forest plots are commonly used to display results.
• Heterogeneity is assessed using I² statistics.
• Publication bias may be evaluated using a funnel plot.
• Meta-analysis occupies the highest level of evidence.
• Systematic review summarizes evidence qualitatively.
• Meta-analysis provides both qualitative and quantitative synthesis.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The blood glucose level of 5 individuals was 110, 94, 102, 98, 96. Consider the following statements: 1. The range is 16. 2. The median is 98. 3. The standard deviation is √10. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1 and 2 only

• The question tests the basic measures of central tendency and dispersion.
• Given blood glucose values: 110, 94, 102, 98, 96
•

Arrange the values in ascending order: 94, 96, 98, 102, 110

•

Statement 1. The range is 16: Correct.

• Range = Highest value − Lowest value
• = 110 − 94 = 16

• Statement 2. The median is 98: Correct.

• Median is the middle observation after arranging the data.
• Median = 98

• Statement 3. The standard deviation is √10: Incorrect.

• Mean = 100
• Variance = (100 + 36 + 4 + 4 + 16)/5 = 32
• Standard deviation = √32 = 4√2 ≈ 5.66, not √10.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The event related to vaccination which can be a contraindication for the next vaccination of similar/identical type is:
options: Abscess at injection site after DPT vaccine
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Encephalopathy following DPT vaccine

Encephalopathy occurring within 7 days of a previous pertussis-containing vaccine (DPT/DTaP), with no other identifiable cause, is a contraindication to further doses of pertussis-containing vaccines. The child should subsequently receive DT (diphtheria-tetanus) vaccine without the pertussis component.

Why not the other options?

• A. Syncope following MMR vaccine: Vasovagal syncope is not a contraindication to future vaccination.
• C. Abscess at injection site after DPT vaccine: Local injection-site reactions or sterile abscesses are not contraindications.
• D. Gastroenteritis following MMR vaccine: Mild adverse events are not contraindications to subsequent doses.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The world's only licensed malaria vaccine, MOSQUIRIX (RTS,S), is prepared from which component of Plasmodium falciparum?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Circumsporozoite protein

RTS,S (brand name MOSQUIRIX) is a recombinant protein-based vaccine that targets the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) of Plasmodium falciparum, the protein found on the surface of the sporozoite — the pre-erythrocytic stage injected by the Anopheles mosquito during a bite.

| Feature | Detail

| ------- | ------

| Vaccine name | RTS,S / MOSQUIRIX

| Target antigen | Circumsporozoite protein (CSP) of P. falciparum

| Carrier/adjuvant | Fused with Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) + AS01 adjuvant

| Status | First licensed malaria vaccine

| Efficacy | \~26–50% (partial protection, wanes over time)

| Stage targeted | Pre-erythrocytic (sporozoite stage) — prevents hepatocyte invasion

Why each distractor is wrong:

• A. Gametocytic protein — Gametocyte-stage antigens are the target of transmission-blocking vaccine candidates (e.g., Pfs25), not RTS,S.
• B. Polysaccharide sheath — Plasmodium has no polysaccharide capsule/sheath; this is a feature of certain bacteria (e.g., pneumococcus), not protozoa.
• D. Lipoprotein envelope — Malaria parasites don't have a lipoprotein envelope in the way enveloped viruses do; this is a distractor with no real basis in Plasmodium biology.

Exam Pearl: Remember "CSP for Circumsporozoite" — RTS,S works by inducing antibodies + CD4+ T-cell response against CSP, blocking sporozoites from invading hepatocytes. A newer vaccine, R21/Matrix-M, also targets CSP but with higher efficacy (\~70-80%) and was WHO-recommended after RTS,S — good to remember for newer-pattern questions, since INICET/NEET PG increasingly tests recent WHO vaccine recommendations.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: True regarding Oral Cholera vaccine ‘Sanchol’ is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Bivalent with 2 doses

Shanchol is an oral killed whole-cell cholera vaccine that is bivalent, providing protection against Vibrio cholerae O1 and O139.

It requires two doses, given at an interval of about 2 weeks, to achieve adequate immunity.

DUKORAL:

Type: Killed whole-cell Vibrio cholerae O1 + recombinant B subunit of cholera toxin (rCTB)

Age: Approved for ≥2 years

Key feature: Contains B subunit toxin → provides additional antitoxin immunity (reduces severity of diarrhea)

Administration: Given orally with bicarbonate buffer (protects antigen from gastric acid)

Schedule:

• ≥6 years: 2 doses (1–6 weeks apart)
• 2–5 years: 3 doses

Protection: Duration \~ 2 years (booster needed thereafter)

Extra benefit: Also offers partial protection against ETEC (traveler’s diarrhea) due to B subunit similarity

Shanchol® / mORCVAX®

• Killed whole-cell vaccine containing:

• V. cholerae O1 (El Tor + Classical biotypes)
• V. cholerae O139

• No B subunit

Age: Approved for ≥1 year

Administration: Oral, no buffer required (major operational advantage in mass campaigns)

Schedule: 2 doses (2 weeks apart)

Protection: Duration \~ 3–5 years (longer than Dukoral in field use)

Public health use:

• Preferred for mass vaccination programs (WHO-recommended in endemic areas)
• Cheaper, easier logistics

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Vaccine kept at the lowest level inside an Ice lined refrigerator (ILR) at PHC:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. OPV

In an Ice Lined Refrigerator (ILR), the lowest level is the coldest zone, most prone to freezing.

OPV is a heat-sensitive but freeze-stable vaccine, so it is safely stored at the lowest level of the ILR.

In contrast, DPT and Hepatitis B are freeze-sensitive and must be kept in warmer zones, while BCG and rotavirus vaccines have different stability considerations.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis (VAPP) is chiefly seen with which of the following strains of oral poliovirus?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. OPV 3

Vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis (VAPP) is most commonly associated with the type 3 strain of the oral polio vaccine (OPV).

Vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis (VAPP) type 3 is a rare complication of the oral polio vaccine (OPV) where the type 3 attenuated strain reverts to a neurovirulent form, causing acute flaccid paralysis. It typically affects a primary vaccine recipient or an unimmunized close contact, rather than sparking wider community outbreaks.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the purpose of exploring heterogeneity in meta-analysis?
options: To assess the risk of bias in the included studies
To determine if the included studies are of high quality
To estimate the overall effect size of the meta-analysis
To identify the potential variation between the included studies
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. To identify the potential variation between the included studies

Heterogeneity in a meta-analysis refers to the variation in study results arising from differences in study populations, interventions, outcomes, or methodology. Exploring heterogeneity helps determine whether the observed differences between studies are due to chance or reflect true clinical or methodological variation, thereby guiding the interpretation of pooled results.

• Exploring heterogeneity identifies the potential variation between included studies and helps assess whether it is appropriate to combine their results in a meta-analysis.

Why not the other options?

• A. To assess the risk of bias in the included studies: Risk of bias is evaluated using dedicated tools (e.g., Cochrane Risk of Bias tool, ROBINS-I), not by heterogeneity analysis.
• B. To determine if the included studies are of high quality: Quality assessment is performed separately using methodological quality assessment tools.
• C. To estimate the overall effect size of the meta-analysis: This is the primary purpose of meta-analysis, whereas heterogeneity analysis evaluates the consistency of study results.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following agencies are playing a key role in running of the COVAX initiative against COVID-19? 1. GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance 2. World Health Organisation (WHO) 3. Ford Foundation 4. Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2 and 4

COVAX is a global initiative launched to ensure equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines worldwide. It is co-led by:

• GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance
• World Health Organization (WHO)
• Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI)

(UNICEF is the key procurement and delivery partner.)

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. GAVI\, the Vaccine Alliance✔️: Co-leads the COVAX initiative.
• 2. World Health Organization (WHO)✔️: Provides technical leadership and policy guidance.
• 3. Ford Foundation❌: Not a partner in running COVAX.
• 4. Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI)✔️: Co-leads vaccine research and development.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following are correct with regard to BCG vaccination? 1. It is a live-attenuated vaccine. 2. It is administered by intramuscular injection. 3. It is derived from Mycobacterium bovis. 4. It is highly immunogenic. Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 3 and 4

Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) is a live-attenuated vaccine derived from Mycobacterium bovis. It is administered intradermally at birth as part of the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) to protect against severe forms of childhood tuberculosis, particularly TB meningitis and miliary tuberculosis.

Why is C correct?

• 1. It is a live-attenuated vaccine✅: BCG contains a live attenuated strain of Mycobacterium bovis.
• 3. It is derived from Mycobacterium bovis✅: Developed from an attenuated strain of M. bovis.
• 4. It is highly immunogenic✅: Induces a strong cell-mediated immune response, providing good protection against severe childhood TB.

Incorrect statement:

• 2. It is administered by intramuscular injection❌: BCG is given intradermally, not intramuscularly.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following does not have polysaccharide vaccine?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hepatitis B

Polysaccharide vaccines are directed against encapsulated bacteria and target their capsular polysaccharide antigens. Conjugation with protein improves immunogenicity in children

Organisms with polysaccharide (or conjugate) vaccines:

• Pneumococcus (Streptococcus pneumoniae)
• Meningococcus (Neisseria meningitidis)
• Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)

Exception:

• Hepatitis B vaccine is not a polysaccharide vaccine; it is a recombinant subunit vaccine (HBsAg)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following events could be caused or precipitated by an active component of vaccine? 1. Anaphylaxis after measles vaccine 2. Encephalopathy after DPT vaccine 3. Adenitis following BCG vaccine 4. Gastroenteritis following MMR vaccine Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2, 3 and 4

Vaccine product-related reactions are adverse events caused by the active component (antigen/live organism) of the vaccine. These include:

• Encephalopathy (rarely) after pertussis-containing (DPT) vaccine.
• BCG adenitis due to replication of the live attenuated BCG bacilli.
• Mild gastroenteritis may occur after live viral vaccines such as MMR, although it is uncommon.

Why not statement 1?

• Anaphylaxis after measles vaccine is usually due to vaccine excipients (e.g., gelatin or neomycin), not the active viral component.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following immunizations are recommended for persons infected with HIV? 1. Hepatitis B vaccine 2. Influenza virus vaccine 3. Pneumococcal vaccine Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2 and 3

People living with HIV (PLHIV) are at increased risk of vaccine-preventable infections due to impaired immunity. Therefore, inactivated vaccines such as Hepatitis B, Influenza, and Pneumococcal vaccines are routinely recommended, while the use of live vaccines depends on the patient’s CD4 count and degree of immunosuppression.

Why is D correct?

• 1. Hepatitis B vaccine✅: Recommended for all susceptible HIV-infected individuals because of the increased risk of chronic HBV infection.
• 2. Influenza vaccine✅: Annual inactivated influenza vaccine is recommended for all PLHIV.
• 3. Pneumococcal vaccine✅: Recommended to reduce the risk of invasive pneumococcal disease; includes PCV followed by PPSV23 as per guidelines.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements about the standard normal distribution curve is true?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Mean = Median

The standard normal distribution (also called Gaussian distribution) is a perfectly symmetrical, bell-shaped curve. Its properties :

Key properties:

| Property | Value

| -------- | -----

| Shape | Perfectly symmetrical, bell-shaped

| Mean | = Median = Mode

| Skewness | Zero (no skew)

| Total area under curve | = 1 (or 100%)

| Mean ± 1 SD | Covers 68.27% of observations

| Mean ± 2 SD | Covers 95.45% of observations

| Mean ± 3 SD | Covers 99.73% of observations

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct about oral rotavirus vaccines? I. The storage should be at 2–8°C II. The vaccine should be used within 2 hours of reconstitution or opening III. Past history of intussusception is a contraindication IV. The vaccine can be given if the baby has ongoing diarrhoea Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. I and III

Rotavirus vaccine is a live attenuated oral vaccine included in the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) to prevent severe rotavirus gastroenteritis, one of the leading causes of severe diarrhea in infants and young children.

The vaccine should be stored at 2–8°C, and a previous history of intussusception is a contraindication to its administration.

Why is C correct?

• I. The storage should be at 2–8°C. ✔

• Correct.
• Rotavirus vaccine must be maintained in the cold chain (2–8°C) to preserve its potency.

• II. The vaccine should be used within 2 hours of reconstitution or opening. ✘

• Incorrect.
• This recommendation applies to certain reconstituted injectable vaccines (e.g., BCG, measles-containing vaccines), not oral rotavirus vaccines.

• III. Past history of intussusception is a contraindication. ✔

• Correct.
• Rotavirus vaccines are contraindicated in infants with:

• Previous intussusception
• Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)
• Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose

• IV. The vaccine can be given if the baby has ongoing diarrhoea. ✘

• Incorrect.
• In infants with moderate or severe acute gastroenteritis/diarrhea, vaccination should generally be deferred until recovery.
• Mild illness is not a contraindication.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding vaccination routes for children? I. Hepatitis B vaccine given in deltoid region has reduced efficacy II. Two vaccines may be given in the same thigh, but separated by 1 inch III. Separate sites are used when administering a vaccine and an immunoglobulin IV. Two intramuscular vaccines may be given on the same day but in separate limbs Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. II and III

Multiple vaccines can be safely administered during the same visit using different anatomical sites. When two injectable vaccines are given in the same limb, they should be administered at least 2.5 cm (1 inch) apart to allow identification of local reactions. Similarly, when a vaccine and an immunoglobulin are administered simultaneously, they should be given at different anatomical sites using separate syringes to avoid interference with vaccine efficacy.

• I. Hepatitis B vaccine given in deltoid region has reduced efficacy. ✘

• Incorrect. In older children, adolescents, and adults, the deltoid is the preferred site for Hepatitis B vaccination.
• Reduced efficacy occurs when the vaccine is administered in the gluteal region due to injection into adipose tissue.

• II. Two vaccines may be given in the same thigh, but separated by 1 inch. ✔

• Correct. Injectable vaccines can be administered in the same thigh, provided the injection sites are at least 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart.

• III. Separate sites are used when administering a vaccine and an immunoglobulin. ✔

• Correct. Vaccines and immunoglobulins should be administered at different anatomical sites with separate syringes.

• IV. Two intramuscular vaccines may be given on the same day but in separate limbs. ✘

• Incorrect. They may be given in separate limbs, but it is not mandatory. They can also be given in the same limb if spaced adequately apart.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statistical terms is incorrectly matched with its associated concept?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Mean, Median – Dispersion

Mean and median are measures of central tendency, not dispersion.

Standard error reflects variability of a sample statistic.

Correlation coefficient measures relationship between variables.

Moments are numerical measures that describe the shape of a distribution about a reference point (usually the mean). They help in understanding not just where the data is centered, but how the data is distributed around that centre.

• First moment (about the mean) → Mean (measure of central tendency)
• Second central moment → Variance (measure of dispersion)
• Third central moment → Skewness (measure of asymmetry of the distribution)
• Fourth central moment → Kurtosis (measure of peak / tail heaviness of the distribution)

Hence, the incorrect match is Mean, Median – Dispersion.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following treatments for a pregnant lady who has been exposed to a patient of chicken pox are correct? 1. Varicella-zoster immune globulin 2. Varicella-zoster vaccine 3. Acyclovir 4. Prednisolone Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1 and 3 only

A susceptible pregnant woman exposed to varicella (chickenpox) should receive Varicella-zoster immune globulin (VZIG) as post-exposure prophylaxis to reduce disease severity. If she develops varicella infection, acyclovir is recommended, particularly if started within 24 hours of rash onset or in severe disease.

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. Varicella-zoster immune globulin (VZIG) ✔️ – Recommended after significant exposure in a non-immune pregnant woman.
• 2. Varicella-zoster vaccine ❌ – A live attenuated vaccine; contraindicated during pregnancy.
• 3. Acyclovir ✔️ – Used if the pregnant woman develops chickenpox, especially in moderate-to-severe disease.
• 4. Prednisolone ❌ – No role in routine post-exposure prophylaxis or treatment of maternal varicella.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following vaccines are given through the intramuscular route? 1. BCG vaccine 2. Hepatitis B vaccine 3. Pentavalent vaccine 4. Inactivated Polio vaccine Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 2, 3 and 4

The following vaccines are administered by the intramuscular (IM) route:

• Hepatitis B vaccine ✔️
• Pentavalent vaccine (DPT-HepB-Hib) ✔️
• Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) ✔️ (full-dose IPV)

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. BCG vaccine❌: Given intradermally.
• 2. Hepatitis B vaccine✔️: Given intramuscularly.
• 3. Pentavalent vaccine✔️: Given intramuscularly.
• 4. Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV)✔️: Given intramuscularly (fractional IPV is given intradermally).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following vaccines are live vaccines?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Measles, OPV, Yellow Fever (17D) Vaccine

All three vaccines in option B. are live attenuated vaccines:

• Measles vaccine → Live attenuated
• OPV (oral polio vaccine) → Live attenuated
• Yellow fever 17D vaccine → Live attenuated

Why not the others?

• A. IPV is inactivated, not live.
• C. IPV is inactivated; plague vaccine is not a live vaccine in the conventional exam classification.
• D. Hib and HBV vaccines are non-live; only OPV is live.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following sets of vaccines is contraindicated in pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Varicella, Measles, Rubella

• (a) Pneumococcal, Hepatitis B, HPV — Incorrect: These are not all contraindicated in pregnancy. Hepatitis B can be given when indicated.
• (b) Rabies, Influenza, Hepatitis A — Incorrect: Rabies PEP and inactivated influenza vaccines can be given during pregnancy when indicated.
• (c) Varicella, Measles, Rubella — Correct: These are live attenuated viral vaccines and are contraindicated during pregnancy because of the theoretical risk to the fetus.
• (d) Diphtheria, Influenza, Pneumococcal — Incorrect: Inactivated influenza and Td/Tdap-containing vaccines can be administered during pregnancy when indicated.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which one of the following vaccines is an exception to the principle “At least 4 weeks interval is needed between two doses of the same vaccine to ensure adequate immune response”?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Rabies vaccine

Rabies vaccine is an exception to the usual 4-week interval principle because the post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) schedule requires doses at shorter intervals:

• Day 0
• Day 3
• Day 7
• Day 14
• Day 28 (when indicated)

Why not other options?

• B. HPV: Doses are separated by months depending on age.
• C. Varicella: 2 doses require a minimum interval of 4 weeks in older children/adults.
• D. Hepatitis B: Given at 0, 1 and 6 months.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which type of graph is most appropriate for representing the following data?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Scatter diagram

A scatter diagram (scatter plot) is used to display the relationship (correlation) between two quantitative variables. Each observation is represented by a point, making it useful for assessing the strength and direction of association between variables.

Why not the other options?

• A. Frequency polygon/curve: Used to display the frequency distribution of continuous data.
• B. Histogram: Represents the frequency distribution of continuous variables using adjacent bars.
• C. Line chart: Used to show trends or changes over time (time-series data).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: While evaluating an influenza vaccine, it demonstrated an efficacy of 90% in randomized controlled trials, an effectiveness of 85%, and a protection rate of 85% in post-surveillance. Which of the following statements is incorrect? a. 90% chance that those who receive the vaccine will not be infected compared to those who were not vaccinated in a real-world scenario b. 85% chance that those who receive the vaccine will not be infected compared to those who were not vaccinated in the clinical trial c. Protection depends on the disease attack rate d. Vaccine effectiveness may be lower than efficacy
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. a and b

Interpret vaccine efficacy, effectiveness, and protection rate correctly. Vaccine efficacy measures the percentage reduction in disease among vaccinated individuals under ideal conditions in randomized controlled trials (RCTs), whereas vaccine effectiveness measures the reduction in disease under real-world (field) conditions. Protection rate represents the proportion of vaccinated individuals protected from disease in the population and is influenced by the background attack rate.

Key Pearls:

• Vaccine efficacy → Assessed in randomized controlled trials (ideal conditions).
• Vaccine effectiveness → Assessed in real-world settings; may be lower than efficacy due to field conditions.
• Protection rate → Depends on the disease attack rate in the population.
• Efficacy ≠ Effectiveness: Trial results cannot be directly interpreted as real-world performance, and vice versa.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: You are a medical officer at PHC collecting data for disease burden in your catchment population. You divide diseased population into mild, moderate and severe groups. And then few are selected from each group for the study. This is which type of sampling?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Stratified random sampling

Sampling is the process of selecting a subset of individuals from a population to represent the entire population. When the population is heterogeneous, researchers often divide it into subgroups (strata) based on certain characteristics before sampling. This method is called stratified sampling.

The population is first divided into homogeneous subgroups (strata) based on disease severity (mild, moderate, severe), and then samples are randomly selected from each stratum.

This defines stratified random sampling, used to ensure adequate representation of all subgroups, improves precision of estimates and reduces sampling error.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: You are shown several vaccine vials with different Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) stages. Based on the condition of the VVMs shown in the image, which of the following vaccine vials is suitable for use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2 only

A Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) indicates cumulative heat exposure of a vaccine.

A vial is usable only when the inner square is lighter than the outer circle (VVM stages 1 and 2).

Once the inner square becomes equal to or darker than the outer circle (stages 3 and 4), the vaccine has lost potency and must be discarded.

Therefore, only vials 1 and 2 are suitable for use.
